excerpt: Same resort, same architect, a year apart — but Gramacho and Vale da Pinta have very different reputations near Carvoeiro. Here's how the crowd-pleaser and the tougher test actually compare.

content.text: Gramacho and Vale da Pinta sit inside the same Pestana resort near Carvoeiro, opened within a year of each other in the early '90s, and share the same architect. Ask around locally, though, and most golfers will tell you the same thing: one of them is the crowd-pleaser, the other is the one serious players ask for by name.
One resort, one designer, a year apart

**Ronald Fream** designed both courses for the Pestana Carvoeiro resort — Gramacho first, opening in 1991 with later input from world number one golfer **Nick Price**, followed by Vale da Pinta in 1992. Both weave through the rocky, wooded terrain typical of this stretch of coast, but the two courses feel genuinely different to play.
Gramacho: the course with 27 greens

Gramacho plays 6,107 metres par 72 and has a genuine design quirk: it's built with 18 fairways but **27 greens**, meaning several holes can be played into a completely different green depending on the day, changing the approach shot each time. It's hosted the Portuguese Ladies Open on multiple occasions, and centuries-old carob, almond and olive trees line the fairways alongside artfully placed lakes and bunkers. It's considered the more approachable of the two, well suited to resort golfers rather than just low handicappers.
Stay inside the resort at [Pestana Gramacho Residences](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/pestana-gramacho-residences.html), a golf aparthotel 500 metres from the clubhouse.
Vale da Pinta: the wilder, tougher sibling

Vale da Pinta plays 6,127 metres par 71, and it's widely considered the stronger test of the two Pestana courses. Ancient olive and carob trees survive as living obstacles throughout the layout, two lakes influence four holes, and strategic dog-legs punish an inaccurate drive more than Gramacho does. Bent-grass greens hold their pace year-round, which matters on a course where precision counts.
Which one should you play?

If you want a fun, varied resort round with a genuine design novelty and a tournament pedigree, play Gramacho. If you want the tougher, more characterful test — tighter driving, ancient trees in play, a course regulars rate as the better of the two — play Vale da Pinta. Green fees start from the same **€95** at both, and since they share a resort, playing both on the same trip is the obvious move.

Want the numbers side by side instead? [Open the course comparator](/?compare=gramacho,vale-da-pinta) to see Gramacho and Vale da Pinta's price, par, handicap limits and facilities pulled straight from our live course data.

excerpt: Two courses where every hole is a par 3, plus one clifftop course with a famous exception — the Algarve's short-game and beginner-friendly rounds, with real par, length and price for each.

content.text: Not every round in the Algarve needs to be five hours and eighteen full-length holes. A par-3 course is the fastest way to sharpen your short game, introduce a beginner to golf without intimidating them, or fit in a round on a travel day. This guide compares two genuine all-par-3 courses and a clifftop nine that is home to the region's most famous par 3. They aren't the only short options: Amendoeira, for example, has a nine-hole par-3 Academy course, covered in our guide to [night golf in the Algarve](/guide/night-golf-in-the-algarve).
Vale de Milho — the purest short-game test

Every one of Vale de Milho's nine holes is a par 3, ranging from around 60 to 160 metres, on a hillside above Carvoeiro with sea views from several tees. Dave Thomas — Ryder Cup player and designer of more than 40 courses, including the Belfry — laid it out in 1990, and it's held up as one of the best dedicated short-game venues in the Algarve, not just a beginner's course. A second nine-hole loop with different tee positions is available if you want to play on.
Balaia: short holes in a resort setting

Balaia's nine holes are also all par 3, running from 58 to 160 metres through the grounds of the Balaia Golf Village resort near Albufeira. The short holes make it a relaxed first stop for newer golfers and juniors, and there is a practice range next to the clubhouse if you want to warm up before you play. Note that the resort's guest information says a handicap is required, without giving a limit, so check with the club if you have only just started. On the club's 2025-26 price list, a visitor's day green fee is **€50**.
The [Balaia Golf Village Resort](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/balaia-golf-village.html) sits right on the course, so it's easy to fit in a few holes before breakfast.
Pine Cliffs: four par 3s and one that will test you

Pine Cliffs isn't a pure par-3 course, as four of its nine holes are par 3s and the rest are short par 4s, but it earns its place here for the **Devil's Parlour**, the par-3 sixth, which the club describes as a 197-metre carry over a ravine, to a green perched on the cliff edge. Martin Hawtree designed the course for what's now the Pine Cliffs Resort, and the club's local rules let players without a handicap play from the red tees, so it is genuinely open to newer golfers, even with that one dramatic exception.
Staying at the [Pine Cliffs Residence](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/pine-cliffs-residence.html) puts the course, and that cliff-edge tee shot, right outside your door.
Looking for more nine-hole options beyond pure par-3 golf? See our full guide to the [Algarve's 9-hole courses](/algarve-9-hole-courses), which also covers Penina Resort.

excerpt: Vale do Lobo's two courses share a resort and a hotel, but one is a clifftop showpiece and the other is classic coastal parkland. Here's how the Royal and the Ocean actually compare.

content.text: Vale do Lobo has two 18-hole courses sharing one resort and one hotel, and golfers booking a trip often assume they're roughly the same round with a different name. They're not. The Royal is a dramatic clifftop course built around one of the most photographed holes in golf; the Ocean is an older, gentler parkland test that runs quietly toward the same coastline. Here's how they actually compare.
One resort, two very different rounds

Both courses sit on the same Vale do Lobo estate on the central Algarve coast, a short drive from Quinta do Lago, and both carry a maximum handicap of 28 for men and 36 for ladies. Beyond that, they don't have much in common. The **Ocean Course** is the original: two nine-hole layouts by Sir Henry Cotton, opened in 1968 and 1972, later combined into today's 18-hole par-73 course. The **Royal Course** came later, designed by American architect Rocky Roquemore from Cotton's original drawings and inaugurated in 1997 as a more sculpted, clifftop par 72.
The Royal: the clifftop showpiece

At 6,005 metres from the white tees, the Royal Course is the shorter of the two, but what it lacks in length it makes up for in drama. Pine-lined fairways and coastal lakes build toward the legendary **16th hole**, a 235-yard par 3 played from a tee perched atop three crumbling sandstone cliffs above the Atlantic — regularly ranked among the most photographed golf holes in Europe, and the closest thing the Algarve has to a signature image. It's a genuinely spectacular round, but the cliffside stretch demands respect from anyone who isn't comfortable under a bit of pressure.
The Ocean: classic coastal parkland

The Ocean Course plays to a par of 73 over 6,122 metres from the white tees, and its character comes from its age rather than its scenery. Gently undulating fairways move through mature woodland before opening up toward the coast, with classic links-style bunkering and exposed greens that pick up the sea breeze on the closing holes. The Golf Club has a netted practice area, a short-game area with bunkers and a putting green to warm up before you start, and the round overall asks for patience and course management more than it asks for a head for heights.
Which one should you play?

If you're playing Vale do Lobo for the photo as much as the golf, or you want the hole people will ask you about when you get home, play the Royal — just be ready for a course that plays as dramatically as it looks. If you'd rather a calmer, more traditional coastal round with fewer heart-in-mouth tee shots, the Ocean is the better match, and its longer par 73 gives a slightly different test of patience. Both courses share the same green fees (from €116 for 18 holes on the club's own online booking for the 2026/27 season), so most golfers visiting for more than a couple of days simply play both — they're different enough to justify it.
Where to stay

The [Dona Filipa Hotel](/hotels/dona-filipa-hotel) sits inside the Vale do Lobo estate itself, a five-star beachfront property within walking distance of both the Royal and the Ocean. It has long offered golfers privileged access to the neighbouring **San Lorenzo** course and to **Pinheiros Altos**, although San Lorenzo is closed for renovation until mid-2028. You can [book the Dona Filipa Hotel directly on Booking.com](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/dona-filipa.html).

Want the numbers side by side instead? [Open the course comparator](/?compare=vale-do-lobo-royal,vale-do-lobo-ocean) to see the Royal and the Ocean's price, par, handicap limits and facilities pulled straight from our live course data.

excerpt: Same designer, same estate, same hotel — but South carries the Portuguese Open history and North got a €9 million modern rebuild. Here's how Quinta do Lago's two original courses actually compare.

content.text: Quinta do Lago's South and North courses were both laid out by William Mitchell in 1974, share the same estate and the same five-star hotel — but forty years of separate history have made them very different rounds. South is the one with the tournament pedigree; North is the one that got a complete modern rebuild. Here's how they actually compare.
One designer, one very different story since

Both courses opened in 1974 as part of William Mitchell's original design for the estate, and both wind through umbrella pines with views over the Ria Formosa Natural Park. But where South has stayed close to its championship roots, North was rebuilt from the ground up in 2014 — a **€9 million redesign** led by Beau Welling working with former European Ryder Cup captain **Paul McGinley**, which went on to be named Europe's Best New Golf Course that year. Every green, tee, bunker and drainage system was rebuilt to modern specification.
South: the championship test

At 6,500 metres par 72, South has hosted the **Portuguese Open eight times** since 1976, most recently in 2001, and it's still regarded as one of the toughest rounds in the Algarve. The front nine favours a draw through tight umbrella-pine corridors; the back nine loops the resort lake and asks for a fade instead. It carries the highest green fee of the two — but our own visitors rate it **4.9 out of 5 across 538 reviews**, the highest-rated course on the whole map.
North: the modern rebuild

North plays a shorter 6,140 metres par 72, and the 2014 redesign added four tee options on every hole, so the same course can play as a gentle introduction or a genuine test depending on which tees you choose. Both courses share the same maximum handicap (28 for men, 36 for ladies), but North is the more forgiving layout, while strategic bunkering and water hazards mean low-handicap players still find plenty to think about.
Which one should you play?

If you want the course with the Portuguese Open history and don't mind paying for it, play South — it's the one people mean when they talk about Quinta do Lago's reputation. If you'd rather a course that adapts to your level, with modern conditioning and a shorter card, North is the better choice, especially for higher handicappers or a first visit to the estate. Green fees run from **€188** on South and **€170** on North, and both share the same practice facilities, so playing both across a trip is easy to justify.
Where to stay

Both courses share the same on-site hotel, [Hotel Quinta do Lago](/hotels/hotel-quinta-do-lago) — a member of Leading Hotels of the World since 1988, with 141 rooms and suites and direct pedestrian access to all three Quinta do Lago courses. You can [book it directly on Expedia](https://www.expedia.com/Algarve-Hotels-Hotel-Quinta-Do-Lago.h17019.Hotel-Information).

Want the numbers side by side instead? [Open the course comparator](/?compare=quinta-do-lago-south,quinta-do-lago-north) to see South and North's price, handicap limits and facilities pulled straight from our live course data.

excerpt: Alamos and Morgado share a designer, a resort and a hotel near Portimão, but the two courses play nothing alike. Here's what actually separates them, and which one suits your handicap.

content.text: Alamos Golf and Morgado Golf sit less than a kilometre apart in the hills north of Portimão, share the same designer and the same on-site hotel, and are often booked together as a two-course package. But mix them up and you could book the wrong round: one is a shorter, tighter and hillier course that rewards accuracy, the other is a wide, open championship layout that has hosted the **Portuguese Open**. Here's what actually separates Alamos from Morgado, and which one suits your game.
One resort, one designer, two very different courses

Both courses belong to the Morgado do Reguengo resort above Portimão, and both were laid out by **Russell Talley of European Golf Design** — Morgado first, in 2003, followed by Alamos in 2006. They share a driving range and practice academy at the clubhouse, and the same on-site hotel, so choosing one course doesn't mean losing access to the other's facilities. What differs is the golf itself: Morgado was built as the resort's championship test, while Alamos was designed deliberately narrower and quieter as its counterpart.
Alamos: shorter, tighter and hillier

Alamos plays to a par of 71 over 5,710 metres, shorter and noticeably tighter than its sister course. Fairways run narrower between mature trees, the course is hilly with some long walks between holes, and the fast, heavily contoured greens are what golfers mention most. The challenge here is accuracy and course management rather than raw length, which suits straight hitters more than wayward ones. The back nine runs alongside two lakes with the Serra de Monchique hills as a backdrop. Both courses share the same maximum handicap of **28 for men and 36 for ladies**.
Morgado: the championship layout that hosted the Portuguese Open

Morgado is the longer round: par 73 over 6,581 metres, but its fairways are some of the widest in the Algarve and there is little rough, so the main hazards are Scottish-inspired pot bunkers and large, undulating greens that punish a poor approach. It's the more decorated course of the two — Morgado hosted the **Open de Portugal** on the European Tour and Challenge Tour in 2017, 2018 and 2019. If you want to play the same layout the professionals competed on, this is it.
Which one should you play?

If you're a higher handicapper, travelling with mixed-ability golfers, or just want a relaxed round where a wayward drive rarely costs a ball, play Morgado, from the forward tees. If you're a straight hitter who enjoys a tighter, more strategic course and tricky greens, and you don't mind a hilly walk (take a buggy), play Alamos. Green fees start from a similar €82 at both, so price isn't the deciding factor, and because the two courses share a hotel and a practice academy, there's nothing stopping you from playing both on the same trip.
Where to stay: one hotel for both courses

Both courses share the same on-site hotel, [NAU Morgado Golf & Country Club](/hotels/nau-morgado-golf-country-club), a 4-star, 98-room property with balconies overlooking the fairways, four outdoor pools and the Club House restaurant serving breakfast, lunch and dinner. Staying here puts you a short walk from both first tees, which makes comparing the two courses across consecutive days genuinely easy. You can [book the hotel directly on Booking.com](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/morgado-golf-and-country-club.html).

Still not sure just from the numbers? [Open the course comparator](/?compare=alamos,morgado) to see Alamos and Morgado's price, slope, handicaps and facilities side by side, pulled straight from our live course data.

excerpt: Six Algarve courses where the Atlantic isn't just scenery — it's part of the round. From cliff-top par 3s to fairways that run along the sand, here's where to find real ocean views.

content.text: Most golf courses in the Algarve promise sea views somewhere on the scorecard, but not all of them put the Atlantic in play. These six are tagged **ocean view** on our map for a reason — real coastal or clifftop holes, not just a glimpse from the clubhouse terrace. They aren't necessarily the only ones with great sea views, so it's worth asking about any other course you're considering. Here's what makes each one worth the detour, and where to stay if you want to wake up to the same view.
Vale do Lobo Royal — the Algarve's most photographed hole

The Royal Course's par-3 16th is played from a tee perched atop three crumbling sandstone cliffs, 235 yards out over the Atlantic — regularly ranked among the most photographed golf holes in Europe. Rocky Roquemore reshaped Sir Henry Cotton's original layout in 1997, and the clifftop finishing stretch is what most people actually picture when they think of Algarve golf. The on-site [Dona Filipa Hotel](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/dona-filipa.html) puts you a short walk from the first tee.
Palmares — 27 holes above Meia Praia beach

Robert Trent Jones Jr.'s redesign spread Palmares across three nines — Alvor, Lagos and Praia — and it's the Praia nine that delivers the goods: genuine links golf above Meia Praia beach, with sweeping Atlantic and estuary views from an elevated driving range. Stay at the on-site [Palmares Beach House Hotel](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/onyria-palmares-beach-house-hostel.html).
Boavista — sea views from the hills above Lagos

Howard Swan's design climbs through cork-oak woodland above Lagos, and the higher the course goes, the more of the Atlantic you see — several holes on the back nine look straight down to the coastline. It's also one of the better-value ocean-view rounds in the western Algarve. On-site: [Boavista Golf & Spa Resort](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/boavista-golf-resort-spa.html).
Pine Cliffs — nine holes, one legendary ravine

Every hole on this nine-hole course sits atop sandstone cliffs above Olhos de Água, and the holes are short par 4s and par 3s. Players without a handicap can play from the red tees, which makes it a good choice even if you're a beginner. The sixth, known as the Devil's Parlour, sends you across a ravine to a green above the ocean — the standout short hole on this coast. It's part of the Pine Cliffs Resort, with the [Pine Cliffs Residence](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/pine-cliffs-residence.html) on site.
Vale de Milho — a sea-view course for every handicap

This nine-hole, all-par-3 course above Carvoeiro is the easiest way to get an Algarve sea view into your golf without needing a low handicap — the longest hole is only 145 metres. It's a genuinely useful short-game course too, not just a novelty stop.
San Lorenzo — closed until 2028

San Lorenzo borders the Ria Formosa lagoon rather than the open sea, but its coastal holes and long-standing reputation as one of continental Europe's best-rated courses earn it a place on this list. But you can't play it for now: San Lorenzo closed for renovation on 19 October 2026 and is not due to reopen until mid-2028. [Quinta do Lago South](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south), five minutes away, also borders the Ria Formosa. See [where to play while San Lorenzo is closed](/guide/san-lorenzo-golf-course-closed-until-2028-where-to-play-instead).
Want to see these six together? [Open the Ocean view filter on the map](/?filters=ocean_view) — it's the same tag that built this list, pulled straight from our live course data.

excerpt: They're not sibling courses, so this isn't a head-to-head — it's a guide to which quick nine-hole round near Albufeira actually fits you: the budget no-pressure par-3, or the bucket-list clifftop hole.

content.text: Balaia and Pine Cliffs aren't sibling courses at the same resort — they're two completely separate clubs that happen to sit a few minutes apart near Albufeira, and both get recommended for the same reason: a proper round in under two hours. Beyond that, they're not really alternatives to each other. Here's who each one actually suits.
Two different resorts, two different kinds of short round

Balaia is a budget, no-frills par-3 course attached to a 4-star holiday village. Pine Cliffs is a nine-hole course built into the grounds of a 5-star Marriott Luxury Collection resort, with one of the most photographed golf holes in Portugal. Both take roughly the same time to play — but one is designed to remove pressure, and the other is designed to give you a story to tell.
Balaia: the no-pressure par-3

Every one of Balaia's nine holes is a par 3, running from 67 to 160 metres from the yellow tees, which makes it one of the genuinely easiest ways to get a beginner or a junior onto a real golf course. It opened in 2001 and sits inside the Balaia Golf Village estate, with a 40-bay driving range and golf academy on site if you want to work on your swing first. A day's golf costs visitors **€50** on the club's 2025-26 price list, among the cheapest rounds in the Algarve.
Stay right on the course at the [Balaia Golf Village Resort](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/balaia-golf-village.html).
Pine Cliffs: the bucket-list clifftop hole

Pine Cliffs plays nine holes to a par of 33, perched on sandstone cliffs above Olhos de Água. Martin Hawtree designed it, and it's built around the sixth, the **Devil's Parlour**: a 197-metre par 3 played from 60 metres above the Atlantic, over a ravine, to a green on the cliff edge. It's genuinely playable for beginners thanks to the short holes, but that one tee shot is not for the faint-hearted. Nine holes cost visitors from **€57** on the club's 2025/26 price list.
The course sits inside the resort, with the [Pine Cliffs Residence](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/pine-cliffs-residence.html) right on site.
Which one should you play?

If you're introducing a beginner to golf, playing with juniors, or just want a relaxed, cheap round with zero pressure, play Balaia. If you want the photo, the resort experience, and one genuinely thrilling tee shot over the ocean — even if the rest of the round is gentler than it looks — play Pine Cliffs. Neither replaces a full 18-hole day out; both are exactly what they're built to be: a good two hours of golf that doesn't ask much of your schedule.

excerpt: Refunds, rain vouchers and cancellation deadlines at Algarve golf clubs, how often it actually rains each month, and what to do if the weather turns on your tee time.

content.text: Rain rarely stops play in the Algarve, and when it does, don't expect your money back. At the clubs we checked, a green fee isn't refunded just because it rains: if the course stays open, your booking stands. If the club **closes the course** because of the weather, you usually get a **rain voucher** to play the holes you missed on another day, typically within 12 months, rather than a refund. And free cancellation normally ends **days or weeks before** your tee time, so by the time a bad forecast appears it's usually too late to cancel for free.
How often does it rain in the Algarve?

Not often. Even in the wettest months, it rains on about one day in four, and from June to August it hardly rains at all. These are the official long-term averages from IPMA, Portugal's weather service:

content.note: Source: IPMA climate normals 1991–2020 for Faro (centre and east) and Sagres (west). A rainy day is one with at least 1 mm of rain. Each month links to our guide to Algarve golf in that month.
content.caption: Average rainy days and rainfall by month

content.text: November and December are the wettest months, with about seven or eight rainy days. A rainy day here means one with at least 1 mm of rain, not necessarily a whole day of it. If you can choose your dates, see [the best time to play golf in the Algarve](/guide/algarve-golf-season-best-time-to-play-golf).
What the clubs' booking terms say
Every club sets its own rules, so these are examples from clubs that publish their booking conditions, not a rule for every course:

headers: If the weather closes the course

content.text: **Your course isn't in the table?** For the other Algarve courses, we couldn't find enough published information about what happens if it rains or when you can cancel for free, so we've left them out rather than guess. That includes Pestana's courses (Gramacho, Vale da Pinta, Silves, Alto Golf, Vila Sol and Pestana Ferragudo), Salgados, Penina, Amendoeira, Morgado and Alamos, Castro Marim and Pine Cliffs. If you're booking one of them, ask the club about its cancellation and rain policy before you pay.

Vilamoura Golf spells out how its rain vouchers work. If play is stopped and you've played **fewer than 9 holes** of an 18-hole round, you get an 18-hole voucher; if you've played **9 or more**, a 9-hole voucher. Twilight and 9-hole rounds get a 9-hole voucher. The vouchers are personal, can't be transferred, and those issued in the low or mid season can't be used in high season. You have to ask for one at reception straight after play is stopped.

[Boavista](/courses/boavista) is the most generous on paper. If the course is closed on the day you're due to play, you're first offered another day, or a rain check voucher if you can't make it. If it closes after you've started, you get an 18-hole voucher if you've played fewer than 5 holes and a 9-hole voucher after that. [Monte Rei](/courses/monte-rei) gives a rain check voucher only if you've completed no more than 9 holes, and says plainly that rain and strong winds are not reasons to close the course.

Vale do Lobo, Quinta do Lago, Quinta da Ria and Quinta do Vale use almost the same wording: the club decides when to close the course and when it's safe to reopen, it pays no compensation for the closure, and a voucher is only issued in what they call extreme situations, when the course doesn't reopen that day. At [Ombria](/courses/ombria), play is suspended with a buzzer during thunderstorms and the situation is checked every 15 minutes; if there's still time to finish your round that day, there's no refund. Ombria also suspends play for heavy rain when at least four greens are flooded.
If it's raining but the course is open

This is the case that catches most golfers out. None of the booking conditions we read gives you a refund because it's raining while the course is open. Once the free cancellation deadline has passed, Vale do Lobo says the booking "cannot be cancelled, altered or refunded", and Vilamoura Golf, Monte Rei and Palmares charge late cancellations and no-shows in full. Monte Rei says it gives no refunds "in the event of inclement weather", and Vilamoura Golf, Monte Rei and Palmares all say they don't refund for delayed or cancelled flights or injuries, and recommend travel insurance.

So if the forecast is wet, your choice is usually to play in waterproofs, or to talk to the club before your tee time and ask whether it will move your booking. Some clubs may help, but it's their decision.
Buggies after heavy rain

To protect the course, clubs can restrict buggies when it's wet. Vale do Lobo and Vilamoura Golf both say they can restrict or ban buggies because of the weather, Ombria can limit buggies at any time, and Penina's price list warns that golf carts can be restricted due to weather conditions. That can mean keeping to the paths or no buggies at all, which matters if you rely on one. Ask the club when you check in, or call ahead if you can't walk the course. Our [golf buggy hire guide](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve) has more.
If you booked through an agency or website

Booking through a tee-time website usually doesn't change the rules: the course's own policy applies. Golfscape, for example, says each course defines its cancellation policy, which is shown when you book and in your confirmation email. AlgarveGolf.net says that if a course is unplayable, you must go to the course before your tee time to ask for a rain check or a free cancellation, and that refunds and rain checks depend on each course's policy. See our guide to [booking tee times in the Algarve](/guide/how-to-book-tee-times-in-the-algarve).
What to do on a rainy golf day

**Before you book:** read the cancellation deadline. If your dates might change, a club with a short deadline, such as 48 hours at Vale do Lobo, Boavista or Benamor, is more flexible than one that asks for 15 or 45 days.
**On the day:** don't just stay away. Call the club or go to reception before your tee time and ask whether the course is open and whether buggies are allowed. A no-show is normally charged in full.
**If play is stopped:** go to reception straight away and ask for a rain voucher. Check how many holes it covers, how long it's valid and whether you can use it in a different season.
**Pack for it:** waterproofs, a spare glove, an umbrella and a towel. Most of the Algarve's rain falls between October and April.
Rainy day plan B

If you'd rather not play in the rain, some clubs have places to keep practising under cover. [Salgados](/courses/salgados) has two Foresight Sports golf simulators in its clubhouse. [Quinta da Ria](/courses/quinta-da-ria/practice-facilities) has a Foresight simulator and five covered bays at its driving range, and [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio/practice-facilities) has four covered practice tees. The Pestana Golf Academy has covered hitting bays too. See our list of [Algarve driving ranges](/driving-ranges) for more.
Frequently asked questions
Can you play golf in the rain in the Algarve?
Yes. A course stays open in the rain unless the club decides to close it because of the weather, and the club also decides when to reopen.
Do you get a refund if it rains?
Not usually. At the clubs we checked, you don't get a refund because of rain. If the club closes the course, you may get a rain voucher to play the missed holes another day, normally within a year.
What is the rainiest month in the Algarve?
November and December, with about seven rainy days in Faro and eight in Sagres. December has the most rain in Faro, about 90 mm on average. July and August have almost none.

excerpt: One designer touched both, thirty years apart, but the Old Course and the Millennium play nothing alike. Here's how Vilamoura's most-compared pair actually differ, and which one suits your game.

content.text: Vilamoura has five golf courses, but the Old Course and the Millennium are the two that get compared most, mostly because they sit at opposite ends of the resort's history: one is a 1969 classic that's just been named Portugal's best, the other is a Y2K-era course built from recycled holes of an older layout. Here's how they actually differ.
One architect, thirty years apart

Frank Pennink laid out the Old Course in 1969, and it's stayed the benchmark for Vilamoura golf ever since, remodelled by **Martin Hawtree** and reopened in 1997. Hawtree's fingerprints are on the Millennium too — he designed it from scratch in 2000, reusing nine holes that had originally belonged to the old 27-hole Laguna course and building an entirely new back nine around them. So in a sense, the same designer shaped both, just at very different points in his career and with very different briefs.
Old Course: recently crowned the best in Portugal

At 6,254 metres par 73, the Old Course plays through mature umbrella pines with five par-5s that reward strategic play over raw power, and it hosted the Portuguese Open in its early years. In 2025 it was named **Portugal's Best Golf Course at the World Golf Awards**, and it's currently under fresh investment from new management, with bunker, tee and green renovations completed in 2024. It's also the highest-rated course in our own data for the area, at **4.6 out of 5 across 489 reviews**.
Millennium: newer, wider, more forgiving

The Millennium plays a shorter 6,176 metres par 72, with wide fairways and gentle undulations that suit mid-to-high handicappers without feeling dumbed down for better players. It shares a relaxed clubhouse terrace with the neighbouring Laguna course, overlooking the closing holes — a nice spot to watch the sunset if you're playing late in the day.
Which one should you play?

If you want the course with the pedigree, the recent award and a proper test through mature pines, play the Old Course — it's priced accordingly, from **€215**. If you'd rather a friendlier, wide-open round that won't punish a stray drive as hard, the Millennium is the better fit, and considerably cheaper, from **€88**. Neither has an on-site hotel, but both sit within easy reach of Vilamoura's marina hotels, so accommodation isn't the deciding factor here — the golf is.

Want the numbers side by side instead? [Open the course comparator](/?compare=vilamoura-old-course,vilamoura-millennium) to see the Old Course and Millennium's price, par, handicap limits and facilities pulled straight from our live course data.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Vilamoura costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-vilamoura-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: Same operator, very different ages — Silves has been open since 2006 with a reputation for excellent conditioning, while Pestana Ferragudo only opened its doors this month. Here's what we know about both.

content.text: Both courses belong to the Pestana group and sit inland from the coast, but that's about where the similarity ends. Silves has been open since 2006 and has a settled reputation for excellent conditioning. Pestana Ferragudo, on the other hand, only opened its doors on **1 September 2026** — so this comparison is really the old guard against the newest course in the Algarve.
Eighteen years apart

Silves was designed by **Fausto Nascimento and Peter Booth** and opened in 2006 near the ancient Moorish town it's named after. Pestana Ferragudo, designed in-house by Pestana, is only a few weeks old at the time of writing — a genuinely new addition to the region's golf map, part of a wider residential development in Ferragudo village across the river from Portimão.
Silves: a known quantity, praised for its conditioning

Silves plays 5,615 metres par 70 over gently hilly terrain, with panoramic views over orange and olive groves and a layout that rewards accuracy more than power — a standout run of par-3s and four memorable par-5s. It's consistently well-regarded for how well it's maintained, which matters when so many Algarve courses struggle with conditioning in the peak summer months.
Pestana Ferragudo: too new to have a track record

Ferragudo plays 5,841 metres par 72 — longer than Silves — through parkland terrain that makes full use of the natural landscape. Having only opened this month, there's no track record yet on conditioning, pace of play or how it holds up once summer traffic properly arrives. If you're an early adopter who likes trying a course before the reviews pile up, this is your chance; if you'd rather wait for it to bed in, that's a reasonable call too.
Which one should you play?

If you want a reliable, well-conditioned round with an established reputation, play Silves — green fees start from **€95**. If you're curious about the newest course in the Algarve and don't mind being one of its first few thousand rounds, Ferragudo is worth the detour, with green fees from **€130** on Pestana's price list.

Want the numbers side by side instead? [Open the course comparator](/?compare=silves,pestana-ferragudo) to see Silves and Pestana Ferragudo's par, length and facilities pulled straight from our live course data.

excerpt: Same price, minutes apart, but Laguna and Pinhal couldn't be more different once you're on them — one is open and water-laced, the other classic pine-lined parkland. Here's how Vilamoura's other pair compares.

content.text: Vilamoura has five golf courses, and after the Old Course and the Millennium, Laguna and Pinhal are the pair most golfers end up choosing between. They sit minutes apart, cost the same to play, and couldn't look more different once you're actually on them.
The exception and the pedigree

Pinhal has the longer history: **Frank Pennink** laid it out in 1976 as the second course ever built in Vilamoura, after the Old Course, and **Robert Trent Jones Sr.** partly redesigned it in 1985. Laguna came later, in 1990, designed by **Joseph Lee** as a deliberate change of pace from Vilamoura's tree-lined norm — open, exposed, and built around water rather than pines.
Laguna: open, exposed, water everywhere

At 6,121 metres par 72, Laguna breaks the Vilamoura mould with few trees and a links-like feel — the wind is a constant factor here in a way it isn't on the pine-sheltered courses nearby. Eleven of the eighteen holes border its numerous lakes, and 79 bunkers demand precision rather than raw distance. It's a genuinely different test if you've already played the more classic Algarve parkland layouts.
Pinhal: classic pine-lined parkland

Pinhal plays 6,353 metres par 72 through the umbrella pines that define most of Vilamoura, with elevation changes keeping the round interesting from hole to hole. It's the quieter, more traditional option of the resort's five courses, and popular with golfers who return to Vilamoura year after year and know the course well enough to use the local knowledge it rewards.
Which one should you play?

If you want a proper change of scenery from tree-lined Algarve golf — more wind, more water, a links-adjacent feel — play Laguna. If you'd rather the classic pine-framed round with genuine Vilamoura pedigree, play Pinhal. Prices are close, from **€88** at Laguna and **€101** at Pinhal on the club's online booking, so it really comes down to which kind of test you're after. Since they're a short drive apart, most golfers staying in Vilamoura for more than a few days play both.

Want the numbers side by side instead? [Open the course comparator](/?compare=vilamoura-laguna,vilamoura-pinhal) to see Laguna and Pinhal's price, par, handicap limits and facilities pulled straight from our live course data.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Vilamoura costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-vilamoura-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: Where to stay to play Pine Cliffs: the three Luxury Collection hotels on the resort plus seven well-rated alternatives nearby, from about €50 a night, with drive times, breakfast hours and golf perks.

content.text: [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs) is one of the most scenic short courses in Europe: a 9-hole Martin Hawtree layout on the ochre clifftops of Olhos de Água, just east of Albufeira. Its most famous hole is the sixth, the **Devil's Parlour**, a par 3 that asks for a 197-metre carry over the edge of the cliffs.

So where should you stay to play it? This guide covers 10 of the best hotels near Pine Cliffs Golf Course: three inside Pine Cliffs Resort itself, a few minutes' walk or a short shuttle ride from the first tee, and seven well-rated alternatives nearby, from apartments at around €50 a night to five-star spa resorts.
Map of hotels near Pine Cliffs Golf Course
The black pin is the golf clubhouse (tap it to see course details). The blue pins are the hotels in this guide; tap one to check prices and availability.
How we chose these hotels

Every hotel on this list is rated at least 8 out of 10 by guests on Booking.com and is within about 25 minutes of the course by car. Drive times are calculated by road to the golf clubhouse. Breakfast hours and golf services come from each hotel's own website wherever possible, and we only mention a golf perk if the hotel actually states it.

Prices are the lowest average nightly rates we found in October 2026, usually for the quietest month of the year (November to February). Spring, autumn and especially summer cost considerably more, so use them as a guide rather than a quote.
Hotels inside Pine Cliffs Resort

Staying on the resort puts the course on your doorstep and gets you **lower green fees than visitors pay** (see the price table further down). The resort has 12 restaurants, the Serenity Spa and the Porto Pirata kids' club for children aged 1 to 8. Two things to know: Pine Cliffs charges a facility fee on all bookings, which covers resort parking and the internal shuttle, and breakfast is a supplement of €36 per adult unless it is included in your rate.

Besides the three Luxury Collection properties below, the resort also rents Pine Cliffs Gardens, Pine Cliffs Suites and Pine Cliffs Village apartments and townhouses through its own website. Pine Cliffs Suites overlooks the golf course.

content.name: Pine Cliffs Residence, a Luxury Collection Resort
content.text: The resort itself calls this **"the best option for golfers and their families"**: spacious apartments close to the Clubhouse and overlooking the course, so you can walk to your tee time. With two- and three-bedroom apartments, it works especially well for a family or a small group of golfers sharing.
perks: Lower green fees for resort guests
content.distanceLabel: Inside the resort, overlooking the course

content.name: Pine Cliffs Hotel, a Luxury Collection Resort
content.text: The resort's original five-star hotel, with rooms a five-minute stroll from Praia da Falésia. The concierge can arrange tee times and transfers, and in our research it was the cheapest of the three Luxury Collection properties, a good fit if you only need a room rather than an apartment.
perks: Lower green fees for resort guests
content.distanceLabel: Inside the resort, about 3 min by car

content.name: Pine Cliffs Ocean Suites, a Luxury Collection Resort & Spa
content.text: Suites and apartments in the same building as the award-winning Serenity Spa, with free access to its Oasis Thermal area. All rooms interconnect, which makes it popular with families. A good choice if a round on Pine Cliffs is one part of a holiday where the spa matters as much as the golf.
perks: Lower green fees for resort guests
content.distanceLabel: Inside the resort

content.text: Best value hotels near Pine Cliffs (under €100 a night)

content.name: The Pátio Suite Hotel
content.text: The closest good-value option to Pine Cliffs: the hotel says it is **just 200 metres from the golf course**, and by road it is a 7-minute drive to the clubhouse. One- and two-bedroom apartments, several pools, a kids' club and a free transfer to the beach make it a smart base for families or golfers on a budget.
perks: 200 m from the course (per the hotel)

content.name: Balaia Golf Village Resort
content.text: A self-catering resort with **its own 9-hole executive course** ([Balaia](/courses/balaia)), plus a practice range and golf academy, 10 minutes from Pine Cliffs. Its "Algarve Golf Break" package includes two rounds at Balaia. Ideal for a short-game holiday: play Balaia in the morning, and the Devil's Parlour in the afternoon.
perks: Club hire when booking a tee time

content.name: Grande Real Santa Eulália Resort & Hotel Spa
content.text: A large five-star resort on Santa Eulália beach that can be surprisingly affordable out of season. The concierge sells green fees for local courses, breakfast starts at 7.30am and the 1,000 m² thalassotherapy spa is ideal for tired legs after a round.
perks: Green fees sold at the concierge

content.text: Mid-range hotels near Pine Cliffs (€100 to €150 a night)

content.name: PortoBay Blue Ocean
content.text: The **highest-rated hotel on this list (9.2 on Booking.com)** sits on the clifftop just west of the resort, a 7-minute drive from the clubhouse. Formerly TUI Blue Falésia, it is not adults-only, but it has a lounge area reserved for adults and a calm, couple-friendly feel. Note that its sister hotel next door, PortoBay Falésia, is closed for refurbishment until May 2027.

content.name: Hotel Vila Galé Cerro Alagoa
content.text: A practical four-star in Albufeira itself, for golfers who want restaurants and nightlife on the doorstep in the evening. Breakfast is served **from 7am**, so an early tee time at Pine Cliffs, 17 minutes away, is easy. There is a spa with a heated indoor pool for the cooler months.
Luxury hotels with golf services near Pine Cliffs

content.name: EPIC SANA Algarve Hotel
content.text: A five-star resort above Falésia beach, just east of Pine Cliffs and 9 minutes from the clubhouse by car. The hotel offers **special green fees at various Algarve golf courses**, breakfast runs from 7am to 11am, and there is a large 1,500 m² spa. Rated 9.0 by Booking.com guests.
perks: Special green fees at Algarve courses

content.name: Domes Lake Algarve, Autograph Collection
content.text: The best pick for golfers who want to play more than Pine Cliffs. This lakeside resort in Vilamoura has a **dedicated golf concierge** that arranges tee times, transfers and instructors, offers free shuttles to nearby golf courses and runs lessons with the Vilamoura Golf Academy. Pine Cliffs is around 26 minutes away by car.
Pine Cliffs green fees and opening hours

Pine Cliffs is **open to visitors as well as resort guests**, and guests pay less. On the resort's 2025/26 price list, 9 holes cost visitors **€57 in low season and €76 in high season**, and 18 holes (the loop played twice) cost €80 and €99. Resort guests pay €53 and €64 for 9 holes, and €74 and €88 for 18. Low season runs from late November to January and from June to mid-September; the rest of the year is high season.

This price list runs until 31 October 2026, so check the resort's website for the new season's prices. The first tee time is 8am and the last is 5.20pm, and you can book online through the resort's website. Club sets can be hired from €30 for 9 holes, and players without a handicap must play from the red tees.
Tips for golfers staying near Pine Cliffs
**Book your tee time in advance.** With only nine holes and plenty of resort guests, Pine Cliffs can fill up, especially in spring and autumn. If you are staying on the resort, ask the concierge.

**Combine it with other courses.** The resort allows two hours for a nine-hole round, so it pairs well with a second course on the same trip. [Balaia](/courses/balaia) is 10 minutes away, and the Vilamoura courses such as the [Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course) are around 20 minutes east. Not sure which short course suits you? Read our comparison [Balaia vs Pine Cliffs](/guide/balaia-vs-pine-cliffs-which-quick-round-near-albufeira-should-you-play).
**Getting there.** Faro Airport is about 40 km away, roughly 45 minutes to an hour by car. If you stay outside the resort, a hire car makes it easy to reach the course and the rest of the Algarve.
Frequently asked questions
Which hotel is closest to Pine Cliffs Golf Course?

Pine Cliffs Residence, inside the resort, overlooks the course and is close to the Clubhouse. Outside the resort, The Pátio Suite Hotel says it is about 200 metres from the course, a 7-minute drive to the clubhouse by road.
Can you play Pine Cliffs if you are not staying at the resort?
Yes. Pine Cliffs is open to visitors, who pay slightly higher green fees than resort guests. Tee times can be booked online through the resort's website.
Is there a cheap hotel near Pine Cliffs?
Yes. Balaia Golf Village Resort has apartments from about €50 a night in the quieter months, and The Pátio Suite Hotel from about €60. Both are within 10 minutes of the course.
Playing several courses? Find the best base for your trip

If Pine Cliffs is just one stop on your golf trip, try **Find Your Base** on the [Algarve Golf Map](/). Pick the courses you want to play and it shows you the area that sits closest to all of them, along with well-rated hotels nearby, so you spend less time driving and more time on the course.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Albufeira costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-albufeira-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: There is no hotel at Ferragudo Golf Course yet. Here are 11 of the best places to stay nearby, from Pestana's own golf apartments to luxury resorts, with drive times, breakfast hours and golf perks.

content.text: [Pestana Ferragudo](/courses/pestana-ferragudo) is the newest course in the Algarve and the new flagship of the Pestana group: an 18-hole, par-73 parkland layout that opened in 2026 between the fishing village of Ferragudo and Carvoeiro. It sits right next to Pestana's two older courses, [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho) and [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta), which makes this corner of the western Algarve a very good base for a golf trip.

This guide answers one question: **where should you stay to play Ferragudo Golf Course?** Below are 11 hotels, resorts and villas within roughly 25 minutes of the first tee, starting with Pestana's own golf apartments next door, followed by places rated above 8 out of 10 by guests, from good-value rooms at around €50 a night to some of the best resorts in Portugal.
Is there a hotel at Ferragudo Golf Course?

Not yet. The course is part of Pestana Ferragudo Village, a new golf and residential development, and Pestana lists a boutique hotel among its planned facilities, but there is no opening date or booking page for it so far. For now, every golfer playing Ferragudo stays somewhere nearby and drives to the course.

The closest thing to an on-site hotel is Pestana Gramacho Residences, Pestana's own golf apartments on the neighbouring Gramacho course, about 12 minutes from Ferragudo by road. It is first on our list below. The closest well-rated hotel is actually Água Hotels Riverside, about 6 minutes away on the Ferragudo side of the Arade river.
Map of hotels near Ferragudo Golf Course
The black pin is the course (tap it to see course details). The blue pins are the hotels in this guide; tap one to check prices and availability.
How we chose these hotels

Apart from Pestana Gramacho Residences, which we include because it is part of the same golf resort, every hotel on this list has a guest rating of at least 8 out of 10 on Booking.com and is no more than about 25 minutes from the course by car. Drive times are calculated by road, not in a straight line. We checked breakfast hours and golf services on each hotel's own website wherever possible, and we only mention a golf perk if the hotel or its operator actually states it.

Prices are the lowest nightly rates we found in October 2026 for the cheapest room or apartment, usually in the quieter months of November to February. Spring and autumn, which are peak golf season, cost more, so treat them as a guide rather than a quote.
Pestana's own golf apartments

content.name: Pestana Gramacho Residences
content.text: Pestana's golf apartments sit right on the [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho) course, part of the same Pestana golf resort as Ferragudo, and Pestana describes the property as "the perfect place for golf lovers". You get a golf academy on the doorstep, breakfast from 7am, a free internal shuttle and apartments with kitchens, about 12 minutes from Ferragudo and 6 minutes from Vale da Pinta. Its guest score of **7.8 on Booking.com** is a little lower than the rest of this list, but no other option puts you on a Pestana course with a golf academy on the doorstep.
Best value hotels near Ferragudo Golf Course (under €70 a night)

content.name: Água Hotels Riverside
content.text: On the Ferragudo side of the Arade river, this is both the **closest well-rated hotel to the course**, about 6 minutes away, and the cheapest. It serves **breakfast from 7am**, which suits early tee times. There is a spa with sauna and jacuzzi, a gym that opens at 6am and free parking. Some guests find the décor a little dated, but for a golf trip on a budget it is hard to beat.

content.name: Pestana Palm Gardens
content.text: Clifftop studios and apartments in Carvoeiro run by Pestana, the same group that owns Ferragudo. Pestana says guests get **exclusive benefits and discounts at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta**, so it is a smart base if you want to play all three Pestana courses. Breakfast starts at 8am and is charged separately, but every unit has a kitchen, so an early bite before your round is easy.
perks: Discounts at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta

content.name: Jupiter Marina Hotel
content.text: A stylish hotel on Portimão marina aimed at couples, with a spa, a rooftop bar and a free shuttle to Praia da Rocha beach. It scores **9.0 on Booking.com**, unusually high for the price, and breakfast starts at 7.30am. A good pick for golfing couples who want restaurants and nightlife within walking distance after the round. Parking is paid.
Mid-range hotels and villas near the course (€70 to €130 a night)

content.name: Vale d'Oliveiras Quinta Resort & Spa
content.text: A five-star spa resort about 11 minutes from Ferragudo and only about 400 metres from Gramacho, according to the resort, with an à la carte restaurant, 24-hour room service and breakfast from 7.30am. It is popular with families, so it also works if you are travelling with non-golfers.

content.name: Vale da Lapa Village Resort
content.text: Five-star villas set in gardens a few minutes from the course, with a spa, indoor pool and restaurant. At **9.3 on Booking.com** it is the best-rated resort this close to Ferragudo. The villas suit a group of friends who want their own space, and some have private pools for the end of the day.

content.name: Quinta do Algarvio Village
content.text: Self-catering apartments with full kitchens and a saltwater pool that is heated in winter, around 12 minutes from the first tee. Guests rate it a remarkable **9.4 on Booking.com**. Members of the operator's Carvoeiro Clube Group club get discounts on golf within the group. There is no breakfast service, so plan to stock the fridge. You will need a car.

content.name: Vale de Milho Village
content.text: Two- and three-bedroom townhouses, **each with its own private pool**, next to the [Vale de Milho](/courses/vale-de-milho) par-3 course, where guests get 20% off green fees. Prices are for the whole townhouse, so split between four golfers it is excellent value. It is a good choice for groups who want a short-game warm-up on the doorstep before heading to Ferragudo.
perks: 20% off green fees at Vale de Milho

content.text: Luxury hotels and golf resorts within 25 minutes

content.name: Penina Hotel & Golf Resort
content.text: The Algarve's original golf resort, with three courses on site including the Sir Henry Cotton-designed [Penina Championship](/courses/penina-championship). Penina's "Best Available Rate for Golfers" includes **a complimentary round every day** on one of its courses (a handicap certificate is needed for the Championship course). Combine a few rounds there with a day at Ferragudo, 15 minutes away. Breakfast starts at 7am.
perks: Free daily round on the golfer rate

content.name: Tivoli Carvoeiro Algarve Resort
content.text: A five-star clifftop resort a short walk from Carvoeiro village, with sea views, a full spa and indoor and outdoor pools. It is one of the most established golf-holiday hotels in this area: UK golf tour operators sell packages here that include rounds at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta, and Ferragudo is about 23 minutes away.

content.name: Vila Vita Parc
content.text: One of the finest resorts in Portugal, on the clifftops at Porches. For golfers it has a driving range, a golf simulator, a 9-hole pitch and putt, an 18-hole putting green and a resident pro, and the resort says it offers **preferential rates and tee times at most Algarve courses**. Ideal if you are travelling with a non-golfing partner who wants a world-class spa and beach.
Ferragudo Golf Course green fees by season

According to Pestana's current price list, a round at Ferragudo costs around **€130 in low season** (December, January and June to August), **€200 in high season** (November, February, May and September) and **€230 in premium season** (March, April and October). Twilight rounds from 13:30 cost €80, which is a great option if your hotel is close by. Prices change, so confirm with the club before you book.
Tips for golfers staying near Ferragudo

**Hire a car.** None of the hotels above confirms a golf shuttle to Ferragudo, and the course is around 50 minutes to an hour from Faro Airport. Having your own car also makes it easy to add nearby courses such as [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho), [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta), [Alto Golf](/courses/alto-golf) and [Morgado Golf](/courses/morgado), all within a short drive.

**Check breakfast times before you book.** If you like an early tee time, Pestana Gramacho Residences, Água Hotels Riverside and Penina all serve breakfast from 7am. Self-catering apartments and villas are the other way to get out early.

**Play all three Pestana courses.** Ferragudo, Gramacho and Vale da Pinta are all within about 12 minutes of each other. Pestana Gramacho Residences puts you right between them, and Pestana Palm Gardens guests get discounts at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta.

Not sure Ferragudo is the right course for you? Read our comparison [Silves vs Pestana Ferragudo](/guide/silves-vs-pestana-ferragudo-the-established-course-and-the-brand-new-one), or browse every course in the area on the [Algarve golf map](/).
Frequently asked questions
Which hotel is closest to Ferragudo Golf Course?

Água Hotels Riverside, on the Ferragudo side of the Arade river, is the closest at around 6 minutes by car. Vale d'Oliveiras Quinta Resort & Spa and Vale da Lapa Village Resort are both about 11 minutes away, and Pestana's own Gramacho Residences and the Jupiter Marina Hotel about 12.
Is there a cheap hotel near Ferragudo Golf Course?
Yes. Água Hotels Riverside, 6 minutes from the course, has rooms from about €49 a night outside the summer months, and Pestana Palm Gardens has apartments from about €51.
Where should a group of golfers stay near Ferragudo?

For groups, villas and townhouses usually work out cheapest per person. Vale de Milho Village (private pool with every townhouse) and Vale da Lapa Village Resort (five-star villas) are both within about 20 minutes of the course.
Playing several courses? Find the best base for your trip

If Ferragudo is just one stop on your golf trip, try **Find Your Base** on the [Algarve Golf Map](/). Pick the courses you want to play and it shows you the area that sits closest to all of them, along with well-rated hotels nearby, so you spend less time driving and more time on the course.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to the Algarve costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: Plan a self-organised golf weekend in the Algarve: four bases near Faro Airport, two courses and three hotels in each, and what it costs per person, month by month. Not package prices.

content.text: A self-organised golf weekend in the Algarve, flying in on Friday, playing on Saturday and Sunday and flying home on Monday, costs **from about €406 to €928 per person**, excluding flights, based on the example weekends below. That covers two rounds, three nights in a shared room, a small hire car and food.

**These figures are for a weekend you organise yourself, booking the hotel, green fees and car separately. They aren't package prices.** We've picked four bases within about 45 minutes of Faro Airport, so you spend the weekend on the course rather than on the road. **Last checked: November 2026.**

**Quick answer:** for the shortest transfer, stay around Quinta do Lago or Vale do Lobo, 20 to 30 minutes from the airport. For the most choice of courses and hotels, pick Vilamoura. For the lowest weekend cost, look at Albufeira in January or Tavira in winter and summer.

content.note: Two rounds, three nights sharing a room and a small hire car, plus food. Only green fees change by month: hotel prices are autumn 2026 'from' rates, so summer weekends will usually cost more. Albufeira has no data for November and December because we don't have Salgados' online rate for those months.
content.caption: Golf weekend cost per person by month, value to premium hotel, excluding flights
headers: Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo

content.text: The plan: arrive Friday, play Saturday and Sunday, fly home Monday

We've built every example around the same simple weekend. It works whatever time your flight lands on Friday and whatever time it leaves on Monday, so you never play a round with one eye on the clock.

**Friday:** land at Faro, pick up the car and check in. If you land early enough, see the twilight ideas below. **Saturday:** a morning round on the first course. **Sunday:** a morning round on the second. **Monday:** breakfast, return the car and fly home.

Costs are per person for **two people sharing a room and a small hire car**. **Included:** two green fees, three hotel nights, the car and food and drink. **Not included:** flights, fuel, tolls, car insurance extras, buggies (except where the green fee includes one), club hire and range balls. Breakfast may be extra, depending on the rate you book.
If you land early on Friday

A twilight round on the day you arrive turns two rounds into three for not much extra. On the dates we checked, [Vale do Lobo's](/courses/vale-do-lobo-royal) late-afternoon rates cost €76 to €101 and the Sunset rate included a shared buggy, [Salgados](/courses/salgados) sold twilight rounds from €47 to €99, and [Benamor](/courses/benamor) had a €59 twilight rate in January, June, July, August and December. Start times depend on the season, so check you'll have enough daylight before you book. Our [night golf guide](/guide/night-golf-in-the-algarve) covers the floodlit options too.
If you fly home late on Monday

All eight courses in this guide have a driving range, so a practice session, or a short round where the club sells one, is a good way to fill the morning. Leave plenty of time to return the car and check in, and remember your clubs will need to go through as oversized baggage if you brought your own.
Where to stay for a golf weekend

These four bases are all within about 45 minutes of Faro Airport, and in each one both suggested courses are under 25 minutes from the hotels. They're examples, not the only good options: we've left some courses and hotels out only because we didn't have reliable prices for them. Each base lists three hotels at different prices.

Hotel prices are the lowest "from" rates we found in autumn 2026, for the whole room, split between two people. Weekend nights can cost more than midweek, and according to Statistics Portugal (INE) the average rate for an occupied room in the Algarve was **€217.80 in August 2025**, so expect to pay noticeably more in summer.
Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo: closest to the airport

The two estates sit side by side, about 20 to 30 minutes from Faro Airport, so you can be at the hotel within an hour of landing. We've paired the [South Course](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south) at Quinta do Lago with the [Royal](/courses/vale-do-lobo-royal) at Vale do Lobo, home of the famous clifftop par-3 16th. The two rounds cost **€304 in January and December and €435 in April**. Both courses set a handicap limit of 28 for men and 36 for ladies.

content.text: Simple apartments and studios on the Almancil side, rated **8.5 on Booking.com** and from about €54 a night in October, which is rare for this area. It has no golf services of its own, but it's about 6 minutes from the Royal and 10 from the South Course.

Vilamoura: the most courses and hotels in one place

Vilamoura is about 30 to 35 minutes from Faro Airport and has four courses open to visitors, plus the marina for dinner. We've paired the [Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course), the resort's best known, with [Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium). The two rounds cost **€303 in December and €433 in March, April and May**. All Vilamoura courses set a handicap limit of 28 for men and 36 for ladies.

Studios and apartments have kitchenettes. Basic, but hard to beat if you just want a clean bed next to the first tee.

Albufeira: the lowest cost in winter

Albufeira's courses are about 45 to 50 minutes from Faro Airport, the longest transfer of the four, but the green fees are lower. We've paired [Salgados](/courses/salgados) with the [Faldo Course](/courses/amendoeira-faldo) at Amendoeira, about 18 minutes apart. The two rounds cost **€178 in January and €351 in April and May**. **Amendoeira's online rate includes a buggy, if available**, while at Salgados a buggy costs €50 extra. Both set a handicap limit of 28 for men and 36 for ladies.

For a longer stay, see [what a 5-night trip to Albufeira costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-albufeira-cost) or [the cheapest golf near Albufeira](/guide/cheapest-golf-near-albufeira).
Tavira: the quieter east

Tavira's courses are about 40 to 45 minutes from Faro Airport, in the quieter eastern Algarve. We've paired [Benamor](/courses/benamor) with [Quinta de Cima](/courses/quinta-de-cima), about 11 minutes apart. The two rounds cost **€166 in December and €253 in March and April**, the lowest of our four bases in most months. Quinta de Cima's sister course, [Quinta da Ria](/courses/quinta-da-ria), is on the same resort if you'd like a change.

For more places to stay, see our guides to [hotels near Benamor](/guide/hotels-near-benamor-golf) and [hotels near Quinta da Ria](/guide/hotels-near-quinta-da-ria-golf), and compare the courses in [Quinta da Ria vs Quinta de Cima](/guide/quinta-da-ria-vs-quinta-de-cima-which-tavira-course-should-you-play).
Travel light: hire clubs instead of flying them

On a weekend trip, the golf bag can cost more trouble than it's worth. Online, most airlines flying into Faro charge roughly £35–£45 or €40–€45 each way for golf clubs on Jet2, Ryanair, easyJet, Aer Lingus and TAP, so about €80 to €90 return per person. You then wait for it at oversized baggage on Friday and check it in early on Monday.

Hiring is usually simpler for two rounds. Shops in the Algarve that publish prices charge from €25 to €40 a day, and some companies deliver to your hotel or let you collect at the airport. If everything else fits in a cabin bag, you can walk straight out of arrivals. Compare companies in our [golf club hire comparison](/club-rental) and our guide to [hiring golf clubs at Faro Airport](/guide/hiring-golf-clubs-at-faro-airport). If you'd rather bring your own set, check the rules for [Ryanair](/guide/ryanair-golf-clubs-what-it-costs-to-fly-with-your-own-set-to-the-algarve), [easyJet](/guide/golf-clubs-on-easyjet-rules-sizes-and-what-it-actually-costs) and [Jet2](/guide/jet2-golf-clubs-fees-weight-limits-and-why-you-shouldn-t-leave-booking-late).
Hire car or transfer?

We've counted a small hire car because in every base the two courses are a short drive apart. Kayak's average for a small car at Faro Airport is about €15 a day, so three days shared between two people is about €22.50 each before fuel and tolls. You can [compare car hire for your dates](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw).

If you stay beside one course and are happy to take taxis to the other, a transfer may work out cheaper. Pre-booked sedans from Faro Airport were quoted from about €34 to Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo, €35 to Vilamoura, €48 to Albufeira and €55 to Tavira in October 2026, per vehicle each way. You can [compare transfers on GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA), and our [Faro Airport to the golf courses guide](/guide/faro-airport-to-algarve-golf-courses) has drive times to every course.
The best months for a golf weekend

Green fees are lowest in winter in most of our bases: two rounds cost €304 around Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo in January and December, €303 in Vilamoura in December, €178 in Albufeira in January and €166 in Tavira in December. Spring and early autumn are the most expensive, and also the busiest, so book tee times early if you're going then.

Summer green fees are often lower too, but the heat makes afternoon rounds hard work and hotels cost the most. For weather and what each month is like on the course, see our [guide to the Algarve golf season](/guide/algarve-golf-season-best-time-to-play-golf).
Booking your tee times

On a weekend you have only two slots to fill (see [how to book tee times in the Algarve](/guide/how-to-book-tee-times-in-the-algarve)), so book them as soon as your flights are confirmed. Weekend mornings tend to be popular, and in spring and October the best times go early. Every course page on our map links to the club's website, and for [Quinta do Lago South](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south), [Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium), [Salgados](/courses/salgados), [Amendoeira Faldo](/courses/amendoeira-faldo) and [Quinta de Cima](/courses/quinta-de-cima) you can also check and book tee times online there. Ask the hotel too: the Conrad and Domes Lake both have golf concierges, and some hotels, like the Marriott at Salgados, sell their own stay-and-play rates.
Golf weekend in the Algarve: common questions
Is a weekend long enough for a golf trip to the Algarve?

Yes, if you pick a base close to Faro Airport. Flights from the UK and Ireland are short, and from Quinta do Lago, Vale do Lobo or Vilamoura you're at the hotel within an hour of landing. Two rounds, or three with a Friday twilight round, is a comfortable weekend.
Does the price include flights?
No. We've left flights out because fares change so much by date, airline and departure airport. Add the golf bag fee if you're flying your own clubs, or hire a set locally instead.
Do I need a handicap?

Yes, for every course in this guide. Quinta do Lago, Vale do Lobo, Vilamoura, Salgados, Amendoeira and Benamor set a limit of 28 for men and 36 for ladies, and Quinta de Cima asks for 36 for everyone. See [do you need a handicap to play golf in the Algarve?](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve) for every course's rules.
Would I save money with a package?

Possibly. Some of the hotels in this guide sell their own golf packages, and holiday companies set their own prices. Our figures show what the same weekend costs if you book everything yourself, so you can compare. For a longer trip, see [how much a golf trip to the Algarve costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost).

excerpt: Both sit in the Golden Triangle and cost a similar green fee, but Laranjal and Pinheiros Altos have taken very different paths in recent years. Here's an honest comparison, backed by real player reviews.

content.text: Both courses sit in the Golden Triangle around Almancil, both cost a similar green fee, and both get overshadowed by the bigger names next door — Quinta do Lago's own South and North courses, and San Lorenzo across the road, which is closed for renovation until 2028. But Laranjal and Pinheiros Altos have taken very different paths in recent years, and it shows.
A newer course and an older, layered one

Laranjal is the youngest of Quinta do Lago's three courses, designed by **Jorge Santana da Silva** and opened in 2009 on what was once a working orange grove — hence the name. Pinheiros Altos has a longer, more complicated history: **Ronald Fream** designed the original two nines in 1992, Peter McEvoy and Howard Swan later reworked and modernised the layout, and Santana da Silva added a third nine in 2007 to make it the 27-hole course it is today.
Laranjal: the pick of the Golden Triangle right now

At 6,480 metres par 72, Laranjal routes five par-5s, eight par-4s and five par-3s through cork oaks, umbrella pines, the original orange trees and five lakes, with Penn A4 bentgrass greens that hold their pace year-round. It's consistently one of the best-reviewed courses on our map.
Pinheiros Altos: a strong layout that needs investment

Pinheiros Altos plays as three interchangeable nine-hole loops — Pines, Corks and Olives — each par 36, giving a genuinely varied combination depending on which two you play. Worth knowing before you book: player reviews over the past couple of years have consistently flagged scorched fairways, patchy greens and worn cart paths, a noticeable step down from how the course used to be rated. The layout itself and the setting inside the Ria Formosa are still genuinely good — it's the upkeep that's fallen behind, and it's fair to go in with tempered expectations until that changes.
Which one should you play?

If you want the more reliably well-maintained round in this part of the Golden Triangle, play Laranjal — it's the safer bet by a clear margin right now. Pinheiros Altos is still worth playing for the variety of its three nines and the price, from **€99** against Laranjal's **€170**, but temper your expectations on conditioning rather than the resort-glossy version you might see in older photos.

Want the numbers side by side instead? [Open the course comparator](/?compare=quinta-do-lago-laranjal,pinheiros-altos) to see Laranjal and Pinheiros Altos' price, handicap limits and facilities pulled straight from our live course data.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Quinta do Lago costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-quinta-do-lago-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: The 14 Algarve hotels genuinely built on the same estate as a golf course — from Monte Rei to Penina — grouped by region, with real prices and booking links.

content.text: Plenty of Algarve hotels are "near" a golf course — a ten-minute drive, a shuttle bus, a partnership with the club down the road. Fewer hotels actually have a course built into their own grounds, where you can walk from your room to the first tee with your clubs already waiting at the pro shop.

Staying at one of these usually means preferential or discounted green fees for hotel guests, no need for a rental car to reach the course, and practical perks like secure club storage and drying rooms after a wet round. Below are the 14 Algarve hotels with a genuine on-site golf course, grouped by region from east to west.
East Algarve
1. Monte Rei Golf & Country Club Hotel

Set on a private 1,000-acre estate near Vila Nova de Cacela, [Monte Rei](/hotels/monte-rei-hotel) pairs villa and apartment residences in traditional Portuguese architecture with the [Monte Rei North Course](/courses/monte-rei) — a Jack Nicklaus Signature design that held the title of Portugal's number one golf course for 15 consecutive years before being overtaken by Terras da Comporta in the 2026 rankings. The estate's restaurant, Vistas, is run by chef André Simão and holds a Selected listing in the Michelin Guide Portugal.
2. Robinson Club Quinta da Ria

This 4-star all-inclusive resort sits between the [Quinta da Ria](/courses/quinta-da-ria) and [Quinta de Cima](/courses/quinta-de-cima) courses in the unspoiled eastern Algarve, with all 259 rooms overlooking either the fairways or the Ria Formosa nature reserve. The all-inclusive package covers two restaurants, three pools, a spa, gym, tennis courts and a kids' club — a practical option for golfing families.
3. Castro Marim Golfe & Country Club

Near the Spanish border, on the far-eastern edge of the Algarve, [this resort](/hotels/castro-marim-golf-club) offers 75 air-conditioned accommodations and private village houses — several with their own hot tubs or fireplaces — built around the [Castro Marim](/courses/castro-marim) 27-hole layout between the Guadiana River and the Atlantic.
Golden Triangle — Almancil & Vale do Lobo
4. Hotel Quinta do Lago

A member of the Leading Hotels of the World since 1988, [Hotel Quinta do Lago](/hotels/hotel-quinta-do-lago) is a five-star property with direct pedestrian access to all three courses on the estate: [South](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south), [North](/courses/quinta-do-lago-north) and [Laranjal](/courses/quinta-do-lago-laranjal). Its 141 rooms and suites, two restaurants, spa and indoor pool make it one of the definitive bases for a Golden Triangle golf trip.
5. Dona Filipa Hotel

Inside the exclusive Vale do Lobo estate, the five-star [Dona Filipa Hotel](/hotels/dona-filipa-hotel) sits on-site at [Vale do Lobo Royal](/courses/vale-do-lobo-royal) and [Ocean](/courses/vale-do-lobo-ocean), a two-minute walk from the beach, with tennis courts, a spa and acclaimed dining. Its long-standing link with the neighbouring San Lorenzo course is on hold while San Lorenzo is closed for renovation until mid-2028.
Loulé hills
6. Viceroy at Ombria Algarve

A newer luxury eco-resort in the hills near Querença, the [Viceroy at Ombria Algarve](/hotels/viceroy-ombria) is built beside the award-winning [Ombria Golf](/courses/ombria) course. Accommodation ranges from rooms with private terraces to two-bedroom residences with private pools, with an emphasis on sustainability and blending into the natural Algarve landscape.
Albufeira
7. Pine Cliffs Residence

Part of Marriott's Luxury Collection, [Pine Cliffs Resort](/hotels/pine-cliffs-residence) sits on the red sandstone cliffs above Praia da Falésia with direct beach access via a cliffside lift, alongside the [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs) 9-hole course. The resort spans two- and three-bedroom apartments, a spa, and around a dozen dining venues.
8. Balaia Golf Village Resort

A 4-star self-catering resort built around the 9-hole [Balaia Golf Village](/courses/balaia) course, spread across a hillside estate near Albufeira with 508 apartments and studios, six outdoor pools and two restaurants.
Carvoeiro & Portimão
9. Pestana Gramacho Residences

A 4-star golf aparthotel within 500 metres of the [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho) clubhouse, part of the wider Pestana Carvoeiro golf resort. All 57 studios and apartments have balconies overlooking the fairways, and a shuttle bus connects guests to the other Pestana courses nearby.
10. Penina Hotel & Golf Resort

The Algarve's original five-star hotel. Sir Henry Cotton built [Penina](/hotels/penina-hotel) in 1966 on a 360-acre estate that was previously rice paddies, planting over 360,000 trees to create the parkland setting that still surrounds the [Championship](/courses/penina-championship) and [Resort](/courses/penina-resort) courses today — the first 18-hole golf course built in the Algarve.
11. NAU Morgado Golf & Country Club

A 4-star, 98-room hotel overlooking the [Morgado](/courses/morgado) and [Alamos](/courses/alamos) courses near Portimão, with rooms and terraces facing the fairways, four outdoor pools and a golf academy at the clubhouse.
Silves
12. Amendoeira Golf Resort

A 4-star resort of self-catering apartments and villas set within the Amendoeira estate, home to the [Faldo](/courses/amendoeira-faldo) and [O'Connor Jr](/courses/amendoeira-oconnor) courses. Facilities include two outdoor pools, six tennis courts and five-a-side football pitches.
Lagos
13. Boavista Golf & Spa Resort
