A 5-star holiday village on the hills above Lagos, pairing townhouse and apartment accommodation with the 18-hole [Boavista](/courses/boavista) course. The Essential Fitness & Spa adds a heated indoor pool, sauna and steam room to the outdoor pools and tennis courts.
14. Palmares Beach House Hotel

A boutique 5-star property set between the 27th green and the driving range of the 27-hole [Palmares](/courses/palmares) course, overlooking Meia Praia beach and Lagos Bay. With just 22 rooms and suites, it's one of the more intimate options on this list.

Prices and availability change often, so treat the figures on each hotel's page as a starting point rather than a quote — always confirm current rates and any golf package terms directly with the resort or through the booking link before you commit.

**Prefer all-inclusive?** Our guide to [all-inclusive golf hotels in the Algarve](/guide/all-inclusive-golf-hotels-in-the-algarve) explains what all-inclusive covers (not your green fees) and shows examples near the courses.

excerpt: Same designer, same estate, same all-inclusive hotel near Tavira — but Quinta de Cima bills itself as the championship test, and the numbers back it up. Here's how the two compare.

content.text: Quinta da Ria and Quinta de Cima sit on the same estate near Tavira, share a designer, opened months apart, and share the same all-inclusive hotel. They're about as close to sibling courses as it gets in the eastern Algarve — but the resort itself markets one of them as the tougher test, and the numbers back that up.
Same architect, same year, same estate

Both courses were designed by **Rocky Roquemore** and opened in 2002 — Ria first, in March, followed by Cima that July — on a 660,000 m² estate inside the Ria Formosa Natural Park. Both use bentgrass throughout, on tees, fairways and greens, which is a step up from the Bermuda grass used on most Algarve courses and keeps conditioning consistent whichever one you play.
Quinta da Ria: the scenic original

Ria plays a shorter 6,053 metres par 72 across two loops of nine, each with two par 5s, five par 4s and two par 3s, with five purpose-built lakes bringing water into play on several holes. It's the more scenic of the two, with panoramic views over the Ria Formosa lagoon and the eastern Algarve hills, and, like Quinta de Cima, it accepts handicaps up to 36 for men and ladies.
"The Championship Course": Quinta de Cima

Cima is longer and, by the resort's own description, the more exacting of the two — its own website calls it simply **"The Championship Course."** At 6,586 metres par 72 (four par 3s, ten par 4s, four par 5s), a creek crosses several fairways to create strategic water hazards, and it carries the same maximum handicap of 36 for all players, but the extra length and tighter demands mean it plays harder in practice.
Which one should you play?

If you want the more scenic, slightly shorter round with lagoon views, play Ria first. If you want the genuine championship test — more length, tighter water hazards, the course the resort itself puts forward as the serious one — play Cima. Green fees start from the same **€100** at both, so most golfers staying nearby simply play both across a trip.
Where to stay

Both courses share the same on-site hotel, [Robinson Club Quinta da Ria](/hotels/robinson-quinta-da-ria), a 4-star all-inclusive resort with 259 rooms overlooking either the fairways or the Ria Formosa nature reserve, three pools, a spa and a kids' club. You can [book it directly on Booking.com](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/robinson-club-quinta-da-ria.html).

Want the numbers side by side instead? [Open the course comparator](/?compare=quinta-da-ria,quinta-de-cima) to see Ria and Cima's price, length, handicap limits and facilities pulled straight from our live course data.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Monte Rei costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-monte-rei-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: A step-by-step guide to planning an Algarve golf trip — flights, transfers vs car hire, choosing your courses, picking a base, and whether to bring or rent your clubs.

content.text: The Algarve has 38 golf courses active today, spread along a coastline you can drive end to end in about two hours. That's the appeal, and also the trap: with this much choice, it's easy to spend more time deciding than playing. This guide walks through the trip in order — getting there, getting around, picking your courses, picking your base, and sorting your clubs — so you can book it once and get back to planning your round, not your logistics.
When to go

If you want the best conditions and don't mind paying for them, aim for late April into May, or late September into October — long warm days, courses at their best, and the highest green fees and busiest tee sheets of the year to go with it. For better value with still-reliable weather, target February or the stretch from late September to mid-November, where fees sit in the low-to-mid band and the courses are calmer. For the cheapest golf outright, June to August has the lowest green fees of the year because most visitors are at the beach rather than on the course — you just need to tee off early to beat the heat. December and January are just as cheap for both golf and hotel rooms, with shorter days and a higher chance of rain as the trade-off.

That's the short version. We've written a full month-by-month breakdown — temperatures, rainfall, green-fee swings and hotel occupancy for every month of the year — in our [Algarve golf season guide](/guide/algarve-golf-season-best-time-to-play-golf).
Getting there

Almost every trip starts and ends at Faro Airport (FAO), which sits close enough to the coast that you can be on the first tee within the hour of landing — it's under 30 minutes by car to the central resorts around Vilamoura, Vale do Lobo and Albufeira, and roughly 45 minutes to an hour if you're heading to Lagos in the west or Monte Rei in the east.

From the UK, **Ryanair** runs the widest network into Faro — direct routes from London Stansted, Manchester, Birmingham, Bristol, Edinburgh, Belfast and Glasgow, among others. **easyJet** and **Jet2** both fly direct from London Luton, Manchester, Birmingham and Bristol, and **British Airways** connects from London Heathrow and Gatwick. From Ireland, **Ryanair** and **Aer Lingus** both fly direct from Dublin, with Ryanair also covering Cork, Shannon, Knock and Kerry. If you're coming from elsewhere in Europe, Faro also has direct connections from Germany, the Netherlands and Spain — worth checking against Faro directly before routing through Lisbon.

Most of those airlines charge extra for golf clubs, and the rules vary more than you'd expect. As a rough guide: Ryanair charges **£40 per bag, per one-way flight** booked online and easyJet around **£42** — so budget £80–£85 return, and the same again for a second bag for a travel companion. Jet2 starts from **£35 per item** online, but it's worth booking the clubs the same day you book the flight, since sports equipment space on golf routes can sell out in peak season. British Airways is the exception: on a Standard fare or above, a golf bag under 23kg can travel completely free as your included checked bag, provided it's the only hold item you're bringing. Aer Lingus carries clubs free in Business class, and charges around **€40 per bag online** in Economy. If you'd rather not deal with any of this, the next section covers renting instead.

For the exact fees, size limits and booking quirks of each carrier, see our guides for [Ryanair](/guide/ryanair-golf-clubs-what-it-costs-to-fly-with-your-own-set-to-the-algarve), [easyJet](/guide/golf-clubs-on-easyjet-rules-sizes-and-what-it-actually-costs), [Jet2](/guide/jet2-golf-clubs-fees-weight-limits-and-why-you-shouldn-t-leave-booking-late), [British Airways](/guide/british-airways-and-golf-clubs-when-it-s-free-and-when-it-isn-t) and [Aer Lingus](/guide/aer-lingus-golf-clubs-free-in-business-here-s-what-economy-pays).
Getting from the airport to your base
Once you land, you've got two realistic options: a transfer, or a rental car. Which one makes sense depends on how spread out your golf plans are.
Airport transfers

If you're staying at one resort for the whole trip — especially somewhere like Quinta do Lago, Vale do Lobo or Monte Rei, where the course, hotel and restaurants are all walkable — a private transfer straight from the airport is usually the easier and cheaper call than a car you'll barely use. No parking to sort, no unfamiliar roundabouts after a long flight, and no deposit held on a credit card. You can [book a transfer here](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA).
Renting a car

If your plan involves playing courses in more than one region — say, a round in Vilamoura, another near Carvoeiro, and a day trip out to Lagos — a rental car gives you the flexibility to do that without relying on taxis for every round, and means you're not tied to a single resort for evenings out. Given the region runs close to 150km from the Spanish border to the western tip, a car pays for itself quickly if you're moving around. You can [compare rental car options here](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw). Most Algarve courses have ample free parking, so the car costs you nothing extra once you're there.
Choosing which courses to play

With 38 active courses on our database, spanning parkland, links-style and resort layouts from designers like Jack Nicklaus, Nick Faldo, Arnold Palmer and Sir Henry Cotton, the honest answer to "which course should I play" depends on your handicap, your budget and how far you're willing to drive between rounds. Green fees across the region run from roughly €40 at the more relaxed 9-hole courses to over €200 at the flagship championship layouts, so the spread in price is as wide as the spread in difficulty.

Rather than work from a single "best of" list, use our [interactive course map](/) to filter by region, price, difficulty and designer, and compare up to four courses side by side before you commit to a tee time. If you'd rather start from a shortlist, a few of our roundups are a good starting point: [the 8 best Algarve golf courses for beginners](/guide/the-10-best-algarve-golf-courses-for-beginners), [the 10 best Algarve golf courses for seniors](/guide/the-10-best-algarve-golf-courses-for-seniors), [the best ocean view golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-best-ocean-view-golf-courses-in-the-algarve), and [the Algarve's best par-3 courses](/guide/the-algarve-s-best-par-3-golf-courses) if you're looking for something shorter to mix into the week.
Where to stay

Once you have a rough idea of which courses you want to play, work backwards to where you should sleep. Staying 40 minutes from every course on your list will eat into your trip fast, and the Algarve's golf is spread across several distinct clusters — the Golden Triangle around Almancil and Vale do Lobo, the Vilamoura and Albufeira resorts, the Carvoeiro and Portimão courses further west, and the quieter eastern cluster around Tavira and Monte Rei — so your base matters more here than in a smaller destination.

Our [Find Your Base](/) tool does this calculation for you: pick the courses you want to play, and it shows you which towns and hotels sit closest to all of them, so you're not driving across the region every morning. If playing straight from your hotel's own fairway matters to you, we've also put together a list of [Algarve hotels with a golf course on-site](/guide/algarve-hotels-with-a-golf-course-on-site) — resorts like Quinta do Lago, Monte Rei and Penina, where the course is part of the same estate as the hotel.
Bring your clubs or rent them

This usually comes down to how particular you are about your own set versus how much you're carrying through the airport, and the maths doesn't always favour bringing your own. Once you count the outbound fee, the return fee, and the risk of a shaft bent in the hold, a week of rental clubs can come in cheaper than a single golf bag flown both ways — our research found standard rental sets running at roughly **€12–€25 a day**, with better rates the longer you book.

Several rental operators also deliver straight to your hotel or first course rather than making you collect from the airport — useful if you're arriving late, renting a car separately, or just don't want to carry a golf bag through arrivals. We've compared the [rental options at Faro Airport](/guide/hiring-golf-clubs-at-faro-airport), including which ones offer that hotel delivery, if you'd rather travel without your own set at all.

If you're bringing your own, check the specific baggage policy for your airline before you book — the fees and size limits vary more than people expect, and they're cheaper to add in advance than to pay for at the gate.
A few practical things to sort early

**Book tee times ahead of time** (see [how to book tee times in the Algarve](/guide/how-to-book-tee-times-in-the-algarve)), especially from May to September and for the busiest courses — Quinta do Lago, Vilamoura Old Course and Monte Rei among them. Walk-up availability at the popular clubs gets thin in high season.

**Reserve your buggy in advance too**, if you want one. Not every course has a large buggy fleet, and they can sell out independently of tee time availability — few green fees include one as standard.

**Check the dress code before you pack.** Most Algarve clubhouses expect a collared shirt and tailored shorts or trousers, and several require soft spikes on the course — trainers and jeans are usually turned away at the pro shop.

Once you've got your flights, your base and your course list sorted, the rest of the trip takes care of itself. Start with the [course map](/) to build your shortlist, then use [Find Your Base](/) to lock in where you'll sleep.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to the Algarve costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

**Only have a weekend?** Our [guide to a golf weekend in the Algarve](/guide/golf-weekend-in-the-algarve) costs a Friday-to-Monday trip with two rounds, from four bases within about 45 minutes of Faro Airport.

**Travelling as a group?** Our guide to [Algarve golf trips for groups and golf societies](/guide/algarve-golf-trips-for-groups-and-golf-societies) covers golf villas and apartments, booking tee times together, buggies and minivans.

**Prefer all-inclusive?** Our guide to [all-inclusive golf hotels in the Algarve](/guide/all-inclusive-golf-hotels-in-the-algarve) explains what all-inclusive covers (not your green fees) and shows examples near the courses.

excerpt: Both sit minutes apart near the Spanish border, but one carries a Seve Ballesteros design and the other offers three flexible nines and its own resort. Here's how the east Algarve's two courses compare.

content.text: Tucked into the far eastern corner of the Algarve near the Spanish border, Castro Marim and Quinta do Vale are the two courses for golfers who've already done Vilamoura and Quinta do Lago and want somewhere quieter. They're a few minutes apart, but one carries a genuinely famous name behind the design.
A big-name design vs a flexible 27-hole resort

Quinta do Vale is the work of **Seve Ballesteros**, opened in October 2007 as one of his last course designs. Castro Marim has a longer, more layered history: British architect **Terry Murray** designed the original Atlantic and Guadiana nines, which opened in 2001, before a third nine, the Grouse, was added in 2008 to make it the 27-hole resort it is today.
Quinta do Vale: Seve's creative signature

At 6,206 metres par 72, Quinta do Vale winds through a natural valley with views over the Guadiana River towards Spain, built around an unusual balance of six par-3s, six par-4s and six par-5s — deliberately avoiding the same par at consecutive holes. It's classic Ballesteros: wide, strategic fairways and creative use of dog-legs and water rather than sheer length. It's also the cheaper of the two to play, from **€67**, and it uses the standard Algarve handicap limit of 28 for men and 36 for ladies, while Castro Marim asks for a certificate without publishing a maximum.
Castro Marim: three nines, played your way

Castro Marim's 27 holes split into three distinct nines — Atlantic, Grouse and Guadiana — that can be combined in any pairing, so no two rounds need to feel the same. The combined championship layout reaches 6,282 metres par 72, and the resort has its own on-site hotel, which Quinta do Vale doesn't, making it the easier of the two to build a full stay-and-play trip around.
Which one should you play?

If the designer's name matters to you, or you want a single, tightly designed 18 holes, play Quinta do Vale. If you'd rather the flexibility of three nines and the option to stay on site, play Castro Marim. Green fees start from **€67** at Quinta do Vale and **€87** at Castro Marim, and both are close enough together that visiting golfers based in the east often play both across a trip.
Where to stay

Castro Marim has its own on-site resort, [Castro Marim Golfe & Country Club](/hotels/castro-marim-golf-club), with private village houses, three pools and a clubhouse restaurant overlooking the course. You can [book it directly on Booking.com](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/castro-marim-golfe-and-country-club.html). Quinta do Vale has no on-site hotel — most golfers playing it are staying elsewhere in the east Algarve and driving in.

Want the numbers side by side instead? [Open the course comparator](/?compare=castro-marim,quinta-do-vale) to see Castro Marim and Quinta do Vale's price, par, handicap limits and facilities pulled straight from our live course data.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Monte Rei costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-monte-rei-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: Most Algarve golf courses require an official handicap of 28 for men and 36 for ladies. Here are the exact rules, the courses that don't need one, and how to get a handicap before you go.

content.text: If you are new to golf, or you have played for years without ever getting round to an official handicap, this is usually the first question to settle before booking an Algarve trip. The short answer: on almost every full-length course in the Algarve, **yes, you need an official handicap**, and it has to be below a set limit. But there are genuine exceptions, and a few ways round the rule that most first-timers never hear about.
The short answer

Most 18-hole courses in the Algarve ask for a valid handicap certificate and set a maximum of **28 for men and 36 for ladies**. Players without a handicap, or above those limits, are not usually allowed out on their own.

The exceptions are the short and nine-hole courses, several of which ask for no handicap at all, plus a couple of resorts that let beginners play with a teaching professional or with the manager's permission. If you have never held a handicap, those are where your trip should start.
The standard limit: 28 for men, 36 for ladies

This is the figure you will see again and again, and it comes straight from the courses' own rules. [Quinta do Lago](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south) states that an official handicap certificate is obligatory, with a maximum of 28 for men and 36 for ladies across its three courses. [Vilamoura](/courses/vilamoura-old-course) applies exactly the same limits to the Old Course, Pinhal, Laguna and Millennium. [Ombria](/courses/ombria) sets 28 and 36 in its published rules and asks for your handicap when you book, as do the NAU courses [Morgado](/courses/morgado) and [Alamos](/courses/alamos). [Salgados](/courses/salgados) sets the same 28 and 36 on its course information.

Even [Monte Rei](/courses/monte-rei), one of the most exclusive courses in Portugal, uses the same numbers. Its rules say every guest must provide a valid handicap certificate, with a recommended 28 for men and 36 for ladies.
Courses with a slightly stricter limit

A few courses go a little lower. The Pestana courses near Carvoeiro are the best-known example: [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho) publishes a limit of **27 for men and 35 for ladies** in its club rules, and [Boavista](/courses/boavista) near Lagos is stricter still, at **26 for men and 34 for ladies**. If your handicap sits right on the line, check the course page on our [map](/) before you book. Every course lists its handicap limits for men and ladies.
Courses that accept 36 for men too

A few full-length courses are more relaxed. [Alto Golf](/courses/alto-golf) in Alvor sets a limit of **36 for men and ladies** on its official scorecard, and so do the sister courses [Quinta da Ria](/courses/quinta-da-ria) and [Quinta de Cima](/courses/quinta-de-cima) near Tavira. If your handicap is between 29 and 36, these are your best bets for an 18-hole round.
Why a brand-new handicap can still be too high

Under the World Handicap System, an official Handicap Index can go as high as **54**. That means many golfers who have only just qualified start well above 28, and sometimes above 36. Holding a certificate is not enough on its own: the number on it has to be under the course limit too. If you have just got your first handicap, plan your trip around the short courses below for now, or around the courses you already know you qualify for.
What counts as proof of handicap

You need something official that shows your current Handicap Index: a handicap certificate or card from your home club, or the official app of your national golf union showing your index. Bring it with you, ideally both on your phone and as a printout, and expect to give your handicap when you book. Ombria, for example, asks for your name, nationality and handicap on every reservation.
Some courses check at the desk and some barely look. That is not something to gamble a pre-paid tee time on, though, and a course is within its rights to turn you away.
Two ways round the rule at the big resorts

**Play with a teaching professional.** Quinta do Lago's own rules make an exception to the certificate requirement when you are playing with one of its teaching professionals. A playing lesson on a championship course is a very good way to get your first taste of a big-name layout without a handicap.

**Ask the manager.** Vilamoura's rules say that players with higher handicaps, and beginners, can play with the authorisation of the golf course manager. That is a discretion, not a right, so ask well ahead of your trip rather than at the desk. Monte Rei's rules likewise leave exceptions to the Director of Golf.
Algarve golf courses where you don't need a handicap
These courses do not ask for an official handicap, which makes them the natural starting point for a first golf holiday.
Penina Resort Course, Portimão

Penina's nine-hole Resort Course, designed by Sir Henry Cotton alongside the famous championship course, officially states that no handicap is required. It is a proper full-length nine, par 35, about 2,600 metres from the yellow tees, and can be played twice round as 18. You also get the resort's practice facilities.
Pine Cliffs, Albufeira

The nine-hole clifftop course at the Pine Cliffs resort lets players without a handicap onto the course. The only condition is that they play from the red tees. It is a short but spectacular layout above the beach at Olhos de Água, with its own golf academy.
Vale de Milho, Carvoeiro

A nine-hole, all par-3 course above Carvoeiro, under a kilometre long in total. No handicap is required, but the club does expect you to have had a few lessons and to know basic golf etiquette before you play. For a genuine beginner, it is one of the gentlest introductions in the region.

[Balaia Golf Village](/courses/balaia) near Albufeira is another short par-3 course often recommended to beginners, but it does not belong on the no-handicap list: the resort's guest information says a handicap is required, without giving a limit, so check with the club before you book if you have only just started playing. For more short options, see our guide to [the Algarve's best par-3 golf courses](/guide/the-algarve-s-best-par-3-golf-courses).
How to get a handicap before your trip

The traditional route is to join a golf club at home, play the qualifying rounds and receive a Handicap Index from your club. Under the World Handicap System, you normally need to submit scores from **54 holes**, in any mix of 9- and 18-hole rounds.

You no longer have to join a club, though. In England, **iGolf** from England Golf gives golfers with a home address in England an official handicap through the My England Golf app: you pre-register your rounds, a playing partner verifies the scores, and your index appears once you have submitted 54 holes. Scotland has a similar subscription scheme, **OpenPlay**, run by Scottish Golf. If you live elsewhere, ask your national golf union. Allow a few weeks before you travel to play the rounds.
Check which courses you can play with your handicap

Our [Algarve golf course map](/) can do the checking for you. Use the **Men handicap** or **Ladies handicap** filter at the top of the map, pick your handicap, and the map only shows the courses that accept it, including the ones that don't ask for a handicap at all.

To see it in action, here is the map filtered for [a man with a handicap of 28](/?hcp_m=28) and for [a lady with a handicap of 36](/?hcp_l=36). Change the number to your own, then click any course to see its green fees, facilities and exact handicap rules.
The bottom line

If you already hold a handicap of 28 or under (36 for ladies), almost the whole of the Algarve is open to you. If you don't, start at the courses that do not ask for one, take a lesson or two at an academy, and save the championship courses for when you have an official handicap. Our guide to [the 8 best Algarve golf courses for beginners](/guide/the-10-best-algarve-golf-courses-for-beginners) will help you choose.

**Booking your rounds?** Our guide to [how to book tee times in the Algarve](/guide/how-to-book-tee-times-in-the-algarve) shows how each course takes bookings, when to book and the cancellation rules to check.
**Entering a tournament?** Handicap limits for competitions can be lower than for a normal round. See our guide to [golf tournaments in the Algarve](/guide/golf-tournaments-in-the-algarve).

excerpt: Where to stay to play Vale de Milho, Carvoeiro's nine-hole par-3 course: 10 well-rated hotels all within about 10 minutes, from apartments at around €50 a night to boutique B&Bs, with drive times, breakfast hours and golf perks.

content.text: [Vale de Milho](/courses/vale-de-milho) is one of the friendliest rounds in the Algarve: a nine-hole course just outside Carvoeiro where **every hole is a par 3**. Designed by four-time Ryder Cup player Dave Thomas, it needs no handicap certificate and takes far less time than a full course, which makes it ideal for beginners, families and anyone who wants to sharpen their short game.

Carvoeiro has plenty of places to stay within a few minutes of the first tee. Below are 10 of the best, all rated above 8 out of 10 by guests and **all within about 10 minutes of the course**, from self-catering apartments at around €50 a night to boutique B&Bs and clifftop resorts.
Map of hotels near Vale de Milho Golf
The black pin is the golf course (tap it to see course details). The blue pins are the hotels in this guide; tap one to check prices and availability.
How we chose these hotels

Every hotel here is rated at least 8 out of 10 by guests on Booking.com and is no more than about 11 minutes from the course by road. Drive times are calculated by road to the clubhouse. Breakfast hours and golf services come from each hotel's own website wherever possible, and we only mention a golf perk if the hotel actually states it.

Prices are the lowest average nightly rates we found in October 2026, usually for the quietest winter months. Spring and autumn, peak golf season, cost more, so treat them as a guide rather than a quote.
Closest to the course

content.name: Vale de Milho Village
content.text: The natural choice for this course. The resort says its guests get **an exclusive 20% discount on green fees at Vale de Milho Golf**, which is just a couple of minutes away. Its two- and three-bedroom townhouses each have a private pool and a full kitchen, and the price is for the whole townhouse, so it works out very well for a family or a group of four golfers.
perks: 20% off Vale de Milho green fees

content.name: Rocha Brava Village Resort
content.text: A large self-catering resort of apartments and villas less than a kilometre from the course, with prices from around €55 a night in February. The resort says its reception will **arrange your golf** if you tell them what you need. There is a restaurant, a café-bar serving breakfast, a free shuttle to Carvoeiro beach, tennis, mini golf and a heated indoor pool in winter.
Best value hotels near Vale de Milho (under €90 a night)

content.name: Pestana Palm Gardens
content.text: Clifftop studios and apartments run by Pestana, three minutes from Vale de Milho. Pestana says guests get **exclusive benefits and discounts at its Gramacho and Vale da Pinta courses**, so it is a smart base if you want to add a full 18-hole round to your short-course practice. Breakfast is charged separately, but every unit has a kitchen.
perks: Discounts at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta

content.name: Vale d'El Rei Hotel & Villas
content.text: A quiet, very well-rated hotel and villa complex in the countryside east of Carvoeiro, about 10 minutes from the course. Breakfast starts at 7.30am, there are three outdoor pools and a wellness centre, and the hotel runs a free transfer into Carvoeiro, handy if you want dinner in the village without driving.

content.name: Quinta do Algarvio Village
content.text: Run by the same group as Vale de Milho Village, these self-catering apartments score a remarkable **9.4 on Booking.com**. Members of the operator's Carvoeiro Clube Group club get discounts on golf within the group. There is no breakfast service, but the saltwater pool is heated in winter. You will need a car.
perks: Golf discounts for group club members

content.name: Vale da Lapa Village Resort
content.text: Five-star villas set in gardens, with a spa, indoor pool and restaurant, and breakfast from 7.30am. At 9.3 on Booking.com it is one of the best-rated resorts in Carvoeiro. A great base for a group of friends who want their own villa, and it is also close to the Pestana courses at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta.
Mid-range and boutique stays (€100 to €150 a night)

content.name: Monte Santo Resort
content.text: A five-star resort of spacious suites and townhouses with kitchens, plus a spa and a wellness centre with sauna, Turkish bath and jacuzzi. The resort lists Vale de Milho Golf at 5.2 km, with Gramacho and Vale da Pinta even closer, so it is a comfortable base for playing all three.

content.name: Tivoli Carvoeiro Algarve Resort
content.text: A five-star clifftop resort with sea views, a full spa and indoor and outdoor pools, five minutes from Vale de Milho. It is one of the best-known golf-holiday hotels in Carvoeiro: UK tour operators sell packages here with rounds at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta, and a quick nine at Vale de Milho fits neatly around them.

content.name: Quinta do Ourives
content.text: An exceptionally rated six-room B&B (**9.8 on Booking.com**) five minutes from the course, with breakfast included and a pool with an honesty bar. It has no golf services and breakfast only starts at 8.15am, so it suits relaxed mid-morning rounds rather than early tee times. Minimum stay is three nights.

content.name: Algar Seco Parque
content.text: Self-catering flats, bungalows and suites on the clifftops beside the Algar Seco rock formations, rated 9.3 by guests. The resort can arrange tee times and taxi transfers, and its bistro serves breakfast from 9am to 11am. Vale de Milho is about seven minutes away by car.
Vale de Milho green fees and what to know before you play

According to the club, green fees are the same all year: **€22 for nine holes and €33 for 18**, with juniors paying €15 and €22. Adults play the nine par 3s for a par of 27, while juniors play a customised par-35 layout. You can book online and pay at the clubhouse, and up to four players can share a tee time.

A few things to know. There are no buggies, but trolleys can be hired, and rental equipment is not available for tee times after 3pm. Every player must have their own bag with at least a half set of clubs. The clubhouse serves food and drinks, and lessons are available with a PGA professional. Opening hours change with the seasons (roughly 9am to 5pm in winter and longer in summer), so check the club's website before you go.
Tips for golfers staying near Vale de Milho

**Combine it with a full 18.** Vale de Milho is a short-game course, so many visitors pair it with bigger rounds nearby: [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta) is about 11 minutes away, [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho) about 13 and the new [Pestana Ferragudo](/courses/pestana-ferragudo) about 17. If you are heading there, see our guide to [hotels near Ferragudo Golf Course](/guide/hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course).

**Great for beginners and families.** No handicap is needed and every hole is a par 3, so it is a relaxed place to introduce children or new golfers to the game. Self-catering resorts such as Vale de Milho Village and Rocha Brava work especially well for families.
**Getting there.** Faro Airport is about 70 km away, roughly 50 minutes to an hour by car. Most of the hotels above are a short drive from the course, so a hire car makes life much easier.
Frequently asked questions
Which hotel is closest to Vale de Milho Golf?
Vale de Milho Village, about two minutes away by car, is the closest, and its guests get 20% off green fees. Rocha Brava Village Resort is also less than a kilometre from the course.
Do you need a handicap to play Vale de Milho?
No. Vale de Milho is a nine-hole par-3 course open to all golfers, and no handicap certificate is required.
What is the cheapest place to stay near Vale de Milho?
Pestana Palm Gardens has apartments from about €51 a night in the quieter months, and Rocha Brava Village Resort from about €55. Both are within three minutes of the course.
Playing several courses? Find the best base for your trip

If Vale de Milho is just one stop on your golf trip, try **Find Your Base** on the [Algarve Golf Map](/). Pick the courses you want to play and it shows you the area that sits closest to all of them, along with well-rated hotels nearby, so you spend less time driving and more time on the course.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to the Algarve costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: Where to stay to play the Vilamoura Old Course, Pinhal, Laguna and Millennium: official partner hotels beside the courses, a budget aparthotel by the Old Course and the best marina hotels, with drive times and golf perks.

content.text: Vilamoura is the Algarve's biggest golf destination, with four courses open to visitors within a few minutes of each other: the [Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course), Frank Pennink's 1969 classic through the umbrella pines, its neighbour [Pinhal](/courses/vilamoura-pinhal), and the newer [Laguna](/courses/vilamoura-laguna) and [Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium) courses, which share a clubhouse on the west side of the resort. The fifth course, the Victoria at The Els Club, is now a private members' club.

This guide covers the best golf hotels near Vilamoura: two official partner hotels right beside Pinhal, a budget aparthotel a short walk from the Old Course, and well-rated hotels around the marina, all within about 15 minutes of the first tee.
Map of golf hotels near Vilamoura

The black pins are the four courses (tap one to see course details). Laguna and Millennium share a clubhouse, so their pins sit together. The blue pins are the hotels in this guide; tap one to check prices and availability.
How we chose these hotels

We include a hotel if it is rated at least 8 out of 10 on Booking.com, or at least 7.8 if it offers specific golf services, and is within about 15 minutes of the courses by road. Drive times are calculated by road, not in a straight line. Golf services come from each hotel's own website wherever possible, and we only mention a golf perk if we could find it stated.
Prices are the lowest nightly rates we could reliably find in October 2026, so expect more in spring and summer. Check current rates with the link.
One big name is missing on purpose: the Victoria Golf Resort & Spa, next to The Els Club, closes for renovation from 15 October 2026 and is due to reopen as Fairmont Vilamoura in 2028.
Hotels on the Vilamoura courses
Both of these appear on Vilamoura Golf's own list of partner hotels and sit right beside the Pinhal course, about six minutes from the Old Course and seven from Laguna and Millennium.

content.name: Hilton Vilamoura As Cascatas Golf Resort & Spa
content.text: A five-star resort of hotel rooms and apartments overlooking the Pinhal course, and one of Vilamoura Golf's official partner hotels. You can practically walk to the first tee at Pinhal, and the resort's 7Seven Spa is one of the largest in Portugal. Rooms start from about €112 a night in October, very reasonable for a five-star on the course.

content.name: Vilamoura Garden Hotel
content.text: A four-star hotel 350 metres from the Pinhal course, from about €89 a night in October. It sells **golf packages that combine your room, dining and green fees**, and guests regularly praise the breakfast. The spa across the road has an indoor pool for after your round.
Best value near the Vilamoura courses

content.name: Hotel Apartamento do Golfe
content.text: A simple three-star aparthotel just a short walk from the Old Course clubhouse, and the cheapest well-rated option on this list at around €37 a night in October. Studios and apartments have kitchenettes and balconies. The decor is basic, but for golfers who just need a clean bed next to the course it is hard to beat, and guests mention a courtesy bus into the marina.
perks: Short walk to the Old Course

content.name: Dom José Beach Hotel
content.text: A three-star beach hotel in neighbouring Quarteira that scores an impressive **8.9 on Booking.com** from about €61 a night in October. It has no golf services of its own, but it is about 13 minutes from Pinhal and 15 from the Old Course, and breakfast starts at 7.30am.
Mid-range hotels by Vilamoura Marina
If you want restaurants and bars on your doorstep in the evening, stay by the marina. These hotels are about 8 to 13 minutes from the courses by car.

content.name: Hyatt Regency Vilamoura Algarve
content.text: The former Dom Pedro Vilamoura, which reopened as a Hyatt Regency in January 2026 after a full renovation. It is an official Vilamoura Golf partner and was rated **8.9 on Booking.com**, with breakfast singled out by guests. Golf tour operators list a **free golf shuttle to the four Vilamoura courses**, so check the details when booking. From about €129 a night in October.
perks: Free golf shuttle to the Vilamoura courses (per golf tour operators)

content.name: Dom Pedro Marina
content.text: A small boutique hotel overlooking the marina and another of Vilamoura Golf's partner hotels. Guests rate the breakfast particularly highly, and you can walk to the marina's restaurants in the evening. Pinhal is about eight minutes away.

content.name: Vila Galé Marina
content.text: A four-star hotel a short walk from the marina, with an outdoor pool and a good-value location for a mixed group of golfers and non-golfers. Pinhal is about nine minutes away and the Old Course about 13.
Luxury golf hotels in Vilamoura

content.name: Domes Lake Algarve, Autograph Collection
content.text: The best-rated hotel on this list at **9.1 on Booking.com**, a five-star lakeside resort between the marina and the courses. Its **golf concierge** picks courses to suit your level, arranges transfers and instructors and can hire you professional equipment, and the hotel partners with the Vilamoura Golf Academy for lessons. From about €195 a night in October.
perks: Arranges transfers, instructors and equipment hire
Partnership with the Vilamoura Golf Academy

content.name: Tivoli Marina Vilamoura Algarve Resort
content.text: A big five-star resort right between the marina and the beach, rated **8.9 on Booking.com** from more than 1,600 reviews. It suits golfers travelling with non-golfing partners or family, with the beach, pools and marina all on the doorstep. Pinhal is about 11 minutes away and the Old Course about 14.
perks: Right between the marina and the beach

content.text: Vilamoura green fees and what to know before you play

Green fees are booked online through Vilamoura Golf and change with the season. On the club's online booking, 18 holes cost **about €215 to €301 on the Old Course**, the most expensive of the four, about €101 to €144 on Pinhal, and about €88 to €136 on Laguna and Millennium. Prices change with demand: the Old Course and Pinhal are dearest from March to May, while Laguna and Millennium are cheapest in November and December. The club does not publish a buggy hire price, so ask when you book. See our [guide to golf buggy hire in the Algarve](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve) for prices and rules across the region.

The maximum handicap is 28 for men and 36 for ladies, although beginners can be allowed on with the manager's authorisation. Read more in our guide to [whether you need a handicap to play golf in the Algarve](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve). If you want to work on your game during your trip, the Vilamoura Golf Academy offers lessons; see our guide to [golf lessons in the Algarve](/guide/golf-lessons-in-the-algarve).
Tips for golfers staying in Vilamoura

**Which course should you play?** The Old Course is the famous one, while Millennium is generally the most forgiving for higher handicaps. Laguna also has wide fairways, but several holes need carries over water. Compare them in [Vilamoura Old Course vs Millennium](/guide/vilamoura-old-course-vs-millennium-which-one-should-you-play) and [Laguna vs Pinhal](/guide/vilamoura-laguna-vs-pinhal-which-course-should-you-play).

**Pick your base by course.** If you are mainly playing the Old Course and Pinhal, stay at the hotels around Pinhal or the Apartamento do Golfe. Laguna and Millennium are on the west side, about 10 minutes from the marina hotels.

**More golf nearby.** [Vila Sol](/courses/vila-sol) is right next door, and the Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo courses are about 25 minutes east. See our guide to [hotels near Quinta do Lago golf](/guide/hotels-near-quinta-do-lago-golf) if you want to split your stay.
**Getting there.** Faro Airport is about 24 km away, around 35 minutes by car.
Frequently asked questions
What is the best hotel for golf in Vilamoura?

For being on the course, the Hilton Vilamoura As Cascatas and the Vilamoura Garden Hotel, both official partner hotels right beside Pinhal. For golf services, Domes Lake Algarve has a dedicated golf concierge and the highest guest rating on this list.
What is the cheapest place to stay near the Vilamoura golf courses?
Hotel Apartamento do Golfe, from about €37 a night in October and a short walk from the Old Course. Dom José Beach Hotel in Quarteira, from about €61 and rated 8.9, is the best value by the beach.
Which Vilamoura golf courses are best for beginners?

Millennium is the best choice: it is flat, with wide fairways, and is generally the most forgiving of the four. Laguna also has wide fairways, but several holes need carries over water, which makes it harder for a new golfer. The Old Course is the hardest and most expensive. Beginners without a handicap need the manager's authorisation to play.
Can you play The Els Club (Victoria) course?
Not as a visitor. The Victoria course is now run as The Els Club, a private members' club, so plan your trip around the Old Course, Pinhal, Laguna and Millennium.
Playing several courses? Find the best base for your trip

If Vilamoura is just one stop on your golf trip, try **Find Your Base** on the [Algarve Golf Map](/). Pick the courses you want to play and it shows you the area that sits closest to all of them, along with well-rated hotels nearby, so you spend less time driving and more time on the course.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Vilamoura costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-vilamoura-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

**Looking for all-inclusive?** We couldn't confirm an all-inclusive rate at a Vilamoura hotel, but our guide to [all-inclusive golf hotels in the Algarve](/guide/all-inclusive-golf-hotels-in-the-algarve) includes two in Olhos de Água, about a quarter of an hour from the Laguna and Millennium courses.

excerpt: What golf lessons in the Algarve really cost, from €30 for 30 minutes, plus the best beginner schools and golf academies in every part of the region.

content.text: The Algarve is one of the best places in Europe to learn golf. The weather lets you practise outdoors almost all year, most of the big resorts run a teaching academy with PGA professionals, and lesson prices are often lower than at a UK club. This guide covers what golf lessons in the Algarve actually cost, the beginner schools worth knowing about, and the best academies in each part of the region.

Every price below comes from the academies' own published price lists, checked in November 2026. We note the season where a list is older, and prices can change, so always confirm when you book. You can also browse every academy we have checked, with full price lists, in our [directory of golf academies in the Algarve](/golf-academies).
How much do golf lessons cost in the Algarve?
A one-hour private lesson with a PGA professional costs roughly **€60 to €90**, and a 30-minute lesson around **€30 to €60**. These are the published rates at seven of the region's academies:
**[Castro Marim](/golf-academies/castro-marim-golf-academy) (East Algarve):** €30 for 30 minutes, €60 for an hour, or five 30-minute lessons for €140.

**[Penina](/golf-academies/penina-golf-academy) (Portimão):** €40 for 30 minutes and €65 for an hour on the academy's 2024/25 price list. That list ran until October 2025 and no newer one has been published yet, so ask for current prices.

**[Pestana Golf Academy](/golf-academies/pestana-golf-academy) (Pestana's courses in Carvoeiro, Silves, Portimão and Vilamoura):** €35 for 30 minutes and €65 for an hour on its 2024 price list, the latest it publishes. Bring a friend and an hour for two costs €75 in total.
**[Vilamoura Golf Academy](/golf-academies/vilamoura-golf-academy):** €55 for 30 minutes and €81 for an hour on its 2026 price list, with 15% off for guests at the resort's official hotels.
**[Espiche Golf Academy](/golf-academies/espiche-golf-academy) (Lagos):** €40 for 30 minutes and €65 for an hour on its 2026 flyer, and if you pay for five lessons the sixth is free.

**[Pinheiros Altos Golf Academy](/golf-academies/pinheiros-altos-golf-academy) (Quinta do Lago estate):** €55 for 30 minutes and €90 for an hour for visitors, with unlimited balls, video analysis and club hire included.
**[Quinta do Lago Golf Academy](/golf-academies/quinta-do-lago-golf-academy):** €60 for 30 minutes and €95 for a 50-minute lesson in the resort's online booking system.
Sharing a lesson is the easiest way to save money. At Vilamoura, a one-hour group class for two costs €108, which works out at €54 each. Pestana's two-person hour works out at €37.50 each.
Beginner golf schools: learn in three to five days

If you are starting from scratch, a short beginner school is better value than a string of one-off lessons. You get a structured plan, a few hours of coaching spread over several days, and usually a first round on the course with your teacher at the end.
**Pestana Beginners School:** three days of 90-minute sessions for €162.50 per person, or five days for €250 per person, with a minimum of two people (2024 price list).

**Penina Beginners Golf Clinic:** five days with one hour of coaching a day, covering the full swing, short game, putting and basic rules and etiquette. It ends with a game on the course with the professional. Unlimited range balls, a hand trolley and a set of clubs are included, so you do not need to bring anything. On the 2024/25 list, which ran until October 2025, it cost €284 per person for groups of four to eight, or €355 per person for one to three people.
**Vilamoura lesson packs:** five hours of coaching (or three hours on the range plus two on the course) for €370, or €490 for two people. Every pack includes a nine-hole game with the professional.

**Pinheiros Altos packages:** three days with seven hours of tuition for €600 (or €695 for two people), or five days with 12 hours for €1,000 (€1,100 for two). Both include clubs, balls, video analysis and the green fee for time on the course with the professional.

**Espiche beginners package:** 20 one-hour sessions over 10 weeks for €500, a good fit if you are staying longer or live in the Algarve. There is also a 90-minute Golf Experience introduction for €90 per person.
**[Boavista](/golf-academies/boavista-golf-academy) Start 2 Golf:** a beginners programme of 10 lessons for €175 in Lagos, on a price list published in January 2025.
**Quinta do Lago Golf School:** programmes from half a day to five days at the Paul McGinley Academy, booked through the resort's online booking system. Prices are not published.
Getting your handicap at an Algarve academy

Vilamoura Golf Academy runs a five-day **Handicap Golf Certificate** programme that combines practice on the course with classroom sessions, priced at €899 plus a €170 handicap fee on its 2026 list. It is the only programme of its kind we found on an Algarve academy's price list. For why a handicap matters, and which courses let you play without one, see our guide: [Do you need a handicap to play golf in the Algarve?](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve)
The best golf academies in the Algarve, area by area
Western Algarve: Lagos, Portimão and Carvoeiro

[Penina](/courses/penina-championship) has one of the best practice grounds in the region: an 80-metre-wide natural grass driving range, plus the Resort Course, a nine-hole layout that needs no handicap, so you can take your lesson onto a real course straight away. The **[Pestana Golf Academy](/golf-academies/pestana-golf-academy)** teaches across the Pestana courses, including [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho) in Carvoeiro, in English and German. Further west, [Palmares](/courses/palmares) in Lagos has its own [academy](/golf-academies/palmares-golf-academy), whose professional, Almerindo Sequeira, coaches European Tour player Ricardo Santos, and the [Espiche Golf Academy](/golf-academies/espiche-golf-academy) has four professionals, TrackMan and a new academy cabin that opened in early 2025. Also in Lagos, the [Boavista Golf Academy](/golf-academies/boavista-golf-academy) charges €60 a lesson and runs a junior golf school.
Silves and Albufeira

The [academy at Amendoeira](/golf-academies/amendoeira-golf-academy) is one of the best equipped in Portugal, with TrackMan, V1 video analysis, BodiTrak and SAM PuttLab, a maximum of five students per teacher, and schools from half a day to five days. It also has a nine-hole par-3 Academy course, which the resort says is the only floodlit nine-hole course in Portugal. Near Albufeira, [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs) runs a [golf academy](/golf-academies/pine-cliffs-golf-academy) with PGA instructors next to its clifftop nine-hole course, which you can play without a handicap from the red tees.
Vilamoura

The [Vilamoura Golf Academy](/golf-academies/vilamoura-golf-academy) is based at the [Pinhal course](/courses/vilamoura-pinhal) and uses TrackMan and Flightscope. Alongside private lessons and packs, it runs short themed programmes through the year, such as a Couples Golf Experience (€759 for two), a two-day Short Game Focus (€259) and a Ladies Golf School (€659). Check the academy's calendar for dates. Lessons for groups of up to four are also available.
The Golden Triangle: Quinta do Lago and Pinheiros Altos

[Quinta do Lago](/courses/quinta-do-lago-north) is home to the only [Paul McGinley Academy](/golf-academies/quinta-do-lago-golf-academy) in the world, named after the 2014 European Ryder Cup captain, together with a TaylorMade Performance Centre for club fitting. It offers private lessons, golf schools and on-course playing lessons. A playing lesson is worth knowing about if you don't have a handicap: Quinta do Lago normally requires an official handicap certificate, but not when you play with one of its teaching professionals.

Next door, the [Pinheiros Altos Golf Academy](/golf-academies/pinheiros-altos-golf-academy) is run by three British PGA professionals and has three teaching bays and a Titleist fitting centre. Every lesson includes unlimited balls, V1 video analysis and club hire, and visitors can practise on their own for a €25 day fee.
Eastern Algarve: Castro Marim and Monte Rei

[Castro Marim](/golf-academies/castro-marim-golf-academy) has the lowest published lesson prices on this list, with resident professional Peter O'Connor teaching beginners through to low handicappers. Nine-hole playing lessons cost €75 and 18-hole playing lessons €135, plus the green fee. At the other end of the scale, [Monte Rei](/golf-academies/monte-rei-golf-academy) has PGA professionals and a Swing Studio for lessons and club fitting.
Tips for booking golf lessons in the Algarve
**Book before you travel.** Professionals work by appointment and diaries fill up in spring and autumn, the busiest golf seasons.

**Don't bring clubs for your first lessons.** Academies have clubs you can use, and some clinics include them in the price. Once you are hooked, look at [renting clubs for the rest of the trip](/club-rental) rather than paying the airline fee.
**Ask for a playing lesson.** Nine holes with a professional teaches you how to get round a course, keep up the pace and follow the etiquette, which is exactly what a new golfer finds hardest.
**Stay at the resort.** Several academies give hotel guests better rates, such as the 15% discount at Vilamoura.
Find a golf academy near you

Most Algarve courses have some teaching on site. Our [directory of golf academies in the Algarve](/golf-academies) lists every academy we have checked, with prices, programmes and the courses each one serves, and the [map of courses with a golf academy](/?filters=golf_academy) shows them at a glance, so you can pick the one closest to where you are staying. Once you are ready to play, our guide to [the 8 best Algarve golf courses for beginners](/guide/the-10-best-algarve-golf-courses-for-beginners) will tell you where to start.

excerpt: How to book Algarve tee times: with the club online, on booking sites, through agencies or your hotel. When to book, cancellation rules and what you'll need.

content.text: Booking a tee time in the Algarve is easy: **most courses let you book online on their own website**, and many can also be booked on tee-time booking sites such as Golfscape. Others take bookings by phone, email or a request form. This guide explains your options, when to book, and the cancellation rules to check before you pay.

**Quick answer:** for one or two rounds, book on the club's own website or on a booking site, whichever is simpler for you. For several courses in one trip, a booking site or local agency lets you put everything in one place. For a group or a stay-and-play deal, ask your hotel or an agency. Whichever you choose, book as soon as your flights are confirmed, especially in spring and October. **Last checked: November 2026.**
Four ways to book a tee time in the Algarve
1. On the club's own website

Most Algarve clubs sell tee times online through their own booking page, and many use the same booking system, Golfmanager, so the steps look much the same from one club to the next: pick a date, see the times and prices, and pay. The Pestana group has its own booking site for its six Algarve courses, Alto, Pestana Ferragudo, Gramacho, Vale da Pinta, Silves and Vila Sol, with a maximum of 16 players per online booking.

Prices on clubs' own sites change with the date and with demand, so the same course can cost very different amounts from one month to the next. On several of them we could see prices up to a year ahead when we checked in October 2026. Our course pages show the green fees we found month by month.
2. On a tee-time booking site

Several tee-time booking sites sell Algarve rounds, among them [Golfscape](https://golfscape.com/algarve-golf-courses?a_aid=86l0z1nbxwhs6) and Leading Courses, and a course may be listed on more than one. They let you search several courses at once and book them in one place, which is handy when you're comparing courses for a trip; Golfscape, for example, confirms bookings instantly. Prices aren't always the same as the club's own: **some booking sites can be dearer for the same tee time, while others match or beat it**, so compare the club's price with a booking site or two before you pay. We may earn a commission if you book through our Golfscape links.

Not every course is on every booking site. On Golfscape, for example, the [Vilamoura Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course), both [Vale do Lobo](/courses/vale-do-lobo-royal) courses, [Monte Rei](/courses/monte-rei) and [Morgado](/courses/morgado) weren't bookable when we checked, so for those use the club's own website, an agency or another site that lists them.
3. Through a local golf agency

Algarve agencies such as Tee Times Portugal and AlgarveGolf.net book rounds for you, and some put together multi-round packages and group trips. AlgarveGolf.net, for example, books each tee time directly with the course and confirms once the course does, so it isn't always instant. Agencies are most useful for groups, or if you'd rather hand over the whole itinerary.
4. Through your hotel

Many golf hotels book tee times for guests, and some sell their own stay-and-play rates. Hotels with a golf concierge, such as the Conrad Algarve near Quinta do Lago and Domes Lake in Vilamoura, can book your rounds for you, and Domes Lake also arranges transfers and equipment hire. Our [hotels with a golf course on site](/guide/algarve-hotels-with-a-golf-course-on-site) guide covers the resort hotels.
Where you can book each Algarve course online

This table shows how the courses on our map take bookings from visitors. "Online" means you can see times and book on the club's own website. The last column shows whether the course was on Golfscape when we checked; it's one booking site among several, and other sites and agencies may also sell these courses. Booking options can change, so if something doesn't match, check the club's website. San Lorenzo is closed until 2028 and isn't included.

content.note: Checked on each club's website and on Golfscape, October and November 2026. Penina's online booking link wasn't working when we checked, so contact the club.
content.caption: How to book Algarve golf courses

content.text: When to book your tee times

**As early as you can for spring and October.** These are the busiest months in the Algarve, and morning tee times at the best-known courses go first. If your dates are fixed, book when you book your flights.

**Weekend and morning slots fill first.** If you're flexible, a weekday or an afternoon round gives you more choice, and twilight rates are often much cheaper. Vale do Lobo's late-afternoon rates, for example, were €76 to €101 when we checked, against €116 to €171 for a standard round. See [the best value golf in the Algarve](/guide/best-value-golf-in-the-algarve) for more ways to pay less.
**Last-minute rounds are possible** outside the busy months, because the clubs' own booking pages show live availability. In spring and October, don't count on it.
Check the cancellation rules before you pay
Payment and cancellation rules aren't the same everywhere: each club, and each booking site, sets its own, and some are strict. Two examples from clubs that publish theirs:

**Vilamoura Golf:** free cancellation or changes up to 15 days before play in January, February, July, August, November and December, and up to 30 days before in the other months of 2026, rising to 45 days in those busier months in 2027. After that, cancellations, changes and no-shows are charged in full. Non-refundable rates can't be changed at all.

**Monte Rei:** full payment is required to guarantee the booking. Groups of up to four players can cancel or reduce numbers free of charge up to 15 days before play, and groups of 5 to 23 up to 30 days before. Later changes are charged in full.

Both clubs say they don't refund for delayed or cancelled flights, illness or similar reasons, and recommend travel insurance. Rules differ from club to club and from one booking site to another, so read them before you pay.
What you need when you book

**A handicap certificate.** Most Algarve courses ask for one, usually 28 for men and 36 for ladies, and may ask to see it at check-in. See [do you need a handicap to play golf in the Algarve?](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve) for each course's rules.
**A buggy, if you want one.** Book it with your tee time, as some clubs have limited numbers. Our [golf buggy hire guide](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve) covers prices and rules.
**Clubs.** If you're not flying with your own, you can hire a set at the course or have one delivered. Compare options in our [golf club hire comparison](/club-rental).
**Players' names.** You may be asked for each player's name and handicap when you book, so have them ready, especially for groups.
Common questions about Algarve tee times
Is it cheaper to book directly with the club?

Sometimes. Some booking sites can charge more than the club for the same tee time, while others match the club's price or run their own offers. If price matters, check the club's website and a booking site for the same date before you book.
Can I book a tee time for the same day?

Often, yes, outside the busiest months. Most clubs' booking pages show live availability, so you can see what's free and book from your phone. In spring and October, morning times at popular courses are usually gone well before the day.
Do I pay online or at the course?

It depends on the club and on where you book. Monte Rei, for example, requires full payment to guarantee a booking, while at [Vale de Milho](/courses/vale-de-milho) you book online and pay at the clubhouse before your round. The booking page shows which applies.
How do I book for a group?

Pestana's online booking allows up to 16 players. For bigger groups, contact the club or an agency (see our [guide to Algarve golf trips for groups](/guide/algarve-golf-trips-for-groups-and-golf-societies)), and check the group cancellation terms, which can be stricter: Monte Rei, for example, sets a 30-day deadline for groups of 5 to 23.

**Planning a short trip?** Our [golf weekend in the Algarve](/guide/golf-weekend-in-the-algarve) guide suggests two courses and three hotels in each of four bases near Faro Airport, and our [course map](/) shows every course with its green fees.

excerpt: Where to stay to play Quinta do Lago's South, North and Laranjal courses: the resort's own hotels, The Magnolia and Conrad, plus seven well-rated options from budget apartments to five-star luxury, with drive times and golf perks.

content.text: Quinta do Lago has three 18-hole courses inside one estate on the edge of the Ria Formosa Natural Park, near Almancil. The [South Course](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south) has hosted the Portuguese Open eight times, the [North Course](/courses/quinta-do-lago-north) was redesigned in 2014 by Beau Welling with Paul McGinley, and [Laranjal](/courses/quinta-do-lago-laranjal) was built in 2009 on a former orange grove. South and North start from the same clubhouse, while Laranjal has its own clubhouse at the north-east end of the estate.

This guide covers the best hotels near Quinta do Lago golf: the resort's two partner hotels, four places inside the estate itself and three well-rated options a few minutes outside it, from budget apartments to five-star luxury.
Map of hotels near Quinta do Lago golf

The black pins are the three courses (tap one to see course details). South and North share a clubhouse, so their pins sit together. The blue pins are the hotels in this guide; tap one to check prices and availability.
How we chose these hotels

We include a hotel if it is rated at least 8 out of 10 on Booking.com, or at least 7.8 if it offers specific golf services, and is within about 15 minutes of the courses by road. Drive times are calculated by road to the South and North clubhouse, not in a straight line, and we mention the time to Laranjal where it matters. Golf services come from each hotel's own website wherever possible, and we only mention a golf perk if the hotel actually states it.

Prices are the lowest nightly rates we could reliably find in October 2026. Where we could not find a trustworthy figure, we have left the price out rather than guess, so check current rates with the link.
The resort's own hotels
Quinta do Lago lists two hotels as part of the resort: The Magnolia Hotel and Conrad Algarve. Both sell Stay & Play packages that include rounds on the North, South and Laranjal courses.

content.name: The Magnolia Hotel
content.text: A relaxed, design-led hotel on the edge of the estate and the best-value way to stay with the resort itself. As a Quinta do Lago partner, it gives guests **preferential golf rates** and rates at The Campus sports complex, and its golf packages include free transfers to the courses. On the 3-night Golf & Spa package, each guest chooses two rounds or a 90-minute massage. Rooms start from about €118 a night, and Laranjal is about 10 minutes away.
perks: Preferential Quinta do Lago golf rates
Free golf transfers on golf packages
Golf & Spa packages for 3, 5 or 7 nights

content.name: Conrad Algarve
content.text: The resort's five-star partner hotel, rated **9.0 on Booking.com** and renovated over the 2025–26 winter. Its **golf concierge** arranges your rounds, you can take lessons with the hotel's PGA-qualified pro, and Quinta do Lago sells its Signature Golf Experience packages for 3, 5 or 7 nights here. Breakfast runs from 7am, which suits early tee times.
perks: Lessons with a PGA golf pro
Signature Quinta do Lago Golf Experience packages

content.text: Best value near Quinta do Lago
Quinta do Lago is one of the most expensive places to stay in the Algarve, but these two keep the cost down without a long drive.

content.name: WOT Algarve Soul
content.text: Simple apartments and studios on the Almancil side of the estate, rated **8.5 on Booking.com** and from about €54 a night in October, which is very rare for this area. It has no golf services of its own, and guests describe it as basic but clean, with a breakfast that gets good reviews. You will need a car: it is about 11 minutes to the South and North clubhouse and 14 to Laranjal.

content.name: Vilar do Golf
content.text: Apartments right beside the South Course, two minutes from the clubhouse, rated **8.8 on Booking.com** from more than 1,000 reviews. Prices start from about €103 a night in October, low for somewhere this close to the first tee. The resort offers a **golf club rental service**, and every apartment has a kitchen and a terrace, which suits groups of golfers sharing.
Luxury hotels inside the Quinta do Lago estate

content.name: Hotel Quinta do Lago
content.text: The estate's original five-star hotel, on the waterfront overlooking the Ria Formosa lagoon, with 141 rooms and a **9.1 score on Booking.com**. Its Exclusive Golf packages (3, 5 or 7 nights) include rounds on South and Laranjal, breakfast and a **courtesy shuttle to the Quinta do Lago courses and driving range**. Lessons with a PGA professional can be added from €150. The most expensive option here, from about €397 a night in October.
perks: Golf packages with a courtesy shuttle to the courses
Seafront on the Ria Formosa lagoon

content.name: Wyndham Grand Algarve
content.text: Apartment-style suites two minutes from the South and North clubhouse, with some of the best golf services on this list. Guests get **free golf lockers to store their clubs**, the concierge arranges tee times and golf transfers, and the Golf & Stay offer gives up to 30% off the standard rate when you book your green fees through the hotel (minimum three nights, valid September 2026 to April 2027). Breakfast starts at 7am.
perks: Free golf lockers and club washer
Concierge arranges tee times and transfers

content.name: Martinhal Quinta do Lago Family Resort
content.text: Townhouses and villas with private pools, three minutes from the clubhouse. Martinhal does not list golf services, but if you are bringing the family it is the obvious choice: there is a kids' club and childcare, plus a mini-golf course that recreates famous holes from around the world, so everyone gets a round in.
perks: Townhouses and villas with private pools

content.name: Encosta do Lago Resort Club
content.text: Spacious apartments at the western end of the estate, with the Sanctuary Spa and a restaurant on site. The concierge team will **organise your tee times** at Quinta do Lago and the nearby courses. About eight minutes to the South and North clubhouse.
Just outside the estate

content.name: Ria Park Hotel & Spa
content.text: A five-star hotel in Garrão, between Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo, rated **8.9 on Booking.com**. Its golf packages combine 3, 4 or 7 nights at the hotel with a round on the Quinta do Lago courses, and Vale do Lobo is just as close, which makes it a good base for playing both resorts.
perks: Golf packages with a round at Quinta do Lago

content.text: Quinta do Lago green fees and what to know before you play

Quinta do Lago does not publish a public price list; green fees are booked online and change with demand. On the club's online booking, 18 holes run from **about €188 (December to January and July to August) to €264 (March to May and September) on the South Course**, and from about €170 to €242 on North and Laranjal. A buggy is not included in the standard online green fee, and the club does not publish a hire price, so ask when you book. See our [guide to golf buggy hire in the Algarve](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve) for prices and rules across the region. Hotel packages are often the cheaper way to play, so compare them before booking rounds on their own.

You need a handicap certificate, with a maximum of 28 for men and 36 for ladies. Read more in our guide to [whether you need a handicap to play golf in the Algarve](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve). The dress code is strict: collared shirts, tailored trousers or shorts, socks and soft spikes, and no denim or tennis shoes. There are two driving ranges, one at the main clubhouse and one at Laranjal, plus the Paul McGinley Golf Academy and a TaylorMade Performance Centre.
Tips for golfers staying near Quinta do Lago

**South or North first?** The South is the championship course, the North is more forgiving after its redesign. Read [Quinta do Lago South vs North](/guide/quinta-do-lago-south-vs-north-which-course-should-you-play), or compare [Laranjal and Pinheiros Altos](/guide/quinta-do-lago-laranjal-vs-pinheiros-altos-which-course-should-you-play).

**More golf nearby.** [Pinheiros Altos](/courses/pinheiros-altos) is about 11 minutes from the main clubhouse and the [Vale do Lobo](/courses/vale-do-lobo-royal) courses about 12, so you can play four resorts without moving hotel. If you also want to stay near Vale do Lobo, see our [hotels near Vale do Lobo golf](/guide/hotels-near-vale-do-lobo-golf). Note that neighbouring San Lorenzo closes for renovation on 19 October 2026 and is not due to reopen until 2028.
**Close to the airport.** Faro Airport is only about 20 km away by road, so Quinta do Lago works well even for a short golf break.
Frequently asked questions
Which hotel is closest to Quinta do Lago golf?

Vilar do Golf and Wyndham Grand Algarve are both about two minutes from the South and North clubhouse, followed by Martinhal at three and Hotel Quinta do Lago at five. The resort's own hotels, The Magnolia and Conrad Algarve, are both about six minutes away.
Is Quinta do Lago expensive?

Yes, it is one of the most expensive areas in the Algarve, for both hotels and green fees. The cheapest well-rated options are WOT Algarve Soul, from about €54 a night, and Vilar do Golf, from about €103 a night beside the South Course.
Can you play Quinta do Lago without staying at the resort?

Yes. All three courses take visitors, who book tee times online and pay the public green fees. Staying at The Magnolia gets you preferential golf rates, and several hotels sell packages that include rounds.
Playing several courses? Find the best base for your trip

If Quinta do Lago is just one stop on your golf trip, try **Find Your Base** on the [Algarve Golf Map](/). Pick the courses you want to play and it shows you the area that sits closest to all of them, along with well-rated hotels nearby, so you spend less time driving and more time on the course.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Quinta do Lago costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-quinta-do-lago-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: How to plan a beginner golf holiday in Portugal's Algarve: where you can play without a handicap, booking a golf school, the best resorts to stay at, when to go and what to do about clubs.

content.text: A golf holiday is one of the fastest ways to learn the game: a few days of coaching in the sun, practice every afternoon and your first rounds on a real course, without fitting it all round work. For UK golfers, the Algarve in southern Portugal is the obvious place to do it, with short flights into Faro, mild weather for most of the year and around 40 courses spread along the coast.

The catch is that a first golf trip needs a bit more planning than a regular one. Most full-length courses ask for a handicap, lessons need booking, and where you stay makes a big difference. This guide walks you through planning a beginner golf holiday in Portugal, step by step.
Step 1: check where you can play without a handicap

This is the one thing that catches beginners out. Almost every 18-hole course in the Algarve asks for an official handicap certificate, usually with a maximum of 28 for men and 36 for ladies. If you don't have one yet, your playing options are the shorter courses that don't ask for a handicap, such as Penina's nine-hole Resort Course, Pine Cliffs (from the red tees) and Vale de Milho, plus a playing lesson with a professional.

Our guide [Do you need a handicap to play golf in the Algarve?](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve) goes through the rules course by course. It also covers two ways onto the big championship courses without a handicap.
Step 2: build the trip around lessons

For a true beginner, coaching is what turns a frustrating holiday into a great one. Instead of booking odd lessons when you arrive, book a short **beginner golf school** before you travel. You get a structured plan over three to five days and usually a first round on the course with your teacher at the end.

A few examples from the academies' own price lists: the **Pestana Beginners School** costs €162.50 per person for three days of 90-minute sessions (minimum two people), and Penina's five-day **Beginners Golf Clinic** cost €284 per person in a group on its 2024/25 list, with clubs, a trolley and range balls included. Private lessons generally cost around €60 to €80 an hour.
Our guide to [golf lessons in the Algarve](/guide/golf-lessons-in-the-algarve) compares the main academies, their prices and the beginner programmes, area by area.
Step 3: stay at a resort with a beginner-friendly course

The easiest beginner golf holiday is one where you can walk from your room to the driving range, the academy and a short course that doesn't ask for a handicap. That saves you a hire car, makes it easy to fit in an extra hour of practice, and some resorts give guests a lower green fee too. These four tick most of the boxes.
Penina Hotel & Golf Resort, near Portimão

The classic choice. Penina has a full academy, a large natural-grass driving range, and the nine-hole Resort Course, which needs no handicap, next to the Sir Henry Cotton Championship Course you can work towards. The academy's beginner clinic includes a game on the course with the professional.
Pine Cliffs, Albufeira

A clifftop nine-hole course that players without a handicap can play from the red tees, plus a golf academy with PGA instructors, all inside a large beach resort near Albufeira. Resort guests pay less for a round than visitors, and full club sets can be hired for €30 for nine holes, according to the 2025/26 price list.
Balaia Golf Village, Albufeira

A nine-hole, all par-3 course inside the resort, with a driving range where a bucket of 24 balls costs €2. On the 2025/26 rates, resort guests pay €40 a day for golf (visitors €50), and €80 gets you a day's golf with a half set of clubs. The resort's guest information says a handicap is required, without giving a limit, so check with the club before you book if you have never had one.
Amendoeira Golf Resort, Silves

A good fit if you want to take the coaching seriously. The academy has TrackMan, video analysis and putting technology, keeps groups to five students per teacher, and runs schools from half a day to five days. It also has a nine-hole par-3 Academy course, which the resort describes as the only floodlit nine-hole course in Portugal.
For more options, see our list of [Algarve hotels with a golf course on site](/guide/algarve-hotels-with-a-golf-course-on-site).
Step 4: pick a quiet time of year

As a beginner, a quiet course matters more than perfect conditions, because nothing is more stressful than a group waiting behind you on every shot. Spring and autumn are the Algarve's busiest and most expensive golf seasons. For a first trip, aim for **February** or the **late September to mid-November** stretch, when the weather is usually still good, green fees are lower and tee sheets are calmer.

Summer is the cheapest time for golf and the courses are quiet, but you will want to play early in the morning to avoid the heat. Our [month-by-month guide to the Algarve golf season](/guide/algarve-golf-season-best-time-to-play-golf) has the weather, daylight and price details.
Step 5: don't fly with clubs on your first trip

If you don't own clubs yet, don't buy a set for the holiday. Academies can lend you clubs for lessons, some beginner clinics include them, and every resort above hires sets out.
