If you want your own set for the week, you can [rent golf clubs in the Algarve](/club-rental) and pick them up at your hotel or [at Faro Airport](/guide/hiring-golf-clubs-at-faro-airport).

If you do already have a set, check what your airline charges before you decide. Our guides to flying with golf clubs on [Ryanair](/guide/ryanair-golf-clubs-what-it-costs-to-fly-with-your-own-set-to-the-algarve), [easyJet](/guide/golf-clubs-on-easyjet-rules-sizes-and-what-it-actually-costs) and [Jet2](/guide/jet2-golf-clubs-fees-weight-limits-and-why-you-shouldn-t-leave-booking-late) cover the fees.
A sample five-day beginner golf holiday
**Day 1:** arrive at Faro, check in, and hit a bucket of balls on the range to shake off the journey.
**Days 2 to 4:** a beginner school in the mornings, then practice in the afternoons on the range, putting green and chipping area. Most clinics finish with nine holes alongside your teacher.
**Day 5:** your first round on your own, on a short course that doesn't ask for a handicap, at a quiet time of day. Then lunch at the clubhouse to celebrate.

Once you have caught the bug, step up to a forgiving full-length course on your next trip. Our guide to [the 8 best Algarve golf courses for beginners](/guide/the-10-best-algarve-golf-courses-for-beginners) will help you choose.
Plan your trip on the map

Use our [Algarve golf map](/) to see every course, its green fees, handicap rules and facilities, and the hotels nearby. You can show only the [courses with a golf academy](/?filters=golf_academy), or set your handicap in the filters to see where you can play. For the wider planning (flights, car hire and how many rounds to book), read [how to plan a golf trip to the Algarve](/guide/how-to-plan-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve).

excerpt: Senior golf is about age, not skill - so here's what actually matters: flat terrain, buggy access, permissive handicap limits and good value. Ten Algarve courses that get it right, checked against real course data and independent reviews.

content.text: "Senior" golf has nothing to do with skill level — it's about age, the same way senior tees or a Champions Tour card are. If you're an older golfer planning an Algarve trip, what actually matters isn't difficulty, it's comfort: flat or gently rolling terrain, buggies that are easy to get hold of, permissive handicap limits, and good value. We checked terrain, walkability and handicap rules for every active course on our map against real course data and independent golf sources, and these ten stood out from what we could verify. It isn't a complete list: a course missing here may still suit you, as we sometimes lacked enough information to include it.
1. Salgados

Salgados is about as flat as Algarve golf gets. It's routed through wetlands and lagoons near Albufeira, and independent reviewers consistently describe it as flat and easy to walk, with sea views from several holes. You don't need a buggy here, though you can hire one for €50 for 18 holes if you'd rather ride. Green fees start from **€78**.
2. Vilamoura Millennium

Millennium is Vilamoura's most forgiving course — a flat, gentle walk with wide, open fairways, and the lowest official slope rating of the four Vilamoura Golf courses: 130 from the back tees, against 135 to 140 for Laguna, the Old Course and Pinhal. It's a genuinely golfer-friendly layout rather than a watered-down one. Green fees start from **€88**.
3. Vilamoura Laguna

Laguna sits on flat, low-lying ground and is genuinely flatter than any of Vilamoura's other four courses, with few trees and an open, links-like feel. The trade-off is wind exposure on breezier days, so it's worth checking the forecast before you book. Green fees start from **€88**.
4. Quinta da Ria

Quinta da Ria spreads across 660,000 m² of gently sloping, almost flat terrain near Tavira, and is specifically designed to be walkable for golfers of different abilities. It shares its on-site hotel, [Robinson Club Quinta da Ria](/hotels/robinson-quinta-da-ria), with its sister course. Green fees start from **€100**.
5. Amendoeira O'Connor

The O'Connor course at Amendoeira is laid out over noticeably flatter land than its sister course, the Faldo — golf reviewers consistently call it the easier, more playable of the two. It shares the on-site [Amendoeira Golf Resort](/hotels/amendoeira-golf-resort). Green fees start from **€100**.
6. Morgado

Morgado's fairways were deliberately built wide, inspired by Scottish links tradition, which makes it a forgiving round. It isn't a flat walk, though: one independent guide describes rolling terrain that gets hillier on the back nine and recommends a buggy, and you can hire one at the club. The on-site [NAU Morgado Golf & Country Club](/hotels/nau-morgado-golf-country-club) sits right by the clubhouse. Green fees start from **€82**.
7. Vale do Lobo Ocean

The Ocean course at Vale do Lobo has undulating fairways that lead gently down to the Atlantic. It isn't flat, especially on the back nine, and one independent guide considers a buggy essential, so plan to ride. Buggy hire is available at the club. Green fees start from **€116**.
8. Pine Cliffs

Pine Cliffs is directly recommended for senior golfers by independent reviewers — a short nine-hole loop with an easy walk, ideal if you'd rather not spend a whole day on the course. One honest caveat: reviewers with knee or hip issues specifically note that even this easy walk can be too much. The club's price list has manual and electric trolleys but no buggies, so check with the course first if you'd need to ride. The on-site [Pine Cliffs Residence](/hotels/pine-cliffs-residence) is a 5-star Marriott property. Green fees start from **€57**.
9. Balaia

Balaia's nine-hole, all-par-3 layout is described by golf travel guides as particularly suitable for seniors, and a full round is playable in under two hours. It's also the cheapest course on this list, from **€50**. The [Balaia Golf Village Resort](/hotels/balaia-golf-village) sits right on the course.
10. Vale de Milho

Vale de Milho is the shortest course on this list at just 926 metres, ideal for a gentle short-game workout. Worth knowing before you book: it's a walking course with no buggies available, so it suits mobile seniors more than those who'd prefer to ride. Holes range from as little as 70 metres.

**Staying for the winter?** Our guide to [long-stay golf in the Algarve](/guide/long-stay-golf-in-the-algarve) compares short-term memberships, round packages and golf societies, and explains how long EU and UK visitors can stay.

excerpt: Where to stay to play Penina's Resort and Championship courses: the resort hotel with its free daily round, a top-rated B&B overlooking the course, and four Alvor hotels within 20 minutes.

content.text: Penina Hotel & Golf Resort, between Portimão and Alvor, is where Algarve golf began: Sir Henry Cotton's [Championship Course](/courses/penina-championship) opened here in 1966. Alongside it sits the [Penina Resort Course](/courses/penina-resort), a nine-hole layout of almost 3,000 metres from the white tees that you can play once or twice round for a full 18, and a relaxed option for families, beginners or a warm-up round.

This guide covers where to stay to play Penina. We have kept the list deliberately short and close to the course: the resort hotel itself, a small B&B a few minutes away overlooking the fairways, and four well-rated hotels in Alvor, the nearest town, around 15 to 20 minutes by car.
Map of hotels near Penina Golf Resort
The black pin is Penina (tap it to see the Resort Course details). The blue pins are the hotels in this guide; tap one to check prices and availability.
How we chose these hotels

Every hotel here is rated at least 8 out of 10 by guests on Booking.com and is within about 20 minutes of Penina by road. Drive times are calculated by road to the resort, not in a straight line. Breakfast hours and golf services come from each hotel's own website wherever possible, and we only mention a golf perk if the hotel actually states it.

Prices are the lowest average nightly rates we found in October 2026, usually for the quietest winter months. Spring and autumn, peak golf season, cost more, so treat them as a guide rather than a quote.
Staying at Penina itself

content.name: Penina Hotel & Golf Resort
content.text: The obvious choice if golf is the main reason for your trip. The hotel sits on the Championship Course and the Resort Course is just across the road. Penina's **"Best Available Rate for Golfers" includes breakfast and a complimentary round every day** on one of the resort's courses, for up to two golfers per room and subject to availability (a handicap certificate is needed for the Championship Course: 28 for men, 36 for ladies). There are also three- and seven-night golf packages, a driving range and practice area with PGA professionals, several restaurants including the Sir Henry Cotton Club golf bar, and breakfast from 7am.
perks: Free daily round on the golfer rate
content.distanceLabel: On the resort, Resort Course across the road

content.text: A boutique B&B overlooking the course

content.name: Casa Penina Guesthouse
content.text: A tiny guesthouse with just four suites and a **9.7 rating on Booking.com**, the highest on this list. Its pool overlooks the Penina golf course and breakfast is served facing the fairways. Rates start at about €53 a night in the quieter months (minimum two nights, breakfast €12 per person extra), making it the best-value base for Penina by some distance. It is not suitable for children under 14, and the pool is open from April to October.
Hotels in Alvor, 15 to 20 minutes from Penina
Alvor is the nearest town to Penina: a pretty fishing village with a long beach, restaurants and bars. Staying here means a short drive to the course each morning, but much more to do in the evening.

content.name: RR Alvor Baía Resort
content.text: A large, family-friendly resort of suites with kitchenettes, with a spa, gym and heated hydrotherapy pool. For golfers the useful detail is breakfast: it starts at 7am, and the hotel offers **a breakfast pack for early-morning departures** if you ask at reception the day before, ideal for a first tee time at Penina.

content.name: Pestana Alvor Praia
content.text: A five-star hotel on the clifftop above Praia dos Três Irmãos, which can cost under €90 a night in winter. There is a heated indoor pool, sauna and Turkish bath for after your round, plus a seasonal kids' club. It does not offer specific golf services, but Penina is about 18 minutes away by car.
perks: Heated indoor pool, sauna and Turkish bath

content.text: All-inclusive resorts in Alvor

content.name: Pestana Blue Alvor Beach
content.text: A five-star all-inclusive by Três Irmãos beach, so the price covers meals and drinks. It suits golfers travelling with family: there is a kids' club for 4 to 12-year-olds, a 24-hour gym and a padel court. The hotel does not offer golf services, so book your Penina tee times directly with the resort.

content.name: Tivoli Alvor Algarve – All Inclusive Resort
content.text: A five-star all-inclusive resort with a spa (indoor heated pool, sauna, jacuzzi and Turkish bath) and a complimentary shuttle into Alvor and down to the beach. UK golf tour operators sell golf packages here, typically with rounds at nearby courses such as [Alamos](/courses/alamos), [Salgados](/courses/salgados) and [Morgado](/courses/morgado), and Penina is about 16 minutes away.
perks: Shuttle to Alvor town and beach

content.text: Penina Resort Course green fees and practice facilities

The Resort Course is open to visitors as well as hotel guests. On Penina's most recent published price list (2024/25), visitors paid around **€32 to €34 for nine holes and €53 to €57 for 18**, with small discounts for booking online, and hotel guests paid less. A buggy was €35 for nine holes and €55 for 18, and a full set of hire clubs €25. Penina has not published a newer list, so check current prices when you book.

Both courses share Penina's practice facilities: a natural-grass driving range, putting and chipping greens, a practice bunker and lessons with PGA professionals. Penina's Resort Course page says no handicap is required, though its price lists mention handicap certificates, so confirm when booking. The Championship Course does require one (28 for men, 36 for ladies).
Tips for golfers staying near Penina

**Stay on the resort if golf comes first.** With a free round every day on the golfer rate, Penina Hotel quickly pays for itself if you play daily. If you stay elsewhere, book your tee times directly with Penina.

**Plenty of golf within 20 minutes.** [Alto Golf](/courses/alto-golf) is around 13 minutes away, [Palmares](/courses/palmares) about 16, and [Morgado](/courses/morgado) about 18, so a base near Penina covers most of the western Algarve. Can't decide between Penina's two courses? Read [Penina Championship vs Penina Resort](/guide/penina-championship-vs-penina-resort-which-course-should-you-play).

**Check winter openings.** Some Alvor hotels close for part of the winter. Pestana Dom João II, for example, is closed for renovation until 1 May 2027. Faro Airport is about 70 km away, roughly 45 minutes to an hour by car.
Frequently asked questions
Which hotel is closest to Penina Golf Resort?

Penina Hotel & Golf Resort itself, which sits on the Championship Course with the Resort Course across the road. The closest alternative is Casa Penina Guesthouse, about 4 minutes away by car, whose pool overlooks the golf course.
Can you play the Penina Resort Course without staying at the hotel?
Yes. Penina sells green fees to visitors, and you can book online through the resort's website. Hotel guests pay lower rates.
What is the cheapest place to stay near Penina?
Casa Penina Guesthouse, with rooms from about €53 a night in the quieter months. In Alvor, RR Alvor Baía Resort starts at about €85.
Playing several courses? Find the best base for your trip

If Penina is just one stop on your golf trip, try **Find Your Base** on the [Algarve Golf Map](/). Pick the courses you want to play and it shows you the area that sits closest to all of them, along with well-rated hotels nearby, so you spend less time driving and more time on the course.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Lagos and Portimão costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-lagos-and-portimao-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

**Prefer all-inclusive?** Tivoli Alvor and Pestana Blue Alvor Beach both feature in our guide to [all-inclusive golf hotels in the Algarve](/guide/all-inclusive-golf-hotels-in-the-algarve), which explains what all-inclusive covers for golfers.

excerpt: Where to stay to play Vale do Lobo's Royal and Ocean courses: the resort's own villas and the Dona Filipa Hotel, plus six well-rated hotels within 15 minutes, with drive times, breakfast hours and golf perks.

content.text: Vale do Lobo is one of the most famous golf resorts in Europe, with two 18-hole courses side by side on the coast near Almancil. The [Royal Course](/courses/vale-do-lobo-royal) is home to the clifftop par-3 16th, one of the most photographed holes in Europe, while the [Ocean Course](/courses/vale-do-lobo-ocean) grew out of Sir Henry Cotton's original layouts from 1968 and 1972. Both start from the same Golf Club.

This guide covers the best places to stay near Vale do Lobo golf: two options inside the resort itself and six well-rated hotels within about 15 minutes, in neighbouring Quinta do Lago, Garrão and Quarteira.
Map of hotels near Vale do Lobo golf
The black pins are the Royal and Ocean courses, which share the Golf Club (tap one to see course details). The blue pins are the hotels in this guide; tap one to check prices and availability.
How we chose these hotels

We include a hotel if it is rated at least 8 out of 10 on Booking.com, or at least 7.8 if it offers specific golf services, and is within about 15 minutes of the Golf Club by road. Drive times are calculated by road, not in a straight line. Breakfast hours and golf services come from each hotel's own website wherever possible, and we only mention a golf perk if the hotel actually states it.

Prices are the lowest nightly rates we could reliably find in October 2026. Where we could not find a trustworthy figure, we have left the price out rather than guess, so check current rates with the link.
Staying inside Vale do Lobo

content.name: Vale do Lobo Resort
content.text: Villas, apartments and townhouses rented by the resort itself, so you are never more than a short ride from the first tee. Guests receive the **Vale do Lobo Guest Card, which gives a discount on green fees**, offers on golf equipment rental, a free resort shuttle and 10% off treatments at the Royal Spa. The resort's Play & Stay packages start from €450 for three nights with two golf days. Stays are self-catering, with plenty of restaurants within the resort.
perks: Green-fee discount with the Guest Card
content.distanceLabel: Inside the resort, around the Golf Club

content.name: Dona Filipa Hotel
content.text: The classic hotel within Vale do Lobo, a short walk from the beach and about two minutes from the Golf Club. The hotel highlights easy access to Vale do Lobo, Quinta do Lago, Vilamoura and Ombria, with a **complimentary golf shuttle service**. Its own shuttle to San Lorenzo will matter less for a while, as that course is closed for renovation from 19 October 2026 until mid-2028. Guest scores sit just under 8 out of 10, but for location it is hard to beat.
Best value near Vale do Lobo

content.name: Dom José Beach Hotel
content.text: A three-star beach hotel in Quarteira that scores an impressive **8.9 on Booking.com** and starts at around €70 a night in January. It has no golf services of its own, but breakfast starts at 7.30am and Vale do Lobo is about 14 minutes away by car. The best budget base for the area.
Mid-range hotels near Vale do Lobo

content.name: The Magnolia Hotel
content.text: A stylish golf-focused hotel in Quinta do Lago, six minutes from Vale do Lobo. Its Stay & Play packages include rounds on the Quinta do Lago courses, guests get preferential rates there, and a scheduled shuttle runs to the North, South and Laranjal courses. With breakfast from 7am, it is a great base for combining Vale do Lobo with Quinta do Lago.
perks: Preferential rates at Quinta do Lago courses
Shuttle to Quinta do Lago courses

content.name: Dunas Douradas Beach Club
content.text: Apartments and villas at Garrão, right next to Vale do Lobo, rated a superb **9.3 on Booking.com**. The resort describes itself as "surrounded by the world-famous golf resorts of Vale do Lobo". There are two outdoor pools and an indoor pool, a kids' club, a restaurant serving breakfast from 8am, and airport transfers from €45 per trip for up to four people.
Luxury hotels near Vale do Lobo

content.name: Conrad Algarve
content.text: A five-star hotel in Quinta do Lago, nine minutes from Vale do Lobo, renovated over the 2025–26 winter. Its **golf concierge** arranges your rounds, you can take lessons with the hotel's PGA-qualified pro, and the hotel even has a seasonal beach concession at Vale do Lobo. Breakfast runs from 7am to 11am.
perks: Lessons with a PGA golf pro
Beach concession at Vale do Lobo

content.name: Wyndham Grand Algarve
content.text: Apartment-style suites in Quinta do Lago with some of the best golf services on this list. Guests get **free golf lockers to store their clubs**, the concierge arranges tee times and golf transfers, and the Golf & Stay offer gives up to 30% off the standard rate when you book your green fees through the hotel (minimum three nights, valid September 2026 to April 2027). Breakfast starts at 7am.
perks: Free golf lockers and club washer
Concierge arranges tee times and transfers

content.name: Encosta do Lago Resort Club
content.text: Spacious apartments next to the Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo courses, with the Sanctuary Spa and a restaurant on site. The concierge team will **organise your tee times**, and the resort lists both Vale do Lobo courses among its nearby options.
Vale do Lobo green fees and what to know before you play

Both courses share the same green fees. On the official 2025–26 price list, **18 holes cost from €143 (mid-November to February) up to €204 (early October)**, and nine-hole, twilight and sunset rounds from €93 to €122. Juniors up to 18 pay €72 for 18 holes. Resort guests with the Vale do Lobo Guest Card get a discount on public rates. The price list runs until 31 October 2026, so check the new season's prices before you book.

The maximum handicap is 28 for men and 36 for ladies, and the club may ask to see a certificate. Collared or polo-neck shirts, tailored trousers or shorts with belt loops, socks and proper golf shoes are required. The Golf Club has a netted practice area, a short-game area with bunkers, a putting green and a golf academy, and Spikes Restaurant serves food from early in the day. Tee times can be booked online or by phone.
Tips for golfers staying near Vale do Lobo

**Play both courses.** The Royal and Ocean are very different, so most visitors play both. Not sure which to choose? Read [Vale do Lobo Royal vs Ocean](/guide/vale-do-lobo-royal-vs-vale-do-lobo-ocean-which-course-should-you-play).

**More golf nearby.** [Pinheiros Altos](/courses/pinheiros-altos) is about 13 minutes away, [Quinta do Lago South](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south) about 15 and the [Vilamoura Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course) about 20. Note that San Lorenzo is closed for renovation from 19 October 2026, with reopening scheduled for mid-2028.
**Close to the airport.** Faro Airport is only about 23 km away by road, which makes Vale do Lobo one of the easiest golf resorts to reach for a short break.
Frequently asked questions
Which hotel is closest to Vale do Lobo golf?

The villas and apartments of Vale do Lobo Resort itself, around the Golf Club, followed by the Dona Filipa Hotel, about two minutes away. Outside the resort, Dunas Douradas Beach Club is about seven minutes away and The Magnolia Hotel about six.
Can you play Vale do Lobo without staying at the resort?
Yes. Vale do Lobo Golf Club welcomes members, resort guests and visitors. Visitors pay the public green fees, while resort guests get a discount with the Guest Card.
What is the cheapest place to stay near Vale do Lobo?
Dom José Beach Hotel in Quarteira, from about €70 a night in January and rated 8.9 by guests, is the best value option within 15 minutes of the course.
Playing several courses? Find the best base for your trip

If Vale do Lobo is just one stop on your golf trip, try **Find Your Base** on the [Algarve Golf Map](/). Pick the courses you want to play and it shows you the area that sits closest to all of them, along with well-rated hotels nearby, so you spend less time driving and more time on the course.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Vale do Lobo costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-vale-do-lobo-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: Smartwings charges about €90 per flight for a golf bag up to 32kg on its Warsaw–Faro route, and package holidaymakers book it through their tour operator. Here's how it works.

content.text: Smartwings, the Czech airline, flies to Faro from Warsaw, often on behalf of Polish tour operators. If you're bringing golf clubs, this is one of the more expensive airlines in the series: the official price list puts a golf bag at **€90 per flight**.
How Smartwings handles golf bags

Golf equipment is booked as **sports equipment**, one piece per flight, separately from your checked baggage. If your flight is part of a **package holiday**, Smartwings says you should buy sports equipment carriage through your **tour operator**, using their price list rather than the airline's. So if you booked through a travel company, ask them first, as their price may be different.
Weight limit
A golf bag can weigh up to **32kg**, so there's room for a hard case, clubs, shoes and balls without worrying about the scales.
What it costs

Smartwings' current fees page lists golf equipment up to 32kg at **€90 per piece per flight**, so €180 for a return trip. An older Smartwings document showed a lower price, so if you see a cheaper figure online it's probably out of date. Check the current price when you book.
How to add golf clubs to your booking

Book the golf bag in advance. Third-party guides say Smartwings expects sports equipment to be declared at least 48 hours before departure. For flight-only bookings, use Smartwings' website or customer service; for packages, go through your tour operator.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

At €180 return, flying your own clubs on Smartwings costs more than a week's hire of a good set. Renting at the airport is the obvious alternative. ClubsToHire has a desk in the **Faro Airport arrivals hall**, and MyCaddyMaster has a counter in departures. Both can deliver to resorts if your transfer is waiting.
See our [club hire directory](/shops) for shops near your hotel.
Bottom line
Smartwings' golf fee is high at €90 per flight. If you're on a package, check whether your tour operator charges less. Otherwise, renting in Faro will often work out cheaper.

excerpt: San Lorenzo closed for a major renovation on 19 October 2026 and is not due to reopen until mid-2028. Here are the closest alternatives, from Quinta do Lago South next door to the Vilamoura courses San Lorenzo itself recommends.

content.text: If San Lorenzo was on your Algarve list, you will need a plan B. The course on the edge of the Ria Formosa lagoon, one of the most celebrated in the Algarve, **closed on 19 October 2026 for extensive renovations and is scheduled to reopen in mid-2028**. Here is what we know about the closure and the best courses to play instead, all within half an hour of the Quinta do Lago estate.
Is San Lorenzo golf course closed?

Yes. Hotel Quinta do Lago, on the same estate, states that San Lorenzo "will be closed from 19.10.2026 for extensive renovations and is scheduled to reopen in mid-2028". Some golf booking sites give spring 2028 instead, so treat any reopening date as provisional until the club confirms it. At the time of writing, no details have been published about the architect or exactly what the renovation will change.

Before the closure, the course had been running from temporary facilities after a fire destroyed its clubhouse. San Lorenzo was designed by Joseph Lee and Rocky Roquemore and opened in 1988, with holes running right along the lagoon. The course's own website now invites golfers to book one of the four Vilamoura Golf courses instead.
Quinta do Lago South: the closest match

If you wanted San Lorenzo for its setting, [Quinta do Lago South](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south) is the obvious replacement. It is about **five minutes away by car**, on the same estate, and it also borders the Ria Formosa Natural Park. Designed by William Mitchell and opened in 1974, it has hosted the Portuguese Open several times and was named Portugal's Best Golf Course at the 2024 World Golf Awards.

It is not cheap: green fees on the club's own online booking run from about **€188 to €264**, depending on the season ([see current South green fees](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south/green-fees)). You need a handicap certificate, with a maximum of 28 for men and 36 for ladies.
Quinta do Lago North and Pinheiros Altos: next door

[Quinta do Lago North](/courses/quinta-do-lago-north) shares South's clubhouse and is also about five minutes from San Lorenzo, with green fees from about €170. If you can only play one of the two, our [Quinta do Lago South vs North comparison](/guide/quinta-do-lago-south-vs-north-which-course-should-you-play) explains how they differ.

[Pinheiros Altos](/courses/pinheiros-altos) is San Lorenzo's direct neighbour, around seven minutes by road, and is usually the cheapest round in this corner of the Golden Triangle ([current green fees](/courses/pinheiros-altos/green-fees)). It has 27 holes, played as three nines. Recent player reviews flag patchy conditioning, so read a few before you book.
Vale do Lobo: sea views instead of the lagoon

About 15 minutes west, [Vale do Lobo](/vale-do-lobo/golf-courses) has two courses. The [Royal](/courses/vale-do-lobo-royal) is known for its clifftop holes above the beach, and the [Ocean](/courses/vale-do-lobo-ocean) is classic coastal parkland. You swap San Lorenzo's lagoon for the Atlantic. Our [Royal vs Ocean comparison](/guide/vale-do-lobo-royal-vs-vale-do-lobo-ocean-which-course-should-you-play) will help you choose.
The Vilamoura courses: where San Lorenzo sends its golfers

San Lorenzo's own website points golfers towards the four Vilamoura Golf courses, around 30 minutes away by car. The headline act is the [Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course), Frank Pennink's 1969 pine-lined classic, which won Portugal's Best Golf Course at the 2025 World Golf Awards. Expect green fees from about €215.

For less, [Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium) and [Laguna](/courses/vilamoura-laguna) start at around €88 and [Pinhal](/courses/vilamoura-pinhal) at about €101. Our [Vilamoura golf courses page](/vilamoura/golf-courses) compares all of them side by side.
Where to stay near Quinta do Lago

Staying on the estate puts South, North and Pinheiros Altos within a few minutes' drive. The five-star [Hotel Quinta do Lago](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/quintadolago.html) sits beside the lagoon and scores 9.1 on Booking.com. For more options at different prices, see our guide to [hotels near Quinta do Lago golf](/guide/hotels-near-quinta-do-lago-golf).

Quinta do Lago is only about 22 km from Faro Airport by road, so a [pre-booked airport transfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA) is a simple way to arrive with your clubs if you don't plan to hire a car.
Want to compare more options in the area? Our [Almancil and Golden Triangle golf courses page](/almancil/golf-courses) lists every course nearby with green fees, handicap rules and hotels.

excerpt: airBaltic charges €49.99 each way for golf equipment on its Riga–Faro route, but you can only book it by phone, at a ticket office or through a travel agent. Here are the rules.

content.text: airBaltic flies from Riga to Faro, linking the Baltic states, and connecting passengers from across northern Europe, with the Algarve. Its golf fee is fairly typical, but booking it isn't: airBaltic **doesn't sell golf equipment online**.
How to book a golf bag with airBaltic

airBaltic says golf equipment can **only be bought through its call centre, a ticket office or a travel agency**, not on its website or app. Online offers and discounts don't apply either. As there's a limit on how many sets of sports equipment each flight can carry, call to add it as soon as you've booked.
What it costs

airBaltic's own sports equipment page lists golf at **€49.99 per set each way**, on all Economy fares (Mini, Basic, Classic and Flex). That's about €100 return. The fee is non-refundable, so be sure before you pay. **Business class** passengers and **airBaltic Club VIP** members can bring one set of sports equipment free of charge.
Weight limit and the heavy-bag charge

Each set can weigh up to **23kg**. Over that, airBaltic charges a flat **€60 heavy-baggage fee** at the airport, up to an absolute maximum of 32kg. A tour bag in a hard case can easily go over 23kg, so weigh it beforehand and move shoes or balls into your suitcase if needed.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

Having to phone to add your golf bag, plus a €60 surprise if it's heavy, are good reasons to consider renting. Two companies are based inside **Faro Airport**: ClubsToHire hands sets over in the arrivals hall, and MyCaddyMaster runs a desk in departures.
For more options, see our [Algarve golf club rental directory](/shops).
Bottom line

airBaltic's €49.99 each way is a fair price, but you have to phone or go through a travel agent to book it, and keep the bag under 23kg to avoid an extra €60. If that feels like too much organising, hire a set in Faro instead.

excerpt: West or east of the Golden Triangle? Courses, green fees, drive times from Faro and golf resorts compared, so you can pick the right side of the Algarve.

content.text: Most golfers flying into Faro head for the middle of the Algarve: the Golden Triangle around [Quinta do Lago](/golf-resorts/quinta-do-lago) and [Vale do Lobo](/golf-resorts/vale-do-lobo), plus Vilamoura. That central stretch holds 22 of the region's 38 courses, and 12 of them start from €100 or more. On either side of it, the **western and eastern Algarve** offer two quite different golf holidays, and this guide compares them on the things that decide a trip: the courses, the green fees, the drive from the airport and where to stay.
West vs East Algarve at a glance

**Courses:** the west has 10 courses, nine full-length layouts plus Penina's 9-hole Resort Course, spread between Ferragudo and Vila do Bispo. The east has six full-length courses, all around Tavira and Castro Marim.
**Green fees:** five of the nine western full-length courses start below €80 for visitors. In the east, five of the six start at €100 or less, with Monte Rei the exception from €190.

**From Faro Airport:** the east is the closer side. Monte Rei quotes about 40 minutes by car and the other eastern courses are a similar drive. In the west, Penina quotes about 45 minutes, the Lagos courses are nearer an hour and Santo António, out towards Sagres, is the furthest of all.
**Golf resorts:** both sides have hotels built on a golf estate, four in the west and three in the east, covered further down.
Golf in the western Algarve: more courses, lower green fees

Around Portimão sits the most history. [Penina Championship](/courses/penina-championship), designed by Sir Henry Cotton in 1966, was the first golf course built in the Algarve and starts from €77, while its 9-hole [Penina Resort](/courses/penina-resort) course costs from €28. In the hills behind, [Morgado](/courses/morgado) and [Alamos](/courses/alamos) sit side by side and start from €82 each (we compare them in [Alamos vs Morgado](/guide/alamos-vs-morgado-which-portimao-golf-course-should-you-play)). [Alto Golf](/courses/alto-golf), Sir Henry Cotton's 1991 design in Alvor, is the cheapest 18-hole round in the area from €75, and the brand-new [Pestana Ferragudo](/courses/pestana-ferragudo) opened in 2026 from €130.

Further west, around Lagos, the views take over. [Palmares](/courses/palmares) spreads 27 holes of clifftop and lakeside golf above Meia Praia beach, redesigned by Robert Trent Jones Jr., from €138. [Boavista](/courses/boavista) climbs the hillside above Lagos with sea views from €74, and [Espiche](/courses/espiche), opened in 2012, starts from €65 (see [Boavista vs Espiche](/guide/boavista-vs-espiche-which-lagos-golf-course-should-you-play)). Out on its own near Vila do Bispo, Pepe Gancedo's [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio) is the most remote course in the region, from €57.
Golf in the eastern Algarve: Monte Rei and a compact cluster

The east is smaller but has the headline act. [Monte Rei](/courses/monte-rei), Jack Nicklaus's 2007 design near Vila Nova de Cacela, was ranked Portugal's number one course for 15 years in a row and remains a fixture in European top-10 lists. It is also the most expensive round on either side, from €190.

The rest of the east is far kinder on the wallet. [Quinta da Ria](/courses/quinta-da-ria) and [Quinta de Cima](/courses/quinta-de-cima) give you 36 holes by Rocky Roquemore on one estate beside the Ria Formosa natural park, both from €100 (compared in [Quinta da Ria vs Quinta de Cima](/guide/quinta-da-ria-vs-quinta-de-cima-which-tavira-course-should-you-play)). [Benamor](/courses/benamor), near Tavira, starts from €66. Close to the Spanish border, [Castro Marim](/courses/castro-marim) starts from €87 and Seve Ballesteros's [Quinta do Vale](/courses/quinta-do-vale) from €67 (see [Castro Marim vs Quinta do Vale](/guide/castro-marim-vs-quinta-do-vale-which-east-algarve-course-should-you-play)).
Handicap limits around the Algarve

Most courses on both sides use the standard Algarve limit of **28 for men and 36 for ladies**. In the west, Boavista is slightly stricter at 26 and 34, while Alto Golf accepts up to 36 for men and ladies. In the east, Quinta da Ria and Quinta de Cima also allow 36 for both, Monte Rei, Benamor and Quinta do Vale use 28 and 36, and Castro Marim asks for a handicap certificate without publishing a maximum.

If you play off a high handicap, check the limit before you book, or read [do you need a handicap to play golf in the Algarve](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve) for the full rules and the courses that don't ask for one.
Where to stay on each side

**In the west**, [Penina Hotel & Golf Resort](/golf-resorts/penina) is a five-star hotel built around its two courses, from about €200 a night. [NAU Morgado Golf & Country Club](/golf-resorts/nau-morgado) sits between Morgado and Alamos, [Palmares Beach House](/golf-resorts/palmares) is a boutique five-star overlooking the Palmares course and Meia Praia, and [Boavista Golf & Spa Resort](/golf-resorts/boavista-golf-spa-resort) has townhouses and apartments beside its course. For hotels off the estates, see [hotels near Penina](/guide/hotels-near-penina-golf-resort) and [hotels near Morgado and Alamos](/guide/hotels-near-morgado-and-alamos-golf).

**In the east**, [Monte Rei](/golf-resorts/monte-rei) offers villas and apartments on its private estate, from about €390 a night. [Robinson Club Quinta da Ria](/golf-resorts/robinson-quinta-da-ria) is an all-inclusive resort between its two courses, and [Castro Marim](/golf-resorts/castro-marim-golf-resort) has village houses beside its course, from about €95 a night. More options are in [hotels near Monte Rei](/guide/hotels-near-monte-rei-golf).
So which side should you choose?

**Choose the west** if you want the most courses within reach of one base, lower green fees for most rounds, the history of Penina or the sea views at Palmares and Boavista. It suits longer trips, where playing somewhere different each day matters.
**Choose the east** if you want a shorter transfer from Faro, a round at Monte Rei, 36 holes from a single base at Quinta da Ria, or an all-inclusive stay at the Robinson Club.

The two ends of the region are well over an hour apart by car, so most golfers pick one side rather than splitting the week. If you would rather have everything within half an hour, compare the central [golf resorts](/golf-resorts) or browse every course on the [Algarve golf map](/). Green fees above are the lowest published visitor rates for the 2026/27 season; each course's page has the full price list by month.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to the Algarve costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: Seven minutes apart near Vilamoura: the 1969 Old Course, named Portugal's best in 2025, against Pestana's 27-hole Vila Sol at a noticeably lower green fee. Here's how they compare.

content.text: If you are staying in Vilamoura and want one standout round, the choice often comes down to the **Old Course** and **Vila Sol**. They are only about seven minutes apart by car, both are long-established courses that have hosted the Portuguese Open, and both ask for a handicap of 28 for men and 36 for ladies. The big differences are price, layout and where you sleep.
The Old Course: Vilamoura's 1969 classic

The [Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course) was designed by Frank Pennink and opened in 1969, which makes it one of the oldest courses in the Algarve. It plays through mature umbrella pines at **par 73 and 6,254 metres** from the white tees (5,913 m from the yellows). In 2025 it was named **Portugal's Best Golf Course** at the World Golf Awards.

Today it is part of Vilamoura Golf, alongside Pinhal, Laguna and Millennium. Its clubhouse reopened in December 2024 after a refurbishment. You need a valid handicap certificate (maximum 28 for men and 36 for ladies), and only the club's own buggies are allowed. Green fees on the club's online booking run from about **€215 to €301** ([current Old Course green fees](/courses/vilamoura-old-course/green-fees)).
Vila Sol: 27 holes and a hotel on the course

[Vila Sol](/courses/vila-sol) was designed by Donald Steel and opened in 1991. It hosted the Portuguese Open in 1992 and 1993. It has **27 holes in three nines, Prime, Challenge and Prestige**, each par 36, so any 18-hole round is par 72. From the white tees the combinations measure **6,274 to 6,393 metres**, with slope ratings of 135 to 137 from the white tees on the Portuguese Golf Federation's current table. That makes it a proper test, not an easy alternative.

Pestana runs the course and the five-star [Pestana Vila Sol Golf - Vilamoura](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/pestana-vila-sol-golf-and-conference.html) hotel right next to it, which scores 8.3 on Booking.com. The official 2026 rates are **€140** in December, January and June to August, €195 in most spring and autumn months and €215 at peak. A twilight round costs €60 ([current Vila Sol green fees](/courses/vila-sol/green-fees)). The handicap limit on the official scorecard is 28 for men and 36 for ladies.
Price: the clearest difference

In every season the Old Course costs more than Vila Sol, often by €80 or more for a single round. You are paying for the history, the setting and the 2025 award. If you plan to play several rounds, Vila Sol's twilight rate and its three nines make it the better value option.
Which one should you play?

**Play the Old Course** if this is your one big round in Vilamoura and you want a classic: a 1969 parkland course under the pines, with five decades of reputation behind it. **Play Vila Sol** if you would rather keep the budget for a second round, want a hotel on the course, or are staying several days and fancy trying different nine-hole combinations. Since they are so close, plenty of golfers play both.
Where to stay

The Pestana Vila Sol hotel is the only one of the two with a hotel on the course. The Old Course has no hotel of its own, but the hotels around Vilamoura marina are around 10 minutes away by car. See our guide to [golf hotels near Vilamoura](/guide/golf-hotels-near-vilamoura) for options at every price.
Both courses are around 25 to 30 km from Faro Airport by road, and a [pre-booked transfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA) gets you there with your clubs without hiring a car.

Want the numbers side by side? [Open the course comparator](/?compare=vila-sol,vilamoura-old-course) to compare price, handicap limits and facilities, or see every course in the area on our [Vilamoura golf courses page](/vilamoura/golf-courses).

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Vilamoura costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-vilamoura-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: Lagos' two best-known courses could hardly be more different: Palmares' 27 holes above Meia Praia beach against Boavista's hillside round for around half the green fee. Here's how they compare.

content.text: If you are basing yourself in Lagos, the first golf decision is usually **Palmares or Boavista**. They are about 18 minutes apart by car. Palmares is the showpiece, with 27 holes running down towards the beach. Boavista is the hillside course on the edge of town, at a much lower green fee. Here is how they compare.
Palmares: 27 holes above Meia Praia
[Palmares](/courses/palmares) opened as an 18-hole course in 1975. Robert Trent Jones Jr. redesigned it in 2011, creating today's 27 holes in three nines:

**Alvor** (parkland on the hillside with tree-lined fairways), **Lagos** (parkland and lakes leading into the dunes) and **Praia** (links golf by the sea). The club says 90% of its tee boxes have ocean views. In October 2026 Jones's firm announced it was finishing improvements across all three nines, including wider fairways, more short grass around the greens, renovated bunkers and a new short-game area.

Green fees on the club's own online booking start at **€138**, are around €159 in late autumn and reach €183 in spring and early autumn ([current Palmares green fees](/courses/palmares/green-fees)). In winter the club also sells an 18-hole rate with a shared buggy included, which was €105 when we checked. Palmares doesn't publish a handicap limit on its website, so bring your certificate and check when you book.
Boavista: hillside golf on the edge of Lagos

[Boavista](/courses/boavista) was designed by Howard Swan and opened in 2002, about nine minutes from Lagos town centre. It looks out over the Bay of Lagos to the east and the Monchique hills to the north. The 6th and 8th holes play over a ravine, and the 9th tee is the highest point on the course. The back nine drops down to streams, lakes and bridges.

It is **par 71**, measuring 6,167 metres from the back tees and 5,747 m from the whites. Its slope ratings (135 from the white tees) make it one of the tougher tests around Lagos. Boavista has the strictest handicap rule of the two: its own rules allow a maximum of **26 for men and 34 for ladies**. When we checked in November 2026 the driving range was temporarily closed for repairs.

Boavista is much cheaper. Its online rate starts at about **€74** in low season, and its published rates for November 2026 to December 2027 run from €86 to €126 ([current Boavista green fees](/courses/boavista/green-fees)).
Which one should you play?

**Choose Palmares** for the setting: sea views from almost every tee, a links-style nine by the beach and the newly improved course. It is one of the most memorable rounds in the western Algarve, and the price reflects that. **Choose Boavista** if you want a demanding round with views at around half the price, or if you are staying in Lagos and want the course closest to town. Higher handicappers should note Boavista's limit of 26 for men before booking.
Where to stay

Both courses have accommodation on site. At Palmares, the [Palmares Beach House Hotel](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/onyria-palmares-beach-house-hostel.html) is a small five-star boutique hotel that scores 8.9 on Booking.com, and the resort also has apartments next to the 10th hole. Boavista is a five-star resort village of villas, listed on Booking.com as [Bela Colina Holidays - Boavista Golf & Spa](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/boavista-golf-resort-spa.html), where it scores 9.1.
Lagos is about 85 to 95 km from Faro Airport by road. If you are not hiring a car, a [pre-booked transfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA) is the easiest way to get there with your clubs.

Still deciding? Read our [Boavista vs Espiche comparison](/guide/boavista-vs-espiche-which-lagos-golf-course-should-you-play), [open the course comparator](/?compare=palmares,boavista), or see all three Lagos courses on our [Lagos golf courses page](/lagos/golf-courses).

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Lagos and Portimão costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-lagos-and-portimao-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: Where to stay to play Morgado and Alamos near Portimão: the NAU Morgado resort hotel beside both first tees, plus the best options in Penina, Portimão, Ferragudo and Alvor, with drive times, golf perks and green fees.

content.text: The NAU Morgado Golf & Country Club, in a quiet valley a few kilometres north of Portimão, has two 18-hole courses by Russell Talley of European Golf Design. [Morgado](/courses/morgado) is the longer par 73, inspired by links golf with wide fairways, deep pot bunkers and big undulating greens, while [Alamos](/courses/alamos) is a tighter par 71 with views across a reservoir to the Serra de Monchique. Both share the same practice complex, with two practice tees, two chipping greens, two putting greens and a golf academy.

The resort has its own hotel right beside the courses. Beyond that, the countryside around it is empty, so every other good option is 18 to 26 minutes away in Penina, Portimão, Ferragudo or Alvor. This guide covers the best hotels near Morgado and Alamos golf in each of those places.
Map of hotels near Morgado and Alamos golf
The black pins are the two courses (tap one to see course details). The blue pins are the hotels in this guide; tap one to check prices and availability.
How we chose these hotels

We include a hotel if it is rated at least 8 out of 10 on Booking.com, or at least 7.8 if it offers specific golf services. We normally only list places within about 15 minutes of the course, but apart from the resort hotel there is nothing well rated that close, so we have included the best hotels within about 25 minutes. Drive times are calculated by road to the clubhouse, not in a straight line.
Prices are the lowest nightly rates we found on the hotel's own website or a price-comparison site in October 2026, so treat them as a guide. Check current rates with the link.
Staying at the resort

content.name: NAU Morgado Golf & Country Club
content.text: The four-star hotel of the resort, about 300 metres from both courses, so you can walk to the first tee. It scores **8.5 on Booking.com**, from about €93 a night in October, with spacious rooms and family duplexes, several of them overlooking the course, and a choice of bed and breakfast, half board or semi all-inclusive. Golf tour operators selling NAU packages also list a second round on the same day for €25, subject to availability. Guests are less enthusiastic about the breakfast than the rest of the stay.
perks: About 300 m from both first tees
Bed and breakfast, half board or semi all-inclusive

content.text: Golf resort nearby

content.name: Penina Hotel & Golf Resort
content.text: The Algarve's original golf resort, about 18 minutes from Morgado. Penina's "Best Available Rate for Golfers" includes breakfast and **a complimentary round every day** on one of its own courses, so you can mix free rounds at Penina with a day or two at Morgado and Alamos. Breakfast starts at 7am. See our full guide to [hotels near Penina Golf Resort](/guide/hotels-near-penina-golf-resort).
perks: Free daily round on the golfer rate

content.text: Best value near Morgado and Alamos

content.name: Casa Penina Guesthouse
content.text: A tiny four-suite guesthouse next to Penina, rated an outstanding **9.7 on Booking.com**, from about €53 a night in the quieter months (minimum two nights). Breakfast is served facing the fairways for €12 extra. About 21 minutes from Morgado.

content.name: Água Hotels Riverside
content.text: A good-value hotel on the Arade river near Ferragudo, from about €49 a night, with breakfast from 7am and a gym that opens at 6am, which suits early tee times. About 23 minutes from Morgado, and close to the Pestana courses at Ferragudo and Gramacho if you want to play more.

content.name: Jupiter Marina Hotel
content.text: A stylish hotel on Portimão marina rated **9.0 on Booking.com**, from about €65 a night. Breakfast starts at 7.30am and there is a spa and rooftop bar, with restaurants within walking distance in the evening. About 24 minutes from Morgado.
perks: Free shuttle to Praia da Rocha

content.text: All-inclusive in Alvor

content.name: Tivoli Alvor Algarve – All Inclusive Resort
content.text: A five-star all-inclusive resort near Alvor beach, with a spa and a kids' club. UK golf tour operators sell golf packages here, typically with rounds at Alamos and Morgado as well as Penina and Salgados, which makes it a good choice for a family holiday with a few rounds thrown in. About 26 minutes from Morgado.
Morgado and Alamos green fees and what to know before you play

NAU does not publish a public price list; tee times are booked online through the club. On the club's online booking, 18 holes cost **from about €82 in winter and high summer**, €98 in June and €120 to €128 in September and October, the same for both courses. Ask about a buggy when you book.

The maximum handicap is 28 for men and 36 for ladies on both courses; see [do you need a handicap to play golf in the Algarve](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve). The clubhouse has a restaurant, bar and pro shop, and you can hire clubs and buggies on site.
Tips for golfers staying near Morgado and Alamos
**Which course first?** Morgado is longer and more open, Alamos shorter and tighter. Read [Alamos vs Morgado](/guide/alamos-vs-morgado-which-portimao-golf-course-should-you-play) to decide.
**You will need a car.** The resort is in the countryside north of Portimão, and everything apart from the resort hotel is around 20 minutes away by road.

**Combine it with Penina.** The three Penina courses are about 18 minutes away, so Morgado, Alamos and Penina make an easy five or six-round week. Compare the two Penina courses in [Penina Championship vs Penina Resort](/guide/penina-championship-vs-penina-resort-which-course-should-you-play).
Frequently asked questions
Is there a hotel at Morgado golf?
Yes. NAU Morgado Golf & Country Club is a four-star hotel about 300 metres from both the Morgado and Alamos first tees, rated 8.5 on Booking.com.
Where else can I stay near Morgado and Alamos?

The nearest alternatives are around Penina, about 18 to 21 minutes away, including the Penina Hotel & Golf Resort and the tiny Casa Penina Guesthouse. Portimão marina and Ferragudo are about 23 to 24 minutes away.
What is the cheapest place to stay near Morgado?
Água Hotels Riverside, from about €49 a night, and Casa Penina Guesthouse, from about €53, both around 20 minutes from the course.
Playing several courses? Find the best base for your trip

If Morgado and Alamos are just one stop on your golf trip, try **Find Your Base** on the [Algarve Golf Map](/). Pick the courses you want to play and it shows you the area that sits closest to all of them, along with well-rated hotels nearby, so you spend less time driving and more time on the course.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Lagos and Portimão costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-lagos-and-portimao-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

**Prefer all-inclusive?** Our guide to [all-inclusive golf hotels in the Algarve](/guide/all-inclusive-golf-hotels-in-the-algarve) explains what all-inclusive covers (not your green fees) and shows examples near the courses.

excerpt: The Algarve has one floodlit golf course: Amendoeira's 9-hole Academy course. How night golf works there, approximate prices, booking and hotels nearby.

content.text: Night golf in the Algarve comes down to one place: the floodlit **Academy course** at [Amendoeira Golf Resort](/courses/amendoeira-faldo), in the countryside between Albufeira and Silves. It is a nine-hole par-3 course with lights around every hole, and the resort says it is the only floodlit nine-hole course in Portugal. We could not find another floodlit course, driving range or pitch and putt anywhere in the region.
This guide covers how night golf at Amendoeira works, roughly what it costs, how to book a floodlit round (you cannot do it online), what to know before you go and where to stay nearby.
Where can you play night golf in the Algarve?

Only at Amendoeira. The Algarve has around forty golf courses, but the rest close at dusk. Driving ranges follow daylight too: Vilamoura's Old Course range, for example, lists opening hours to 4pm in winter and 7pm in summer.

So if you search for night golf in Albufeira or Vilamoura, Amendoeira is the answer. It is about 26 minutes by car from the centre of Albufeira, 16 minutes from Armação de Pêra and around 40 minutes from Vilamoura.
The floodlit Academy course at Amendoeira

The Academy course sits between Amendoeira's two 18-hole championship courses, the [Faldo](/courses/amendoeira-faldo) and the [O'Connor Jnr](/courses/amendoeira-oconnor). It was designed by Steve Richardson and opened around 2008 as part of the resort's golf academy.

All **nine holes are par 3s**, which makes it a par 27, and the course measures about 700 metres in total. Each hole has three sets of tees that change the line into the green, so it plays differently each time you go round. The signature hole is the **7th**, where two of the three tees play over water.

The resort pitches it at beginners and at anyone who wants to sharpen their short game, and says it suits the whole family. Under the lights it is also a fun group outing: golf travel writers describe groups finishing 18 holes on the Faldo or O'Connor during the day, having dinner at the clubhouse, then heading out for a floodlit nine. In the resort's online booking system the course appears as the "António Parreira Afonso Pitch & Putt", so don't be confused if you see that name.

If you are still choosing between the two big courses for your daytime round, read [Amendoeira Faldo vs O'Connor: which should you play?](/guide/amendoeira-faldo-vs-o-connor-which-silves-golf-course-should-you-play). For more short courses across the region, see [the Algarve's best par-3 golf courses](/guide/the-algarve-s-best-par-3-golf-courses).
How much does night golf at Amendoeira cost?
Amendoeira doesn't publish a price for floodlit play, so the figures below are **approximate**. Check them with the resort before you go.
**Nine holes in daylight: €16.** This is the visitor rate in the resort's online booking system, and it was the same on every date we checked between November 2026 and August 2027.

**The floodlights: roughly €100 an hour (approximate).** You pay to have the lights switched on. A 2024 National Club Golfer review says golfers pay for the electricity, "and not necessarily a green fee", and a guest reported paying 100 euros an hour for the lights in 2019. We could not find a more recent figure, so treat it as a rough guide.

Because the lighting is charged per session rather than per player, night golf makes most sense for a group. As an approximate example, if eight friends share an hour under the lights at around €100, that is about **€12 to €13 each**. For a couple, the same hour costs the full amount, so it is worth asking the resort when you book.
How to book a floodlit round

Night golf at Amendoeira **can't be booked online**. The resort's booking system only shows daytime tee times on the Academy course, with the last start at about 3.50pm in winter and 5.30pm in summer. To play under the floodlights, contact the resort directly:
**Phone:** +351 282 320 800 (resort) or +351 282 320 671 (reservations).
**Email:** reservations@amendoeiraresort.com. **Address:** Morgado da Lameira, 8365-006 Alcantarilha.
When you get in touch, ask what the lights cost, the latest time you can play (a golf guide puts the limit at 11pm) and whether you can hire clubs in the evening.
What to know before you play

**Dress code.** Amendoeira's dress code applies on all its courses: collared shirts with sleeves, tucked in, and golf shoes. T-shirts, denim, sportswear and very short shorts are not allowed. The resort warns that players who don't meet the dress code won't be allowed to play and their green fee won't be refunded.

**Handicap.** The resort doesn't publish a handicap requirement for the Academy course, and it is aimed at beginners, but check when you book if you have never played. For the rest of the region, see our guide on [whether you need a handicap to play golf in the Algarve](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve).
**Getting there and back.** Amendoeira is inland, off the main roads, and a night round finishes late. If you plan to have a drink at the clubhouse, stay at the resort or book a taxi for the return.

**Lessons.** The Amendoeira academy is one of the best equipped in Portugal, with TrackMan and video analysis. If you want to combine a lesson with your night round, see [golf lessons in the Algarve](/guide/golf-lessons-in-the-algarve).
Where to stay near Amendoeira for night golf

For night golf, staying close matters more than usual. You finish late, the course is in the countryside, and nobody wants a long drive back. The obvious choice is the resort itself, but there are two excellent rural guesthouses within 15 minutes and two golf resorts on the coast a little further away.

We include hotels rated at least 8 out of 10 on Booking.com, within about 15 minutes of the course by road. We made two exceptions: Vila Vita Parc and the Algarve Marriott Salgados are 18 minutes away, but each has golf of its own. Drive times are calculated by road. Prices are the lowest nightly rates we could reliably find in October 2026, and where we couldn't find a trustworthy figure we have left the price out rather than guess.

content.name: Amendoeira Golf Resort
content.text: The only place where you can walk back to your room after a floodlit round. The resort's apartments and villas are a few minutes from the Academy course, with the [Faldo](/courses/amendoeira-faldo) and [O'Connor Jnr](/courses/amendoeira-oconnor) courses on the same site, so you can play 18 holes by day and nine under the lights in the evening without getting in a car. Guests rate it **9 out of 10 on Booking.com**. The apartments are self-catering, and there is a clubhouse restaurant on site.

content.name: Quinta das Piteiras
content.text: A small rural guesthouse in the countryside near Silves, with just five rooms, a small pool and an original farmhouse that dates from 1900. It scores an outstanding **9.9 on Booking.com**. It has no golf services, but it is a peaceful base 12 minutes from Amendoeira and close to Silves's castle and old town.

content.name: Villa Bora-Bora
content.text: Rustic, fully equipped apartments in the countryside near Pêra, with a saltwater pool, gardens and its own restaurant and bar, plus a small fado stage that occasionally hosts music evenings. Guests rate it **9.7 on Booking.com**. It is 14 minutes from the course, and handy for a group that wants its own kitchen.

content.name: Algarve Marriott Salgados Golf Resort & Spa
content.text: The golf hotel of the [Salgados](/courses/salgados) resort, by the beach between Albufeira and Armação de Pêra, from about €123 a night in October. It sells Stay & Play packages with the Salgados course, so you can play a championship course during the day and drive 18 minutes inland for a floodlit nine in the evening. See all the options in our guide to [hotels near Salgados golf course](/guide/hotels-near-salgados-golf-course).

content.name: Vila Vita Parc
content.text: One of the finest resorts in Portugal, on the clifftops at Porches, from about €250 a night in October. For golfers it has a nine-hole pitch and putt, an 18-hole putting green, a driving range, a golf simulator and a resident pro, and the resort offers **preferential rates at Algarve golf courses**. A good choice if you are travelling with a partner who wants a world-class spa and beach while you play.
perks: Pitch and putt, driving range and golf simulator

content.text: Night golf in the Algarve: quick answers
Is there night golf in Albufeira or Vilamoura?
No. The nearest floodlit course is the Academy course at Amendoeira, about 26 minutes by car from Albufeira centre and around 40 minutes from Vilamoura.
Can you book night golf online?
No. Online booking on the Academy course only covers daytime tee times. For a floodlit round, phone or email the resort.
How late can you play?
A golf guide puts the limit at 11pm. Amendoeira doesn't publish evening hours, so confirm when you book.
Is Amendoeira the only floodlit golf course in Portugal?
That is what the resort says, and we couldn't find another one. To plan the rest of your trip, explore every course on our [Algarve golf map](/).

excerpt: Planning an Algarve golf trip for a group or society: golf villas and apartments near the courses, booking tee times together, buggies, minivans and tips for the organiser.

content.text: Taking a golf society or a group of friends to the Algarve is mostly about logistics: somewhere everyone can stay together, tee times one after another, enough buggies and a vehicle big enough for all the golf bags. This guide covers each of those, with examples of golf villas and apartments close to the courses that suit groups.

**Quick answer:** base the group at a resort with several courses close together, such as Vilamoura, Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo, or Amendoeira, so nobody spends the trip driving. Book self-catering apartments or resort villas with two or three bedrooms, reserve consecutive tee times as early as you can, and book minivans or larger hire cars with room for the bags. **Last checked: November 2026.**
What changes when you travel as a group

**Tee times come in four-balls.** A group of 8 needs two consecutive tee times, a group of 16 needs four, and the bigger the group, the earlier you need to book to get them together, especially in spring and October.

**Online booking has limits.** Clubs' own booking pages are handy for a four-ball or two, but larger groups may need to book with the club directly. Pestana's booking site, for example, takes up to 16 players in one online booking. Our guide to [how to book tee times in the Algarve](/guide/how-to-book-tee-times-in-the-algarve) shows how each course takes bookings.

**Group terms can be stricter.** Some clubs set different cancellation rules for groups. Monte Rei, for example, lets groups of up to four cancel free of charge up to 15 days before play, but groups of 5 to 23 need to cancel 30 days ahead, and groups of 24 or more are handled by its events team. Check the terms before you collect everyone's money.
**Group rates aren't usually advertised.** We didn't find published group green fees on the club websites we checked, so if you're a large group, ask the club or a local agency what they can offer.
Choosing courses that work for a group
The easiest group trips stay in one place and play several courses there. Some examples:

**Vilamoura:** four courses open to visitors, the [Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course), [Pinhal](/courses/vilamoura-pinhal), [Laguna](/courses/vilamoura-laguna) and [Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium), all booked through Vilamoura Golf, with the marina for evenings out.

**Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo:** three Quinta do Lago courses, [South](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south), [North](/courses/quinta-do-lago-north) and [Laranjal](/courses/quinta-do-lago-laranjal), plus the two Vale do Lobo courses next door, the [Royal](/courses/vale-do-lobo-royal) and [Ocean](/courses/vale-do-lobo-ocean). It's the closest golf to Faro Airport.

**Albufeira:** two courses on one resort at Amendoeira, the [Faldo](/courses/amendoeira-faldo) and [O'Connor](/courses/amendoeira-oconnor), with [Salgados](/courses/salgados) and [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs) nearby.

**Carvoeiro:** Pestana's [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho) and [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta) are on the same resort, and Pestana's other courses nearby, such as [Silves](/courses/silves) and [Pestana Ferragudo](/courses/pestana-ferragudo), are on the same booking site.

Mixed-ability groups should check handicap limits too. Most courses ask for 28 for men and 36 for ladies, but rules vary, so see [do you need a handicap to play golf in the Algarve?](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve). If some of the group are beginners, [the best Algarve courses for beginners](/guide/the-10-best-algarve-golf-courses-for-beginners) has options.
Golf villas and apartments for groups

For a group, self-catering apartments and resort villas usually work better than hotel rooms: everyone has a shared kitchen and living space, and you can often fit the whole group into a few units. Below are examples run by the resorts themselves or by established hotels, so they have proper reviews and can be booked online. They're examples, not the only good options, and we've left some places out only because we couldn't check enough details.
Prices are the lowest "from" rates we found, usually for the smallest unit, so a two- or three-bedroom villa will cost more. Where no price is shown, we couldn't confirm one.
Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo

content.name: Vale do Lobo Resort
content.text: Villas, apartments and townhouses rented by the resort itself, rated **8.4 on Booking.com**, so the group is never more than a short ride from the first tee. Guests get the **Vale do Lobo Guest Card, with a discount on green fees**, offers on equipment rental and a free resort shuttle. Stays are self-catering, with plenty of restaurants within the resort.
perks: Green-fee discount with the Guest Card

content.name: Vilar do Golf
content.text: Apartments right beside the South Course, rated **8.8 on Booking.com**, from about €103 a night in October. Every apartment has a kitchen and a terrace, which suits golfers sharing, and the resort offers a **golf club rental service**.

content.name: Encosta do Lago Resort Club
content.text: Spacious self-catering apartments at the western end of the estate, rated **8.7 on Booking.com**, from about €200 a night. The concierge team will **organise your tee times** at Quinta do Lago and nearby courses, which saves the organiser a job.

content.text: Vilamoura

content.name: Hilton Vilamoura As Cascatas Golf Resort & Spa
content.text: A five-star resort with hotel rooms and apartments overlooking Pinhal, rated **8.5 on Booking.com**, from about €112 a night in October. It's one of Vilamoura Golf's official partner hotels, and the apartments give a group space to get together after the round.

content.name: Hotel Apartamento do Golfe
content.text: A simple three-star aparthotel a short walk from the Old Course clubhouse, rated **8.3 on Booking.com**, from about €37 a night in October. Studios and apartments have kitchenettes. Basic, but a budget-friendly base for a group that mostly wants to play golf.

content.name: Amendoeira Golf Resort

content.name: Marriott Residences Salgados Resort

perks: Suites with one to three bedrooms
