perks: Lower green fees for resort guests
content.distanceLabel: Inside the resort, overlooking the course

content.text: Carvoeiro

content.name: Pestana Gramacho Residences
content.text: Pestana's own golf apartments on the Gramacho course, with studios and **one- and two-bedroom apartments**, from about €56 a night on Pestana's website. It's rated **7.8 on Booking.com**, a little lower than the others, but it has golf on the doorstep, a free internal shuttle and breakfast from 7am.
content.distanceLabel: On the Gramacho course

content.name: Vale d'El Rei Hotel & Villas
content.text: A quiet hotel and villa complex east of Carvoeiro, rated **9.0 on Booking.com**, from about €87 a night. It has three outdoor pools and a free transfer into Carvoeiro, so the group can have dinner in the village without anyone having to drive.
content.distanceLabel: Gramacho about 14 min

content.text: Private villas

Privately owned villas can be good value for a big group, but they come and go and are harder to check, so we haven't listed any. If you book one, check how far it is from your courses by car, whether there's parking for all your vehicles and somewhere safe to keep the golf bags, and what the deposit and cancellation terms are.
Getting the group and its golf bags around

**From the airport, book minivans.** A standard car won't take four golfers and four bags. In October 2026 we found pre-booked minivans from Faro Airport for about €44 to Vilamoura, an eight-seat van for about €44 to Quinta do Lago, and a minivan for about €64 to Albufeira, per vehicle each way. Tell the company how many golf bags you're bringing. You can [compare transfers on GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA), and our [Faro Airport to the golf courses guide](/guide/faro-airport-to-algarve-golf-courses) has more detail.

**During the trip, larger hire cars.** If you're playing courses spread around the area, a few seven- or nine-seat cars are usually simpler than a fleet of small ones, but check the boot space with the seats in use. You can [compare car hire for your dates](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw). If you're staying on a resort with several courses, you may only need transfers.
Buggies for a group

A buggy takes two players, and Vilamoura Golf, for example, allows only two players and two bags per buggy, so a group of eight needs four. Book them with the tee times, as some clubs have limited numbers. Prices vary by club: among clubs that publish them, a buggy for 18 holes costs €48 at Benamor, €50 at Salgados and €55 at Pestana's courses, so roughly €25 each for two players sharing. Some green fees already include one, such as Amendoeira's online rate. See our [golf buggy hire guide](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve).
Golf clubs: bring or hire?

With a big group, the airline fees for golf bags add up quickly, and so does the space they take in the vans. Hiring sets locally can be simpler, and some companies deliver to your villa or hotel. Compare options in our [golf club hire comparison](/club-rental) and our guide to [hiring golf clubs at Faro Airport](/guide/hiring-golf-clubs-at-faro-airport).
Tips for the trip organiser
**Collect names and handicaps early.** Some clubs ask for them when you book, and you'll need them anyway to pair up four-balls.

**Know the payment and cancellation terms before you take deposits.** If the club charges in full and won't refund after a deadline, make sure the group knows. Travel insurance is worth recommending, as clubs such as Vilamoura Golf and Monte Rei don't refund for cancelled flights.
**Keep the first and last days light.** Plan the first round for the day after you arrive, or a short twilight round, and keep the last day free for travel.

**Running your own competition?** Agree the format and handicap allowances before you go, and ask the club whether it can give the group consecutive tee times and somewhere to meet for prize giving afterwards.
Golf group trips to the Algarve: common questions
Do Algarve golf clubs give group discounts?
Some may, but we didn't find group green fees published on the club websites we checked. Ask the club, or a local agency that books groups, before you book individually.
How far ahead should a golf society book?
As early as you can, especially for spring and October, when consecutive morning tee times at the best-known courses go first. Book the accommodation and tee times together so the dates match.
What is the best area of the Algarve for a group golf trip?

Somewhere with several courses close together, so the group can play different courses without long drives. Vilamoura, Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo, and Amendoeira are good examples, and Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo are also the closest to Faro Airport.

**Planning the budget?** See [how much a golf trip to the Algarve costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost) if you book it yourself, or our [golf weekend in the Algarve](/guide/golf-weekend-in-the-algarve) guide for a shorter trip.

**Prefer all-inclusive?** Our guide to [all-inclusive golf hotels in the Algarve](/guide/all-inclusive-golf-hotels-in-the-algarve) explains what all-inclusive covers (not your green fees) and shows examples near the courses.

**Want a ready-made competition?** Our guide to [golf tournaments in the Algarve](/guide/golf-tournaments-in-the-algarve) lists amateur events with prize-giving dinners that groups can enter together.

excerpt: Where to stay to play Salgados Golf near Albufeira: the three resort hotels beside the course, a five-star beach hotel at a budget price and the best options nearby, with drive times, golf perks and the official 2026 green fees.

content.text: [Salgados Golf](/courses/salgados) sits on flat coastal land between Albufeira and Armação de Pêra, right beside the Salgados Lagoon nature reserve and a few hundred metres from the beach. Water comes into play on most holes, the birdlife is a constant companion, and the course was named World's Best Golf Course Renovation at the 2025 World Golf Awards. It is managed by Troon.

This guide covers the best hotels near Salgados golf course: the three resort hotels you can walk to the first tee from, a five-star beach hotel next door at a three-star price, and well-rated options in Albufeira and Armação de Pêra, all within 15 minutes.
Map of hotels near Salgados golf course
The black pin is Salgados Golf (tap it to see course details). The blue pins are the hotels in this guide; tap one to check prices and availability.
How we chose these hotels

We include a hotel if it is rated at least 8 out of 10 on Booking.com, or at least 7.8 if it offers specific golf services, and is within about 15 minutes of the clubhouse by road. Drive times are calculated by road, not in a straight line. Golf services come from each hotel's or the club's own website wherever possible, and we only mention a golf perk if we could find it stated.

Prices are the lowest nightly rates we could reliably find in October 2026. Where we could not find a trustworthy figure, we have left the price out rather than guess, so check current rates with the link.
Staying at the Salgados resort

Salgados Golf sells its Stay & Play packages with three resort hotels: the Algarve Marriott Salgados, the Westin Salgados and the Marriott Residences. All three are part of the same resort as the course, so you can walk from your room to the first tee. Some packages add half board or seasonal discounts.

content.name: Algarve Marriott Salgados Golf Resort & Spa
content.text: The golf hotel of the resort, with 228 rooms and suites, four outdoor pools and the Wellness Hub Salgados spa, and some balconies look straight over the course. It is one of the club's three Stay & Play hotels and the first tee is a short walk away. From about €123 a night in October, and guests rate the breakfast buffet highly.

content.name: Marriott Residences Salgados Resort
content.text: 172 suites with one to three bedrooms, ten pools and a kids' club, beside the course. It is the best option on the resort for groups of golfers sharing or for families, and it is also one of the club's Stay & Play hotels. From about €127 a night in October.
perks: Suites with one to three bedrooms

content.name: The Westin Salgados Beach Resort
content.text: The five-star option on the resort and the best rated of the three at **8.8 on Booking.com**, with direct access to Salgados Beach. Its partnership with Hyperice and Bala means proper recovery and training kit, which golfers playing several days in a row will appreciate. About four minutes from the clubhouse by car.
Best value near Salgados

content.name: Wine & Books by the Sea, Algarve Resort
content.text: The former VidaMar resort, a five-star hotel on Salgados Beach just next to the course, from about €74 a night in October, a remarkable price for a five-star. It has no golf services of its own, but you are five minutes from the clubhouse, and there is a spa with a heated indoor pool and several restaurants. Guests rate the breakfast highly.

content.name: Hotel Baía Grande
content.text: A four-star hotel near Praia da Galé, about nine minutes from Salgados, from around €57 a night in October. Nothing fancy, but well rated, and guests praise the breakfast. A good budget base if you are also planning to play courses east of Albufeira.
Mid-range hotels near Salgados

content.name: Kimpton Atlântico Algarve
content.text: A stylish beachfront hotel at Praia da Galé with indoor and outdoor pools, rated **8.4 on Booking.com** from more than 1,200 reviews. From about €127 a night in October, about 12 minutes from Salgados.

content.name: Vila Galé Náutico
content.text: A four-star family hotel in Armação de Pêra, a couple of hundred metres from the beach, with a kids' club and several pools. A good choice if you are travelling with family and want a lively seaside town on your doorstep. About 13 minutes from Salgados.
Luxury hotels near Salgados

content.name: W Algarve
content.text: A five-star resort on the cliffs above Praia da Galé, seven minutes from Salgados and rated **8.9 on Booking.com**. A good choice if you want a more design-led, social hotel to come back to after your round.

content.name: Vila Vita Parc
content.text: One of the most celebrated resorts in Portugal, rated an exceptional **9.5 on Booking.com**, set in clifftop gardens near Porches. From about €246 a night in October, and about 15 minutes from Salgados. Pick it if the golf is part of a special trip rather than the whole point.
Salgados green fees and what to know before you play

Salgados is one of the better-value championship courses in the Algarve. On the official 2026 price list, **18 holes cost €91 in low season** (January, July, August and December), €119 in mid season (February, June and November) and €163 in high season (March to May, September and October). Nine holes cost €60 to €115.

A buggy costs €50 for 18 holes and a trolley €6, and you can hire a premium Callaway set with a sleeve of balls for €50. If you are hiring anyway, the club's promotions combining a player, buggy and clubs (from €158 in low season) save money. Prices are valid until 31 December 2026.

Salgados sets a maximum handicap of 28 for men and 36 for ladies, so bring your handicap certificate. Its 2026 policies add that golfers of every level are welcome, as long as they keep up with the group in front. Wear what you would at any upscale golf club, with closed shoes, and expect to change if you turn up in T-shirts or beachwear. There is a short-game practice area, a putting green and a chipping green, plus golf simulators and lessons. Not sure what you need? See [do you need a handicap to play golf in the Algarve](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve).
Tips for golfers staying near Salgados
**Bring the camera.** The lagoon next to the course is a protected nature reserve, and its wetland birdlife is part of the experience, especially early in the morning.

**More golf nearby.** [Balaia Golf Village](/courses/balaia) is about 24 minutes east for a quick nine holes, and [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho) about 27 minutes west. If you are planning a short-course round, compare [Balaia and Pine Cliffs](/guide/balaia-vs-pine-cliffs-which-quick-round-near-albufeira-should-you-play).
**Getting there.** Faro Airport is about 50 km away, a little under an hour by car.
Frequently asked questions
Which hotel is closest to Salgados golf course?

The Algarve Marriott Salgados and the Marriott Residences Salgados are both right beside the course, about two minutes from the clubhouse by car, and you can walk to the first tee. The Westin Salgados is about four minutes away.
What is the cheapest place to stay near Salgados?
Hotel Baía Grande, from about €57 a night in October, and Wine & Books by the Sea, a five-star beach hotel from about €74 a night, just five minutes from the course.
Do you need a handicap to play Salgados?

Yes. The club's course information sets a maximum handicap of 28 for men and 36 for ladies, so bring your handicap certificate. Golfers of every level within those limits are welcome, as long as you keep pace with the group in front.
Playing several courses? Find the best base for your trip

If Salgados is just one stop on your golf trip, try **Find Your Base** on the [Algarve Golf Map](/). Pick the courses you want to play and it shows you the area that sits closest to all of them, along with well-rated hotels nearby, so you spend less time driving and more time on the course.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Albufeira costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-albufeira-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: Enter Air flies charter holidays from Gdańsk to Faro, and golf bags are usually sorted through your tour operator. Here's what to check, including a possibly low weight limit.

content.text: Enter Air is a Polish charter airline that flies from Gdańsk to Faro, almost always as part of a package holiday sold by a tour operator. That changes how you handle golf clubs: the questions about price and weight are usually answered by **your tour operator**, not the airline's website.
How golf bags work on a charter flight

Since Enter Air mainly flies for tour operators, extras like sports equipment are normally added through whoever sold you the holiday. Their price can differ from the airline's own fee list, so ask them directly when you book, and get the golf bag confirmed in writing on your booking.
What it might cost

We couldn't access Enter Air's official fee schedule directly. A third-party summary of it lists golf equipment at around **€40 each way**. Treat that as a rough guide only, and use the figure your tour operator gives you.
Check the weight limit carefully

The same summary gives a weight limit of just **18kg** for golf equipment, well below the 23–32kg most airlines in this series allow. A full set in a padded travel bag can easily weigh more than that. As we can't confirm the figure from Enter Air itself, ask your tour operator for the exact limit and weigh your bag before you leave home.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

With a possible 18kg limit and a package booking in between you and the airline, bringing your own clubs on Enter Air takes some organising. Renting avoids all of it. ClubsToHire hands over sets in the **Faro Airport arrivals hall**, and MyCaddyMaster from a counter in departures. Hotel delivery is also an option with both.
Other rental companies are listed in our [Algarve club hire directory](/shops).
Bottom line

On Enter Air, your tour operator is the one to ask about golf bags: get the price and weight limit confirmed when you book. If the weight limit really is as low as 18kg, hiring clubs in Faro may be far simpler.

excerpt: Where to stay to play Monte Rei, the Algarve's most celebrated course: the resort's own villas and residences, a rural guesthouse 12 minutes away and the best hotels on the coast and in Tavira, with drive times and golf perks.

content.text: [Monte Rei Golf & Country Club](/courses/monte-rei) is the most celebrated course in the Algarve: a Jack Nicklaus Signature design that opened in 2007 and was ranked Portugal's number one for 15 years in a row. It sits on its own in the hills behind the coast near Vila Nova de Cacela, in the quiet eastern Algarve, with water in play on eleven holes and views over the Serra do Caldeirão.

That setting is part of the appeal, but it also means there are few hotels on its doorstep. This guide covers where to stay near Monte Rei golf: the resort's own villas and residences, a rural guesthouse 12 minutes away and the best-rated hotels on the coast and in Tavira, 20 to 30 minutes' drive away.
Map of hotels near Monte Rei golf
The black pin is Monte Rei (tap it to see course details). The blue pins are the places to stay in this guide; tap one to check prices and availability.
How we chose these hotels

We include a hotel if it is rated at least 8 out of 10 on Booking.com, or at least 7.8 if it offers specific golf services. The resort's own accommodation is always included, with its real score. Usually we only list places within about 15 minutes of the course, but Monte Rei is so isolated that we have also included a few outstanding hotels 20 to 30 minutes away, which is the realistic choice for most visitors.

Drive times are calculated by road, not in a straight line. Golf services come from each hotel's or the club's own website wherever possible. Rates in this corner of the Algarve change a lot by date, so we have not printed prices we could not verify in euros; check current rates with each link.
Staying at Monte Rei

content.name: Monte Rei Golf & Country Club
content.text: The only way to sleep on the course: one to three-bedroom Clubhouse Residences apartments near the clubhouse, linked villas, and three and four-bedroom villas with their own pools. The resort's **Short Stay package** gives you three nights in a Clubhouse Residences apartment with breakfast and two rounds with a shared buggy, and the **Golfers Retreat** seven nights with four rounds. On Booking.com the accommodation scores only 6.8 from a small number of reviews, well below the course's reputation, so read the recent reviews before you book.
perks: Golf packages with rounds and a shared buggy
Apartments and villas with private pools
content.distanceLabel: On the resort, next to the clubhouse

content.text: Closest place to stay outside the resort

content.name: Casa de Campo Vale do Asno
content.text: A small rural guesthouse in the pine forest just east of Monte Rei, about 12 minutes from the clubhouse along country roads. It has a saltwater pool, a breakfast that Booking.com guests rate 9.4, and it even suggests playing the Jack Nicklaus course to its guests. Peaceful and personal rather than luxurious.
perks: Rural guesthouse in a pine forest

content.text: Beach hotels near Monte Rei
The nearest stretch of coast is around Praia Verde and Altura, about 20 minutes south of the course. Stay here if you want the beach on your non-golf days.

content.name: Octant Praia Verde
content.text: A design-led boutique hotel among the pines above Praia Verde, rated an excellent **9.3 on Booking.com**. A wooden boardwalk takes you down to one of the best beaches in the eastern Algarve, many rooms look out to sea and some suites have their own plunge pool. It has no golf services of its own, but Monte Rei is about 22 minutes away.
Golf resorts near Monte Rei
Both of these sit on their own golf courses, so you can combine a day at Monte Rei with rounds closer to your bed.

content.name: Robinson Quinta da Ria
content.text: An all-inclusive Robinson club set right between the [Quinta da Ria](/courses/quinta-da-ria) and [Quinta de Cima](/courses/quinta-de-cima) courses, rated **8.4 on Booking.com**. Its golf academy has its own driving range, short course, three putting greens and bunkers, and it sells golf packages that bundle green fees with your stay. A strong choice for a week of golf with Monte Rei as the highlight, about 26 minutes away.
perks: Between the Quinta da Ria and Quinta de Cima courses
Golf academy with range, short course and putting greens

content.name: Castro Marim Golfe & Country Club
content.text: Two to four-bedroom villas, many with private pools, on the 27-hole [Castro Marim](/courses/castro-marim) course, rated **8.8 on Booking.com**. It is a relaxed, family-friendly base in the countryside near the Spanish border, with a kids' club at the clubhouse. Monte Rei is about 27 minutes away.
Staying in Tavira

content.name: Ozadi Tavira Hotel
content.text: If you would rather have restaurants and an old town to walk around in the evening, Tavira is the best base in the eastern Algarve. The four-star Ozadi on the edge of town scores **9.0 on Booking.com** from nearly 1,000 reviews. It has no golf services, and Monte Rei is just under 30 minutes away.
perks: Four-star hotel on the edge of Tavira

content.text: Monte Rei green fees and what to know before you play

Monte Rei is one of the most expensive courses in the Algarve. On the club's online booking, 18 holes run from **about €190 in November and December to €312 in spring and early summer**, and the price includes a buggy and range balls. The club does not publish a price list; tee times are booked online and must be paid in full in advance. Cancellations are free up to 15 days before you play for groups of up to four.

A maximum handicap of 28 for men and 36 for ladies is recommended. Read more in [do you need a handicap to play golf in the Algarve](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve). The experience is a big part of the price: the club describes valet parking, a buggy to the practice area, a briefing on the tee and 12-minute gaps between tee times, so you rarely see another group.
Tips for golfers staying near Monte Rei
**You will need a car.** There is no public transport to the course, and everything apart from the resort is 12 to 30 minutes away by road.

**Make it part of an eastern Algarve trip.** Quinta da Ria, Quinta de Cima, Castro Marim and [Quinta do Vale](/courses/quinta-do-vale) are all within about half an hour. Compare them in [Quinta da Ria vs Quinta de Cima](/guide/quinta-da-ria-vs-quinta-de-cima-which-tavira-course-should-you-play) and [Castro Marim vs Quinta do Vale](/guide/castro-marim-vs-quinta-do-vale-which-east-algarve-course-should-you-play).
**Book early in spring and autumn.** With wide gaps between tee times there are fewer slots than on most courses, so the best times go quickly in the busy months.
Frequently asked questions
Is there a hotel at Monte Rei?
There is no traditional hotel, but the resort rents its own Clubhouse Residences apartments and villas, some with private pools, and sells golf packages that include rounds and a shared buggy.
What is the closest place to stay near Monte Rei?
Apart from the resort itself, Casa de Campo Vale do Asno, a rural guesthouse about 12 minutes away. The nearest beach hotels, around Praia Verde, are about 20 minutes away.
Is Monte Rei worth the price?

For most keen golfers, yes, at least once. It is consistently ranked among the best courses in Europe, and the price includes a buggy, range balls and an unhurried round. If you are on a budget, pair it with better-value courses nearby such as Quinta da Ria or Castro Marim.
Playing several courses? Find the best base for your trip

If Monte Rei is just one stop on your golf trip, try **Find Your Base** on the [Algarve Golf Map](/). Pick the courses you want to play and it shows you the area that sits closest to all of them, along with well-rated hotels nearby, so you spend less time driving and more time on the course.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Monte Rei costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-monte-rei-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: All-inclusive hotels near Algarve golf courses, from Albufeira and Alvor to Lagos and Tavira: what all-inclusive covers (not green fees), drive times and golf services.

content.text: An all-inclusive hotel can make a golf holiday simpler: meals and drinks are paid for before you arrive, and you only have the golf to think about. But there's a catch golfers should know first. **All-inclusive rates cover food and drink at the hotel, not your green fees.** This guide explains what that means for a golf trip and shows examples of well-rated all-inclusive hotels within easy reach of Algarve golf courses.

**Quick answer:** the only all-inclusive hotel in this guide that sits on a golf course is Robinson Quinta da Ria, near Tavira, between the Quinta da Ria and Quinta de Cima courses. For the busiest golf areas, look at Olhos de Água and Albufeira, a short drive from Pine Cliffs, Balaia, Salgados and the Vilamoura courses, or at Alvor, next to Alto Golf. **Last checked: November 2026.**

**How to read this guide:** some hotels are all-inclusive only, while others sell all-inclusive as one option alongside bed and breakfast or half board, and you choose the board when you book. Each hotel below says which applies. Ratings are from Booking.com, drive times are by road to the course, and these are examples, not the only all-inclusive hotels in the Algarve.
What all-inclusive covers on a golf holiday

**Included:** meals and drinks at the hotel, within the hotel's own rules. Some hotels sell more than one all-inclusive level: Tivoli Alvor, for example, offers All-Inclusive and All Inclusive Premium.

**Usually not included:** green fees, buggies, club hire and transport to the course, plus anything you eat or drink at the golf club. Some hotels sell golf separately: Robinson Quinta da Ria, for example, sells golf packages that bundle green fees with your stay. Check what your rate includes before you book.
Is all-inclusive worth it if you play golf every day?

It depends on your routine. If you play in the morning and have lunch at the clubhouse, you'll pay for a meal you've already paid for at the hotel. Golfers who play most days may find half board, or bed and breakfast, better value.

All-inclusive works best when the golf is part of the holiday rather than all of it: if you play every other day, if you're travelling with a partner or family who won't play, or if you'd rather not think about money once you're there. Before booking, also check what time breakfast starts if you want early tee times.
All-inclusive golf hotels near Albufeira and Vilamoura

These three are on the coast east and west of Albufeira. We couldn't confirm an all-inclusive rate at a hotel inside Vilamoura itself when we checked, but the two in Olhos de Água are about 14 to 17 minutes from the Vilamoura Laguna and Millennium courses.

content.name: 3HB Guarana
content.text: An all-inclusive hotel about 300 metres from Barranco das Belharucas beach in Olhos de Água, formerly ClubHotel Riu Guarana, rated **8.7 on Booking.com**. It's the closest hotel in this guide to [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs) and [Balaia](/courses/balaia), two 9-hole courses about 5 to 6 minutes away, and the Vilamoura courses are about a quarter of an hour by car.
content.distanceLabel: Balaia about 5 min · Pine Cliffs about 6 min · Vilamoura Laguna about 14 min

content.name: AP Adriana Beach Resort
content.text: An all-inclusive resort set in gardens about 300 metres from Falésia beach, rated **8.4 on Booking.com** from almost 2,000 reviews. [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs) is about 12 minutes away, and [Vilamoura Laguna](/courses/vilamoura-laguna) and [Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium) about 17.
content.distanceLabel: Pine Cliffs about 12 min · Vilamoura Laguna about 17 min

content.name: NAU São Rafael Suites
content.text: A suite hotel at Sesmarias, west of Albufeira, rated **8.1 on Booking.com**. Despite "All Inclusive" in its name, it also sells bed and breakfast rates, so **choose the all-inclusive rate when you book** if that's what you want. [Salgados](/courses/salgados) is about 10 minutes away.
content.distanceLabel: Salgados about 10 min · Balaia about 17 min

content.text: All-inclusive golf hotels near Portimão and Alvor
Two all-inclusive hotels next to each other near Alvor, both about 5 to 6 minutes from [Alto Golf](/courses/alto-golf) and about 17 minutes from [Penina](/courses/penina-championship).

content.name: Tivoli Alvor Algarve – All Inclusive Resort

content.text: How much does an all-inclusive golf hotel cost?

All-inclusive rates change a lot with the season, the room and the all-inclusive level, so we haven't quoted prices here. Use the button under each hotel to see the rates for your dates, and compare the all-inclusive rate with half board or bed and breakfast where the hotel offers them. Then add your green fees: our course pages show them month by month, and our guide to [how much a golf trip to the Algarve costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost) shows how a whole trip adds up.
Getting from your hotel to the course

Apart from Robinson Quinta da Ria and the Morgado hotel, you'll need to get to the course each day. A small hire car is usually the simplest option, and you can [compare car hire for your dates](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw). From Faro Airport, a pre-booked transfer avoids hunting for a taxi with a golf bag: [compare transfers on GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA), and see our [Faro Airport to the golf courses guide](/guide/faro-airport-to-algarve-golf-courses) for drive times.
All-inclusive golf in the Algarve: common questions
Do all-inclusive hotels include green fees?

Usually not. All-inclusive covers food and drink at the hotel. Some hotels sell golf packages that add green fees, such as Robinson Quinta da Ria, and tour operators sell packages at others, such as Tivoli Alvor, so check exactly what a package includes.
Which all-inclusive hotel is closest to a golf course?

Of the hotels in this guide, Robinson Quinta da Ria, which sits between the Quinta da Ria and Quinta de Cima courses. 3HB Guarana is about 5 to 6 minutes from Pine Cliffs and Balaia, and the two Alvor hotels about 5 to 6 minutes from Alto Golf.
Is there an all-inclusive hotel in Vilamoura?

We couldn't confirm an all-inclusive rate at a Vilamoura hotel when we checked in November 2026. 3HB Guarana and AP Adriana Beach Resort in Olhos de Água are about 14 to 17 minutes from the Laguna and Millennium courses. For hotels in Vilamoura itself, see our [golf hotels near Vilamoura](/guide/golf-hotels-near-vilamoura) guide.
Is there an adults-only all-inclusive golf hotel?
AP Cabanas Beach & Nature, near Tavira, is adults friendly, recommended for guests aged 14 and over, and offers all-inclusive as an option.
**Want to stay on the course instead?** See our guide to [Algarve hotels with a golf course on site](/guide/algarve-hotels-with-a-golf-course-on-site).

excerpt: The Algarve's gentlest 18-hole courses on the official FPG slope ratings, from Pestana Ferragudo up, plus which tees, handicap rules and terrain make a course easier.

content.text: Which are the **easiest golf courses in the Algarve**? On the official numbers, the course rating and slope rating the Portuguese Golf Federation (FPG) gives every course, the gentlest full-length course is **[Pestana Ferragudo](/courses/pestana-ferragudo)**, with a slope of **118** from its longest tees. [Silves](/courses/silves) (120) and [Benamor](/courses/benamor) (121) come next. But a low slope doesn't always mean an easy day out: some of the lowest-rated courses are among the hilliest in the Algarve, and the tees you play can change the numbers a lot.

All ratings come from the FPG's national course rating table, which we downloaded again on 18 November 2026 and checked tee by tee against our own data. Clubs re-rate their courses from time to time, so the figures can change.
How we ranked them

**Slope rating** measures how much harder a course is for an average club golfer than for a scratch golfer, on a scale from 55 to 155, where 113 is standard difficulty. **Course rating** is the score a scratch golfer is expected to shoot. Both depend on the tees, so to compare like with like we use each course's longest men's tees, the same basis as our guide to [the hardest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-hardest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve). The last two columns show the range across all the tees each course has rated, for men and for women.
The 10 lowest-rated 18-hole courses in the Algarve

content.note: Source: FPG national course rating table, checked 18 November 2026. Junior tees are not included. Click a course for the ratings of every tee and a course handicap calculator. San Lorenzo (closed until 2028) and the private Els Club are left out.
content.caption: 18-hole Algarve courses with the lowest slope ratings

content.text: Every other 18-hole course in the Algarve is rated 132 or higher from its longest tees. You'll find the full table in [the hardest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-hardest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
The three easiest full-length courses
1. Pestana Ferragudo: slope 118

[Pestana Ferragudo](/courses/pestana-ferragudo), near Ferragudo across the river from Portimão, opened in 2026 and is the newest course in the Algarve. From its white tees it plays 5,841 metres, par 72, with a slope of **118** and a course rating of 70.8, more than a shot under par. From the yellow tees it's rated **113**, exactly standard difficulty. The handicap limit on its scorecard is 28 for men and 36 for ladies.
2. Silves Golf: slope 120

[Silves Golf](/courses/silves), one of Pestana's courses, is a short par 70 of 5,592 metres from the white tees, with a slope of **120** and a course rating of 69.2. Its scorecard sets a handicap limit of 28 for men and 36 for ladies. The numbers flatter it a little on foot, though: Teetimes.pt describes rolling fairways with more climbing on the back nine and recommends a buggy.
3. Benamor: slope 121

[Benamor](/courses/benamor) near Tavira, laid out from Sir Henry Cotton's plans, measures 5,497 metres, par 71, from the white tees on the club's own hole-by-hole page, with a slope of **121** and a course rating of 68.2. Its booking terms ask for a handicap of 28 for men and 36 for ladies. Like Silves, it's easier on the scorecard than on the legs: Teetimes.pt calls the fairways very undulating and recommends a buggy.
Four more at 128 or 129
Four courses sit close behind, and they couldn't be more different:

[Quinta da Ria](/courses/quinta-da-ria) (128) near Vila Nova de Cacela is laid out on gently sloping ground running down towards the Ria Formosa, and accepts handicaps up to 36 for men and ladies. Its sister course [Quinta de Cima](/courses/quinta-de-cima) (129) is the longest course on this list at 6,586 metres from the white tees, but also fairly flat, and it also accepts handicaps up to 36 for men and ladies, according to the Robinson resort on the estate.

[Salgados](/courses/salgados) (129) near Albufeira is one of the easiest courses in the Algarve to walk, but it has plenty of water and is exposed to the wind. Its handicap limit is 28 for men and 36 for ladies. [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio) (129) near Salema is the opposite: the club itself recommends a buggy for its hills, and it doesn't publish a handicap limit.
Low slope doesn't always mean easy

The slope rating measures how hard it is to score, not how hard it is to get round. Several of the lowest-rated courses are hilly: Teetimes.pt recommends a buggy at Silves and Benamor, and Santo António's own website does too. If you'd rather walk, [Salgados](/courses/salgados), [Quinta da Ria](/courses/quinta-da-ria), [Quinta de Cima](/courses/quinta-de-cima) and [Vilamoura Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium) combine a low slope with gentle terrain. See [Algarve golf courses you can walk](/guide/algarve-golf-courses-you-can-walk) and [the hilliest courses](/guide/hilly-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Wind and water matter too. A flat seaside course like Salgados can play much harder on a windy day than its rating suggests.
Choose your tees, but check the club's rules

Moving forward a set of tees can make as much difference as choosing a lower-rated course. At [Vilamoura Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium/slope-rating), for example, the men's slope runs from 130 from the white tees down to 116 from the red tees. Every course on our site has a slope rating page showing all its tees.

You can't always pick any tee you like, though. Clubs set their own rules: Vale do Lobo's booking conditions, for example, say men play from the yellow tees and ladies from the red, and only players with a handicap of 9 or less may use the white tees, with the starter's permission. Ask which tees you can use when you book.
What it means for your handicap

Under the World Handicap System, your course handicap is your Handicap Index multiplied by the slope and divided by 113, plus the difference between the course rating and par. A golfer with a Handicap Index of 18 gets a course handicap of **14** from the yellow tees at Pestana Ferragudo (slope 113, course rating 67.7, par 72), against **27** from the longest tees at Monte Rei, the Algarve's hardest course. Each course's slope rating page has a calculator.
Easiest to get onto: handicap rules

If you don't have a handicap, or yours is high, the rating matters less than the club's rules. Most Algarve courses ask for a handicap certificate, usually up to 28 for men and 36 for ladies. Among the courses in our table, [Alto Golf](/courses/alto-golf), [Quinta da Ria](/courses/quinta-da-ria) and [Quinta de Cima](/courses/quinta-de-cima) accept handicaps up to 36 for men and ladies. Three courses need no handicap at all: [Penina Resort](/courses/penina-resort), [Vale de Milho](/courses/vale-de-milho) and [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs), where players without a handicap play from the red tees. Our guide to [handicap rules in the Algarve](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve) has the details for every course.
Short courses

Some 9-hole courses are rated as two loops of nine. [Balaia](/courses/balaia), a par-3 course near Albufeira, has the lowest slope in the Algarve: 83 to 84 for men. [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs), a 9-hole clifftop course, is rated 102 to 107 for men, and [Penina Resort](/courses/penina-resort) 116 to 122. [Vale de Milho](/courses/vale-de-milho) in Carvoeiro, a 9-hole par-3 course, has no FPG rating. See [the Algarve's 9-hole courses](/algarve-9-hole-courses).
Frequently asked questions
What is the easiest golf course in the Algarve?

On the official ratings, Pestana Ferragudo is the easiest 18-hole course, with a slope of 118 from its longest tees and 113 from the yellow tees. Silves (120) and Benamor (121) come next. Among short courses, Balaia, a 9-hole par-3 course, has the lowest slope in the Algarve at 84.
Which Algarve golf course is best for beginners?

The slope is only part of the answer: handicap rules, terrain and practice facilities matter as much. Our guide to [the best Algarve golf courses for beginners](/guide/the-10-best-algarve-golf-courses-for-beginners) looks at all of them.
Is a low slope rating good for a high handicapper?

Yes. The lower the slope, the fewer extra shots a higher-handicap golfer is expected to need compared with a scratch player, so your course handicap will be lower and the course should feel more manageable.
Want to compare courses yourself? Open the [Algarve golf course map](/) to filter by difficulty, price and handicap.

excerpt: Eleven minutes apart in the eastern Algarve: Benamor, a short course among old olive and cork trees laid out from Henry Cotton's plans, against Quinta da Ria inside the Ria Formosa Natural Park. Here's how they compare.

content.text: If you are staying in or around Tavira, two of the most practical rounds are **Benamor**, just outside town, and **Quinta da Ria**, near Vila Nova de Cacela. They are about 11 minutes apart by car. Benamor is the shorter, better-value course. Quinta da Ria has the bigger views and a resort on site. Here is how they compare.
Benamor: short, scenic and good value

The family that owns the Benamor estate asked Sir Henry Cotton to draw up a course in 1986. Cotton died the following year, and the course was completed from his plans by architect Howard Swan, opening in the spring of 2000. [Benamor](/courses/benamor) is **par 71 and only 5,497 metres**, one of the shorter 18-hole courses in the Algarve.

The club describes the land as undulating rather than hilly, with mountain views to the north and the Atlantic to the south. Fairways run between centuries-old olive, cork, carob, fig and almond trees, with water and bunkers in play. You need a handicap certificate (maximum 28 for men and 36 for ladies). Men play from the yellow tees and ladies from the red.

Benamor's internet rates are **€66** in low season (December, January and June to August), €95 in mid-season and €103 in high season (mid-September to November and mid-February to mid-May). Afternoon tee times in low season drop to €59 ([current Benamor green fees](/courses/benamor/green-fees)). There is a driving range with mats and a grass tee, plus chipping and putting greens.
Quinta da Ria: golf inside the Ria Formosa Natural Park

[Quinta da Ria](/courses/quinta-da-ria) was designed by Rocky Roquemore and opened in March 2002, inside the Ria Formosa Natural Park, with views over the Atlantic and Cacela Velha beach. It is **par 72 and 6,053 metres** from the white tees, about 600 metres longer than Benamor. It is laid with bentgrass throughout, and has hosted events including the Portugal Algarve Seniors Open in 2005 and the Portugal Algarve Ladies Open in 2008.

Quinta da Ria asks for a handicap certificate, with a limit of 36 for both men and ladies. Green fees on the club's online booking started at about **€100** when we checked, rising to around €150 at peak ([current Quinta da Ria green fees](/courses/quinta-da-ria/green-fees)). Its winter offers include a buggy. The practice facilities are excellent, with a 300-metre driving range and a nine-hole pitch-and-putt academy course.
One thing to check before a summer trip: according to the resort on site, Quinta da Ria opens only on Tuesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays and Sundays from early July to the end of August.
Which one should you play?

**Choose Benamor** if you want good value, a manageable length and a quieter round among old trees. It is a sensible pick for higher handicappers and anyone staying in Tavira itself. **Choose Quinta da Ria** for the setting and the full resort experience, especially if you are staying on site or want excellent practice facilities. If you have two days in the east, play one each day, since they are so close.
Where to stay

Benamor has no hotel on site, but Tavira is only about 13 minutes away. Quinta da Ria has the all-inclusive [Robinson Quinta da Ria](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/robinson-club-quinta-da-ria.html), which scores 8.4 on Booking.com, within walking distance of both Quinta da Ria and its sister course, [Quinta de Cima](/courses/quinta-de-cima).

Benamor is about 50 km from Faro Airport by road and Quinta da Ria a little further. A [pre-booked transfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA) gets you there with your clubs if you are not hiring a car.

Want to compare the sister courses too? Read [Quinta da Ria vs Quinta de Cima](/guide/quinta-da-ria-vs-quinta-de-cima-which-tavira-course-should-you-play), [open the course comparator](/?compare=benamor,quinta-da-ria), or see every course in the east on our [Tavira golf courses page](/tavira/golf-courses).

excerpt: Amateur golf tournaments in the Algarve for 2026/27: dates, courses, handicap limits and entry prices for events in Vilamoura, Vale do Lobo, Quinta do Lago, Penina and the east.

content.text: The Algarve has a busy calendar of amateur golf tournaments that visitors can enter, mostly in winter and spring. Most are week-long events with several rounds, a welcome cocktail and a prize-giving dinner, and many are sold as packages with a hotel. This guide lists the events announced for the 2026/27 season, what they cost where the organisers publish it, and the handicap you'll need.

**Quick answer:** the main season runs from December to March, with more events in May. You'll need a handicap certificate from your home club, and limits vary: the Vilamoura events ask for a maximum of 24 for men and 28 for ladies, Vale do Lobo's Amateur Week 26 and 32. Enter early, as some events have closing dates or limited places. **Last checked: November 2026.**

Dates and prices come from the organisers' own pages where we could find them; where an event is only listed by a golf agency, we say so. Formats and prices can change, so confirm with the organiser before you book flights. This isn't a complete list of every competition in the Algarve.
Algarve amateur golf tournaments 2026/27 at a glance

content.note: * Dates from a golf agency's 2026/27 tournament calendar (Tee Times, October 2026); we couldn't find them on the host club's own website, so check with the organiser. Other dates are from the host club's website.

Vale do Lobo Spring Amateur Tournament (16th)*
content.caption: Amateur tournaments announced for December 2026 to May 2027

content.text: How Algarve amateur tournaments work

**Format.** Most are played over several days on handicap, usually Stableford or medal (stroke play) with net and gross prizes, and separate men's and ladies' categories. Some add pairs or team rounds at the end of the week.

**Entry.** You'll need a handicap certificate from your home club, and the organiser may ask to see it. The entry fee normally covers the competition rounds and the social events: a welcome cocktail and a prize-giving dinner. Several events also sell packages with a week's accommodation, and some have a cheaper option for a non-playing partner.
**Booking.** Enter directly with the organiser: the host club or hotel, or the agency running the event. Check the closing date for entries and what happens if you cancel.
The main tournaments in more detail
Grande Troféu de Vilamoura, 4–7 December 2026

One of the biggest amateur golf competitions in Portugal, held since 1987. The 38th edition starts with a practice round on Friday 4 December, followed by three competition rounds across the [Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course), [Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium) and [Pinhal](/courses/vilamoura-pinhal). It's a 54-hole medal competition within each category, with net and gross prizes for men and ladies. **Maximum handicap:** 24 for men and 28 for ladies. **Entry:** €495 per golfer, including three rounds, range balls, a pull trolley, halfway snacks, a welcome cocktail, a cocktail evening and the gala dinner with prize giving; €145 for non-golfers. Register online through Vilamoura Golf.
Vilamoura International Golf Classic, 9–16 January 2027

A week-long event for amateurs from around the world, with a practice round on [Pinhal](/courses/vilamoura-pinhal) and competition rounds on [Laguna](/courses/vilamoura-laguna), [Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium) and the [Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course). **Maximum handicap:** 24 for men and 28 for ladies. It's sold as a package with seven nights at the Hilton Vilamoura with breakfast, five rounds, a pull trolley, range balls, snacks on the course, two cocktail evenings and a farewell dinner: **€1,313 per golfer sharing a twin room**, €1,715 in a single room, and €667 for a non-golfer sharing. Register with the Hilton Vilamoura events team.
Vale do Lobo Amateur Week, 24–30 January 2027

The 33rd edition, played on the [Royal](/courses/vale-do-lobo-royal) and [Ocean](/courses/vale-do-lobo-ocean) courses. Two Stableford qualifying rounds decide who goes through to a singles matchplay knockout, alongside greensomes and fourball days for everyone, with a prize-giving on the final Saturday. **Maximum handicap:** 26 for men and 32 for ladies. **Entry for visitors:** €756, which includes seven days of unlimited golf and the prize-giving dinner or lunch. The Play & Stay package with seven nights in the resort starts **from €1,089** per person, based on full room occupancy, and a non-golfer option costs €530. **Closing date:** 17 January 2027.
Quinta do Lago Golden Tournament

The 2026 edition was listed for late November and early December, with five rounds: two on [Laranjal](/courses/quinta-do-lago-laranjal), one on [North](/courses/quinta-do-lago-north) and two on [South](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south). The club's page lists **€1,122 per person**, including a buggy, electric or pull trolley, range balls, a welcome cocktail, a midweek dinner and a gala dinner with prize giving. Accommodation isn't included. Watch the Quinta do Lago website for future dates.
East Algarve Golf Trophy, 6–13 February 2027

Five rounds across the eastern Algarve, at [Benamor](/courses/benamor), [Castro Marim](/courses/castro-marim), [Monte Rei](/courses/monte-rei), [Quinta do Vale](/courses/quinta-do-vale) and [Quinta da Ria](/courses/quinta-da-ria), with a free day midweek. According to the agency's calendar, prices start at €1,133 per person sharing, with seven nights at Vila Galé Tavira, breakfast, shared car hire, a welcome reception and a prize-giving dinner.
Penina Golf Week, 9–15 May 2027

Three competition rounds and a pairs finale on the [Penina Championship](/courses/penina-championship) course, the Algarve's first. According to the agency's calendar, it costs €803 per person sharing, with six nights at the Penina Hotel & Golf Resort.
Summer tournaments in Vilamoura
If you're visiting in summer, Vilamoura Golf runs a series of four individual competitions in August across its four courses. Check the Vilamoura Golf website for dates and entry details.
Professional and championship golf to watch

**Portugal Invitational (PGA Tour Champions).** The PGA Tour's over-50s tour held its first event in Portugal at The Els Club Vilamoura from 31 July to 2 August 2026, as part of a five-year partnership. Dates for 2027 hadn't been announced when we checked. The same course, then called Victoria, hosted the European Tour's Portugal Masters from 2007 to 2022.

**Portuguese International Amateur Championships.** The Portuguese Golf Federation's 2027 calendar puts the 98th Portuguese International Ladies Amateur Championship at [Penina](/courses/penina-championship) on 27–30 January, and the men's championship at [Amendoeira](/courses/amendoeira-faldo) on 10–13 February. These are championships for elite amateurs, but they're a chance to see top amateurs on courses you can play yourself.
Tips for entering a tournament

**Check the handicap limit first.** Limits differ from event to event, and some are lower than the usual 28 for men and 36 for ladies needed to play the courses. See [do you need a handicap to play golf in the Algarve?](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve)
**Enter early.** Places can be limited and some events set closing dates, such as 17 January 2027 for Vale do Lobo's Amateur Week.
**Plan around tournament weeks.** If you're not playing in an event, check whether a course you want is hosting one during your trip, as visitor tee times may be harder to find.
**Bringing a non-golfer?** Several events offer a cheaper partner option that includes the social evenings, such as €145 at the Grande Troféu and €530 for Vale do Lobo's Play & Stay package.

**Where to stay:** if the tournament doesn't include accommodation, see our guides to [golf hotels near Vilamoura](/guide/golf-hotels-near-vilamoura), [hotels near Vale do Lobo](/guide/hotels-near-vale-do-lobo-golf), [hotels near Quinta do Lago](/guide/hotels-near-quinta-do-lago-golf) and [hotels near Penina](/guide/hotels-near-penina-golf-resort).
Algarve golf tournaments: common questions
Can visitors enter golf tournaments in the Algarve?

Yes. Events such as the Vilamoura International Golf Classic, the Grande Troféu de Vilamoura and Vale do Lobo's Amateur Week are open to amateurs with a valid handicap certificate, and Vale do Lobo publishes a separate entry fee for visitors.
When is the Algarve golf tournament season?

Mostly from late November to March, with more events in May. There are fewer in summer, although Vilamoura runs a series in August. See our [guide to the Algarve golf season](/guide/algarve-golf-season-best-time-to-play-golf) for what each month is like.
How much does an Algarve golf tournament cost?

It depends on what's included. Among the events in this guide, entry only ranges from €495 at the Grande Troféu de Vilamoura to €756 for visitors at Vale do Lobo's Amateur Week, while week-long packages with accommodation start at about €800 to €1,300 per person sharing.

content.text: [Boavista](/courses/boavista) is a hillside course by Howard Swan on the west side of Lagos, with views over the Bay of Lagos to the east and the Monchique hills to the north. Its 6th and 8th holes play over a ravine, and the back nine drops down to streams, lakes and bridges.

excerpt: Sir Henry Cotton's first Algarve course against the one Pestana calls his last, 15 minutes apart near Portimão. A long, historic par 73 or a shorter, cheaper par 70? Here's how Penina and Alto Golf compare.

content.text: Between Portimão and Alvor, 15 minutes apart, sit two courses linked to the same man: Sir Henry Cotton, three-time Open champion. **Penina** was the first 18-hole course built in the Algarve, in 1966. **Alto Golf**, opened in 1991, is described by its operator Pestana as the last course Cotton designed. Their names may be linked, but they play very differently.
Penina Championship: where Algarve golf began

Penina's [Sir Henry Cotton Championship Course](/courses/penina-championship) was built on former rice paddy fields, which explains its streams and water hazards on flat ground. It is a long course: **par 73 and 6,273 metres** from the white tees. The back nine alone is par 38, because four of its five par 5s come in pairs. With official slope ratings of 143 from the whites and 138 from the yellows, it is one of the more demanding courses in the western Algarve.

The club says the course has hosted the Portuguese Open ten times. Its signature hole is the par-3 13th, with a lake on the right, which the club notes was voted one of the best 500 holes in the world. You need a handicap certificate, with a maximum of 28 for men and 36 for ladies.

Penina has not published a visitor price list since 2024/25, when its online rates ran from €85 to €121. Check our [Penina green fees page](/courses/penina-championship/green-fees) for current prices before you book.
Alto Golf: shorter, cheaper, more welcoming

[Alto Golf](/courses/alto-golf) in Alvor was inaugurated in 1991. Today it is a much shorter course than Penina: the current official scorecard shows **par 70 and 5,432 metres** from the white tees. Its 16th hole was once famous as a 600-metre-plus par 5, one of the longest holes in Europe. It has since been shortened, and the longest hole is now the par-5 18th at 506 metres.
Alto is also the more welcoming of the two for higher handicappers: its official scorecard sets a **handicap limit of 36 for both men and ladies**. It has a driving range and golf academy.

Pestana's published prices are **€75** in December, January and June to August, €115 in November, February, May and September, and €140 in March, April and October. Twilight rounds from 3pm are €50 ([current Alto Golf green fees](/courses/alto-golf/green-fees)).
Which one should you play?

**Play Penina** for the history and the challenge. It is a long, flat championship course where the Algarve's golf story began. It suits lower handicappers who want a proper test. **Play Alto Golf** if you want a more relaxed, shorter round at a lower price, if your handicap is above 28, or if you are fitting golf around a beach holiday in Alvor. Being so close, they also make an easy pair for two days' golf.
Where to stay

Penina has its own five-star hotel, the [Penina Hotel & Golf Resort](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/penina-hotel-golf-resort.html), which scores 8.5 on Booking.com. Hotel guests pay reduced green fees, and the "Best Available Rate for Golfers" room offer includes a free round every day. Alto Golf has no hotel of its own, but Alvor's beach hotels are only a few minutes away. Our guide to [hotels near Penina Golf Resort](/guide/hotels-near-penina-golf-resort) covers both.
Both courses are about 75 to 80 km from Faro Airport by road. A [pre-booked transfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA) is the easiest way to get there with your clubs if you are not hiring a car.

content.text: If you are staying in the far west of the Algarve, around Lagos, Salema or Sagres, two courses keep coming up: **Santo António**, the westernmost course in the Algarve, and **Palmares**, above Meia Praia beach. They are about 30 minutes apart by car and very different in price and style. Here is how to choose.
Santo António: the Algarve's westernmost course

[Santo António Golf](/courses/santo-antonio), formerly known as Parque da Floresta, was designed by Pepe Gancedo and opened in 1987. It runs over the hills behind the fishing village of Salema, near Budens. It is **par 71 and 5,712 metres** from the white tees, and the club describes it as a mixture of heath and parkland.

Its signature hole is the short par-3 5th. The par-5 9th, the hardest hole on the card, finishes with a steep uphill third shot over a ravine. On the way home, the 15th plays over a lake and water comes into play on the 16th and 17th. The terrain is hilly, so the club recommends a buggy.

Santo António is one of the best-value 18-hole rounds in the Algarve. Its official 2026 rates are **€57** for most of the year and €68 from March to May and in September and October. Twilight rounds from 1:30pm are €35 ([current Santo António green fees](/courses/santo-antonio/green-fees)). The club doesn't publish a handicap limit, so bring your certificate and check when you book.
Palmares: 27 holes above the beach

[Palmares](/courses/palmares), on the far side of Lagos, opened in 1975. Robert Trent Jones Jr. redesigned it in 2011, creating 27 holes in three nines: Alvor and Lagos are parkland and lakes, and Praia is links golf by the sea. The club says 90% of its tee boxes have ocean views, and in October 2026 the course was finishing improvements that include wider fairways and more short grass around the greens.

It costs a lot more. Green fees on the club's online booking start at **€138** and reach €183 in spring and early autumn, with a winter rate including a shared buggy that was €105 when we checked ([current Palmares green fees](/courses/palmares/green-fees)).
Which one should you play?

**Choose Santo António** if you are staying around Salema, Burgau or Sagres, want a relaxed round, or are playing several days and watching the budget. At €57 it costs well under half of Palmares. **Choose Palmares** if you want one memorable round with sea views and links golf by the beach, and don't mind paying for it. Staying in Lagos itself, Palmares is closer at about 15 minutes, against around 25 minutes to Santo António.
Where to stay

At Santo António, the resort's own villas are listed on Booking.com as [Quinta da Floresta - Santo António Villas, Golf & Spa](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/parque-da-floresta.html), where they score 7.9. At Palmares, the five-star [Palmares Beach House Hotel](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/onyria-palmares-beach-house-hostel.html) scores 8.9. Lagos, between the two, has the widest choice of hotels.

This is the most remote corner of the Algarve: Santo António is more than 100 km from Faro Airport by road. A [hire car](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw) makes the most sense for exploring the far west, or you can book a [private transfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA) to your hotel.

Want to compare more courses nearby? [Open the course comparator](/?compare=santo-antonio,palmares), read [Palmares vs Boavista](/guide/palmares-vs-boavista-which-lagos-golf-course-should-you-play), or see our [Vila do Bispo](/vila-do-bispo/golf-courses) and [Lagos](/lagos/golf-courses) golf course pages.

excerpt: The Algarve's cheapest 18-hole courses ranked by their real 2026/27 green fees, from €57 at Santo António, plus nine-hole rounds from €22 and the best twilight deals.

content.text: Golf in the Algarve doesn't have to mean paying €200 a round. The most famous courses, such as the Vilamoura Old Course, Monte Rei and Quinta do Lago South, start at €188 to €215 for a single round. But plenty of full 18-hole courses cost a third of that. Here are the **cheapest golf courses in the Algarve**, ranked on their real green fees.
How we ranked them

Each price is the **lowest standard green fee a visitor can book for one round on their own**: no member, resident, junior or multi-round rates, and no packages that bundle a buggy. We took prices from each club's official price list or its own online booking for the 2026/27 season, checked in October 2026. Twilight rates are listed separately below. Prices change with the season, and most clubs that sell online adjust them day by day, so treat each figure as a starting point. Every course links to its own green fees page with the month-by-month prices. This ranking only covers courses whose prices we could check, so another course may be cheaper on a given day.
The 10 cheapest 18-hole golf courses in the Algarve
1. Santo António, Vila do Bispo: from €57

[Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio) is the cheapest 18-hole course in the Algarve and also the westernmost, in the hills behind the fishing village of Salema. Its official 2026 rates are **€57** for most of the year and €68 from March to May and in September and October, with twilight rounds from 1:30pm for €35. It is par 71 and 5,712 metres, designed by Pepe Gancedo, and hilly enough that the club recommends a buggy. The club doesn't publish a handicap limit, so check when you book. [Santo António green fees](/courses/santo-antonio/green-fees)
2. Espiche, Lagos: from €65

[Espiche](/courses/espiche), west of Lagos, was designed by Peter Sauerman and opened in 2012. It plays 5,890 metres, par 72, through native scrub with views to the Monchique hills. On the club's own online booking it cost **€65** in December and €68 for most of the low and shoulder months, rising to €99 in spring. Summer twilight rounds were €54. [Espiche green fees](/courses/espiche/green-fees)
3. Benamor, Tavira: from €66

[Benamor](/courses/benamor), just outside Tavira, was laid out from Sir Henry Cotton's plans and opened in 2000. At 5,497 metres, par 71, it is one of the shortest 18-hole courses in the region. Its internet rates are **€66** in low season (December, January and June to August), €95 in mid-season and €103 in high season, with afternoon tee times in low season for €59. The handicap limit is 28 for men and 36 for ladies. [Benamor green fees](/courses/benamor/green-fees)
4. Quinta do Vale, Castro Marim: from €67

[Quinta do Vale](/courses/quinta-do-vale), near the Spanish border, is a Seve Ballesteros design that opened in 2007. It plays 6,206 metres, par 72, with views over the Guadiana River. On the club's online booking it was **€67** in December and €68 in January and from June to August, rising to €99 in spring. The handicap limit is 28 for men and 36 for ladies. [Quinta do Vale green fees](/courses/quinta-do-vale/green-fees)
5. Boavista, Lagos: from €74

[Boavista](/courses/boavista), on the edge of Lagos, is a hillside Howard Swan design from 2002 with views over the Bay of Lagos. Its online rate starts at about **€74** in low season, and its published rates for November 2026 to December 2027 run from €86 to €126. It has the strictest handicap rule on this list: 26 for men and 34 for ladies. [Boavista green fees](/courses/boavista/green-fees)
6. Alto Golf, Alvor: from €75

[Alto Golf](/courses/alto-golf) in Alvor, which Pestana describes as the last course Sir Henry Cotton designed, costs **€75** in December, January and June to August, €115 in November, February, May and September, and €140 in March, April and October. Twilight rounds from 3pm are only €50. It is par 70 and 5,432 metres, and it accepts handicaps up to 36 for men and ladies, which makes it one of the easiest full courses to get onto. [Alto Golf green fees](/courses/alto-golf/green-fees)
7. Penina Championship, Portimão: from about €77

[Penina Championship](/courses/penina-championship), Sir Henry Cotton's 1966 course and the first 18-hole course built in the Algarve, is a surprise at this end of the list. Penina hasn't published a visitor price list since 2024/25, so our figure comes from booking agents: from about **€77** when we checked in September 2026. Its last official list started at €85 online. The handicap limit is 28 for men and 36 for ladies. [Penina green fees](/courses/penina-championship/green-fees)
8. Salgados, Albufeira: from €78

[Salgados](/courses/salgados), on flat coastal land behind Praia da Galé, has water in play on almost every hole and the Salgados Lagoon nature reserve next door. On the club's online booking it cost **€78** in January, July and August and up to €139 in spring and autumn. Twilight rounds started at €47 in those cheaper months. The handicap limit is 28 for men and 36 for ladies. [Salgados green fees](/courses/salgados/green-fees)
9. Morgado and Alamos, Portimão: from €82

The twin NAU courses north of Portimão share a clubhouse, a practice ground and a price list. [Morgado](/courses/morgado) is the longer and more open of the two at 6,581 metres, par 73; [Alamos](/courses/alamos) is shorter and tighter at 5,710 metres, par 71. Both cost **€82** in January and December (and in high summer) on the club's online booking, rising to €128 in spring. The handicap limit is 28 for men and 36 for ladies. Read [Alamos vs Morgado](/guide/alamos-vs-morgado-which-portimao-golf-course-should-you-play) to choose between them.
10. Castro Marim: from €80 to €87

[Castro Marim](/courses/castro-marim) has 27 holes in three nines near the Spanish border. Its official 2026 price list starts at **€80** for 18 holes in low season, while its online booking was showing €87 when we checked. The club asks for a handicap certificate but doesn't publish a maximum. [Castro Marim green fees](/courses/castro-marim/green-fees)

Just outside the top 10, [Vilamoura Laguna](/courses/vilamoura-laguna) and [Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium) start at **€88** in late autumn and winter, the cheapest way to play in Vilamoura. [Ombria](/courses/ombria), near Loulé, dropped to €85 in June but costs €99 to €216 the rest of the year.
The cheapest nine-hole rounds
If you only want a short round, or you are a beginner, nine holes cost far less:

**[Vale de Milho](/courses/vale-de-milho), Carvoeiro: €22.** A nine-hole, all par-3 course, 926 metres in total, with the same price all year. No handicap is needed, but the club expects you to have had a few lessons.

**[Penina Resort Course](/courses/penina-resort), Portimão: about €28.** A proper nine-hole par 35 by Sir Henry Cotton, with no handicap required. As with the Championship Course, Penina publishes no current rates, so this is the booking agents' price.
**[Balaia](/courses/balaia), Albufeira: €50 day fee.** A nine-hole par-3 course at Balaia Golf Village. The resort says a handicap is required but gives no limit.

**[Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs), Albufeira: €57 to €76.** Nine clifftop holes above the beach, including the famous par-3 Devil's Parlour. Players without a handicap are welcome from the red tees. For more short courses, see [the Algarve's best par-3 golf courses](/guide/the-algarve-s-best-par-3-golf-courses).
The cheapest twilight golf

Twilight rates for late-afternoon tee times can cut the price of a full course by a third or more. The cheapest we found on 18-hole courses were **€35 at Santo António** (from 1:30pm), **€47 at Salgados**, **€50 at Alto Golf** (from 3pm), **€54 at Espiche** in summer and **€55 at Pestana's [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho), [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta) and [Silves](/courses/silves)**. Pestana's [Vila Sol](/courses/vila-sol) and the new [Pestana Ferragudo](/courses/pestana-ferragudo), which start at €140 and €130 for a standard round, offer twilight for €60 and €80. Our [twilight golf guide](/guide/twilight-golf-in-the-algarve) has the start times and how much daylight you get each month. Just check the sunset time: in midwinter a late tee time may not leave enough light for 18 holes.
How to pay less at any Algarve course

**Pick your months.** At most courses on this list, the cheapest months are December, January and June to August. Spring (March to May) and October are the most expensive, because that is when most golfers visit. Our guide to the [Algarve golf season](/guide/algarve-golf-season-best-time-to-play-golf) explains the trade-offs month by month.
**Book on the club's own website.** Many clubs sell their lowest online rates directly. Boavista's web rate, for example, is lower than its published rack rate.

**Look west or east.** The cheapest courses are at the two ends of the Algarve: around Lagos, Portimão and Vila do Bispo in the west, and Tavira and Castro Marim in the east. The Golden Triangle and Vilamoura's best-known courses are the most expensive. Our guide to [west vs east Algarve](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf) compares the two sides, and each town page, from [Lagos](/lagos/golf-courses) to [Tavira](/tavira/golf-courses), puts every local green fee in one table.

**Check your handicap first.** A cheap round is no use if you can't get on. Most of these courses ask for 28 for men and 36 for ladies; Alto Golf accepts 36 for everyone, and Boavista is stricter at 26 and 34. Our guide to [handicap rules in the Algarve](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve) has the details.
Want to compare prices yourself? Open the [Algarve golf course map](/) to see every course's green fees, handicap limits and facilities side by side.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to the Algarve costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

**Booking your rounds?** Our guide to [how to book tee times in the Algarve](/guide/how-to-book-tee-times-in-the-algarve) shows how each course takes bookings, when to book and the cancellation rules to check.

**Playing several times a week?** Our guide to [long-stay golf in the Algarve](/guide/long-stay-golf-in-the-algarve) explains when a short-term membership or a round package works out cheaper than paying per round.

excerpt: Planning a golf stag do in the Algarve? Albufeira or Vilamoura, group booking and cancellation rules, dress codes that catch stag groups out, courses for non-golfers and what the golf costs per person.

content.text: A golf stag do in the Algarve works best when the golf is booked like a group trip, not added as an afterthought. Base yourselves in **Albufeira** if the nights out matter most, or **Vilamoura** if the golf does. Book tee times in four-balls and check each club's group cancellation deadline before you collect anyone's money. And make sure the group knows the dress code: matching stag T-shirts and fancy dress won't get you onto any of the courses whose dress codes we checked.

This guide is for whoever is organising it. It covers where to stay, which courses suit a mixed group, the club rules that catch stag groups out, and what the golf costs per person. **Last checked: November 2026.**
Albufeira or Vilamoura?

**Albufeira** is the Algarve's party town, with its nightlife centred on "the Strip", Avenida Sá Carneiro in Montechoro. The nearest full 18-hole course, [Salgados](/courses/salgados), is 17 minutes from the old town, and there are two short 9-hole courses within 20 minutes. **Vilamoura** is quieter at night, with bars and restaurants around the marina and a casino, but it has more golf on the doorstep: five courses that take visitors.

content.note: Lowest visitor green fee for one round. Drive times from Albufeira old town without traffic (Mapbox). Pine Cliffs: 2026/27 price list; Balaia: 2025/26 price list; the others: each club's online booking, October 2026. Not a complete list: see Albufeira golf courses on our map for all of them.
content.caption: Courses within about 25 minutes of Albufeira

content.text: If you stay in Albufeira and want 18 holes, Salgados is the obvious choice: it's the nearest full course, it's flat, and it's one of the cheapest in this part of the Algarve. If you stay in Vilamoura, [Laguna](/courses/vilamoura-laguna) and [Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium) are the cheapest of its courses. Our guides to the [cheapest golf near Albufeira](/guide/cheapest-golf-near-albufeira) and the [cheapest golf in Vilamoura](/guide/cheapest-golf-in-vilamoura) compare every course month by month, and [where to stay in the Algarve for golf](/guide/where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf) compares the other bases.
Booking golf for a stag group

**Tee times come in fours.** Courses send players out in four-balls, so a group of 8 needs two tee times in a row and a group of 12 needs three. If your numbers don't divide by four, expect to be paired with other golfers. Vilamoura Golf is the strictest we found: it always pairs players into four-balls, and if anyone refuses to be paired, they aren't allowed to play and don't get a refund. It only guarantees a group of its own if you ask in advance and pay the green fees needed to fill the four-ball.
**Groups have longer cancellation deadlines.** Free cancellation for a big group can end a month or more before you play. These are the published deadlines at some clubs:

content.note: Source: each club's published booking conditions, checked 18 November 2026. Some clubs also charge a small cancellation fee. Check the conditions shown when you book, as they can change.
rows: 5 to 23 players: 30 days. 24 or more: at the club's discretion
5 to 15 players: 72 hours. More than 15: 15 days
5 to 15 players: 15 days. More than 16: 30 days
