content.caption: Free cancellation by group size at some Algarve clubs

content.text: **Expect to pay up front.** Quinta do Lago, Quinta da Ria and Quinta do Vale take full payment when you book, and Monte Rei asks for full payment to guarantee a booking. Monte Rei and Vilamoura Golf both say they don't refund for delayed or cancelled flights, so it's worth telling everyone to get travel insurance. If it rains, see [what happens if it rains on your Algarve golf trip](/guide/what-happens-if-it-rains-on-your-algarve-golf-trip).

**Collect names and handicaps early.** Some clubs ask for each player's handicap when you book, and you'll need them anyway to split the group into four-balls. Our guide to [how to book tee times in the Algarve](/guide/how-to-book-tee-times-in-the-algarve) explains how each course takes bookings.
Dress codes: what the stag can't wear

This is the part of the planning that's easiest to overlook. Matching T-shirts and fancy dress are popular on stag dos, but every club whose dress code we checked either bans T-shirts on the course or asks for a collared shirt, and some say so in very plain terms:
**Vilamoura Golf:** no sports shorts, beachwear, blue denim, cargo shorts or T-shirts. Its rules say that if you're not properly dressed, you won't be allowed on the course.
**Pine Cliffs:** no denim, beachwear, tops, T-shirts or **football-style shirts**.
**Salgados:** players wearing T-shirts, lounge, gym or beach wear, **offensive items**, or clothes with holes will need to change before they play.
**Quinta do Vale:** no swim shorts, shirts without a collar, T-shirts, jeans, trainers or leggings.
**Ombria:** shirts must have a collar and sleeves (except for ladies), and no jeans, swimming trunks or short Bermudas.

What works everywhere is a **collared golf shirt**, golf trousers or tailored shorts, and **golf shoes with soft spikes**. If you want the group to match on the course, order printed collared polos rather than T-shirts, and keep the design clean, since Salgados, for one, asks players with offensive items to change. Save the fancy dress for the evening.
Trainers aren't allowed at clubs such as Boavista, Espiche and Quinta do Vale, so anyone without golf shoes should hire a pair. Pine Cliffs, for example, hires golf shoes for €18.
Behaviour, drink and pace of play
Clubs expect groups to keep up and behave, and several say in their rules that they can turn you away or send you off without a refund:
**Vilamoura Golf** can refuse entry to anyone who doesn't behave appropriately, causes a disturbance, disturbs other players, or turns up drunk.

**Ombria** doesn't allow any alcohol on the course except drinks bought from the club, so no coolers or your own cans. Staff can refuse to serve anyone who seems drunk, and players who don't follow staff instructions are asked to leave without a refund.
**Quinta do Lago, Quinta da Ria and Quinta do Vale** say that not following the course rules or the ranger's instructions can mean being removed from the course without a refund.

**Pace of play is enforced too.** Ombria and Monte Rei expect 18 holes in 4 hours 30 minutes. At Pine Cliffs, nine holes should take 2 hours, and players must pick up once they reach double par on a hole. Salgados expects you to keep up with the group in front.

**Don't be late.** Quinta do Lago, Quinta da Ria and Quinta do Vale ask you to check in 30 minutes before your tee time, and if you're late you may lose your slot without a refund. After a big night, an early tee time is the one most likely to go wrong, so think about the timing when you book.
Buggies and hire clubs

**A buggy takes two.** Vilamoura Golf and Boavista allow two players and two bags per buggy, so a group of eight needs four. Book them with the tee times. Among clubs that publish prices, a buggy for 18 holes costs €48 at Benamor, €50 at Salgados and €55 at Pestana's courses, so about €25 each for two players sharing. [Laguna](/courses/vilamoura-laguna)'s Laguna on Wheels offer includes a shared buggy on new bookings made by 31 December 2026, with some dates excluded. See our [golf buggy hire guide](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve).
**Check who can drive.** Boavista, Monte Rei and Ombria don't let anyone under 18 drive a buggy, and Quinta do Vale only lets driving licence holders drive one.

**Everyone needs their own clubs.** Boavista, Ombria and Pine Cliffs all say each player must have their own bag and clubs, so two players can't share a set. Salgados hires a premium Callaway set with a sleeve of balls for €50 for 18 holes, and Pine Cliffs hires a full set for €30 for nine holes. For a big group, flying everyone's clubs can cost more than hiring: compare prices in our [golf club hire comparison](/club-rental) and our guide to [hiring golf clubs at Faro Airport](/guide/hiring-golf-clubs-at-faro-airport).
When not everyone plays golf

Most stag groups mix keen golfers, occasional players and people who've never played. That matters, because most 18-hole courses in the Algarve ask for a **handicap certificate**, usually up to 28 for men and 36 for ladies. Anyone without one can't normally play there on their own.

Near Albufeira, [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs) is the course everyone can play: it's a 9-hole clifftop course, and players without a handicap can play from the red tees. [Balaia](/courses/balaia) is an easy 9-hole par-3 course, but it asks for a handicap, so check with the club first. Further west, [Penina Resort](/courses/penina-resort) near Portimão and [Vale de Milho](/courses/vale-de-milho) in Carvoeiro are also 9-hole courses that don't need one. Our guide to [handicap rules in the Algarve](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve) covers every course.

**Non-golfers who want to come along** should ask the club first. Vale do Lobo, for example, lets players' guests follow them on the course if Golf Reception agrees, as long as they follow the same dress code and join only at the 1st or 10th tee.
Formats that suit a mixed group
A full medal round with everyone counting every shot is slow, and no fun for beginners. Two formats work better for a stag group:

**Texas scramble:** everyone in the four-ball tees off, the team picks the best shot, and everyone plays the next shot from there. It's an informal team format, not part of the Rules of Golf, but it keeps the weaker players in the game and the round moving.

**Stableford:** each player scores points on each hole against their handicap, and once you can't score any more points on a hole, you can pick up. It's an official format in the Rules of Golf, and it fits clubs that want you to pick up, such as Pine Cliffs at double par.
Whatever format you play, each player still has to meet the course's own handicap rule.
Example: three nights in Albufeira, two rounds
Here's one way to fit the golf around a three-night stag do in Albufeira. It's just an example: you could swap either round for a course in Vilamoura.

**Day 1, arrive:** Faro Airport to Albufeira by minivan. In October 2026 we found pre-booked minivans for about €64 per vehicle each way. If you land early, Salgados sells twilight rounds from €47 in January, July and August.
**Day 2, the main round:** 18 holes at Salgados, with a late-morning tee time.
**Day 3, the short round:** nine holes at Pine Cliffs, which everyone can play, with or without a handicap.
**Day 4:** home.

Pine Cliffs: 2026/27 price list, low-season visitor rate (21 November 2026 to 31 January 2027 and 1 June to 14 September 2027); €79 in high season; club hire €30 for nine holes. Not included: flights, accommodation, transfers, food and drink.

content.text: In spring and autumn the same two rounds cost more: Salgados goes up to €139 and Pine Cliffs to €79. For the rest of the trip, see [how much a golf trip to Albufeira costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-albufeira-cost) and [Faro Airport to Albufeira with golf clubs](/guide/faro-airport-to-albufeira-with-golf-clubs). If you're staying in Vilamoura instead, minivans from the airport were about €44 when we checked; see [Faro Airport to Vilamoura with golf clubs](/guide/faro-airport-to-vilamoura-with-golf-clubs).
Booking through a stag company?

Stag-party companies often sell golf as one activity among many. That's fine, but check exactly what you're buying before you pay: **which course**, **how many holes**, whether it's a **par-3 course** or a full 18-hole course, and whether clubs, buggies and transfers are included. Then check that course's handicap rule and dress code against your group, as the rules above still apply.
Golf stag do in the Algarve: common questions
Is Albufeira or Vilamoura better for a golf stag do?

Albufeira has the bigger nightlife, with Salgados and two short courses within about 20 minutes. Vilamoura has more golf close by, with five courses that take visitors, and quieter evenings around the marina. If the golf is the main event, Vilamoura is easier; if the nights out are, Albufeira.
Can we wear matching stag shirts on the course?

Not if they're T-shirts: Vilamoura Golf, Pine Cliffs, Salgados, Quinta do Vale and Boavista are among the clubs that don't allow them. Printed collared golf polos are the safer choice, as long as the design isn't offensive.
Can people who don't play golf join a golf stag do?

Yes, on the right course. Pine Cliffs near Albufeira lets players without a handicap play from the red tees, and Penina Resort and Vale de Milho don't need one either. Most 18-hole courses ask for a handicap certificate.
How far ahead should we book?
As early as you can for a big group, but check the cancellation deadline first: at some clubs, free cancellation for groups ends 30 days or more before you play.

**Organising a bigger group or a golf society?** Our guide to [Algarve golf trips for groups and golf societies](/guide/algarve-golf-trips-for-groups-and-golf-societies) covers resort villas, minivans and booking several tee times together, and [golf transfers without a car](/guide/algarve-golf-transfers-without-a-car) explains how to get the group to the course and back.

excerpt: TUI fly Deutschland charges from €65 each way to carry golf clubs to Faro if you book ahead, and from €105 at the airport. Here are the weight limit and how to add a golf bag.

content.text: TUI fly Deutschland runs seasonal flights to Faro from Düsseldorf, Frankfurt, Hannover and Stuttgart, often as part of a TUI package holiday. It's a separate airline from the UK's TUI Airways, with its own rules: there's no phone-only booking here, but the golf fee is one of the higher ones in this series, and it rises sharply if you leave it until the airport.
Flying from the UK instead? See our separate guide to [TUI Airways and golf clubs](/guide/tui-airways-golf-clubs-why-you-can-t-just-add-them-online).
How TUI fly handles golf bags

Golf equipment is booked as **sports baggage**, separate from your normal checked baggage allowance. The advance price covers **one piece of sports equipment per passenger per sport**, so a golf bag and a bike, for example, would be charged separately.
Weight limit
A golf bag can weigh up to **30kg**, which is enough for a full set, shoes and balls in a padded travel cover. Anything heavier is charged extra, so weigh it before you leave for the airport.
What it costs

According to TUI's own help page, golf baggage costs **from €65 per piece per flight** when booked in advance. Leave it until the airport and it's **from €105 per flight**. That's about €130 return if you book ahead, or €210 if you don't. Prices are listed as "from" amounts, so check the exact figure when you book.
How to add golf clubs to your booking

You can add sports baggage while booking a flight on tui.com, either in the second step or under **Extras**, or later through the TUI service centre. If you've booked a package through a travel agent, ask them to add it. Package and tour-operator conditions can differ from flight-only bookings, so it's worth checking.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

At €65 each way, a TUI fly return costs more than many golfers spend on a full week of hire clubs. Two rental companies operate inside **Faro Airport (FAO)**: ClubsToHire hands sets over in the arrivals hall and MyCaddyMaster at a counter in departures. Either can also take the clubs to your hotel if your package includes a transfer.
Our [club rental directory](/shops) covers the rest of the Algarve too, from Lagos to Tavira.
Bottom line

TUI fly is straightforward: book the golf bag in advance and pay from €65 each way, or pay from €105 at the airport. Since it's one of the pricier fees on Faro routes, compare the return cost with renting before you decide.

excerpt: TUI fly Belgium charges €40 per flight for a golf bag declared when you book, and doubles it if you only mention it at the airport. Here are the rules for Brussels–Faro.

content.text: TUI fly Belgium flies Brussels to Faro in season, mostly for TUI package holidays. Its golf bag fee is one of the more reasonable in this series, but the conditions of carriage are strict about one thing: the airline wants to know about your golf bag **when you book**. Turn up at the airport with one it wasn't expecting and you pay twice as much, and it might not be accepted at all.
How TUI fly Belgium handles golf bags

Golf bags count as **sports equipment** and are charged separately from your normal checked luggage. TUI fly Belgium accepts **one golf bag per passenger**, and the carriage conditions say sports equipment has to be notified at the time of booking.
Weight limit
A golf bag can weigh up to **32kg**, which is one of the more generous limits in this series. That leaves room for a sturdy hard case as well as your clubs, balls and shoes.
What it costs

TUI fly Belgium's conditions of carriage set the golf bag fee at **€40 per flight**. If you only declare it at the airport, an administrative charge of **another €40 per flight** is added, making it €80 each way. Booked properly, a return trip costs about €80; leave it to check-in and it's €160. The airline also warns that late-declared sports equipment may be refused if the hold is already full.
How to add golf clubs to your booking

Add the golf bag while you book on tuifly.be, or ask TUI or your travel agent to add it to an existing booking. With limited hold space on summer holiday flights, the earlier you declare it the better.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

Remembering to declare a golf bag in time is easy enough, but there's still a bag to collect from oversize baggage and get on the transfer coach. Hiring at the airport saves the hassle: ClubsToHire hands sets over in the **Faro Airport arrivals hall**, and MyCaddyMaster works from a counter in the departures terminal. Both can deliver to your hotel instead.
Prefer to pick up near your resort? Browse our [list of Algarve club rental shops](/shops).
Bottom line

TUI fly Belgium's €40 per flight is fair, as long as you add the golf bag when you book. If you leave it to the airport, you'll pay double and risk it being refused. Add the bag when you book the holiday, or rent in Faro instead.

excerpt: Brussels Airlines lists golf equipment at €80 each way within Europe and never includes it on Economy Light. Here are the size rules and fare details for Brussels–Faro.

content.text: Brussels Airlines flies from Brussels to Faro, so it's useful for Belgian golfers and for anyone connecting through Brussels from further afield. As part of the Lufthansa Group, it has similar rules to Lufthansa, with a high fee if you have to pay: **€80 each way** on European routes.
How Brussels Airlines treats golf clubs

Brussels Airlines classes golf as a **special baggage item**. Its sports equipment page lists a fee for golf bags, but also says sports equipment can count toward your free checked baggage allowance on some fares, provided you stay within the number of bags and weight your ticket includes. **Economy Light** never includes golf equipment, and on short-haul **Economy Basic** fares sports gear is charged as an extra. Whether your fare covers it isn't always obvious, so check in Manage Booking before you assume either way.
What counts as one golf bag

One item is **a golf bag with a set of clubs, balls and tees, plus one pair of golf shoes**. Combined dimensions can be up to **220cm**, the same generous size limit as Lufthansa, so oversized travel cases aren't a problem.
What it costs

If you do have to pay, Brussels Airlines' sports equipment page lists golf at **€80 each way** within Europe. That makes a return trip to Faro €160, one of the most expensive in this series. Some fees are calculated in the currency of the departure airport, so the exact amount may differ slightly; check before you book.
How to add golf clubs to your booking
Register your golf bag through **Manage Booking** on brusselsairlines.com or with the service centre before you travel. This matters even if your fare includes it, so the airline knows to expect it.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

At €160 return, flying your own clubs with Brussels Airlines costs about the same as a week's hire of a good set, especially if you're on Light or Basic. Two companies offer rental clubs inside **Faro Airport (FAO)**. ClubsToHire is in the arrivals hall and MyCaddyMaster has a counter in departures, so you can have clubs in hand before you reach the car park.
For hire shops spread across the region, see our [Algarve rental directory](/shops).
Bottom line

Before booking Brussels Airlines, check whether your fare lets your golf bag count as checked baggage. On Light or Basic fares, expect to pay €80 each way, which is high enough that renting in Faro is worth considering.

excerpt: Volotea charges about €60 per flight for a golf bag of up to 32kg on its seasonal French routes to Faro. Here's how to add one and when renting makes more sense.

content.text: Volotea runs seasonal flights to Faro from five French cities: Brest, Lille, Lyon, Nantes and Strasbourg. For golfers in those regions it's often the only direct option. Its golf policy is simple, with one clear fee and a generous weight limit, but that fee is on the high side for a low-cost airline.
How Volotea handles golf bags

Golf bags are booked as **sports equipment**, separately from standard checked luggage. You can add one when you book, later through **Manage your booking** on volotea.com or the Volotea app, or during online check-in.
Weight limit

Each piece of sports equipment can weigh up to **32kg**, one of the most generous limits in this series. Volotea charges around **€12 per extra kilo** above that, so weigh a heavy tour bag before you leave.
What it costs

Volotea's own partner and group-booking pages list sports equipment, including golf bags, at **€60 per flight**. Some third-party sites quote other figures, both higher and lower, so take €60 each way, or about €120 return, as a guide and check the live price in your booking. As with most airlines, adding it online in advance works out cheaper than paying at check-in.
How to add golf clubs to your booking

The simplest time is when you book the flight. If you've already booked, add the golf bag through Manage your booking, which Volotea allows until shortly before departure. Seasonal Faro flights can be full in summer, so don't leave it until the last day.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

Volotea's Faro routes are short, but €120 return for a golf bag is still a fair chunk of a cheap fare. Renting in Faro avoids it. ClubsToHire hands over sets in the **Faro Airport arrivals hall**, and MyCaddyMaster has a counter in the departures terminal. Both deliver to the main golf areas.
Our [full rental directory](/shops) covers the rest of the Algarve, from Lagos to Tavira.
Bottom line

Volotea makes it easy to bring your clubs: one fee of around €60 a flight and up to 32kg. If you're only playing two or three rounds, though, hiring at Faro Airport may cost less than paying to fly your own set there and back.

excerpt: Edelweiss carries your first sports bag free up to 23kg on every flight, including Zurich–Faro. Here's what fits in that allowance and what happens if your golf bag is heavier.

content.text: Edelweiss, the Swiss leisure airline, flies to Faro from Zurich. For golfers, it has the most generous policy in this whole series: your **first piece of sports equipment travels free on every Edelweiss flight**, whatever fare you've booked, as long as it stays under **23kg**.
How the free golf bag works

Edelweiss puts a golf bag in its "normal" sports equipment category, and the first item in that category costs nothing. It's on top of any suitcase your fare includes, so you don't have to choose between your clubs and your clothes.
What counts as one golf bag

One item covers **one golf bag with a set of clubs, balls and tees, plus one pair of golf shoes**. The combined dimensions (height + width + depth) can be up to **200cm**, so a standard travel cover fits easily.
The catch: anything over 23kg

A golf bag weighing **between 23kg and 32kg** moves into Edelweiss's "big" category, which isn't free. Its published fee for flights within Europe is about **€130 each way** (CHF 150 or £140 depending on where you book). That's a big jump for a few extra kilos, so weigh your packed bag at home and move heavy extras into your suitcase if you're close to the limit. Edelweiss doesn't accept anything over 32kg at all, and a second sports bag is charged as excess baggage.
How to add golf clubs to your booking

Register the golf bag in your booking so Edelweiss knows it's coming. If you need to pay for a heavier bag or extra baggage, Edelweiss recommends booking it online **up to four days before departure**.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

With a free 23kg allowance, bringing your own clubs on Edelweiss usually makes sense. Hiring is mainly for golfers who'd go over the limit, or who'd rather not carry a golf bag around a long trip. If that's you, ClubsToHire has a desk in the **Faro Airport arrivals hall** and MyCaddyMaster has a counter in the departures terminal.
See more rental options across the region in our [club hire directory](/shops).
Bottom line
Edelweiss is the golfer-friendliest airline flying to Faro: a golf bag under 23kg flies free on every fare. Keep it under that weight and there's no reason not to bring your own set.

excerpt: Norwegian charges £35 online or £45 at the airport to fly a golf bag to Faro, but the limit is 23kg, one bag per person and golf gear only. Here's how it works.

content.text: Norwegian flies to Faro from Copenhagen, Oslo and Stockholm, which makes it the obvious choice for Scandinavian golfers heading to the Algarve. Its golf bag fee is quite reasonable, but the limits are tighter than most airlines in this series: **23kg, one golf bag per passenger**, and nothing in it except golf gear.
How Norwegian treats golf clubs

Norwegian sells golf bags as a separate **sports equipment** item. You can't book one as an ordinary checked bag, and it doesn't use up a checked bag allowance either. That means a golf bag is always charged on its own, even if your fare already includes a suitcase.
Weight and size limits

The limit is **23kg** per golf bag, and each passenger can check in **only one**. That's lower than the 30–32kg allowed by Condor, Eurowings or Lufthansa, so weigh a heavy tour bag in its travel case before you leave home. Norwegian also says the bag may only contain golf equipment, so your golf clothes and shoes need to go in your normal checked suitcase instead.
What it costs

On Norwegian's UK site, a golf bag costs **£35 each way if booked online** and **£45 at the airport**, on any route. The Scandinavian and US versions of the site show similar amounts in local currency, and Norwegian notes that its charges can change, so check the price shown in your booking for the Faro flight you're actually taking.
How to add golf clubs to your booking

Add the golf bag as sports equipment when you book on norwegian.com, or later through **My Travels**. It's cheaper online and saves time at check-in. If two of you share one large double golf bag, it still counts as one person's item and must stay under 23kg, so separate bags are usually easier.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

A 23kg limit and no clothes allowed in the golf bag means packing for a Norwegian flight takes some planning. Renting is the easiest way round it. Two rental companies operate inside **Faro Airport (FAO)**: ClubsToHire hands sets over in the arrivals hall and MyCaddyMaster from a counter in the departures terminal, and both also deliver to the main resorts.
For other rental companies and resort-based shops, see our [guide to golf club rental in the Algarve](/shops).
Bottom line

Norwegian's fee is fair and the same on every route, but the rules are stricter than average: one bag each, 23kg maximum and golf gear only. If your set fits within those limits, book it online. If it doesn't, a rental set waiting in Faro saves you rearranging your packing.

excerpt: Condor charges from €54.99 each way to fly golf clubs from Germany to Faro if you book ahead, but €120 at the airport. Here are the weight limits, deadlines and how to avoid the higher fee.

content.text: Condor flies to Faro from Frankfurt all year, and adds Hamburg and Munich in season, so it mainly matters if you're starting your golf trip in Germany. Its golf bag rules are clear enough, but one number stands out from everything else in this series: leave your clubs until check-in and the fee jumps from about **€55 to €120** for the same flight.
How Condor handles golf bags

Condor treats golf equipment as **sports baggage** that has to be registered in advance. It's a separate, paid item rather than something that slips inside your normal checked bag allowance, so budget for it on top of any suitcase. The exception is Business Class, where Condor carries the first piece of sports baggage up to 30kg at no extra charge.
Weight and size limits

Sports baggage can weigh up to **30kg** — a couple of kilos less than the 32kg some airlines allow, but plenty for a full set in a travel case. Condor's size limits are generous: a bag up to 200 x 40 x 100cm or 300 x 40 x 60cm, so any standard golf travel cover fits. Condor also says sports bags should only contain the equipment itself, not clothing, so don't plan on stuffing spare outfits around your clubs.
What it costs

Faro sits in Condor's short-haul zone. According to Condor's own sports baggage page, golf equipment costs **from €54.99 each way** when added in advance, rising to a flat **€120 each way** if you pay at the airport. Over a return trip that's roughly €110 if you plan ahead, or €240 if you don't. Fees can change, so check the live price in your booking before you fly.
How to add golf clubs to your booking

Add the golf bag through **My Booking** on condor.com, or through your travel agent if you booked a package. Condor asks for golf bags to be registered **at least 8 hours before departure**, and you can't do it at the self-service kiosks at the airport, which is another good reason not to leave it to the last minute.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

If the €120 airport price has already caught you out once, or you just don't fancy hauling a 30kg bag through Frankfurt, renting is the simpler option. Two rental companies hand over clubs inside **Faro Airport (FAO)** itself — one in the arrivals hall, one at a counter in the departures terminal — and both can deliver to resorts across the Algarve instead if you'd rather collect there.
Staying further west or east? Our [Algarve club rental directory](/shops) lists more shops and the areas they cover.
Bottom line

With Condor, timing is everything. Register your golf bag online in advance and it's a fairly typical fee for a flight from Germany; turn up at the airport without doing so and you'll pay more than twice as much. If you'd rather not have to think about it at all, renting a set in Faro avoids the fee entirely.

excerpt: Air France treats a golf bag as one of your checked bags, and Flying Blue Silver members and above get an extra golf bag on top. Here's how it works for Paris–Faro.

content.text: Air France flies to Faro from Paris-Charles de Gaulle in season, which makes it handy for golfers from France and for anyone connecting through Paris. There's no special golf fee: your golf bag simply **counts as one of your checked bags**. And if you have Flying Blue status, you may be able to bring it **on top of** your normal allowance.
How Air France treats golf clubs

A golf bag is handled like a **standard checked bag**. If your ticket includes a checked bag, your clubs can use it instead of a suitcase. If you want both a suitcase and clubs, the golf bag is charged as an extra bag. On **Light** fares, which include no checked bag at all, you need to buy one bag to bring your clubs.
The Flying Blue golf bag benefit

Air France and KLM's Flying Blue programme gives **Silver, Gold, Platinum and Ultimate** members **one golf bag in addition to their normal allowance** on flights operated by Air France or KLM. If you or someone in your group has status, your clubs can travel free alongside your suitcase. Check the benefit applies to your ticket before you fly, as airline loyalty perks change from time to time.
Weight limits

In Economy and Premium, the golf bag must weigh no more than **23kg**, the same as a normal checked bag; in Business it can be up to **32kg**. Air France also says the bag should contain golf equipment only, so pack clothes in your suitcase.
What it costs if you have to pay

As the golf bag is charged like any extra checked bag, the price depends on your route and when you buy it. It's cheapest when added online during booking or before you travel, and more expensive at the airport. Check the exact price in your booking for the Paris–Faro flight, as it varies with date and fare.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

If your one included bag is already taken up by a suitcase, or you're connecting through a busy hub like Charles de Gaulle, renting saves you checking a second bag. **Faro Airport** has two rental desks on site: ClubsToHire in arrivals and MyCaddyMaster in departures. Both deliver to resorts across the Algarve if you'd rather not take the clubs in the car.
See our [Algarve club hire listings](/shops) for options near Vilamoura, Quinta do Lago and the western Algarve.
Bottom line

On Air France, your golf bag is just another checked bag, so it may cost nothing if your fare includes one and you can manage without a suitcase. Flying Blue Silver members and above get an extra golf bag on top. Everyone else should compare the cost of an extra bag with hiring clubs in Faro.

excerpt: Finnair never counts golf clubs as part of your included baggage. They're charged like an extra checked bag. Here's what that means on Helsinki–Faro flights.

content.text: Finnair flies to Faro from Helsinki, so it's mainly relevant for Finnish golfers and for anyone connecting through Helsinki from further afield. Its rule is simple, if not cheap: golf equipment is **always special baggage** and is **never part of your included allowance**, whatever fare you book.
How Finnair treats golf clubs

Finnair says golf equipment is always classed as special baggage, outside your normal checked allowance, but priced like an **extra checked bag**. If your ticket includes a suitcase, your clubs are charged on top of it. You can pay when you book or later in **Manage booking**.
Weight, size and what can go in the bag

One set of golf equipment means **a golf bag, clubs and one pair of golf shoes**, all counted in the total weight. The limit is **23kg**, and a heavy-bag charge applies above that. The bag can be up to **190cm** long, which is enough for a standard travel case with a driver.
What it costs

Because golf bags are priced like extra checked bags, the cost depends on your fare and how many bags you already have. On Finnair's table for flights within Europe, prepaid extra bags cost roughly **€32–70 one way online**, and **€70–90 at the airport**. On Economy Classic, where a suitcase is already included, you're likely to pay at the higher online rate. Check the exact price for your flight in Manage booking.
Free for Finnair Plus Platinum members

Finnair Plus **Platinum and Platinum Lumo** members can bring one set of golf equipment free of charge. If someone in your group has that status, check whether it applies to your booking before paying.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

As Finnair always charges extra for golf bags, a return trip from Helsinki costs about the same as hiring clubs for a few days, and that's before any connection. Two rental companies are based inside **Faro Airport**: ClubsToHire in the arrivals hall and MyCaddyMaster at a departures-terminal counter.
For hire shops near the resorts, see our [Algarve golf club rental guide](/shops).
Bottom line

On Finnair, your golf bag is always an extra, charged like a second suitcase, unless you hold Platinum status. Book it online to avoid the airport price, or compare the total with hiring a set once you land in Faro.

excerpt: Spending the winter in the Algarve? Short-term golf memberships, multi-round packages and golf societies compared, how long EU and UK visitors can stay, and where to base yourself.

content.text: Spending a month or more of the winter in the Algarve is a popular way to keep playing golf when it's cold and wet at home. If you play several times a week, paying a full green fee every round adds up fast, so it's worth knowing the alternatives: short-term memberships, multi-round packages and local golf societies. This guide covers those, how long you can stay, and where to base yourself.

**Quick answer:** check how long your passport lets you stay first, as the rules differ for EU and non-EU citizens. For golf, a short-term membership can pay for itself if you play often: Vilamoura Golf's three-month membership costs about the same as 18 rounds at the lowest standard fees we found on its courses from January to March. If you play less, a multi-round package or a golf society's discounted green fees may suit you better. **Last checked: November 2026.**
How long can you stay in Portugal?
EU, EEA and Swiss citizens

If you're from Germany, the Netherlands or another EU country, you can stay in Portugal for up to three months with just your passport or national ID card. **If you stay longer than three months, you must register** for a registration certificate (Certificado de Registo de Cidadão da União Europeia) at the local câmara municipal (town hall). Portugal's official ePortugal website explains the process.
UK citizens and other non-EU visitors

British citizens can visit Portugal without a visa for **up to 90 days in any 180-day period**, according to the UK government's travel advice. Days spent in other Schengen countries in the previous 180 days count towards the 90, and overstaying can lead to a ban from the Schengen area. To stay longer, you need a visa or residence permit.

The EU's new Entry/Exit System (EES) is being rolled out, so on your first trip you may have to register your fingerprints and a photo at the border; there's no charge. ETIAS, the EU's planned travel authorisation for visa-exempt visitors, **isn't in operation yet** and isn't accepting applications, according to the EU's official ETIAS website; it will cost €20 once it starts. Rules change, so check the official sources before you travel.
Ways to pay for golf on a long stay
There are four main options, and the right one depends on how often you play and whether you want to stick to one club or try lots of courses.
1. Pay per round

The most flexible option and the best if you want to play many different courses. It's also the most expensive per round if you play a lot. Green fees vary by course and season; our course pages show them month by month, and twilight rates are often cheaper. See [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve) and [best value golf in the Algarve](/guide/best-value-golf-in-the-algarve).
2. Multi-round packages

Some clubs sell packs of rounds that cost less per round than a standard green fee. [Benamor](/courses/benamor), near Tavira, publishes packs that it says are available all year: **20 rounds for €1,200** (€1,050 for tee times after 2pm), 30 for €1,650, 40 for €2,000 and 50 for €2,500, which works out at €50 to €60 a round. Its standard online green fee runs from €66 to €103 between November and March. It also sells 9-hole packs from 2pm: 10 rounds for €459 or 20 for €859. Ask other clubs whether they offer something similar.
3. Short-term memberships
A few clubs publish memberships for a few months, which suit a winter stay. Two examples:

**Vilamoura Golf:** a membership valid for three, six or twelve consecutive months from purchase, giving unlimited rounds (up to 18 holes a day) on [Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium), [Pinhal](/courses/vilamoura-pinhal) and [Laguna](/courses/vilamoura-laguna), plus 40% off the green fee on the [Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course) and for a limited number of accompanied guests. Prices for memberships valid between 1 October 2026 and 31 December 2027:

content.note: Source: Vilamoura Golf's membership page, November 2026. Members can book tee times only 2 to 6 days ahead, depending on the month.
content.caption: Vilamoura Golf Classic membership prices

content.text: **Benamor:** six-month membership from **€2,033** single or €3,095 for a couple, or €2,269 and €3,396 for its TaylorMade version; annual membership is €2,957 single and €4,609 for a couple. It includes unlimited golf, discounts on guests' green fees, buggies, the shop and restaurant, and a driving-range card.
Other resorts run their own membership schemes, but many don't publish prices for short stays, so contact the club. We didn't find a published seniors' rate among the memberships we checked.
4. Golf societies

Golf societies organise regular competitions at different courses at discounted green fees, and several welcome visitors. They're a good way to meet people and play new courses cheaply. Some examples, with prices from their own websites in November 2026:
**6 Golfe Society:** a **90-day pass for €25**, aimed at temporary stays, or €50 a year. Visitors can also play in up to three competitions a year as guests before joining.
**Chez Carlos Golf Society (Algarve Golf Society):** based in Vilamoura, €30 a year, with competitions every Saturday and most Wednesdays across the eastern, central and western Algarve.
**Golf for Greys:** €75 a year, open to all ages despite the name, offering up to 40% off green fees at various courses.
**Forever Algarve:** an annual membership with discounted green fees at partner courses and credit towards free rounds.
When does a membership pay for itself?

A rough example for Vilamoura Golf's three-month membership (€2,169 for one person) over January to March. Using the lowest standard online green fee we found each month at Millennium, Pinhal or Laguna, a round averages about €122 over those three months. On that basis:

content.note: Per-round figures use the cheapest standard online green fee we sampled each month at Millennium, Pinhal or Laguna (October 2026), averaged over January to March. Real prices vary by date and time, so treat this as a guide.
content.caption: Three months in Vilamoura, January to March: paying per round vs membership, one person

content.text: So if you play more than about one and a half rounds a week, the membership is likely to work out cheaper, and the more you play the bigger the saving. If you play less, or want variety, paying per round or joining a society may suit you better.
Where to stay for a month or more

For a long stay, a self-catering apartment usually makes more sense than a hotel room. Many resorts and aparthotels offer lower rates for longer stays, but few publish them, so **ask for a monthly rate** when you enquire. Pine Cliffs, for example, was offering 25% off stays of four nights or more when we checked.

These apartments, all close to a golf course and rated by guests on Booking.com, are examples to start from. Prices are the lowest nightly "from" rates we found in autumn 2026; a monthly rate may be lower.

content.name: Hotel Apartamento do Golfe
content.text: A simple three-star aparthotel a short walk from the Old Course clubhouse, from about €37 a night in October, with studios and apartments with kitchenettes. A budget base if you take out a Vilamoura Golf membership.
perks: Short walk to the Old Course

content.text: Self-catering villas and apartments that list [Benamor](/courses/benamor), 1.8 km away, among their facilities, rated **8.4 on Booking.com**, from about €75 a night in November. A handy base if you take out a Benamor membership or round package.

content.text: The resort's own self-catering apartments and villas, rated **9.1 on Booking.com**, with the [Faldo](/courses/amendoeira-faldo) and [O'Connor](/courses/amendoeira-oconnor) courses and a floodlit 9-hole Academy course on site. Ask the resort about long-stay rates.
