Rated **7.8 on Booking.com**, a little lower than the others, but with golf on the doorstep and a golf academy next door.
content.distanceLabel: On the Gramacho course

content.text: If you'd rather rent a private apartment or villa for the winter, check the distance to your courses, parking, and the deposit and cancellation terms before you pay.
Practical tips for a long golf stay

**Health cover.** EU citizens should bring their European Health Insurance Card (EHIC); UK residents can use a UK Global Health Insurance Card (GHIC) or a valid UK EHIC. Both cover necessary state healthcare, not private treatment, so take out travel insurance too.

**A car for the month.** If you're playing different courses, you'll need a car. A monthly rental can work out cheaper per day than a short hire, so compare rates for your dates: [compare car hire](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw). For the airport run with your golf bags, you can [compare transfers on GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA).

**Your handicap.** Keep your handicap with your home club and bring a certificate: most Algarve courses ask for one, usually 28 for men and 36 for ladies. See [do you need a handicap to play golf in the Algarve?](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve)
**Clubs.** For a long stay you may prefer to bring your own. If you'd rather not, compare options in our [golf club hire comparison](/club-rental).

**The weather.** Winter is mild but it does rain. See [Algarve golf in December](/guide/algarve-golf-in-december), [January](/guide/algarve-golf-in-january), [February](/guide/algarve-golf-in-february) and [March](/guide/algarve-golf-in-march) for temperatures and rainfall.
Long-stay golf in the Algarve: common questions
Can I join an Algarve golf club for just a few months?
Yes, at some clubs. Vilamoura Golf sells three- and six-month memberships, and Benamor a six-month membership. Others may offer similar options without publishing them, so ask.
Is there a seniors' discount on Algarve golf memberships?

We didn't find a published seniors' rate among the memberships we checked. Golf societies are often the cheapest way for retired winter visitors to play regularly, and Golf for Greys, despite its name, is open to all ages.
How long can I stay in the Algarve without a visa?

EU citizens can stay as long as they like but must register after three months. UK citizens and other visa-exempt non-EU visitors can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area.
**Planning a shorter trip?** See [how much a golf trip to the Algarve costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost) for a five-night example.

excerpt: Animawings charges €50 per flight for golf equipment on its seasonal Bucharest–Faro route. Here's the fee, the weight limits and how it compares with renting in the Algarve.

content.text: Animawings, the Romanian airline, runs seasonal flights from Bucharest to Faro, giving Romanian golfers a direct route to the Algarve. Its golf rules are simple: one flat fee per flight. It does have a weight limit question to check before you pack.
How Animawings handles golf bags

Golf equipment travels in the hold as **sports equipment**, booked and paid for separately. Animawings says sports equipment fees are **non-refundable**, so only add it once you're sure you're taking your clubs.
What it costs
Animawings' official fees page lists sports equipment at **€50 per piece per flight**, so about €100 for a Bucharest–Faro return. Check the price shown in your booking, as airline fees can change.
Weight and size limits

Animawings' sports equipment page allows items up to **2 metres long** and **23kg**. Its terms and conditions, however, say an excess-baggage fee applies above **20kg**, with an absolute maximum of 32kg. To be safe, aim to keep your golf bag under 20kg, or check with Animawings which limit applies to your booking.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

Keeping a golf bag under 20kg is a challenge with a full set and a travel case. Renting in Faro avoids having to choose what to leave behind. ClubsToHire has a desk in the **arrivals hall at Faro Airport**, and MyCaddyMaster has a counter in departures.
Browse more rental shops in our [Algarve rental directory](/shops).
Bottom line

Animawings charges €50 per flight for golf equipment, which is easy to budget for. The weight limit is less clear, as Animawings publishes both 20kg and 23kg, so check before you fly or consider hiring clubs in Faro.

excerpt: Azores Airlines charges just €20–25 per golf bag on its Ponta Delgada–Faro flights, but it must be pre-booked. Here are the size rules and how to add it.

content.text: Azores Airlines, part of the SATA group, flies between Ponta Delgada and Faro. It's a small route, but if you're combining golf on São Miguel with a few rounds in the Algarve, or you live in the Azores, this airline has the **lowest golf fee in our whole series**.
How Azores Airlines handles golf bags

All sports equipment, golf included, **must be pre-booked** or confirmed before you check in. If your golf bag fits within your checked baggage allowance, there's no extra charge. If it doesn't, a small fee per piece applies.
What it costs

Azores Airlines' sports equipment page lists golf at **€20 per piece on domestic routes** and **€25 on Europe and Africa routes**. Depending on how Ponta Delgada–Faro is classed on your booking, expect either. Either way, it's far cheaper than any other airline flying to Faro.
Size and weight

Golf equipment can measure up to **130 x 75 x 75cm**. The page lists separate price bands for sports equipment up to 23kg and between 23 and 32kg, so keep your bag under 23kg if you can. The extra 15kg golf allowance mentioned on the same page applies to the sister airline **SATA Air Açores** (inter-island flights), not to Azores Airlines.
How to add golf clubs to your booking
Contact Azores Airlines or use your booking to pre-book the golf bag before you travel. Don't just turn up with it, as the airline says sports equipment needs pre-booking or confirmation.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

At these prices, bringing your own clubs on Azores Airlines makes sense. Hiring is mainly worth it if you'd rather not carry a golf bag on an island-hopping trip. If so, ClubsToHire in the **Faro Airport arrivals hall** and MyCaddyMaster in departures can have a set ready when you land.
For shops across the rest of the Algarve, see our [rental directory](/shops).
Bottom line
At €20–25 per piece, Azores Airlines is the cheapest way to fly golf clubs to Faro, as long as you pre-book the bag. Here, bringing your own set is the obvious choice.

excerpt: Marabu, Condor's sister airline, charges €120 for sports baggage at the airport on its seasonal Hamburg–Faro route. Here's why adding your golf bag in advance is cheaper.

content.text: Marabu is a leisure airline linked to Condor, and it flies to Faro from Hamburg in season. It's a small route, but if you're coming from northern Germany it may be your only direct option. The main thing to know about golf clubs on Marabu is that paying at the airport is expensive.
How Marabu handles golf bags

Golf clubs travel as **sports baggage**, which Marabu's conditions of carriage treat as a paid extra. In **Business Class**, sports baggage up to 30kg travels free, and registration has to be done at least **8 hours before departure**.
What it costs

Marabu's airport service fees list sports baggage up to **30kg** at **€120 per piece** if you pay at the airport. The airline recommends booking extras in advance for the best price, but doesn't publish a separate advance golf fee. A tour operator selling Marabu flights lists sports baggage from about €44.99 each way when booked online with a package, which gives an idea of the difference. Check the advance price in your booking.
How it compares with Condor

As Marabu's rules are close to its sister airline's, our guide to [Condor and golf clubs](/guide/condor-golf-clubs-book-online-or-pay-more-than-double-at-the-airport) is a useful comparison. Condor also charges €120 at the airport and much less if you book ahead.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

If you've forgotten to add your golf bag and are facing the €120 airport fee, renting in Faro could save you money. Pick up a set from ClubsToHire as you walk through **arrivals at Faro Airport**, or from MyCaddyMaster's counter upstairs in the departures terminal.
Check our [Algarve club hire listings](/shops) for more shops and delivery areas.
Bottom line
On Marabu, always add your golf bag in advance. At €120 a piece, the airport price is one of the highest in this series. If you didn't add it in time, hiring a set in Faro will probably cost less.

excerpt: Air Transat counts a golf bag as a normal checked bag on its Toronto–Faro flights, with no oversize charge. Here's how fares, weight and fees work for Canadian golfers.

content.text: Air Transat flies to Faro from Toronto, with Montréal flights due to start in June 2027. For Canadian golfers, it's the main direct way into the Algarve. Golf clubs are simple on Transat: your golf bag is treated like **one of your normal checked bags**, and it isn't charged as oversized.
How Air Transat treats golf clubs

A golf bag counts as a **standard checked bag**. If your fare includes a checked bag, your clubs can be that bag. If you want a suitcase too, or you're on a fare without checked baggage, the golf bag is charged at the normal checked-bag rate. Golf bags are generally **exempt from Transat's oversize fee**, which helps with long travel cases.
Weight limit

Stay under **23kg**. Between 23kg and 32kg, an overweight fee applies, and sources suggest it's substantial. With a hard case and a full set, it's easy to go over, so weigh your bag before you head to the airport.
What it costs if you have to pay

Transat's prices are in Canadian dollars and depend on your fare and route. Third-party guides quote around **C$35–40** for a first checked bag, but those figures may not reflect transatlantic flights. Your booking will show the actual amount. Prepaying online is generally cheaper than paying at the airport, and sources say sports equipment can be prepaid up to 72 hours before departure.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

After an overnight transatlantic flight, waiting at oversize baggage for your clubs isn't much fun. Renting means you can walk straight out. ClubsToHire meets you in the **arrivals hall at Faro**, MyCaddyMaster works from the departures terminal, and either will drop clubs at your resort if you prefer.
Find more rental shops near the main resorts in our [Algarve directory](/shops).
Bottom line

On Air Transat, your golf bag is just a checked bag, with no oversize fee. If your fare includes a bag you're happy to use for clubs, bring them. Otherwise, compare the bag fee with hiring a set when you land.

excerpt: Iberia's seasonal Madrid–Faro flight is handy for Spanish golfers and connections from Latin America. Here's how golf bags are treated and why the fee varies.

content.text: Iberia flies from Madrid to Faro in season. That's useful for golfers in Spain, and for anyone connecting through Madrid from Latin America or other parts of Iberia's network. Unlike many airlines in this series, Iberia doesn't publish one simple golf fee that everyone agrees on, so check a few things before you book.
How Iberia treats golf clubs

On short and medium-haul flights in Europe, golf equipment is generally treated as **sports baggage** with its own fee, not just a normal suitcase. On **Basic** fares, which include no checked bag, you'll always pay. On long-haul flights, golf clubs are more likely to count within your normal checked allowance, which matters if you're connecting in Madrid from outside Europe.
What it costs

We couldn't confirm Iberia's current golf fee from an official source. Third-party guides quote anything from about **€30 to €77 each way** on European routes, depending on the fare and when you add it. Check the price in Manage my booking on iberia.com before you decide.
Size and weight
Plan for a golf bag of no more than **23kg** in Economy. Heavier bags are likely to be charged extra, so weigh yours before you leave home.
If you're connecting through Madrid

If your trip starts outside Europe, your baggage allowance is normally set by the long-haul part of your ticket, and on a single through-ticket your clubs should be checked all the way to Faro. Make sure the Madrid–Faro leg is on the same booking, rather than a separate ticket, so you don't have to collect and re-check your bag.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

With an unclear fee and, for many travellers, a connection in Madrid, hiring clubs at Faro avoids two risks at once: paying more than expected and a golf bag that misses the connection. **Faro Airport** has two rental desks: ClubsToHire in arrivals and MyCaddyMaster in departures.
Our [Algarve club hire directory](/shops) lists more options across the region.
Bottom line

Iberia's golf bag rules depend on your fare and route, and published prices vary a lot. Check the exact price in your booking. If you're connecting, hiring in Faro removes the risk of your clubs arriving late.

excerpt: Luxair charges €80 each way for golf equipment, wants 72 hours' notice and requires a hard case, though LuxairTours packages can include it. Here's what to know for Luxembourg–Faro.

content.text: Luxair flies to Faro from Luxembourg, so it's the natural choice for golfers based in the Grand Duchy and the nearby parts of Belgium, France and Germany. Its rules ask for more preparation than most: Luxair wants **at least 72 hours' notice** and says your clubs must travel in a **hard plastic case**. On a flight-only ticket, you'll also pay one of the higher fees in this series.
How Luxair handles golf equipment

Golf counts as **sports equipment**, booked and paid for separately from your checked bag. Luxair's special equipment page says sports gear must be packed in a **solid protective case made of hard plastic**. A soft travel cover may not meet that rule, so if you only own a padded bag, check with Luxair before you travel.
Weight and size limits

The case can weigh up to **32kg**, with combined dimensions (length + width + height) up to **300cm**, larger than nearly every other airline in this series. Anything bigger or heavier has to go as cargo, which isn't an issue for a normal golf set.
What it costs

Luxair lists a standard fee of **€80 per bag each way** for sports equipment, so €160 for a return trip to Faro. There's a useful exception: on **LuxairTours package holidays** (the Vakanz and Excellence ranges), golf equipment is **included in your baggage allowance**, as long as you book it at least 72 hours before departure. If you're choosing between a flight-only fare and a package, that alone could change the maths.
How to add golf clubs to your booking

Book the golf bag **at least 72 hours before departure**, online, through a travel agency, or by calling Luxair's customer service centre on +352 24561. With that much notice required, it's best to add it as soon as your flight is confirmed.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

If you don't own a hard case, or you're flying flight-only at €80 a leg, renting is worth a look. ClubsToHire has a desk in the **Faro Airport arrivals hall**, and MyCaddyMaster runs a counter in the departures terminal. You can take a set with you there and then, or have it delivered to your accommodation.
You'll find more hire companies in our [directory of Algarve golf shops](/shops).
Bottom line

On a LuxairTours package, flying your clubs is free if you book it 72 hours ahead, so take them. On a flight-only ticket, you'll need a hard case and €160 return, which is when renting in Faro starts to look like the better deal.

excerpt: Icelandair's seasonal Reykjavík–Faro flight links Iceland and North America with the Algarve. Here's how golf bags fit into your baggage allowance and why booking online matters.

content.text: Icelandair flies from Reykjavík-Keflavík to Faro in season. That makes it the obvious choice for golfers in Iceland, and an interesting option for North Americans, since Icelandair's network connects many US and Canadian cities through Keflavík. The good news is that your golf bag doesn't automatically come with a separate fee; it depends on what your fare already includes.
How Icelandair treats golf clubs

On fares that include checked baggage, a golf bag can generally **take the place of one of your included bags**, in which case there's nothing extra to pay. If you want to bring a suitcase and your clubs, or you're on **Economy Light**, which doesn't include any checked bags, the golf bag is charged as an extra bag.
Weight limits
As with Icelandair's standard checked baggage in Economy, plan on a **23kg** limit for a golf bag. A full set in a travel case often comes close, so weigh it before you set off.
What it costs if you have to pay

We couldn't find an up-to-date official Icelandair price for golf bags. The figures online are either old or contradict each other, so we're not quoting one. What sources do agree on is that **adding sports equipment online in advance is cheaper** than paying at the airport. Check the price in Manage booking for your own flights.
If you're connecting from North America

If you're flying via Keflavík from the US or Canada, the baggage allowance on your through-ticket usually applies to the whole journey. That's helpful, as your golf bag is checked once and doesn't need re-booking for the Faro leg. Check that the allowance covers both flights before you go.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

On a long journey with a connection in Iceland, a golf bag is one more thing that can go missing or arrive late. Renting avoids that. ClubsToHire has a desk in the **Faro Airport arrivals hall** and MyCaddyMaster has a counter in departures, so a set can be waiting for you even if your own bag isn't.
For rental shops near your hotel, see our [Algarve club rental directory](/shops).
Bottom line

On Icelandair, a golf bag can usually replace one of your included bags, so whether you pay depends on your fare and whether you're also bringing a suitcase. Book it online if you need to pay. On a long connecting trip, think about whether hiring clubs on arrival is the less stressful option.

excerpt: Two courses 18 minutes apart near Albufeira, at very different prices: the flat, water-lined Salgados by the beach, or Amendoeira's Faldo and O'Connor courses inland. Here's how they compare.

content.text: If you're staying in or around Albufeira, the two full-size courses closest to you are [Salgados Golf](/courses/salgados), down on the coast between Galé and Armação de Pêra, and [Amendoeira Golf Resort](/courses/amendoeira-faldo), inland near Alcantarilha. They're only about 18 minutes apart by road, but they're very different rounds at very different prices. Here's how Salgados and Amendoeira compare, and which one suits your game and your budget.
A flat coastal course or an inland resort with two courses

Salgados is a single 18-hole, par-72 course that opened in 1994 on flat land behind Praia da Galé, next to the Salgados Lagoon nature reserve. Water is the main defence: lakes and lagoons line many of the holes, and the sea breeze adds to the challenge. It's run by Troon and was named World's Best Golf Course Renovation at the 2025 World Golf Awards.

Amendoeira, which opened in 2008, has two 18-hole, par-72 courses side by side in the countryside below Silves: the [Faldo Course](/courses/amendoeira-faldo), designed by Sir Nick Faldo and named Portugal's best golf course at the 2016 World Golf Awards, and the [O'Connor Jnr Course](/courses/amendoeira-oconnor), a greener valley layout with plenty of lakes. If you're choosing between the two, read [Amendoeira Faldo vs O'Connor](/guide/amendoeira-faldo-vs-o-connor-which-silves-golf-course-should-you-play).
Salgados: water, wind and birdlife by the sea

Salgados is a technical course rather than a long one. The greens are relatively flat, but water comes into play on many holes, so the round is about keeping the ball dry and judging the wind off the Atlantic. Its official slope rating is 129 from the back tees and 124 from the yellows, so it's a fair test without being brutal, and the protected lagoon next door means wetland birds are part of the round, especially early in the morning.
Amendoeira: Faldo's championship test and a gentler second course

The Faldo Course is the reason most golfers come to Amendoeira. It's 6,598 metres from the back tees, with rocky outcrops, wild scrub and well-bunkered greens, and it's built around placing the ball in the right spot rather than hitting it a long way. The O'Connor Jnr Course is similar in length (6,708 metres from its back tees, 6,273 from the whites against the Faldo's 6,296) and usually the more forgiving of the two, though its lakes still punish a loose approach.
Green fees: Salgados is the cheaper round

On the official 2026 price list, **18 holes at Salgados cost €91 in low season** (January, July, August and December), €119 in mid season (February, June and November) and €163 in high season (March to May, September and October). Booking on the club's own website has often been cheaper still: we've seen 18 holes from about €78 in low season and around €139 in spring and autumn.

Amendoeira charges the same green fee for both courses. On the resort's own online booking, a round costs from about **€100 in December and January** and around €109 in June, July and August, but it climbs to roughly €190 to €212 in spring and autumn. That's when most golfers visit, so Amendoeira can cost around €70 more per round than Salgados in the same week. Bear in mind that Amendoeira's online green fee includes a buggy, if one is available, while a buggy at Salgados costs €50 extra. See the [Salgados](/courses/salgados/green-fees) and [Amendoeira](/courses/amendoeira-faldo/green-fees) green fees pages for every month.

Salgados also publishes its hire prices: a buggy costs €50 for 18 holes, a trolley €6 and a premium Callaway set with a sleeve of balls €50. If you're bringing your own clubs, read our guide to [hiring golf clubs at Faro Airport](/guide/hiring-golf-clubs-at-faro-airport) for the alternatives.
Handicap, dress code and practice facilities

Salgados sets a maximum handicap of 28 for men and 36 for ladies on its course information, although its rate card says it welcomes golfers of every level as long as they keep up with the group in front. Amendoeira doesn't publish a limit on its own website; golf travel companies list the same 28 for men and 36 for ladies, so bring a handicap certificate to both. Not sure what you need? Read [do you need a handicap to play golf in the Algarve](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve).

Amendoeira's dress code is the stricter of the two: collared shirts with sleeves, tucked into trousers or tailored shorts, plus socks and golf shoes, with no T-shirts or denim. Salgados asks for what you'd wear at any upscale golf club, with closed shoes, and expects you to change if you turn up in T-shirts or beachwear.

For practice, Amendoeira is clearly ahead. It has a driving range, a golf academy with Trackman analysis and a floodlit nine-hole Academy course, which the resort says is the only one in Portugal (see [night golf in the Algarve](/guide/night-golf-in-the-algarve)). Salgados has a short-game practice area, putting and chipping greens, golf simulators and lessons with its teaching professional.
Getting there from Albufeira and Faro Airport

From the centre of Albufeira, Salgados is about 18 minutes by car and Amendoeira about 24. From Faro Airport, Amendoeira is actually slightly quicker, at around 42 minutes along the A22 motorway, while Salgados takes about 47. The two courses are only about 10 km apart, so playing both on the same trip is easy. See all the [golf courses near Albufeira](/albufeira/golf-courses).
Where to stay

Both courses have accommodation on site. At Salgados, the [Algarve Marriott Salgados Golf Resort & Spa](/hotels/algarve-marriott-salgados-golf-resort-spa), the Marriott Residences and the Westin Salgados are part of the same resort, and the club sells Stay & Play packages with all three. Amendoeira has its own apartments and villas, with a minimum stay of two nights. For more options, see the [best hotels near Salgados golf course](/guide/hotels-near-salgados-golf-course).
Which one should you play?

**Play Salgados** if you want a scenic, good-value round close to the beach, you enjoy courses where accuracy and wind matter more than length, or you're visiting in spring or autumn, when the price gap is at its widest. **Play Amendoeira** if you want the Faldo Course's championship test, you're planning more than one round in the same place, or you want proper practice facilities before you tee off. If you're in Albufeira for a week, the honest answer is both: they're 18 minutes apart and offer two very different days of golf.

Want the numbers side by side? [Open the course comparator](/?compare=salgados,amendoeira-faldo,amendoeira-oconnor) to compare Salgados with both Amendoeira courses on price, length, handicap limits and facilities, using our live course data.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Albufeira costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-albufeira-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: On LOT, golf clubs can use your included checked bag on most fares, and cost around €60 each way otherwise. Here's how the rules work on the Warsaw–Faro route.

content.text: LOT Polish Airlines flies from Warsaw to Faro, linking Poland's growing golf community with the Algarve. Like other Star Alliance airlines in this series, LOT doesn't always charge separately for golf clubs: on many fares they can travel **as part of your normal checked allowance**.
How LOT treats golf clubs

If your fare includes a checked bag, your golf equipment can generally take its place as long as it meets the weight and size limits. **Economy Saver** fares include no checked bag on European routes, so on Saver, or if you want a suitcase as well, the golf bag is charged as sports equipment.
What it costs

A LOT fee table lists golf equipment at around **€60 per set each way** on international flights within Europe (250 PLN), and more on long-haul routes. Some third-party sites quote different figures, so treat €60 as a guide and check the price for your flight in Manage booking or with the LOT Contact Center.
Frequent flyer perks

Miles & More **Senator** and **HON Circle** members, and **Star Alliance Gold** members, get an extra piece of baggage that can be golf equipment. If you or someone travelling with you has that status, your clubs could travel free on top of your normal allowance.
Weight limits
Sources disagree on the maximum weight for sports equipment on LOT, so plan for **23kg** if your clubs use a standard checked bag, and check with LOT before travelling with anything heavier.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

If you're on a Saver fare and travelling light, paying €120 return for your golf bag can cost more than the cheapest seats. Hiring in Faro is the easy alternative. ClubsToHire hands over sets in the **airport's arrivals hall**, and MyCaddyMaster at a counter in the departures terminal.
Our [Algarve rental shops page](/shops) lists more options across the region.
Bottom line

On LOT, check your fare first: golf clubs can often use your included bag, and Senator or Star Alliance Gold status adds an extra one. On a Saver fare, expect about €60 each way, and compare that with hiring a set in Faro.

excerpt: United counts a golf bag as a standard checked bag with no oversize fee, so on many transatlantic fares it travels free. Here's what changes on Basic Economy for Newark–Faro.

content.text: United flies from Newark to Faro in season, giving American golfers a direct link to the Algarve. The rules are simple: a golf bag counts as **one of your standard checked bags**, and United waives the oversize fee for golf equipment. Whether it's free depends on your fare.
How United treats golf clubs

Your golf bag is checked like any other bag. On transatlantic Economy fares that include a free checked bag, your clubs can use it. United doesn't charge an oversize fee for golf bags up to **115 linear inches (292cm)**, so a long travel case won't cost extra.
Basic Economy and extra bags

On **Basic Economy** transatlantic fares, sources generally agree you'll pay for your first checked bag, with figures around **US$75 each way**, though they don't all agree. If you're bringing a suitcase and your clubs on any fare, the golf bag will be charged as a second bag. Check the exact fee in your booking.
Weight limit

In Economy, the standard limit is **50lb (23kg)**. Above that, United charges an overweight fee, so weigh your packed bag at home. Moving shoes and balls into your suitcase is the easiest way to save a few pounds.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

If you're on Basic Economy, or you'd rather not risk your own clubs on an overnight flight, renting is worth considering. You'll find ClubsToHire waiting in **Faro's arrivals hall** and MyCaddyMaster at a counter in departures, and both offer delivery to hotels across the Algarve.
For a wider choice of rental shops, see our [Algarve club rental directory](/shops).
Bottom line

On United, your golf bag is just a checked bag with no oversize charge. If your fare includes a free bag, bring your clubs. On Basic Economy, or with a suitcase as well, compare the bag fee with hiring a set in Faro.

excerpt: What April weather in the Algarve means for your golf: afternoons of 21°C, long evenings, courses in top condition and the highest green fees of the year.

content.text: Is April a good month for golf in the Algarve? For conditions, it's one of the best months of the year: afternoons average about **21°C**, there are about five rainy days, the courses are in excellent shape and it stays light until after 8pm. It's also the most expensive month: on 28 of the 30 courses we track, April green fees are the highest of the year.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in April from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay and how to get the most from peak season.
Algarve weather in April for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

content.note: Source: IPMA climate normals 1991–2020 for Faro (station 554) and Sagres (station 533), averaged over 30 years. Rainy days have 1 mm of rain or more; heavy rain days 10 mm or more. Daylight is for the middle of the month; sunset is calculated for the first and last day of April, in Portuguese summer time (the same as UK time).
content.caption: April weather in the Algarve

content.text: April brings the first properly warm afternoons of the year, with an average high of about 21°C in Faro, though mornings still start around 12°C. Rain falls on about five days in the month and heavy rain is rare. Sagres is about a degree and a half cooler in the afternoon, and the far west tends to feel fresher in the Atlantic breeze.
What April weather means on the course

**Fairways and greens.** April is when the Algarve's courses are usually at their best: the grass is growing strongly after the winter rain, fairways are firm and green, and greens are quick and true.

**Tee times.** With more than 13 hours of daylight and sunset after 7.50pm, you can tee off as late as about 3.30pm to 4pm and still finish 18 holes. That opens up an afternoon round after a morning at the beach, or two rounds in one day.
**What to pack.** Short sleeves and a light jumper or windproof for the mornings, plus a light waterproof just in case. The sun is strong by April, so pack sun cream, a cap and sunglasses.
Green fees in April

April is the peak of the Algarve's spring golf season. On 28 of the 30 courses we track, April fees are the highest of the year, so you'll pay full rate almost everywhere. That makes value courses and twilight rounds more important than in any other month.

content.note: The lowest price any visitor can book for one 18-hole round, from each club's official price list or its own online booking, checked in October 2026. All year shows the course's cheapest and dearest months. Prices change, so check before you book.
content.caption: April green fees: 18 holes, visitor rate

content.text: Twilight rounds are the best way to save in April, and the long evenings mean a twilight slot can still give you 18 holes: this April they start from €35 at Santo António and €50 at Alto Golf, and €55 at Pestana's [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho), [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta) and [Silves](/courses/silves). Check the start time when you book. See also [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Where to play in April

Because prices are at their peak almost everywhere, April is the month to think hardest about value. The cheapest 18-hole courses in our table are in the far west and east of the region, such as Santo António, Espiche, Quinta do Vale and Benamor, all around €100 or less.

If you're planning one premium round on your trip, it may be worth moving it to another month: Monte Rei costs €312 in April against €190 in December, and Amendoeira's Faldo Course €212 against €100. If you're weighing up the two ends of the region, read [West vs East Algarve: which side is better for golf?](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf).
Easter, crowds and booking ahead

April is one of the busiest months of the year on the Algarve's courses. The Easter school holidays carry on into early April (Easter Sunday is on 28 March in 2027), and spring golf groups fill the tee sheets throughout the month. Book tee times as early as you can, especially for morning slots at the best-known courses, and book your hotel well ahead.
25 April is a national holiday in Portugal, Freedom Day, so expect some local demand for tee times around that date as well.
Frequently asked questions
Is April a good time to play golf in the Algarve?

Yes, it's one of the best months for conditions: warm afternoons, long days and courses in top shape. It's also the most expensive and one of the busiest months, so book early and look at twilight rates.
Is the Algarve hot in April?
Warm rather than hot. The average high is about 21°C in Faro and 19°C in Sagres, with mornings around 12°C.
Does it rain in the Algarve in April?
A little. Faro averages 39 mm of rain in April over about five rainy days, and Sagres 35 mm over about six. Heavy downpours are rare.
What time does it get dark in the Algarve in April?
The sun sets at about 7.55pm at the start of April and about 8.20pm by the end. You can tee off as late as about 3.30pm to 4pm and still finish 18 holes.
Plan your April golf trip

For a month-by-month comparison of weather, prices and crowds across the whole year, read our guide to the [Algarve golf season and the best time to play](/guide/algarve-golf-season-best-time-to-play-golf), or see the month either side: [Algarve golf in March](/guide/algarve-golf-in-march) and [Algarve golf in May](/guide/algarve-golf-in-may).

Bringing your own clubs? Check what your airline charges in [our Guide](/guide), or see your options for [hiring golf clubs at Faro Airport](/guide/hiring-golf-clubs-at-faro-airport). Not sure whether you need a handicap certificate? Read [do you need a handicap to play golf in the Algarve](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve).
Playing several courses? Use **Find Your Base** on the [Algarve Golf Map](/) to pick your courses and see the area that sits closest to all of them, along with well-rated hotels nearby.

excerpt: SAS lets premium passengers and EuroBonus Silver members and above use a checked bag allowance for golf clubs. Everyone else pays a fee. Here are the rules for flights to Faro.

content.text: SAS flies to Faro from Copenhagen and Stockholm, plus Gothenburg and Oslo in season, so it's mostly relevant for golfers coming from Scandinavia. Whether you pay for golf clubs on SAS depends on who you are as much as what you book: some travellers can **swap an included suitcase for a golf bag** at no extra cost, while everyone else pays a sports equipment fee.
Who can swap a checked bag for a golf bag

SAS lets you use one of your included checked bags for sports equipment if you're travelling in **SAS Plus (Premium Economy) or Business**, or if you hold **EuroBonus Silver, Gold or Diamond** status. In that case the golf bag simply replaces a suitcase, so there's nothing extra to pay as long as you stay within your allowance. Sports equipment is **not included on Light fares**, whatever your status.
Weight and what counts as one golf bag

SAS counts **one golf bag with clubs plus one pair of golf shoes** as a single item, with a maximum weight of **23kg**. That's lower than the 30–32kg some airlines allow, so if you travel with a full tour bag and a hard case, weigh it at home first.
What it costs if you have to pay

SAS's published fee table lists golf bags with skis and snowboards, at around **€85 each way** on routes between Scandinavia and the rest of Europe. Some other sources quote lower prices for golf bags added early in My Trips, and SAS itself says extra baggage is cheaper when bought at least 14 days before departure. As the numbers vary, treat €85 as a rough upper estimate and check the price shown in your own booking.
How to add golf clubs to your booking

Add or register the golf bag in **My Trips** on flysas.com as early as you can. If you're eligible to swap, registering it still makes sure the airline knows it's coming. If you're paying, booking early is the simplest way to avoid the highest price.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

If you don't have SAS status or a premium ticket, a return golf bag fee can cost more than a week of hired clubs. Two rental companies are based inside **Faro Airport (FAO)**: ClubsToHire in arrivals and MyCaddyMaster at a counter in departures. Collect a set when you land, or have them deliver it to your hotel.
More rental companies, including shops near the main resorts, are listed in our [Algarve golf shops directory](/shops).
Bottom line

On SAS, golf clubs can travel free if you're on a Plus or Business ticket or hold EuroBonus Silver or above, because the bag replaces a suitcase. On other tickets, expect a separate fee of up to around €85 each way. In that case, add up the return trip and compare it with renting in Faro before you book.

excerpt: Where to practise golf in the Algarve: driving ranges, short-game areas and range-ball prices published by the clubs, from Lagos to Castro Marim.

content.text: Most Algarve golf courses have somewhere to warm up, but practice facilities vary a lot: some clubs have big grass ranges with dozens of bays and target greens, others a netted hitting area or just a chipping and putting green. This guide brings together what the clubs themselves publish about their driving ranges, short-game areas and range-ball prices, area by area, so you can find a good place to practise near where you're staying.

It isn't a complete list. Some clubs publish very little about their practice facilities, so if a course you like isn't here, it may still have a good range: check its page on our site or ask the club. Opening hours are rarely published anywhere, so it's always worth checking before you go.
What range balls cost in the Algarve
Only some clubs publish a price for range balls. These are the prices on their own price lists:

content.note: Prices as published by each club, checked November 2026. Clubs change prices, so confirm at reception. Benamor sells range tokens at reception but does not publish the price; at Pine Cliffs, range balls are included in the unlimited-golf packages.
rows: Day fee €25 with unlimited balls, €15 after 13:30
content.caption: Range-ball prices published by the clubs

content.text: Western Algarve: Lagos, Alvor and Portimão
Morgado and Álamos

The [practice ground](/courses/morgado/practice-facilities) shared by [Morgado](/courses/morgado) and [Álamos](/courses/alamos) near Portimão is a big one: two natural-grass tees with room for 35 players each, ten target greens marked every 50 metres, two chipping greens with bunkers, and putting greens at each tee. The [Morgado Golf Academy](/golf-academies/morgado-golf-academy) teaches here.
Penina

[Penina](/courses/penina-championship/practice-facilities) has an 80-metre-wide driving range on natural Bermuda grass, with target greens, a chipping green, a practice bunker and a putting green. Its nine-hole Resort Course needs no handicap certificate, so it's a natural next step after a session on the range. See the [Penina Golf Academy](/golf-academies/penina-golf-academy) for lessons and clinics.
Palmares
[Palmares](/courses/palmares/practice-facilities) has a 300-yard driving range set in a natural valley above Lagos, with short-game areas and putting greens, and views of the coast.
Espiche and Santo António

Near Lagos, [Espiche](/courses/espiche/practice-facilities) has a range for up to 29 players on both natural grass and mats, a 400 m² putting green and an 800 m² chipping area. Further west, [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio/practice-facilities), near Vila do Bispo, has 10 open-air and 4 covered practice tees, a putting green beside the range and a short-game area behind the 1st tee, and its 2026 price list gives a token of 48 balls at €4.
Boavista

[Boavista](/courses/boavista#practice) near Lagos has a short-game area with three greens: one for putting, one for chipping and one surrounded by bunkers. Its driving range is currently closed for repair work, with no reopening date given, so check with the club before you go.
Central Algarve: Carvoeiro, Silves and Albufeira
Pestana Golf

The Pestana Golf Academy has covered hitting bays, eight target greens, a chipping area with practice bunkers and a large putting green, and Pestana's price list gives a range token of 50 balls at €7 for its courses ([Gramacho](/courses/gramacho), [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta), [Silves](/courses/silves), [Alto](/courses/alto-golf) and [Vila Sol](/courses/vila-sol)). Pestana's website doesn't say which course each range is at, so ask when you book.
Amendoeira

[Amendoeira](/courses/amendoeira-faldo#practice) has a driving range, putting greens and long and short game practice areas, plus a floodlit nine-hole par-3 academy course between the Faldo and O'Connor courses, useful for evening practice. See the [Amendoeira Golf Academy](/golf-academies/amendoeira-golf-academy).
Balaia, Salgados and Pine Cliffs

[Balaia](/courses/balaia/practice-facilities) has a practice range next to the clubhouse and publishes ball prices from €2 for a bucket of 24. [Salgados](/courses/salgados#practice) lists a short-game practice area, a putting green, a chipping green and golf simulators on its website; independent listings say it also has a driving range, but the club's own site doesn't mention one, so ask. At [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs#practice), range balls are included in the resort's unlimited-golf packages.
Vilamoura, Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo
Vilamoura

Each of the four Vilamoura courses ([Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course), [Pinhal](/courses/vilamoura-pinhal), [Laguna](/courses/vilamoura-laguna) and [Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium)) has its own practice facilities, with a driving range, putting green and chipping area. The [Vilamoura Golf Academy](/golf-academies/vilamoura-golf-academy) is based at Pinhal, where the clubhouse looks over the range.
Pinheiros Altos

[Pinheiros Altos](/courses/pinheiros-altos/practice-facilities) near Almancil publishes a practice fee for visitors: €25 for a day with unlimited balls, or €15 after 13:30. It has room for up to 30 players, two practice putting greens, a chipping and bunker area and three teaching bays, one of them a Titleist fitting centre.
Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo

[Quinta do Lago](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south#practice) has two practice ranges, one at Quinta do Lago and one at Laranjal, plus the Paul McGinley academy and a TaylorMade Performance Centre for fitting. Next door, the [Vale do Lobo](/courses/vale-do-lobo-royal#practice) academy has a netted hitting area rather than an open range, with a grass short-game area with bunkers and a putting green by the clubhouse.
Eastern Algarve: Tavira and Castro Marim
Benamor

[Benamor](/courses/benamor/practice-facilities) near Tavira describes its range in detail: 16 mats at the front, practice on grass at the top end with target flags and distance markers, a chipping and pitching green with a bunker, and a nine-hole putting green between the clubhouse and the range. Balls are sold as tokens at reception.
Quinta da Ria and Quinta do Vale

[Quinta da Ria](/courses/quinta-da-ria/practice-facilities) has a 300-metre range with 70 grass bays and 5 covered bays, a Foresight simulator, a chipping area with a bunker and a nine-hole pitch-and-putt academy course. Close to Castro Marim, [Quinta do Vale](/courses/quinta-do-vale/practice-facilities) has a very large range in two zones (room for 30 players on one side and 65 on the other), a chipping green with a bunker, putting greens and a short-game academy course.
Castro Marim and Monte Rei

[Castro Marim](/courses/castro-marim/practice-facilities) sells balls in three bucket sizes and has a range card that doubles your credit when you top it up with €50 or more. [Monte Rei](/courses/monte-rei#practice) has a driving range, short-game areas and a putting green, improved during its 2026 renovation, and a Swing Studio for teaching and fitting.
Tips for practising in the Algarve
**Check the opening hours.** Very few clubs publish them, and ranges can close earlier than the course or be busy with lessons at certain times.
**Grass or mats?** Where the club says so, we've noted it on each course page. Benamor and Espiche, for example, have both mats and grass.

**Want lessons too?** Many of these practice grounds are home to a teaching academy. See our guide to [golf lessons in the Algarve](/guide/golf-lessons-in-the-algarve) and the [golf academies](/golf-academies) pages for prices and programmes.

excerpt: On most SWISS fares a golf bag travels within your normal baggage allowance, but Economy Light and short-haul Basic fares are excluded. Here's how it works for Geneva–Faro.

content.text: SWISS flies to Faro from Geneva in season, which makes it a useful option for golfers in western Switzerland and nearby France. As a Lufthansa Group airline, its rules are close to Lufthansa's: on most fares, your golf bag **travels free within your normal baggage allowance**, but the cheapest fares don't include it.
How SWISS treats golf clubs

SWISS classes golf equipment as "normal" sports baggage. If it fits within your fare's checked baggage allowance, it travels **at no extra cost** and you don't need to register it separately. The exceptions are **Economy Light**, which has no checked baggage at all, and **Economy Basic on short- and medium-haul flights**, which includes Geneva–Faro. On those fares, a golf bag is always charged as paid sports baggage.
Size and weight

Golf equipment can measure up to **220cm** in total dimensions, the same as Lufthansa and one of the most generous limits in this series. The weight limit follows your fare's checked baggage allowance, which is usually 23kg in Economy.
What it costs if you have to pay

If you're on a Light or Basic fare, or your golf bag goes over your allowance, SWISS charges a sports baggage fee that depends on the route. Published sources disagree on the exact amount for European flights, so we're not quoting one here. Check the price in your booking or with SWISS's baggage calculator before you fly. Paid sports baggage can be registered up to 72 hours before departure.
A tip for frequent golf travellers

SWISS runs a **Golf Traveller** membership that lets members carry golf equipment up to 23kg free on SWISS, Lufthansa and Austrian Airlines flights. It's only worth it if you travel with your clubs several times a year, but if you do, it's worth looking at the current terms.
The alternative: rent clubs right at Faro Airport

If you'd rather keep your one checked bag for a suitcase, or you've booked Light, renting is the simpler option. Two rental companies operate inside **Faro Airport**: ClubsToHire in arrivals and MyCaddyMaster in departures. Collect a set on arrival, or have it delivered to your hotel.
More rental shops and their delivery areas are in our [Algarve shops directory](/shops).
Bottom line

Check your fare before you book: on most SWISS tickets your golf bag simply uses your checked allowance, but on Light or short-haul Basic you'll pay extra. If your allowance is already taken up by a suitcase, hiring clubs in Faro may be the easier option.

excerpt: What December weather in the Algarve means for your golf: average highs of 17°C, about seven rainy days, short afternoons and the cheapest green fees of the year on most courses.

content.text: Is December a good month for golf in the Algarve? For most golfers, yes. Afternoons reach about **17°C**, frost is virtually unknown on the coast, and it's the **cheapest month of the year** to play on 26 of the 29 courses we track. The catch is that December is also the Algarve's wettest month on average, and the days are short, with the sun setting at around 5.15pm.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in December from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay, and what changes around Christmas.
Algarve weather in December for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. We show two stations: Faro, which represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres, at the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

content.note: Source: IPMA climate normals 1991–2020 for Faro (station 554) and Sagres (station 533), averaged over 30 years. Rainy days have 1 mm of rain or more; heavy rain days 10 mm or more. Daylight and sunset are calculated for 1 to 31 December, in Portuguese winter time (the same as UK time).
content.caption: December weather in the Algarve

content.text: The headline is that the temperature hardly changes across the region: whether you're in Lagos, Vilamoura or Tavira, expect afternoons in the mid to high teens and mornings around 10°C. Rain is the variable. December averages around seven rainy days, which leaves roughly three weeks of dry golf, but the rain tends to arrive with Atlantic fronts that can bring two or three wet days in a row. Only about three days in the month see heavy rain.
What December weather means on the course

**Fairways and greens.** After a wet spell, fairways soften and you'll get less roll off the tee, so the courses play a little longer than they do in summer. Some clubs keep buggies on the paths after heavy rain to protect the turf, which means more walking to your ball. On the plus side, the courses are green and receptive, and approach shots hold the greens.

**Tee times.** With under ten hours of daylight and the sun down by about 5.20pm, timing matters more than temperature. A four-hour round needs a tee time no later than about 1pm, and in practice late morning is the sweet spot: the dew has burned off, the air has warmed up and you'll finish in daylight. Early starts are possible, but expect cold hands and wet grass before 9am.

**What to pack.** Layers rather than a heavy coat: a base layer and a windproof or waterproof top that you can take off as the afternoon warms up. Bring a proper waterproof jacket and trousers, an umbrella and a spare glove, and waterproof golf shoes are worth more than usual in December. Sun cream still earns its place on a clear day.

**Rain plans.** If a front comes through, the forecast usually gives you a day or two of warning, so keep your bookings flexible and play the dry days. And if it's dark by half past five, Amendoeira has the only floodlit nine-hole course in Portugal, according to the resort: see [night golf in the Algarve](/guide/night-golf-in-the-algarve).
Green fees in December: the cheapest month of the year

This is where December really pays off. On 26 of the 29 courses we track, December has the lowest green fee of the year, and on average December fees are about **34% below** each course's peak price. The savings are biggest at the courses that charge most in spring and autumn.

content.text: Some clubs also sell cheaper twilight rounds. Twilight rates this December start from €35 at Santo António and €50 at Alto Golf, and Pestana's [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho), [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta) and [Silves](/courses/silves) courses offer them at €55. A late twilight slot in December won't give you 18 holes before dark, so check the start time when you book.

Salgados, near Albufeira, puts December in its low season on its official 2026 price list, at €91 for 18 holes. For the full picture of where to play for less all year round, see [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Where to play in December

Because December is the low season almost everywhere, it's the best month of the year to play the Algarve's big-name courses for less. Amendoeira's Faldo Course costs less than half its spring price, and Quinta do Lago and Monte Rei are around €70 to €120 cheaper than at peak. If there's one premium round on your wish list, December is the time to book it.

East or west makes little difference to the weather this month: the western tip around Sagres sees slightly more rainy days, while Faro gets more rain in total, and temperatures are almost identical. Pick your base for the courses rather than the climate. If you're weighing up the two ends of the region, read [West vs East Algarve: which side is better for golf?](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf).
Christmas, New Year and crowds

Most of December is quiet on the fairways. Tee sheets are open, you can often book a day or two ahead, and rounds tend to flow without long waits. The exception is the fortnight around Christmas and New Year, when UK school holidays bring families and groups out, so book ahead if you're travelling in the last two weeks of the month.

Almost every course in the Algarve sells December tee times, but opening hours on Christmas Day and New Year's Day vary from club to club, so check with the course before you plan a festive round. The same goes for hotels: prices are low, but some seasonal resort hotels close for part of the winter, so check your hotel is open on your dates.
Frequently asked questions
Is December a good time to play golf in the Algarve?

Yes, if you want low prices and quiet courses and you're happy to play around the odd wet day. Afternoons average about 17°C, frost is very rare on the coast and green fees are at their lowest of the year on most courses. The trade-offs are short days and the highest average rainfall of the year in Faro.
Is it warm enough to play golf in the Algarve in December?

Yes. The average daily high is 17°C in both Faro and Sagres, and the average low is around 10°C. Most golfers play in a long-sleeved top or a light jumper, adding a waterproof layer when the weather turns.
How much does it rain in the Algarve in December?

Faro averages 90 mm of rain in December over about seven rainy days, and Sagres 75 mm over about eight. On most other days of the month there's no meaningful rain, but wet spells can last two or three days.
What time does it get dark in the Algarve in December?
The sun sets at around 5.15pm to 5.30pm throughout December, and rises at about 7.30am to 7.50am. To finish 18 holes in daylight, aim to tee off by about 1pm.

content.text: Is March a good month for golf in the Algarve? The weather says yes: afternoons average about **19°C**, there are around six rainy days, and after the clocks go forward at the end of the month it stays light until nearly 8pm. The catch is the price. March is peak season, and on 22 of the 30 courses we track it's already the most expensive month of the year.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in March from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay, and how to plan around Easter.
Algarve weather in March for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

content.note: Source: IPMA climate normals 1991–2020 for Faro (station 554) and Sagres (station 533), averaged over 30 years. Rainy days have 1 mm of rain or more; heavy rain days 10 mm or more. Daylight is for the middle of the month; sunset is calculated for the first and last day of March, in Portuguese local time; the clocks go forward an hour on the last Sunday of March, as in the UK.
content.caption: March weather in the Algarve

content.text: March is noticeably warmer than February, with an average high of almost 19°C in Faro and mornings around 11°C. It isn't the driest month, though: about 47 mm of rain falls over around six days, usually in short spells rather than long wet weeks. The biggest change is the light: the days lengthen by more than an hour over the month, and the clock change moves sunset from about 6.25pm to almost 7.55pm.
What March weather means on the course

**Fairways and greens.** With spring growth under way, the courses come into good shape in March: fairways firm up between showers, the grass thickens and greens pick up pace. After a wet day, expect a little less roll.

**Tee times.** Until the clocks change, tee off by about 2pm to finish 18 holes in daylight. After the change at the end of the month, you can start as late as about 3.30pm. Morning rounds can be fresh; by early afternoon it's usually short-sleeve weather in the sun.
**What to pack.** Short sleeves for the afternoons, a light jumper or windproof for the mornings, and a waterproof jacket for the showers. Sun cream and a cap become essential this month.
Green fees in March

March is when the Algarve's spring peak begins. On 22 of the 30 courses we track, March is already at the course's highest price of the year, and on average fees are only about **5% below** peak. The exceptions are worth knowing: Amendoeira's Faldo Course charges €138 in March against €212 in April and May, and [Salgados](/courses/salgados) €102 on its own booking site against €139 in April.

content.text: If you want to keep costs down, look at twilight rounds, which start from €35 at Santo António and €50 at Alto Golf this March, and €55 at Pestana's [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho), [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta) and [Silves](/courses/silves). Or see [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Where to play in March

The weather is very similar across the region in March, so choose your base for the courses and the price. The western courses in our table, such as Santo António, Espiche and [Boavista](/courses/boavista), are among the best value in peak season. If you're weighing up the two ends of the region, read [West vs East Algarve: which side is better for golf?](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf).
Easter, crowds and the clock change

March gets busier as it goes on. Spring golf packages fill the tee sheets, and Easter brings the busiest stretch of the spring: in 2027, Easter Sunday is on 28 March, so the UK Easter school holidays run from late March into April. Book tee times and hotels well ahead if you're travelling then, and expect popular courses to be fully booked at peak times.

The clocks go forward an hour on the last Sunday of March, the same day as in the UK, so there's no time difference to think about. Easter weekend in 2027 is also the weekend the clocks change, so double-check your tee time on 28 March.
Frequently asked questions
Is March a good time to play golf in the Algarve?

Yes, for the weather and the courses. Afternoons average 19°C, the courses are coming into their best condition and the days are long after the clocks change. It is peak season, though, so green fees are high and tee times book up, especially around Easter.
Is the Algarve warm in March?
Warm enough for golf in short sleeves on most afternoons. The average high is 19°C in Faro and 18°C in Sagres, with mornings around 11°C.
How much does it rain in the Algarve in March?
Faro averages 47 mm of rain in March over about six rainy days, and Sagres 49 mm over a similar number. The rain usually comes in short spells.
What time does it get dark in the Algarve in March?
The sun sets at about 6.25pm at the start of March. After the clocks go forward on the last Sunday of the month, sunset moves to about 7.50pm.

content.text: Is June a good month for golf in the Algarve? Yes, if you tee off early. Afternoons average about **27°C**, it barely rains, and these are the longest days of the year, with sunrise around 6.15am and sunset around 8.50pm. And as the heat builds, green fees fall: on 11 of the 30 courses we track, June shares the lowest price of the year.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in June from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off to beat the heat, what you'll pay and where to play.
Algarve weather in June for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

content.note: Source: IPMA climate normals 1991–2020 for Faro (station 554) and Sagres (station 533), averaged over 30 years. Rainy days have 1 mm of rain or more. Daylight is for the middle of the month; sunrise and sunset are calculated for the first and last day of June, in Portuguese summer time (the same as UK time).
content.caption: June weather in the Algarve

content.text: June is the start of the Algarve summer. The average high in Faro is almost 27°C, with around five days above 30°C, while Sagres in the far west averages 24°C and has only about one. Rain is very rare: about 5 mm falls in the whole month, usually on a single day or none at all. With almost 15 hours of daylight, you can plan your golf around the cooler hours.
What June weather means on the course

**Fairways and greens.** Courses are well irrigated through the summer, so they stay green, but the fairways run firm and fast in June. You'll get plenty of roll off the tee, and you'll need to land approach shots short of the flag.

**Tee times.** The best time to play in June is early: tee off between 7am and 9am and you'll finish before the hottest part of the day. Late afternoon is the other comfortable window: with sunset around 8.50pm, a 4.30pm start still gets you round before dark.
**What to pack.** Light, breathable golf clothes, a hat, sunglasses and high-factor sun cream. Carry more water than you think you'll need, and consider taking a buggy for a midday round.
Green fees in June

June is when green fees start to drop into the summer low season. On 11 of the 30 courses we track, June shares the lowest price of the year, and on average fees are about **28% below** each course's peak. Amendoeira's Faldo Course falls to €109, from €212 in May, and Gramacho to €95, from €155.

See also [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Where to play in June

From June onwards, the west of the Algarve is noticeably cooler than the centre and east: about three degrees cooler in the afternoon on average, with far fewer hot days. If you don't enjoy playing in the heat, courses near Lagos and Sagres, such as Santo António, Espiche and [Boavista](/courses/boavista), are a good choice, and they're among the cheapest in our table too. Inland courses tend to be hotter than the coast. Read [West vs East Algarve: which side is better for golf?](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf) to compare the two ends of the region.
Crowds and what else is on in June

Golf traffic thins out through June as the weather warms up, so tee times are easier to find than in spring. Hotels go the other way: rooms fill up and prices rise as the beach season begins, so you may pay less for your golf and more for your hotel than in April.
10 June is Portugal Day, a national holiday, and June is the month of the popular saints' festivals in Portuguese towns, with street parties and grilled sardines.
Frequently asked questions
Is June a good time to play golf in the Algarve?
Yes, if you're happy to play early or late in the day. It's warm and dry, the days are the longest of the year, and green fees fall to low-season levels on many courses.
Is it too hot to play golf in the Algarve in June?

Not usually. The average high in Faro is about 27°C, with around five days above 30°C in the month. The west is cooler, at around 24°C. Play early in the morning or late in the afternoon and drink plenty of water.
Does it rain in the Algarve in June?
Very rarely. Faro averages 5 mm of rain in June, and less than one rainy day.
What time does it get light and dark in the Algarve in June?
The sun rises at about 6.15am and sets between about 8.45pm and 8.55pm, which gives you almost 15 hours of daylight for golf.

content.text: Is February a good month for golf in the Algarve? For many golfers it's one of the best. Afternoons average about **17°C**, February is the driest month of the winter in Faro, with around five rainy days, and the days stretch out noticeably, with the sun setting after 6pm by the end of the month. The catch is that green fees start to rise as the spring golf season gets going.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in February from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay and when it gets busy.
Algarve weather in February for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

Daylight is for the middle of the month; sunset is calculated for the first and last day of February, in Portuguese winter time (the same as UK time).
content.caption: February weather in the Algarve

content.text: February is a touch warmer than January, with an average high of 17°C in Faro, and drier: about 42 mm of rain over five rainy days, the lowest of any winter month. Sagres is slightly cooler and wetter, with six rainy days. Daylight grows by almost an hour over the month, which makes a big difference to how late you can tee off.
What February weather means on the course

**Fairways and greens.** Courses are usually drying out from the winter rain by February, but fairways can still be soft after a wet spell, so don't expect summer roll. Greens are in good condition but not yet at their spring pace.
**Tee times.** To finish 18 holes in daylight, tee off by about 1.30pm in early February and by about 2pm at the end of the month. Mid-morning starts give you the best of the day's warmth.

**What to pack.** Layers still rule: a base layer, a light jumper and a waterproof jacket. You'll often shed the jumper by the back nine on a sunny afternoon. Bring waterproof trousers and an umbrella just in case, and sun cream, because the February sun has more strength than it feels.
Green fees in February

February is a transition month. Some courses keep their low-season prices, but many move into their spring rates: on average, February fees are about **15% below** each course's peak price, against about a third below in January. The jump can be steep at the resort courses, so if your dates are flexible, compare the price with late January before you book.

For more ways to save, see [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Where to play in February

The weather is very similar across the region in February: the west gets about one more rainy day a month and is slightly cooler, but not enough to plan around. Choose your base for the courses and prices you want. The western courses around Lagos and Sagres have the lowest green fees in our table this month, and Espiche and Santo António stay at or near their low-season prices. If you're weighing up the two ends of the region, read [West vs East Algarve: which side is better for golf?](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf).
Crowds and what else is on in February

Courses are generally quiet in the first half of February and get busier through the month. The UK's February half-term brings a busier week, usually in the middle of the month, when families and groups arrive, so book tee times ahead if you're travelling then.

The almond blossom is at its best in the Algarve countryside in February, and carnival comes to Portugal before Lent: Carnival Tuesday falls on 9 February in 2027, with parades in towns such as Loulé. It's a good time to visit as more seasonal hotels reopen ahead of spring, but check your hotel is open on your dates.
Frequently asked questions
Is February a good time to play golf in the Algarve?
Yes. It's usually the driest month of the winter, afternoons average 17°C and the days are getting longer. Green fees rise during February on many courses, so it's not quite as cheap as January.
Is the Algarve hot in February?
No, it's mild rather than hot. The average high is 17°C in Faro and 16°C in Sagres, and the average low is about 9°C. That's comfortable golfing weather in a long-sleeved top.
How much does it rain in the Algarve in February?
Faro averages 42 mm of rain in February over about five rainy days, and Sagres 49 mm over about six. Days of heavy rain are rare, at one or two a month.
What time does it get dark in the Algarve in February?
The sun sets at about 5.55pm at the start of February and about 6.25pm at the end. To finish 18 holes in daylight, tee off by about 1.30pm to 2pm.

excerpt: What May weather in the Algarve means for your golf: afternoons of 23°C, only about four rainy days, light until nearly 9pm and peak-season green fees.

content.text: Is May a good month for golf in the Algarve? Many golfers think it's the best of all. Afternoons average about **23°C**, rain falls on only about four days, and by the end of the month it's light until about 8.45pm. As in April, you pay for it: on 18 of the 30 courses we track, May shares the highest green fee of the year.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in May from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay and where to play.
Algarve weather in May for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

content.note: Source: IPMA climate normals 1991–2020 for Faro (station 554) and Sagres (station 533), averaged over 30 years. Rainy days have 1 mm of rain or more; heavy rain days 10 mm or more. Daylight is for the middle of the month; sunset is calculated for the first and last day of May, in Portuguese summer time (the same as UK time).
content.caption: May weather in the Algarve

content.text: May is warm, dry and long. The average high is 23.5°C in Faro and mornings start around 15°C. Faro has about nine or ten days of 25°C or more in an average May, but only about one above 30°C, so it rarely gets uncomfortably hot. The far west is cooler: Sagres averages 21.5°C, with only three or four days above 25°C. Rain is light, at about 26 mm over four days.
What May weather means on the course

**Fairways and greens.** Courses are usually in excellent condition in May: firm, fast fairways that give you plenty of roll, and quick greens. Bring your short game, because firm greens can be hard to hold.

**Tee times.** You have more than 14 hours of daylight, so you can tee off as late as about 4pm and still finish. Morning tee times are the most comfortable as the month warms up, and late afternoon rounds are a pleasure as the heat goes out of the day.

**What to pack.** Summer golf kit: short sleeves, shorts if the club's dress code allows them, a cap, sunglasses and plenty of sun cream. A light windproof for an early start, and a refillable water bottle.
Green fees in May

May stays in the Algarve's spring peak. On 18 of the 30 courses we track, May shares the highest price of the year, and on average fees are only about **5% below** peak. Some courses ease off slightly: Gramacho charges €155 in May against €180 in March and April.

This May they start from €35 at Santo António and €50 at Alto Golf, and €55 at Pestana's [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho), [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta) and [Silves](/courses/silves). See also [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Where to play in May

In May the west starts to feel cooler than the centre and east, by about two degrees in the afternoon, which suits golfers who don't like the heat. The western courses in our table, such as Santo António, Espiche and Boavista, are also among the cheapest this month. If you're weighing up the two ends of the region, read [West vs East Algarve: which side is better for golf?](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf).
Crowds and what else is on in May

May is busy on the courses, with spring golf groups and plenty of couples taking advantage of the weather before the summer school holidays. The UK's late-May bank holiday and half-term week, at the end of the month, bring a busier spell, so book ahead if you're travelling then. 1 May is a public holiday in Portugal.
Hotels are busy but not yet at their summer peak, so you'll usually find more choice and lower room rates than in July and August.
Frequently asked questions
Is May a good time to play golf in the Algarve?

Yes, it's one of the best months for weather and course conditions: warm, dry afternoons, long days and firm, fast courses. It's peak season, though, so green fees are high and you should book tee times ahead.
Is the Algarve hot in May?
Warm, and occasionally hot. The average high is 23.5°C in Faro, with about one day above 30°C in an average May. The far west, around Sagres, is about two degrees cooler.
Does it rain in the Algarve in May?
Not much. Faro averages 26 mm of rain in May over about four rainy days, and Sagres 22 mm over about four.
What time does it get dark in the Algarve in May?
The sun sets at about 8.20pm at the start of May and about 8.45pm by the end, so there's time for a full afternoon round.

excerpt: What January weather in the Algarve means for your golf: afternoons of 16°C, about six rainy days, ten hours of daylight and some of the lowest green fees of the year.

content.text: Is January a good month for golf in the Algarve? It's one of the best-value months of the year. Afternoons average about **16°C**, frost is virtually unknown on the coast, and on 20 of the 30 courses we track January shares the lowest green fee of the year. The trade-offs are short days, with the sun setting between about 5.25pm and 5.55pm, and around six rainy days in the month.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in January from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay, and how busy it gets.
Algarve weather in January for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

Daylight is for the middle of the month; sunset is calculated for the first and last day of January, in Portuguese winter time (the same as UK time).
content.caption: January weather in the Algarve

content.text: January is the coolest month of the year, but only just: the average high is 16°C in both Faro and Sagres, and the average low is a little over 8°C. Rain falls on about six days in Faro and seven in Sagres, which leaves more than three weeks of dry golf, and only one or two days in the month see heavy rain. The days get longer through the month, with sunset about half an hour later by the end of January than at the start.
What January weather means on the course

**Fairways and greens.** After the wet weeks of late autumn and December, fairways can be soft in January and the ball won't run far, so courses play a little longer than their yardage suggests. Some clubs keep buggies on the paths after heavy rain. The upside is lush, green turf and greens that hold a well-struck approach.

**Tee times.** With under ten hours of daylight in early January, aim to tee off by about 1pm if you want to finish 18 holes in daylight, a little later by the end of the month. Late morning is the sweet spot: the frost-free mornings can still be chilly and dewy, and the warmest part of the day is early afternoon.

**What to pack.** Think layers: a base layer, a jumper or fleece and a waterproof jacket you can take off as the day warms up. Waterproof trousers, an umbrella and a spare glove are worth their space, and a beanie for the first few holes of an early round. On a clear day you'll still want sun cream.
Green fees in January

January is part of the Algarve's winter low season. On 20 of the 30 courses we track, January shares the lowest green fee of the year, and on average fees are about **33% below** each course's peak price. The big-name courses offer the largest savings in cash terms.
