content.text: Twilight rounds are cheaper again: this January they start from €35 at Santo António, €47 at [Salgados](/courses/salgados) and €50 at Alto Golf, and Pestana's [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho) and [Silves](/courses/silves) courses offer them at €55. With the light going by late afternoon, check the start time so you know how many holes you'll get in. For more ways to save, see [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Where to play in January

Temperatures are almost identical across the region in January, so pick your base for the courses you want to play rather than the weather. The west sees slightly more rainy days than the centre and east, but the difference is about one day a month. If you're weighing up the two ends of the region, read [West vs East Algarve: which side is better for golf?](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf).

Low-season prices make January a good time to tick off a premium course: Amendoeira's Faldo Course costs €100, less than half its spring price, and Quinta do Lago South €188 against €264 at peak. Short of time on a winter afternoon? A nine-hole course such as [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs) or [Balaia](/courses/balaia) fits neatly into the daylight.
Crowds and what else is on in January

After the New Year week, January is one of the quietest months on the Algarve's fairways. Tee sheets are open, you can often book a day or two ahead, and rounds tend to flow at a good pace. The almond trees start to blossom in the Algarve countryside from late January, which brightens up the inland courses.
Prices for hotels are generally low, but some seasonal resort hotels close for part of the winter, so check your hotel is open on your dates before you book flights.
Frequently asked questions
Is January a good time to play golf in the Algarve?

Yes, if you want low prices and quiet courses. Afternoons average 16°C, frost is very rare on the coast, and green fees are at or near their lowest of the year on most courses. Expect short days and about six rainy days in the month.
Is the Algarve warm enough for golf in January?
Yes. The average daily high is about 16°C in both Faro and Sagres, and the average low around 8°C. Most golfers play in a long-sleeved top and a jumper, with a waterproof layer for showers.
How much does it rain in the Algarve in January?
Faro averages 49 mm of rain in January over about six rainy days, and Sagres 53 mm over about seven. Heavy rain, of 10 mm or more in a day, falls on only one or two days in the month.
What time does it get dark in the Algarve in January?
The sun sets at about 5.25pm at the start of January and about 5.55pm by the end. To finish 18 holes in daylight, aim to tee off by around 1pm.

excerpt: Vilamoura is 30–35 minutes from Faro Airport. Taxi, transfer, Uber, bus and car hire options compared for golfers travelling with clubs.

content.text: Vilamoura is about 25km from Faro Airport, or roughly 30 to 35 minutes by road. If you're carrying golf clubs, the best option is usually a pre-booked transfer, from about €35 for a sedan, or a metered taxi at roughly €25–35. There is a direct bus, but it runs only a few times a day and doesn't reach the courses.

content.note: Transfer prices quoted in October 2026 by a fare-comparison site. Taxi range is our estimate based on the old and new national tariffs. Checked November 2026.
rows: Best: tell them about your bags
Fine for one or two bags
Good if you choose the right size
content.caption: Your options at a glance

content.text: How far is each Vilamoura course from the airport?
Vilamoura's four Vilamoura Golf courses and nearby Vila Sol are all within a few minutes of each other, so it makes little difference to your transfer which one you're playing first.

content.note: Road-routing estimates from the terminal without traffic, rounded to the nearest 5 minutes. Victoria is a private members' club and isn't open to visitors.

content.text: Pre-booked transfer: the easy choice with golf clubs

Your driver tracks your flight and waits in arrivals, so a delay doesn't cost you extra or leave you hunting for a car with a heavy bag. Quotes for Vilamoura in October 2026 were about **€35 for a sedan** carrying up to three people and **€44 for a minivan**, per vehicle. For a four-ball, the minivan works out at about €11 each, and it's the only sensible choice with four golf bags.
When you book, give the number of golf bags as well as passengers. You can compare companies and vehicles on [GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA).
Taxi: good value for one or two golfers

The taxi rank is right outside arrivals, and there's no fixed fare to Vilamoura: you pay what the meter shows. Portugal's new national tariff began on 23 October 2026, with a €2 flag fall plus €0.58 per km and €0.28 per minute in its first year. On that basis a weekday daytime trip comes to about **€23–25**. Meters don't have to be updated until 21 January 2027, and on the old tariff the same trip is about €27 by day and €33 at night or at weekends.
Two golfers should manage in a saloon or estate taxi, though the bags may need the rear seat folded down. If you see a small car at the front of the rank, it's fine to ask for a bigger one.
Uber and Bolt from the airport to Vilamoura

Both apps pick up at Faro Airport, with directions to the pickup point shown in the app. Prices move with demand, so compare the quote with the taxi fare above. Golf bags are the catch: a standard car may not take one, so choose a larger category such as UberXL, and message the driver before they set off. If you arrive late at night and the driver can't fit the bag, the taxi rank is your fallback.
Is there a bus from Faro Airport to Vilamoura?

Yes. **Vamus line 55** links the airport with Almancil, Quarteira and Vilamoura. According to the independent [Algarve Bus Info timetable](http://www.algarvebus.info/055.htm), buses leave the airport at 08:30, 10:30, 14:30, 15:30, 17:30 and 19:20, taking about 40 to 50 minutes. At weekends and on holidays it's listed as running only from 1 May to 31 October. It stops on Avenida Engenheiro João Meireles, not at the marina, and it doesn't go to the golf courses.

Those times can change, so check [Vamus](https://www.vamusalgarve.pt/vamus/schedules) before relying on them. Honestly, with a golf bag and a long wait between departures, this one is for golfers on a very tight budget. Vilamoura has no railway station either, so the train isn't a realistic alternative.
Should you hire a car for a Vilamoura golf trip?

If you're only playing around Vilamoura, you may not need one, as courses are close together and short taxi rides between them add up slowly. It starts to make sense if you also plan to play Quinta do Lago, Salgados or further afield, or want to reach early tee times without arranging a pickup each day. The A22 motorway is toll-free, and the courses are easy to reach from it. Compare prices on [EconomyBookings](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw), and check the boot size before you book: four golfers will need a people carrier.
Leave the clubs at home?

Skipping the golf bag would let you take any of the options above. [ClubsToHire](/shops/clubstohire-faro-airport) has a desk in the airport's arrivals hall, so you can collect a set when you land or have it delivered to your hotel.
Plan the rest of your trip

Still choosing where to stay? See our guide to [golf hotels near Vilamoura](/guide/golf-hotels-near-vilamoura), or browse [all the golf courses in Vilamoura](/vilamoura/golf-courses). If you're comparing other parts of the Algarve, our [drive times from Faro Airport to every course](/guide/faro-airport-to-algarve-golf-courses) will help.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Vilamoura costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-vilamoura-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

content.text: Albufeira's golf courses are about 45 to 50 minutes from Faro Airport, and it's the first area where the choice of transport starts to matter. A sedan transfer at about €48 is the most reliable option with clubs, while a taxi costs roughly €40–60 depending on the tariff and time of day. There's also a direct Aerobus, though not one that suits a golf bag.

content.text: These three aren't next to each other. Pine Cliffs and Balaia lie east of the town, while Salgados is out to the west, so check which one is nearest your hotel before you pick your transport.
Transfer or taxi to Albufeira?

Here the two cost much the same, so certainty is the main reason to book. A sedan was quoted at **€48** and a minivan at **€64** in October 2026, which is €16 each for a four-ball. You'll find live offers on [GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA), and it's worth giving the bag count when you request them.

A taxi may come out cheaper on a weekday, at about €40 under the new national tariff. On a meter that hasn't yet been updated, which is allowed until 21 January 2027, the same trip is about €51 by day and €61 at night or at weekends. So if you land late on a Saturday, the fixed price is likely to be the better deal.
Is the Aerobus worth it with a golf bag?

**Vamus Aerobus line 56** leaves from a stop to the left of the main terminal entrance and runs direct to Albufeira, at about €11 per person with a discount on returns. There are more departures from May to October than in winter, and guides put the last one at about 18:15. Check the latest [Vamus timetable](https://www.vamusalgarve.pt/vamus/schedules) before relying on it.

It works for a light traveller going into town, but it won't take you to Pine Cliffs, Balaia or Salgados. Adding a taxi at the far end with a heavy bag removes most of the saving, unless you're travelling alone on a tight budget.
Should you hire a car in Albufeira?

We'd lean towards yes if you're staying more than a few days. Because the courses are spread out, a daily taxi to a different one soon adds up, and a car also puts Vilamoura and Amendoeira within easy reach. Check the boot size on [EconomyBookings](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw) before you book, since small cars struggle with a golf travel bag.
Prefer not to fly with clubs?
If you only plan on a couple of rounds, it may be easier to rent. [ClubsToHire](/shops/clubstohire-faro-airport) is based in the airport arrivals hall, and also delivers to the Albufeira area.

excerpt: What July weather in the Algarve means for your golf: hot afternoons of 29°C, no rain, quiet courses and some of the lowest green fees of the year.

content.text: Is July a good month for golf in the Algarve? It's hot, but it can be very good value. Afternoons average about **29°C** in Faro, it hardly ever rains, and green fees are at or near their lowest of the year: on 14 of the 29 courses we track, July shares the lowest price. The secret is to play early or late, and to pick your courses with the heat in mind.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in July from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay and where it's cooler.
Algarve weather in July for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

content.caption: July weather in the Algarve

content.text: July is the hottest month of the year in Faro, with an average high of 29.4°C and about 13 days above 30°C. Nights are warm too, at around 20°C. The far west is much cooler: Sagres averages just over 25°C, with only two or three days above 30°C. Rain is almost non-existent, at about 1 mm in the whole month.
What July weather means on the course
**Fairways and greens.** The courses are irrigated and stay green, but fairways are hard and fast in July and the ball runs a long way. Greens can be firm and a little slower than in spring.

**Tee times.** Play at dawn or in the evening. A tee time between about 7am and 8.30am will have you finished before the worst of the heat, and with sunset after 8.40pm, a 4.30pm start still gets you round in daylight. Avoid the middle of the day if you can: it's hard on your body and your scorecard.

**What to pack.** Lightweight, breathable golf clothes, a wide-brimmed hat, sunglasses and high-factor sun cream. Carry at least a litre of water for a round, and take a buggy if you're playing anywhere near midday.
Green fees in July

July is summer low season for golf in the Algarve. On 14 of the 29 courses we track, July shares the lowest price of the year, and on average fees are about **34% below** each course's peak, the joint biggest saving of any month. Amendoeira's Faldo Course costs €109, against €212 in spring, and Quinta do Lago South €188, against €264.

See also [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Where to play in July: head west to stay cool

In July, where you play makes a real difference to the heat. Sagres, at the western tip, averages about 25°C against more than 29°C in Faro, and has about three days above 30°C in the month against 13. The western courses around Lagos and Sagres, such as Santo António, Espiche and [Boavista](/courses/boavista), are also among the cheapest in our table. Inland courses tend to be hotter than the coast, so book those for early morning.
Read [West vs East Algarve: which side is better for golf?](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf) to compare the two ends of the region.
Crowds and what else is on in July

Courses are quiet in July, because most visitors are on the beach rather than the fairway, so you can usually find tee times at short notice. Hotels are the opposite: July is high season, with UK, Irish and Portuguese school holidays overlapping in the second half of the month, so book your accommodation well ahead and expect higher room rates.
Frequently asked questions
Is July a good time to play golf in the Algarve?
Yes, if you can handle the heat and play early or late. Courses are quiet and green fees are among the lowest of the year, but hotels are at their busiest and most expensive.
Is it too hot to play golf in the Algarve in July?

It can be in the middle of the day. Faro averages 29°C in July, with about 13 days above 30°C. Tee off before 8.30am or after about 4.30pm, carry plenty of water, and consider the cooler west, where Sagres averages about 25°C.
Does it rain in the Algarve in July?
Almost never. Faro averages about 1 mm of rain in the whole of July.
What time does it get light and dark in the Algarve in July?
The sun rises between about 6.15am and 6.35am and sets between about 8.40pm and 8.55pm, giving you around 14 and a half hours of daylight.

excerpt: What August weather in the Algarve means for your golf: hot afternoons of 29°C, no rain, early starts, and green fees at their summer low.

content.text: Is August a good month for golf in the Algarve? Like July, it's hot but good value. Afternoons average about **29°C** in Faro, it barely rains, and green fees are at their summer low: on 14 of the 29 courses we track, August shares the lowest price of the year. Play early or late, and the courses are yours.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in August from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay and where it's cooler.
Algarve weather in August for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

The days are getting shorter, though: by the end of August the sun sets about 8pm, more than half an hour earlier than at the start.
What August weather means on the course
**Fairways and greens.** Irrigated courses stay green through August, but the fairways are hard and fast, and you'll get lots of roll off the tee. Firm greens reward a lower, running approach.

**Tee times.** Early morning is the best time to play: tee off between about 7am and 8.30am and you'll finish before the midday heat. Sunrise moves later during the month, from about 6.35am to 7am. Late-afternoon rounds work too, but with sunset moving earlier, a start around 4pm is about the latest for 18 holes by the end of the month.

**What to pack.** Lightweight, breathable clothes, a wide-brimmed hat, sunglasses and high-factor sun cream. Carry plenty of water, and take a buggy for any round that runs into the middle of the day.
Green fees in August

August is summer low season for golf. On 14 of the 29 courses we track, August shares the lowest green fee of the year, and on average fees are about **34% below** each course's peak. The savings at the big-name courses are large: Gramacho costs €95 against €180 in spring, and Amendoeira's Faldo Course €109 against €212.

content.text: This August twilight rounds start from €35 at Santo António, €47 at [Salgados](/courses/salgados) and €50 at Alto Golf, and €55 at Pestana's [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho) and [Silves](/courses/silves). See also [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Where to play in August: the cooler west

As in July, the west of the Algarve is noticeably cooler in August: Sagres averages about 26°C against 29°C in Faro, with around three days above 30°C instead of 12. Courses around Lagos and Sagres, such as Santo António, Espiche and [Boavista](/courses/boavista), are a sensible choice for golfers who don't like the heat, and they're among the cheapest in our table. Inland courses tend to be hotter than the coast, so play those at first light.
Read [West vs East Algarve: which side is better for golf?](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf) to compare the two ends of the region.
Crowds and what else is on in August

August is the busiest month of the year in the Algarve as a whole, but not on the golf courses: tee sheets are open and you can often book at short notice. Hotels are at their fullest and most expensive, with school holidays running through most of the month, so book your room early. 15 August is a public holiday in Portugal.
Frequently asked questions
Is August a good time to play golf in the Algarve?
Yes, if you play early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Green fees are among the lowest of the year and the courses are quiet, but hotels are at their busiest and most expensive.
Is it too hot to play golf in the Algarve in August?
The middle of the day can be. Faro averages 29°C in August, with about 12 days above 30°C. Tee off early, carry plenty of water, and consider the west of the region, where Sagres averages about 26°C.
Does it rain in the Algarve in August?
Very rarely. Faro averages 3 mm of rain in August and less than one rainy day.
What time does it get light and dark in the Algarve in August?
The sun rises between about 6.35am and 7am, and sets at about 8.40pm at the start of August and about 8pm by the end.

excerpt: What September weather in the Algarve means for your golf: warm afternoons of 26°C, very little rain, quieter courses after the school holidays and green fees heading back up.

content.text: Is September a good month for golf in the Algarve? Many golfers think it's the best month of the year. The summer heat eases to an average high of about **26°C**, rain falls on only about two days, and the courses get quieter once the school holidays end. Green fees are heading back up, though: on average they're only about 12% below each course's peak.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in September from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay and where to play.
Algarve weather in September for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

content.note: Source: IPMA climate normals 1991–2020 for Faro (station 554) and Sagres (station 533), averaged over 30 years. Rainy days have 1 mm of rain or more. Daylight is for the middle of the month; sunrise and sunset are calculated for the first and last day of September, in Portuguese summer time (the same as UK time).
content.caption: September weather in the Algarve

content.text: September is still summer in the Algarve, but a gentler one. The average high in Faro is about 26°C, with around three days above 30°C, and Sagres averages about 25°C. Mornings are warm, at around 18°C. Rain returns, but only just: about 22 mm in Faro over two days. The days shorten by more than an hour over the month.
What September weather means on the course
**Fairways and greens.** Courses come out of the summer firm and fast, and generally in good condition. Expect plenty of roll off the tee and firm greens, especially early in the month.

**Tee times.** The heat is less of a problem than in July and August, so mid-morning tee times become comfortable again. To finish 18 holes in daylight, tee off by about 3.30pm in early September and by about 3pm at the end of the month.
**What to pack.** Summer golf kit: light, breathable clothes, a cap, sunglasses and sun cream. A light layer for early starts at the end of the month, and a small umbrella just in case.
Green fees in September

September is when green fees climb back towards their autumn peak. On average they're about **12% below** each course's highest price, against about a third below in July and August, and on 6 of the 30 courses we track September is already at the year's top rate. Amendoeira's Faldo Course, for example, goes from €109 in August to €197 in September.

content.note: The lowest price any visitor can book for one 18-hole round, from each club's official price list or its own online booking, checked in October 2026. All year shows the course's cheapest and dearest months. Prices change, so check before you book.
content.caption: September green fees: 18 holes, visitor rate

content.text: Twilight rounds take the edge off: this September they start from €35 at Santo António and €50 at Alto Golf, and €55 at Pestana's [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho), [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta) and [Silves](/courses/silves). See also [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Where to play in September

The west is still a little cooler than the centre and east in September, by about one and a half degrees, but the difference is much smaller than in midsummer, so you can choose your base for the courses. The best value in our table is in the west and east, with Espiche and Santo António at €68 and Quinta do Vale at €79. If you're weighing up the two ends of the region, read [West vs East Algarve: which side is better for golf?](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf).
Crowds and what else is on in September

The beach crowds thin out once UK schools go back at the start of September, and hotel prices generally ease from their August peak. The golf season goes the other way: autumn golf groups start to arrive through the month, so tee sheets get busier towards the end of September. Book ahead for the second half of the month.
Frequently asked questions
Is September a good time to play golf in the Algarve?
Yes, it's one of the best months: warm but not too hot, very little rain, firm courses and quieter beaches. Green fees are rising towards their autumn peak, so it isn't as cheap as summer.
Is it still hot in the Algarve in September?
Warm rather than hot. The average high is about 26°C in Faro and 25°C in Sagres, with around three days above 30°C in Faro.
Does it rain in the Algarve in September?
Not much. Faro averages 22 mm of rain in September over about two rainy days, and Sagres 19 mm over two or three.
What time does it get dark in the Algarve in September?
The sun sets at about 8pm at the start of September and about 7.20pm by the end. Tee off by about 3pm to 3.30pm to finish 18 holes.
Plan your September golf trip

excerpt: What October weather in the Algarve means for your golf: afternoons of 23°C, the first autumn rain, the clocks going back and autumn peak green fees.

content.text: Is October a good month for golf in the Algarve? Yes, it's the heart of the autumn golf season. Afternoons average about **23°C**, early October can still feel like summer, and the courses are in good shape. The trade-offs are the return of the rain, about six rainy days on average, and the price: October is autumn peak season, and fees are only about 8% below each course's highest rate on average.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in October from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay and what changes when the clocks go back.
Algarve weather in October for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

content.note: Source: IPMA climate normals 1991–2020 for Faro (station 554) and Sagres (station 533), averaged over 30 years. Rainy days have 1 mm of rain or more; heavy rain days 10 mm or more. Daylight is for the middle of the month; sunset is calculated for the first and last day of October, in Portuguese local time; the clocks go back an hour on the last Sunday of October, as in the UK, which moves sunset from about 6.40pm to 5.40pm.
content.caption: October weather in the Algarve

content.text: October is warm, with an average high of about 23°C in Faro and 22°C in Sagres, and mornings around 16°C. It's also the month the rain comes back: Faro averages 56 mm over about six days, with about two days of heavy rain, and Sagres a little more. In an average October, Faro still has about seven days of 25°C or more.
What October weather means on the course

**Fairways and greens.** Courses are generally in good condition in October. After the first heavy rain, fairways soften and the ball stops running so far. Some clubs carry out autumn maintenance around this time, so it's worth asking about course conditions when you book.

**Tee times.** Until the clocks go back on the last Sunday of October, tee off by about 2.30pm to 3pm to finish 18 holes in daylight. After the change, sunset moves to about 5.40pm and the latest sensible tee time to about 1.30pm.
**What to pack.** Short sleeves for most afternoons, a light jumper for the mornings and a waterproof jacket and umbrella for the showers. Sun cream is still essential.
Green fees in October

October is the Algarve's autumn peak for golf. On 10 of the 30 courses we track, October is at the year's highest price, and on average fees are only about **8% below** each course's peak. There are some savings at the very top end: Monte Rei costs €245 in October against €312 in spring.

content.text: Twilight rounds help keep costs down: this October they start from €35 at Santo António and €50 at Alto Golf, and €55 at Pestana's [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho), [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta) and [Silves](/courses/silves). Remember that the daylight runs out faster after the clocks go back. See also [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Where to play in October

Temperatures are similar across the region in October, and the west gets slightly more rain than the centre and east, so pick your base for the courses. The cheapest courses in our table this month are in the far west and east, with Santo António at €68 and Espiche at €90. If you're weighing up the two ends of the region, read [West vs East Algarve: which side is better for golf?](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf).
Crowds, half-term and the clock change

October is one of the busiest months on the Algarve's courses, as golfers from northern Europe arrive for the autumn season. Book tee times and hotels as early as you can, especially for morning slots at the best-known courses. The UK's October half-term falls in the last week or so of the month, adding families to the mix.

The clocks go back on the last Sunday of October, the same day as in the UK, so there's no time difference to worry about, but sunset jumps an hour earlier overnight. 5 October is a public holiday in Portugal.
Frequently asked questions
Is October a good time to play golf in the Algarve?
Yes, it's one of the most popular months: warm afternoons, courses in good shape and plenty of daylight until the clocks change. It's peak season, though, so prices are high and tee times book up.
Is it still warm in the Algarve in October?
Yes. The average high is about 23°C in Faro and 22°C in Sagres, and early October can still feel like summer.
How much does it rain in the Algarve in October?
Faro averages 56 mm of rain in October over about six rainy days, and Sagres 61 mm over about seven, with about two days of heavy rain.
What time does it get dark in the Algarve in October?
The sun sets at about 7.15pm at the start of October and about 6.40pm just before the clocks go back. After the change, on the last Sunday of the month, sunset is around 5.40pm.
Plan your October golf trip

excerpt: What November weather in the Algarve means for your golf: afternoons of 20°C, the rainy season starting, short days and green fees beginning to fall.

content.text: Is November a good month for golf in the Algarve? It's a good-value month if you're flexible about the weather. Afternoons still average about **20°C**, but November is one of the wettest months of the year, with about seven rainy days in Faro, and the days are short, with sunset between about 5.15pm and 5.35pm. Green fees start to fall: on 7 of the 29 courses we track, November shares the lowest price of the year.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in November from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay and where to play.
Algarve weather in November for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

content.note: Source: IPMA climate normals 1991–2020 for Faro (station 554) and Sagres (station 533), averaged over 30 years. Rainy days have 1 mm of rain or more; heavy rain days 10 mm or more. Daylight is for the middle of the month; sunset is calculated for the first and last day of November, in Portuguese winter time (the same as UK time).
content.caption: November weather in the Algarve

content.text: November is mild: the average high is about 20°C in Faro and 19°C in Sagres, and mornings are around 12°C. It's also when the Algarve's rainy season gets going. Faro averages 76 mm over about seven days, and Sagres 82 mm over about eight, making November the wettest month of the year in the far west. The rain usually comes with Atlantic fronts, so a wet spell of a few days is often followed by a run of clear, calm weather.
What November weather means on the course

**Fairways and greens.** After the first heavy autumn rain, fairways soften and play longer, and some clubs restrict buggies to the paths after a downpour. Greens are receptive and hold approach shots well.
**Tee times.** With about ten hours of daylight and sunset around 5.20pm, tee off by about 1pm to finish 18 holes. Late morning is the most pleasant time to start.

**What to pack.** Layers: short sleeves may still do on a sunny afternoon, but bring a jumper and a good waterproof jacket and trousers. An umbrella, a spare glove and waterproof golf shoes are worth packing in November.
Green fees in November

November is when green fees start to come down after the autumn peak. On 7 of the 29 courses we track, November shares the lowest price of the year, and on average fees are about **17% below** each course's peak. Some courses drop sharply: Monte Rei costs €190 in November against €312 in spring, and the Vilamoura Laguna and Millennium courses are both under €100.

content.text: This November twilight rounds start from €35 at Santo António and €50 at Alto Golf, and €55 at Pestana's [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho), [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta) and [Silves](/courses/silves). With the light going early, check the start time when you book. See also [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Where to play in November

Temperatures are almost the same across the region in November, but the west is wetter: Sagres averages about two more rainy days than Faro. If the forecast is unsettled, the centre and east may give you a slightly better chance of dry rounds. The Vilamoura courses are good value this month, with [Vilamoura Laguna](/courses/vilamoura-laguna) at €88 and [Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium) at €92. If you're weighing up the two ends of the region, read [West vs East Algarve: which side is better for golf?](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf).
Crowds and what else is on in November

The courses quieten down through November after the busy autumn season, and tee times get easier to find, especially later in the month. Hotels are generally cheaper too, but some seasonal resort hotels close for part of the winter, so check that yours is open on your dates. 1 November is a public holiday in Portugal.
Frequently asked questions
Is November a good time to play golf in the Algarve?
Yes, if you're flexible about the weather. Afternoons are still mild, the courses are quieter than in October and green fees are starting to fall. Expect about seven rainy days and short afternoons.
Is the Algarve warm in November?
Mild. The average high is about 20°C in Faro and 19°C in Sagres, with mornings around 12°C.
How much does it rain in the Algarve in November?
Faro averages 76 mm of rain in November over about seven rainy days, and Sagres 82 mm over about eight. In the far west, November is the wettest month of the year.
What time does it get dark in the Algarve in November?
The sun sets at about 5.35pm at the start of November and about 5.15pm at the end. Tee off by about 1pm to finish 18 holes in daylight.

excerpt: Vilamoura, Quarteira and the Golden Triangle put the most courses within a short drive; Albufeira suits groups, Carvoeiro and Tavira are quieter, and Lagos is cheaper. Every base compared, with drive times and hotels.

content.text: The best place to stay for golf in the Algarve depends on how many courses you want to play and what you want from your evenings. If golf comes first, **Vilamoura, Quarteira and the Golden Triangle around Almancil** put the most courses within a short drive, and they are the closest bases to Faro Airport. **Albufeira** suits groups who want nightlife, **Carvoeiro and Tavira** are quieter, and **Lagos and Alvor** are the bases for the western courses, where green fees are often lower.
Use **Find Your Base** on our map: tick the courses, choose how far you are happy to drive, and it shows the area where they all overlap, with the hotels inside it.
content.title: Already know which courses you want to play?
content.buttonLabel: Find your base on the map

content.text: The main golf bases compared

content.note: Drive times from each town centre without traffic (Mapbox, checked 16 November 2026), rounded to the nearest 5 minutes. Counts include 9-hole courses and leave out San Lorenzo (closed until mid-2028) and The Els Club (private). 'Cheapest' is the lowest visitor green fee we list for an 18-hole course within 30 minutes; prices change through the year.
content.caption: Golf courses within a short drive of each base

content.text: The numbers show why golfers keep coming back to the central Algarve: from Almancil, nine courses are within about 15 minutes. In the far west and east there are fewer courses close together, but they are usually cheaper and quieter. Summer traffic on the coast road can add a lot to these times, so in July and August allow extra.
Which base suits your trip?
You want to play as many courses as possible

Stay in **Vilamoura, Quarteira or Almancil**. From Quarteira, 7 courses are within about 15 minutes, including the four Vilamoura Golf courses, Pestana Vila Sol and the two Vale do Lobo courses, and 14 are within half an hour. See [golf near Quarteira](/quarteira/golf-courses) and the [Vilamoura golf courses](/vilamoura/golf-courses).
Luxury and the best-known courses

Stay in the **Golden Triangle**, the area between Almancil, Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo. It has the Algarve's best-known courses, including [Quinta do Lago South](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south) and the clifftop holes of [Vale do Lobo Royal](/courses/vale-do-lobo-royal), and five-star hotels and resort villas. Expect some of the highest green fees in the region: Quinta do Lago South starts at €188. See the [hotels near Quinta do Lago](/guide/hotels-near-quinta-do-lago-golf) and [hotels near Vale do Lobo](/guide/hotels-near-vale-do-lobo-golf).
A golf trip on a budget

Look west to **Lagos and Praia da Luz**, or east to **Tavira**. Around Lagos, [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio) starts at €57, [Espiche](/courses/espiche) at €65 and [Boavista](/courses/boavista) at €74. In the east, [Benamor](/courses/benamor) starts at €66 and [Quinta do Vale](/courses/quinta-do-vale) at €67. You'll have fewer courses within a short drive, so plan two or three rounds rather than six. Our guide to [the best-value golf in the Algarve](/guide/best-value-golf-in-the-algarve) has more ideas.
A short break or a weekend

Stay close to the airport. Almancil and Vilamoura are around 30–35 minutes from Faro Airport, so you can play on the day you land. [Faro](/faro/golf-courses) itself has no course, but Quinta do Lago Laranjal is about 20 minutes from the city. Our [golf weekend in the Algarve](/guide/golf-weekend-in-the-algarve) guide plans three nights and two rounds from four different bases.
Nightlife and group trips

**Albufeira** is the Algarve's party town. Its nightlife is centred on "the Strip", Avenida Sá Carneiro in the Montechoro area, about 3 km east of the old town. The closest courses are [Balaia](/courses/balaia), about 15 minutes away, and [Salgados](/courses/salgados) and [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs), about 20, with the Vilamoura courses around 25. If you'd rather have restaurants and bars than clubs, **Vilamoura's marina** is busy in the evenings and has a casino. For tips on organising a society or a group, read [golf trips for groups](/guide/algarve-golf-trips-for-groups-and-golf-societies).
Peace and quiet

**Tavira** is a historic town on the river Gilão and is much quieter than the central resorts, with [Benamor](/courses/benamor) about 15 minutes away and the two Quinta da Ria courses about 20. **Carvoeiro** is a small cliffside village with Gramacho, Vale da Pinta and Vale de Milho all within about 15 minutes. **Praia da Luz** is a small resort west of Lagos, about 10 minutes from Boavista.
Golfers with non-golfing partners, families or beginners

Pick a base with a short course that needs no handicap certificate, so everyone can play. [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs) (9 holes) is next to [Olhos de Água](/olhos-de-agua/golf-courses), the 9-hole [Penina Resort](/courses/penina-resort) course is about 15 minutes from [Alvor](/alvor/golf-courses), and [Vale de Milho](/courses/vale-de-milho), a 9-hole par-3 course, is in Carvoeiro. [Balaia](/courses/balaia), another 9-hole par-3 course near Albufeira, does ask for a handicap. For lessons, see the [Algarve golf academies](/golf-academies).
Without a car

The easiest way is to stay at a resort with its own course, so the first tee is a walk away: see our list of [Algarve hotels with a golf course on site](/guide/algarve-hotels-with-a-golf-course-on-site). The train line along the coast stops in the centre of Lagos, Faro and Tavira, but Albufeira's station is several kilometres outside the town, and most courses are a taxi ride from the nearest station. For getting from the airport, see [Faro Airport to the Algarve golf courses](/guide/faro-airport-to-algarve-golf-courses).
The bases one by one
A few well-rated hotels in each base, all checked for our other hotel guides. Prices are the lowest we found for a recent date and change with the season, so check your own dates.
Vilamoura and Quarteira

Vilamoura is built around its marina, with the four Vilamoura Golf courses and Pestana Vila Sol all within about 15 minutes. Quarteira, its beach-town neighbour, is just as close to the courses. From Vilamoura's marina, 13 courses are within 30 minutes. More in [golf near Quarteira](/quarteira/golf-courses) and [golf hotels near Vilamoura](/guide/golf-hotels-near-vilamoura).
Open Find Your Base with these courses already ticked to see hotels in the area where they overlap.

content.name: Dom José Beach Hotel
content.text: A three-star beach hotel in Quarteira, rated **8.9 on Booking.com** and from about €61 a night in October. It has no golf services of its own, but Pinhal is about 13 minutes away and the Old Course about 15, and breakfast starts at 7.30am.

content.name: Hilton Vilamoura As Cascatas Golf Resort & Spa
content.text: A five-star resort overlooking the Pinhal course and one of Vilamoura Golf's official partner hotels, rated **8.5 on Booking.com** and from about €112 a night in October. The Old Course is about 5 minutes away.
content.locationLabel: Next to the Pinhal course, Vilamoura

content.name: Tivoli Marina Vilamoura Algarve Resort
content.text: A big five-star resort right between the marina and the beach, rated **8.9 on Booking.com** from more than 1,600 reviews. It suits golfers travelling with non-golfing partners or family, with the beach, pools and marina all on the doorstep. Pinhal is about 11 minutes away and the Old Course about 14.
perks: Right between the marina and the beach
content.locationLabel: Between the marina and the beach, Vilamoura

content.text: Almancil and the Golden Triangle

Quinta do Lago's three courses, Pinheiros Altos and the two Vale do Lobo courses are all about 10 minutes from Almancil, and Vilamoura is around 15–20. The area is known for five-star hotels and resort villas, but there are simpler apartments too. More in [hotels near Quinta do Lago](/guide/hotels-near-quinta-do-lago-golf).
Open Find Your Base with these courses already ticked to see hotels in the area where they overlap.

content.name: WOT Algarve Soul
content.text: Simple apartments and studios on the Almancil side, rated **8.5 on Booking.com** and from about €54 a night in October, which is rare for this area. It has no golf services of its own, but it's about 6 minutes from the Royal and 10 from the South Course.
content.locationLabel: Almancil side of the Golden Triangle

content.name: Vilar do Golf
content.text: Apartments right beside the South Course, two minutes from the clubhouse, rated **8.8 on Booking.com** and from about €103 a night in October. The resort offers a **golf club rental service**, handy if you're travelling light, and every apartment has a kitchen.

content.name: Conrad Algarve
content.text: A five-star hotel rated **9.0 on Booking.com**, from about €170 a night in October. Its **golf concierge** can book your rounds, and breakfast starts at 7am, which suits an early tee time. It sits between the two courses, 6 minutes from the South and 8 from the Royal.
perks: Lessons with a PGA golf pro
Signature Quinta do Lago Golf Experience packages
content.locationLabel: Between Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo

content.text: Albufeira and Olhos de Água

Albufeira has the most hotels and nightlife in the Algarve. The short courses at Balaia and Pine Cliffs are closest, with Salgados and the Vilamoura courses within about 25 minutes. Olhos de Água, a quieter beach village just to the east, is the better pick if you want to be closer to Vilamoura. More in [golf near Olhos de Água](/olhos-de-agua/golf-courses) and the [cheapest golf near Albufeira](/guide/cheapest-golf-near-albufeira).
Open Find Your Base with these courses already ticked to see hotels in the area where they overlap.

content.name: Alfagar Village
content.text: Clifftop apartments above Santa Eulália beach, just three minutes from Balaia and rated 8.8 by guests. It has no golf services of its own, but it is one of the closest and best-value options, with a heated indoor pool and gym for the cooler months, massages on request and a paid airport transfer.

content.name: PortoBay Blue Ocean
content.text: A clifftop hotel just west of Pine Cliffs, rated **9.2 on Booking.com** and from about €113 a night. It is not adults-only, but it has a lounge area reserved for adults and a calm, couple-friendly feel. Breakfast starts at 7.30am.

content.name: Pine Cliffs Ocean Suites, a Luxury Collection Resort & Spa
content.text: Suites and apartments at the Pine Cliffs resort, which has its own 9-hole clifftop course that needs no handicap. All rooms interconnect, which makes it popular with families, and guests get free access to the resort's Oasis Thermal area.
perks: Lower green fees for resort guests

content.text: Carvoeiro and Armação de Pêra

Carvoeiro is a small cliffside village, with Gramacho, Vale da Pinta and the 9-hole Vale de Milho all within about 15 minutes and Pestana Ferragudo about 15–20. A little further east, Armação de Pêra is the closest town to Salgados and Amendoeira. More in [golf near Armação de Pêra](/armacao-de-pera/golf-courses) and [hotels near Vale de Milho](/guide/hotels-near-vale-de-milho-golf).
Open Find Your Base with these courses already ticked to see hotels in the area where they overlap.

content.name: Pestana Palm Gardens
content.text: Clifftop studios and apartments in Carvoeiro run by Pestana, the same group that owns Ferragudo. Pestana says guests get **exclusive benefits and discounts at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta**, so it is a smart base if you want to play all three Pestana courses. Breakfast starts at 8am and is charged separately, but every unit has a kitchen, so an early bite before your round is easy.
perks: Discounts at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta

content.name: Tivoli Carvoeiro Algarve Resort
content.text: A five-star clifftop resort a short walk from Carvoeiro village, rated **8.6 on Booking.com**, with sea views, a full spa and indoor and outdoor pools. UK golf tour operators sell packages here that include rounds at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta.

content.name: Vila Vita Parc
content.text: A clifftop resort near Porches rated an exceptional **9.5 on Booking.com**, from about €246 a night in October. It's 15 minutes from Salgados and 18 from Amendoeira. Pick it if the weekend is a special occasion rather than just a golf trip.
content.locationLabel: Clifftop near Porches and Armação de Pêra

content.text: Portimão and Alvor

Portimão and Alvor are the bases for the Sir Henry Cotton courses: [Alto Golf](/courses/alto-golf) is about 5 minutes from both, and [Penina](/courses/penina-championship) about 15–20. Pestana Ferragudo is about 15 minutes from Portimão, Gramacho and Vale da Pinta about 20, Morgado about 25 and Álamos about 30. More in [golf near Alvor](/alvor/golf-courses) and [hotels near Penina](/guide/hotels-near-penina-golf-resort).
Open Find Your Base with these courses already ticked to see hotels in the area where they overlap.

content.name: Jupiter Marina Hotel
content.text: A stylish hotel on Portimão marina, with a spa, a rooftop bar and a free shuttle to Praia da Rocha beach. It scores **9.0 on Booking.com**, unusually high for the price, and breakfast starts at 7.30am. Parking is paid.

content.name: RR Alvor Baía Resort
content.text: A large, family-friendly resort of suites with kitchenettes, with a spa, gym and heated hydrotherapy pool. For golfers the useful detail is breakfast: it starts at 7am, and the hotel offers **a breakfast pack for early-morning departures** if you ask at reception the day before, ideal for a first tee time at Penina.

content.name: Penina Hotel & Golf Resort
content.text: The Algarve's original golf resort, with the 18-hole Championship and the 9-hole Resort course on site. The Championship course was designed by Sir Henry Cotton. Penina's "Best Available Rate for Golfers" includes **a complimentary round every day** on one of its courses (a handicap certificate is needed for the Championship course). Breakfast starts at 7am.
perks: Free daily round on the golfer rate

content.text: Lagos and Praia da Luz

Lagos has a lively old town and a marina, with Boavista about 10 minutes away and Palmares and Espiche about 20. Praia da Luz is quieter and closer to Boavista, Espiche and Santo António. Green fees here are among the lowest in the Algarve, but Vilamoura and Quinta do Lago are about an hour away. More in [golf near Praia da Luz](/praia-da-luz/golf-courses) and [hotels near Boavista](/guide/hotels-near-boavista-golf).
Open Find Your Base with these courses already ticked to see hotels in the area where they overlap.

content.name: Hotel Marina Rio
content.text: A four-star hotel opposite Lagos marina, a short walk from the old town, rated **9.0 on Booking.com** from more than 1,000 reviews. A private garage is available if you reserve in advance. About 9 minutes from Boavista.

content.name: Belavista da Luz
content.text: A four-star wellness hotel in Praia da Luz, rated **8.5 on Booking.com** from more than 1,000 reviews, with a spa. About 8 minutes from Boavista.

content.name: Palmares Beach House Hotel
content.text: The five-star boutique hotel on the Palmares resort, adults only, with just 20 rooms including two suites. It scores **8.9 on Booking.com**, and Palmares sells Stay & Play packages that combine a stay with rounds on its 27 holes. Right at Palmares.
Tavira and the east

Tavira is the base for the eastern courses: Benamor about 15 minutes away, Quinta da Ria and Quinta de Cima about 20, and Quinta do Vale and Castro Marim about 25–30. Monte Rei, the Jack Nicklaus course, is about 35 minutes from Tavira and closer to Monte Gordo. More in [golf near Monte Gordo](/monte-gordo/golf-courses) and [hotels near Quinta da Ria](/guide/hotels-near-quinta-da-ria-golf).
Open Find Your Base with these courses already ticked to see hotels in the area where they overlap.

content.name: Hotel Don Rodrigues
content.text: A small hotel rated **8.8 on Booking.com**, from €65 a night **with breakfast** on its own website. It has an outdoor pool and free parking, and it's 12 minutes from Benamor. Breakfast starts at 8am, so for an early tee time ask about something to take with you.

content.name: OZADI Tavira Hotel
content.text: A four-star hotel on the edge of Tavira, rated **9.0 on Booking.com** from more than 3,700 reviews and from about €77 a night in November. Benamor is about 6 minutes away, and it has two pools and free parking.

content.name: Pousada Convento Tavira
content.text: A Pousada in a former 16th-century convent in the centre of Tavira, rated **9.0 on Booking.com** and from €131 a night on its own website. You can walk to the old town's restaurants after the round. Breakfast runs from 8am to 11am.
Faro

Faro is the Algarve's capital and the airport is on the edge of the city, but there is no golf course in Faro itself. It works for a night before an early flight or a short city break with a round at [Quinta do Lago Laranjal](/courses/quinta-do-lago-laranjal), about 20 minutes away. For hotels in the city, see [golf near Faro](/faro/golf-courses).
Plan the rest of your trip

Once you've picked a base, compare green fees in the [full list of Algarve golf courses](/courses), check [how to get from Faro Airport to your base with clubs](/guide/faro-airport-to-algarve-golf-courses), and if you're not bringing your own set, read our [club rental guide](/club-rental).
Tick the courses you want to play in **Find Your Base** and the map shows the best area to stay, with the hotels inside it.

excerpt: Lagos golf courses are about an hour from Faro Airport, Santo António further still. Car hire, transfer, taxi, Aerobus and train compared for golfers.

content.text: Lagos's golf courses are about an hour from Faro Airport, and the far west takes up to about 1h 15. This is the longest trip most Algarve golfers make, and it's where a hire car makes the strongest case for itself: one-way transfers cost about €80–110, and a taxi can reach €120. Each option is compared below.

content.note: Taxi and transfer figures for Lagos from fare-comparison and local guide sites, 2026, which vary by date. Courses further west cost more.
rows: Fine for one or two bags, but pricey
content.caption: Your options at a glance

content.text: Drive times to Lagos and far-west courses

content.note: Road-routing estimates from the terminal without traffic, rounded to the nearest 5 minutes.

content.text: Why a hire car often wins for Lagos

A return transfer from the airport comes to roughly €160 to €215 before you've played a hole, so compare that with the price of a car for your dates. You'll probably want one anyway: Palmares and Boavista are close to Lagos, but Espiche and Santo António are further out towards Sagres, and Penina and Morgado are a short drive east.
The A22 takes you most of the way, with no tolls since January 2025. Compare airport rental deals on [EconomyBookings](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw), and pick something with a long boot.
Transfers for a group of four

For a four-ball, a minivan at about **€126** works out at just over €30 each, one way, with room for everybody's bag. One or two golfers will pay roughly €80 to €110 for a sedan, depending on the company and date. Compare current offers on [GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA).
What a taxi costs from Faro to Lagos

A taxi all the way to Lagos is about **€74** on a weekday under the new national tariff, but it's about €98 by day and €118 at night or at weekends on a meter that hasn't been updated. Meters have until 21 January 2027 to change. With such a wide gap, a fixed price is the safer choice.
Can you take the bus or train with clubs?

The **Vamus Aerobus** runs direct to the centre of Lagos in about 1h 55 for about €17. There are around seven departures a day from May to October and far fewer in winter, with the last reported at 18:15. The train is cheaper, at about €8 plus about €2.80 for bus 16 from the airport to Faro station, but the rail leg alone takes about 1h 45.

Neither is built for a golf bag, and you'd still need a car from Lagos to any of the courses. Check [Vamus](https://www.vamusalgarve.pt/vamus/schedules) and [CP](https://www.cp.pt) for current times if you're travelling light with hired clubs.
Hire your clubs near the course

A long journey is a good reason to leave your bag at home. The [Algarve rental directory](/shops) lists shops across the region, and [ClubsToHire](/shops/clubstohire-faro-airport) is available at the airport itself.
Where to stay in the western Algarve

Choose from our guides to [hotels near Palmares](/guide/hotels-near-palmares-golf), [Boavista](/guide/hotels-near-boavista-golf), [Espiche](/guide/hotels-near-espiche-golf) and [Santo António](/guide/hotels-near-santo-antonio-golf). There's more on the [courses around Lagos](/lagos/golf-courses), and the [full table of times from Faro Airport](/guide/faro-airport-to-algarve-golf-courses) covers the rest of the Algarve.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Lagos and Portimão costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-lagos-and-portimao-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: Tavira's golf courses are about 40–45 minutes from Faro Airport, and Monte Rei about an hour. Transfer, taxi, train and car hire compared for golfers.

content.text: Tavira's golf courses are about 40 to 45 minutes from Faro Airport, Castro Marim about 50 and Monte Rei about an hour. A transfer to Tavira costs from about €55, and a taxi roughly €35–50. With clubs, Monte Rei is the one to plan carefully, as the last stretch runs on local roads.

content.note: Tavira transfer price from a fare-comparison site, October 2026. Taxi ranges are our estimates from the old and new national tariffs. Checked November 2026.
rows: Fine for one or two bags
content.caption: Your options at a glance

content.text: Drive times to the eastern Algarve courses

content.note: Road-routing estimates from the terminal without traffic, rounded to the nearest 5 minutes.

content.text: Getting to Monte Rei

[Monte Rei](/courses/monte-rei) is inland, north of the A22, and most of its route is fast motorway. The slower part comes after you leave it, on rural roads for the final few kilometres. We calculate about an hour for the 65km, and other published times range from about 45 to 60 minutes, so an hour is a sensible figure to plan around.

A taxi all the way works out at about €55 on the new tariff and up to €85 on the old one at night; one guide quotes €70–90. Don't count on finding a taxi waiting at a rural resort for the trip back. It makes sense to pre-book both directions, or ask the resort if it can arrange your transfer.
Tavira by taxi or transfer

A pre-booked sedan to Tavira was quoted at about **€55** in October 2026, while a taxi costs about €35 on a new meter and €43–52 on an old one until meters change by 21 January 2027. For one or two golfers landing on a weekday, the taxi rank may be cheaper. For a group, or to know your price in advance, [GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA) can quote for a vehicle with room for everybody's bag.
Is the train from Faro to Tavira worth it?

Tavira is the one golfing town where the train is at least tempting. It takes about 40 to 50 minutes from Faro station and costs only a few euros. But the airport has no station, so you'd start with bus 16 or a taxi into Faro, and all told it's about an hour and a half. You'd also need a taxi from Tavira station to the course.
That's two changes with a golf bag, and space on regional trains can be tight. It's a sensible choice only if you've arranged hire clubs and are staying in town.
Hiring a car for the east

Benamor and the two Quinta courses are all near Tavira, Quinta do Vale and Castro Marim are towards the Spanish border, and the A22 links them all without tolls. If you're planning to play a few of them, a car works well, and is the easiest way to include Monte Rei. Compare options on [EconomyBookings](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw).
Save yourself the baggage

Leave the bag behind and collect a set at the airport from [ClubsToHire](/shops/clubstohire-faro-airport). Or read our guide to [renting clubs at Faro](/guide/hiring-golf-clubs-at-faro-airport) for other choices.
Plan your golf trip in the east

See our picks for [hotels near Monte Rei](/guide/hotels-near-monte-rei-golf), [Benamor](/guide/hotels-near-benamor-golf), [Quinta da Ria](/guide/hotels-near-quinta-da-ria-golf) and [Castro Marim](/guide/hotels-near-castro-marim-golf), or browse [Tavira](/tavira/golf-courses) and [Castro Marim](/castro-marim/golf-courses) course pages. For other areas, use our [drive times from Faro Airport to every course](/guide/faro-airport-to-algarve-golf-courses).

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Monte Rei costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-monte-rei-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: Penina and Portimão's courses are 55–65 minutes from Faro Airport. Taxi, transfer, Aerobus, train and car hire compared for golfers with clubs.

content.text: Golf around Portimão and Alvor, including Penina, is about 55 to 65 minutes from Faro Airport. At this distance the meter really starts to add up: a taxi runs from about €60 to €95, against about €81 for a pre-booked sedan. Which is cheaper depends largely on what time you land.

content.note: Transfer and taxi figures from a fare-comparison site, October 2026, for Portimão. Prices vary by date and your exact destination.
rows: About €60 on a new meter, €78–94 on an old one
Fine for one or two bags
Best for late arrivals and groups

content.text: Drive times to Penina, Morgado and other western courses

content.note: Road-routing estimates from the terminal without traffic, rounded to the nearest 5 minutes.

content.text: When does a taxi beat a transfer?

With two tariffs running until 21 January 2027, a taxi fare to Portimão is hard to predict. On a meter already updated to the new national rate, a weekday daytime journey comes to about **€60**, which beats a fixed-price car. On one still using the old rate, the same trip costs about **€78**, or **€94** at night and at weekends.

So if you land on a weekday afternoon, the rank is worth a try, and you can ask the driver for an estimate first. If you land after dark or at the weekend, or there are three of you with clubs, we'd book ahead. A sedan was quoted at **€81** in October 2026, and [GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA) lets you compare offers and request a larger vehicle.
Getting to Penina

[Penina](/courses/penina-championship) is a common choice on this route, and the resort has its own hotel. It's about 74km from the airport, between Portimão and Alvor. Give your driver the resort's name rather than just Portimão, as it isn't in the town itself.
Aerobus and train with a golf bag

The **Vamus Aerobus** calls at Portimão for about €14 per person, and the regional train costs about €6.80, but the airport has no station, so you'd first have to get into Faro. Neither drops you at a course. Both can save money for a golfer who has hired clubs and is staying in town; with a travel bag, they're more trouble than they're worth.
A hire car for the west

Morgado and Alamos, Alto, Penina and Ferragudo are in different directions, and a car lets you play them all without arranging a pickup each morning. It also opens up Lagos and Carvoeiro as day trips. See what's available on [EconomyBookings](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw), and make sure the boot will take your bags.
Rent your clubs instead

Close to an hour's drive is a long way to carry a bag you could leave at home. Our guide to [hiring clubs at Faro Airport](/guide/hiring-golf-clubs-at-faro-airport) covers the companies at the terminal, including ClubsToHire.
Plan your stay in the western Algarve

We have guides to [hotels near Penina](/guide/hotels-near-penina-golf-resort), [hotels near Morgado and Alamos](/guide/hotels-near-morgado-and-alamos-golf) and [hotels near Ferragudo](/guide/hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course). You can also browse [golf courses around Portimão](/portimao/golf-courses), or see [how long the drive takes to every other course](/guide/faro-airport-to-algarve-golf-courses).

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Lagos and Portimão costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-lagos-and-portimao-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: Hotel golf shuttles, private transfers, taxis and Uber: how to get from your hotel to the golf course in the Algarve without a hire car, and what it costs.

content.text: You don't need a hire car to play golf in the Algarve, but you do need a plan for getting to the first tee. The options are a **free hotel golf shuttle** (several hotels in Vilamoura and Quinta do Lago run one), a **private golf transfer** booked in advance, a **taxi** or **Uber**, or staying at a resort where the course is a short walk away. Short trips are cheap: a taxi from Quarteira to Pestana Vila Sol should cost around €5–10. Longer ones add up quickly, so where you stay matters more than anything.
Your options at a glance

content.note: Costs checked 17 November 2026. Taxi figures are our own estimates from the official tariff; see below.

From about €30 each way per car

Metered; about €5–25 for most short trips

content.caption: Getting from your hotel to the golf course

content.text: Free hotel golf shuttles

Some hotels run their own shuttle to nearby courses, which is the easiest option if your tee times fit its timetable. These are examples we found on the hotels' own websites in November 2026, not a complete list:

**[Vila Galé Marina](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/vilagalemarina.html)**, Vilamoura: free transport for golfers to the Old Course, Pinhal, Millennium and Laguna. The hotel also lists Victoria, now [The Els Club](/courses/victoria-els-club), which has since become a private members club.

**[Hotel Quinta do Lago](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/quintadolago.html)**: a free shuttle to the golf courses within Quinta do Lago, according to the hotel's FAQ. See our [hotels near Quinta do Lago](/guide/hotels-near-quinta-do-lago-golf) for more places to stay there.
**[Domes Lake Algarve](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/domes-lake-algarve.html)**, Vilamoura: free shuttles to the golf courses, plus paid VIP shuttles, according to the resort's golf page.
**[As Cascatas Resort & Spa](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/as-cascatas.html)**, Vilamoura: a free shuttle to the [Pinhal](/courses/vilamoura-pinhal) course.

Golf package sellers also list transfers or shuttles at hotels such as Tivoli Marina Vilamoura, the Hilton Vilamoura As Cascatas and the Dom Pedro hotels in Vilamoura, but these can depend on the package you buy. Whatever you book, ask the hotel which courses the shuttle serves, what time it leaves and whether you need to reserve a seat.
Private golf transfers

A private transfer is a car or minibus booked for your group, with room for golf bags. It is the most reliable option for an early tee time or a course more than 20 minutes away. Prices are per vehicle, so they work out cheaper per person in a group of three or four. You can compare transfer quotes on [GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA), or book with a local company that specialises in golf.
To give you an idea of prices, this is what Algarserra, a transfer company based in Vilamoura, publishes for one-way trips from Vilamoura:

content.note: Source: Algarserra's published golf transfer prices, "prices each way", including taxes and tolls, checked 17 November 2026. Other companies charge differently, and some quote per person.
content.caption: Golf transfer prices from Vilamoura (one way, per vehicle)

content.text: Remember to book the return leg as well: most rounds take four to five hours, and a driver won't normally wait at the course. If you plan to play the same course several times, ask for a price for the whole week.
Taxis

Taxis in Portugal are metered, so there is no fixed price per trip. A new national taxi tariff came into force on 23 October 2026, and taxi meters have until January 2027 to switch over, so for now the same journey can cost a little more or less depending on the taxi. These are our estimates for some typical hotel-to-course trips, from a weekday daytime trip on the new tariff up to a weekend trip:

Rounded to the nearest €5.

content.text: For an early tee time, book the taxi the evening before through your hotel reception, and for the trip back ask the clubhouse to call one when you finish. With three or four golf bags, ask for a larger car or an estate.
Uber and Bolt

Uber has operated in the Algarve since 2016, when it launched in Faro, Vilamoura and Albufeira, and it now covers the main towns. Drivers are easier to find in the busy central areas than in small villages or very early in the morning. Uber's own advice is that boot space is not guaranteed, so with golf bags choose **UberXL** and message the driver to check your bags will fit. Bolt also operates in the Algarve, including at Faro Airport.
Stay where you can walk to the first tee

The simplest way to play without a car is to stay at a resort with its own course, so the first tee is a short walk from your room. Our list of [Algarve hotels with a golf course on site](/guide/algarve-hotels-with-a-golf-course-on-site) covers them. If you want to play a few different courses, choose a base with several courses close together: from Quarteira or Almancil, seven to nine courses are within about 15 minutes. Our guide to [where to stay in the Algarve for golf](/guide/where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf) compares every base.
Tick the courses you want to play in **Find Your Base** and the map shows the area where they are all a short drive away, with the hotels inside it.
content.title: Choose a base close to your courses
content.buttonLabel: Find your base on the map

content.text: Trains and buses

The Algarve's coastal railway stops in the centre of Lagos, Faro and Tavira, but most golf courses are a taxi ride from the nearest station, and timetables rarely suit an early tee time. Albufeira's station is several kilometres outside the town. Local buses are fine for getting around town, but carrying a golf bag on them every day is not practical.
Transfers or a hire car?

Transfers make sense if you stay close to the courses you want to play. From Vilamoura, a round at Quinta do Lago costs €65 in transfers there and back, or about €16 each for four golfers. Further away the numbers grow quickly: a round at Penina from Vilamoura costs €125 in transfers, before the green fee. If you plan to play courses in different parts of the Algarve, or you are a couple rather than a four-ball, a hire car is likely to work out cheaper, so compare a quote for your dates.

You can compare hire car prices at Faro Airport on [EconomyBookings](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw). With golf bags, choose an estate car or an SUV with a large boot. Our [Faro car hire guide](/guide/faro-car-hire-for-golfers) covers which cars fit golf bags, deposits and tolls.
Getting from Faro Airport

For the first and last journey of your trip, see our guide to [getting from Faro Airport to the Algarve golf courses](/guide/faro-airport-to-algarve-golf-courses), with taxi, transfer and bus options for every area. Transfers with room for golf bags can be booked on [GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA).

excerpt: Golf buggy hire prices at Algarve courses, which green fees include a buggy, and the rules on who can drive, checked against official club sources.

content.text: Golf buggy hire in the Algarve costs between **€40 and €55** for 18 holes at the courses that publish a price, and a few courses include a buggy in the green fee. Many clubs don't publish a hire price at all, and the rules on who can drive differ from one course to the next.

We checked each course's own price list, rules and online booking system, and this guide only includes what those sources state. Where a club doesn't publish something, we say so, and a course missing from a list here may simply not publish that information. **Last checked: November 2026.**
Algarve golf buggy prices by course
These are the current hire prices published by the clubs themselves. Most lists don't say whether the price is per buggy or per person, so it's worth asking when you book.

content.note: Source: each club's official price list or website, checked November 2026. Salgados publishes its prices as valid until 31 December 2026.
content.caption: Published buggy hire prices

content.text: [Pestana](/courses/gramacho) also lists a twilight buggy at €40 for its courses. [Boavista](/courses/boavista)'s tariff shows a single €45 price without saying whether it covers 18 or 9 holes.
[Penina](/courses/penina-championship)'s last published list showed €55 for 18 holes and €35 for 9, but that list expired in October 2025, so contact the course for the current price.
Algarve golf courses where a buggy is included
At these courses, the green fee already covers a buggy, which is worth remembering when you compare prices with other courses.
**[Ombria](/courses/ombria)**: the club's rules say green fees always include a buggy on a shared basis, subject to availability. It may charge for a second buggy if you don't want to share.
**[Monte Rei](/courses/monte-rei)**: the club's online booking lists a buggy as part of its standard and twilight green fees.

**Amendoeira ([Faldo](/courses/amendoeira-faldo) and [O'Connor](/courses/amendoeira-oconnor))**: the online green fees are marked "Buggy included, if available". That wording means you shouldn't assume one is guaranteed, particularly if a buggy is essential for you.

[Vale do Lobo](/courses/vale-do-lobo-royal) includes a shared buggy on its Sunset green fee for full-paying adults, though not on its standard rate. Quinta do Lago states the opposite for its standard online rates: the buggy is not included.
Courses with buggies but no published hire price
You can get a buggy at these courses, but we couldn't find a current hire price from the club. Contact the course for the price before you travel:

[Quinta do Lago South](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south), [North](/courses/quinta-do-lago-north) and [Laranjal](/courses/quinta-do-lago-laranjal); [Vale do Lobo Royal](/courses/vale-do-lobo-royal) and [Ocean](/courses/vale-do-lobo-ocean); the four Vilamoura courses ([Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course), [Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium), [Pinhal](/courses/vilamoura-pinhal) and [Laguna](/courses/vilamoura-laguna)); [Palmares](/courses/palmares); [Espiche](/courses/espiche); [Quinta da Ria](/courses/quinta-da-ria), [Quinta de Cima](/courses/quinta-de-cima) and [Quinta do Vale](/courses/quinta-do-vale); [Morgado](/courses/morgado) and [Alamos](/courses/alamos); and [Pestana Ferragudo](/courses/pestana-ferragudo).
For [Pinheiros Altos](/courses/pinheiros-altos), we couldn't find current buggy details from an official source, so contact the course directly.
Algarve courses that may not have buggies
[Vale de Milho](/courses/vale-de-milho), a short 9-hole course, says plainly that it doesn't have buggies to hire but does offer trolleys.

The price lists at [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs) and [Balaia](/courses/balaia) include trolleys but no buggies. Neither club says outright that it has none, so contact the course if you need one.
Golf buggy rules: age limits and where you can drive
If a junior in your group wants to drive, check first, as the minimum age isn't the same everywhere.

content.note: Source: each club's published rules, checked November 2026.
