Two players and two bags per buggy
Two people per buggy; golf courses only, never public roads
Stay on paths, or in the rough where there are none; two players and two bags; only the club's own buggies
Two people per buggy; can be restricted by the weather
content.caption: Published buggy rules

content.text: The **90-degree rule** means you stay on the path until you're level with your ball, then turn straight across the fairway to reach it and return the same way.

[Quinta do Vale](/courses/quinta-do-vale) is the only club we found that publishes a driving licence requirement: its booking conditions say only driving licence holders may drive its buggies. Elsewhere, if that matters to you or your group, ask when you book.

Weather can also change your plans. Vilamoura's course manager can stop buggies being used when necessary to protect the course, and Ombria and Penina state similar restrictions, so a buggy isn't guaranteed after heavy rain, even if you've paid for a round.
How to pay less for a buggy
The simplest saving is a rate that bundles the green fee with a shared buggy. These are the offers published at the time of writing:
**Quinta do Vale**: until 30 November 2026, €130 for one player with a buggy or €225 for two sharing, which works out at €112.50 each.
**Quinta da Ria and Quinta de Cima**: in December 2026, €120 for one player with a buggy or €220 for two sharing. In January 2027, it's €125 or €230.
**Quinta do Lago North and Laranjal**: from 1 December to 31 January, €170 per person for two players sharing a buggy.

**Vilamoura Laguna**: a free shared buggy on new bookings made by 31 December 2026, for play from 19 October 2026 to 31 December 2027. It isn't valid from 1 April to 31 May or from 16 September to 18 October 2027.
[Palmares](/courses/palmares) and [Espiche](/courses/espiche) also sell online rates that include a buggy, with prices that vary by date. Compare the two options before adding a buggy on arrival.
Is a golf buggy worth it in the Algarve?

It depends on the course, the season and how far you like to walk. A buggy makes the most sense on hilly courses and in the summer heat, and for anyone who finds a full 18 holes on foot too tiring. [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio) is one example: the club itself lists a buggy as recommended, and adds that its buggies don't have GPS.

If you do want one, reserve it when you book your tee time rather than leaving it until you arrive, because several clubs describe buggies as subject to availability. If you'd rather stay on foot, see our guide to [Algarve golf courses you can walk](/guide/algarve-golf-courses-you-can-walk).

**Booking your rounds?** Our guide to [how to book tee times in the Algarve](/guide/how-to-book-tee-times-in-the-algarve) shows how each course takes bookings, when to book and the cancellation rules to check.

**Travelling as a group?** Our guide to [Algarve golf trips for groups and golf societies](/guide/algarve-golf-trips-for-groups-and-golf-societies) covers golf villas and apartments, booking tee times together, buggies and minivans.

excerpt: Flat and gently rolling Algarve golf courses that suit walkers, short 9-hole options and trolley hire prices, checked against club and independent sources.

content.text: You don't need a buggy to enjoy golf in the Algarve. Several courses have flat or gently rolling ground that suits walkers, and a handful of short 9-hole courses are an easy way to play on foot.

This isn't a complete list. We've only included courses where we found enough information from the club or an independent golf guide, so a course that isn't mentioned here may still be a good walk. Terrain is also a matter of opinion: what feels easy to one golfer can feel tiring to another. **Last checked: November 2026.**
Flat Algarve golf courses that are easy to walk

**[Salgados](/courses/salgados)** has the strongest evidence of any course we checked. The club describes it as set on the flatlands behind Praia de Galé, Where2Golf says players generally walk it, and Teetimes.pt calls it totally flat, with a buggy optional. Flat doesn't mean easy, though: there's plenty of water, and the site is exposed to the wind.

**[Penina Championship](/courses/penina-championship)** is listed by Teetimes.pt as flat, with some gentle slopes on the approaches to the greens. Golfbreaks also describes its relatively flat appearance as deceptive, because of the streams and water hazards. The club itself mentions subtle slopes and raised greens.
**[Quinta do Lago Laranjal](/courses/quinta-do-lago-laranjal)** is described by Teetimes.pt as flat, with no severe slopes, and easy to walk. It's exposed, so expect to feel any breeze.
**[Vilamoura Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium)** is listed by Teetimes.pt as flat with minor slopes.

**[Amendoeira O'Connor](/courses/amendoeira-oconnor)** stays down in the valley on flat terrain among orange groves, according to Teetimes.pt, which contrasts it with the Faldo course on the hillside. The online green fee includes a buggy, if one is available, so walking won't save you money here.
Gently rolling courses near Tavira
**[Quinta da Ria](/courses/quinta-da-ria)** spans what the club calls gently sloping terrain leading towards the Ria Formosa. Teetimes.pt describes long rolling slopes and a fairly flat course.
**[Quinta de Cima](/courses/quinta-de-cima)**, its neighbour, has gentle, long rolling fairways with few major inclines, according to Teetimes.pt.
Short 9-hole courses for an easy round on foot
If you'd rather not walk 18 holes, a 9-hole course is the simplest answer.
**[Penina Resort Course](/courses/penina-resort)** is listed by Teetimes.pt as flat and easy walking. At 2,987 metres from the white tees, it's still a proper 9-hole course.

**[Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs)** is described by Teetimes.pt as flat with slight rolling slopes. Its price list has manual and electric trolleys but no buggies, so check with the course first if you might need to ride.
**[Vale de Milho](/courses/vale-de-milho)** is the shortest course we track, at 926 metres. The club doesn't have buggies to hire, but it does offer trolleys. Rental equipment is available until 3pm.
**[Balaia](/courses/balaia)** is a short par-3 course with a pull trolley on its price list, though Teetimes.pt notes it's hilly for a par 3.
More Algarve courses where a buggy may be optional
On these courses, the sources we checked don't treat a buggy as a must, so they may suit fit walkers, although most have some slopes:

[Espiche](/courses/espiche)'s own website calls it enjoyable to walk, while also mentioning elevation changes. Golfbreaks describes [Vilamoura Laguna](/courses/vilamoura-laguna) as a flatter, links-style layout.

Teetimes.pt lists a buggy as optional at [Quinta do Lago South](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south) and [Vilamoura Pinhal](/courses/vilamoura-pinhal), and as needed only if essential at [Alto Golf](/courses/alto-golf), the [Vilamoura Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course), [Vila Sol](/courses/vila-sol), [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta) and [Pinheiros Altos](/courses/pinheiros-altos). At Pinheiros Altos, the same guide says the Olives nine is flat, while the Pines and Corks nines are more undulating.
Courses where you may want a buggy

Some golfers walk these too, but the sources we checked point towards riding. [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio) says its course runs over hills and lists a buggy as recommended. Teetimes.pt calls a buggy essential at [Castro Marim](/courses/castro-marim), [Boavista](/courses/boavista), [Quinta do Vale](/courses/quinta-do-vale), [Quinta do Lago North](/courses/quinta-do-lago-north) and [Vale do Lobo Ocean](/courses/vale-do-lobo-ocean). It also recommends one at [Vale do Lobo Royal](/courses/vale-do-lobo-royal), [Benamor](/courses/benamor), [Morgado](/courses/morgado) and [Alamos](/courses/alamos).

For prices and rules, see our [guide to golf buggy hire in the Algarve](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve). It also covers courses where a buggy comes with the green fee. You can also read more about [hilly golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/hilly-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Algarve golf trolley hire prices
A trolley takes most of the effort out of walking. These are prices published by the clubs for 18 holes:

content.text: Before you walk an Algarve golf course
**Check that walking is allowed.** Golfbreaks notes that walking policies vary by course, so ask when you book, especially if the green fee includes a buggy.
**Choose your tee time for the season.** In summer, an early start avoids the worst of the heat. Take plenty of water too, as the [Algarve golf in July](/guide/algarve-golf-in-july) guide explains.
**Reserve your trolley.** Rentals can be limited, and Balaia says its equipment is allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.

excerpt: Which Algarve golf courses are hilly, where a buggy makes sense and which green fees include one, based on club and independent golf sources.

content.text: Plenty of Algarve golf courses climb into the hills behind the coast, with great views and some tiring walks between shots. If you're planning a round on foot, or just want to know when to book a buggy, these are the hilly courses worth knowing about.

There's no official measure of how hilly a golf course is, so this isn't a ranking. We've grouped the courses using what the clubs and independent golf guides say, and we've noted where those guides disagree. It isn't a complete list either: a course missing here may still be hilly, as we only included those we found enough information about. **Last checked: November 2026.**
Hilly Algarve courses where a buggy is the safer choice

**[Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio)** says its course runs over hills behind the village of Salema, and lists a buggy as recommended. Teetimes.pt describes severe slopes on and across most fairways, with rarely a flat lie. Buggy hire costs €40 for 18 holes or €25 for 9.

**[Castro Marim](/courses/castro-marim)** is described by Teetimes.pt as hills and valleys, quite short in length, but hard to walk. The club's own website quotes a magazine's description of its "undulating contours". Buggy hire costs €45 for 18 holes or €28 for 9.

**[Boavista](/courses/boavista)** rises to a high tee at the 9th before dropping into a valley of lakes on the way home, according to Teetimes.pt, which calls a buggy essential. The club lists buggy hire at €45.

**[Quinta do Vale](/courses/quinta-do-vale)** sits in a natural valley above the Guadiana River. Teetimes.pt notes that the back nine is more undulating and calls a buggy essential. The club doesn't publish a separate hire price, so contact the course.
Hilly courses where the green fee includes a buggy
At these three, the hills matter less because a buggy comes with the online or standard rate, as described in our [guide to golf buggy hire in the Algarve](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve).

**[Ombria](/courses/ombria)** sits in the hills north of Loulé. The club's own hole notes mention a sharp descent, a sharp hillside and a high vantage point. Its green fees include a shared buggy, subject to availability.

**[Monte Rei](/courses/monte-rei)** lies in the foothills of the Serra do Caldeirão. Where2Golf describes several slopes to climb and lists a golf cart as compulsory, and the club's online booking lists a buggy as part of its green fees.

**[Amendoeira Faldo](/courses/amendoeira-faldo)** climbs the hillside, in the words of Teetimes.pt, while its sister O'Connor course stays in the valley. The online green fee includes a buggy, if one is available.
Courses where the back nine is the hillier half
On these courses, the sources we checked point to the second half of the round as the more demanding walk.

**[Morgado](/courses/morgado)** has rolling terrain that gets hillier on the back nine, and Teetimes.pt recommends a buggy. It gives the same advice for its neighbour **[Alamos](/courses/alamos)**, because of its back nine. Contact the course for current buggy prices at both.
**[Silves](/courses/silves)** has rolling fairways that aren't steep, according to Teetimes.pt, with more elevation change on the back nine. Buggy hire costs €55 for 18 holes.

**[Vilamoura Pinhal](/courses/vilamoura-pinhal)** is described by the club as having challenging elevation changes. Teetimes.pt says the undulation is mainly on the back nine, but still lists a buggy as optional.

**[Espiche](/courses/espiche)** has a back nine that climbs into the hills, according to Teetimes.pt. The club mentions elevation changes too, but also calls the course enjoyable to walk, so it may suit fit walkers.
Where golf guides disagree: Vale do Lobo

**[Vale do Lobo Royal](/courses/vale-do-lobo-royal)** shows why terrain is partly a matter of opinion. Teetimes.pt mentions some steep climbs on the back nine, while Where2Golf says the course isn't particularly hilly, though it does mention several slopes to climb and a few longish green-to-tee walks.

Where2Golf says parts of **[Vale do Lobo Ocean](/courses/vale-do-lobo-ocean)** are hillier than the Royal, and Teetimes.pt calls a buggy essential there. Buggy hire is available on both courses, so contact the course for the price.
Other courses with hills to expect
**[Gramacho](/courses/gramacho)** is described by Teetimes.pt as hilly terrain, though the same guide says you only need a buggy if it's essential for you. Buggy hire costs €55 for 18 holes.

**[Palmares](/courses/palmares)** describes itself as a course between ocean and hills, with the rolling hills of its Lagos nine. Teetimes.pt also notes real elevation change on the Alvor nine. Contact the course for the buggy price.
**[Benamor](/courses/benamor)** has very undulating fairways and prominent hills in parts of the course, according to Teetimes.pt. Buggy hire costs €48 for 18 holes or €36 for 9.
Tips for playing a hilly course

**Book your buggy with your tee time.** Several clubs describe buggies as subject to availability, and the rules on who can drive vary. Our [guide to golf buggy hire in the Algarve](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve) has the details by course.
**Plan for the heat.** Summer afternoons make hills much harder work, so an early tee time helps if you plan to walk.
**Ask about buggy restrictions.** Some clubs can limit buggies to protect the course, which may mean extra walking from the path to your ball.
Would you rather avoid the slopes altogether? See our guide to [Algarve golf courses you can walk](/guide/algarve-golf-courses-you-can-walk).

excerpt: What a self-organised 5-night golf trip to Vilamoura costs month by month, with green fees for all four courses and example hotels. Not package prices.

content.text: A self-organised 5-night golf trip to Vilamoura with a round on each of its four courses costs **from about €861 to €1,534 per person**, excluding flights, based on the three example trips below. Green fees are lowest in July and August.

**These figures are for a trip you organise yourself, booking the hotel, green fees, car and food separately. They aren't package prices.** Several Vilamoura hotels sell their own golf packages, which may cost more or less. Your total will depend on your dates and where you stay. **Last checked: November 2026.**

content.note: One round each on the Old Course, Pinhal, Laguna and Millennium, 5 nights sharing a room and a small hire car. Only green fees change by month in these totals: hotel, car and food use the same figures all year, so summer totals in particular are likely to be higher.
content.caption: Vilamoura example trips by month, per person, excluding flights

content.text: What a Vilamoura golf trip includes

Each example uses the same trip as our [guide to the cost of an Algarve golf trip](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost): **5 nights, four rounds, and two people sharing a room and a small hire car**, with costs shown per person. We've counted one round on each of the four Vilamoura courses open to visitors: the [Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course), [Pinhal](/courses/vilamoura-pinhal), [Laguna](/courses/vilamoura-laguna) and [Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium). The fifth course, The Els Club, is a private members' club.

**Included:** green fees, hotel room, small hire car, and food and drink. **Not included:** flights, fuel, tolls, car insurance extras, buggies, club hire and range balls. Breakfast may be extra, depending on the rate you book.
Vilamoura green fees by month

These are the standard online green fees for one round of 18 holes, from Vilamoura Golf's own online booking, sampled in October 2026. Prices change with demand, so check the booking site for your dates.

content.note: Source: Vilamoura Golf's online booking, sampled October 2026.
content.caption: Standard online green fees, 18 holes

content.text: The [Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course) costs €215 to €301 a round, the most of the four in every month. Of the 34 courses whose prices we track, only Monte Rei reaches a higher standard fee. It was named Portugal's Best Golf Course at the World Golf Awards 2025. All four courses set a handicap limit of 28 for men and 36 for ladies, and beginners without a handicap need the manager's authorisation to play.
Where to stay: three example hotels

These are only examples to show how the costs add up. There are plenty of other options, and our [guide to golf hotels near Vilamoura](/guide/golf-hotels-near-vilamoura) covers more of them. Prices are the lowest "from" rates we found in October 2026, for the whole room, so we've split them between two people.

**Value:** [Hotel Apartamento do Golfe](https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html?ss=Hotel%20Apartamento%20do%20Golfe%20Vilamoura), a simple three-star aparthotel a short walk from the Old Course clubhouse, from about €37 a night. Studios and apartments have kitchenettes, which can bring food costs down.

**Mid-range:** [Hilton Vilamoura As Cascatas](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/hilton-vilamoura.html), a five-star resort overlooking Pinhal and one of Vilamoura Golf's official partner hotels, from about €112 a night.
**Premium:** [Domes Lake Algarve](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/domes-lake-algarve.html), a five-star lakeside resort with a golf concierge, rated 9.1 on Booking.com, from about €195 a night.

rows: Hotel, 5 nights, half of a room
content.caption: Per person: cheapest month (July and August) and most expensive (March, April and May)

content.text: Hotel prices are higher in summer

Our hotel figures are autumn "from" rates, so treat them as the starting point. According to Statistics Portugal (INE), the average rate for an occupied room in the Algarve was **€217.80 in August 2025**, the highest of any region in Portugal, while in January 2026 the Algarve's average was below the national figure of €92.10. These are averages across all accommodation, not our example hotels, but expect to pay noticeably more in summer.
Food and drink

Travel budget guides commonly suggest about €40 to €60 per person a day for eating out in the Algarve, although none of them is an official survey. We used €40 a day for the value trip, €50 for the mid-range trip and €60 for the premium trip. A dinner at the marina could easily cost more.
Getting to Vilamoura and around

Faro Airport is about 24 km from Vilamoura, roughly 35 minutes by car. Pre-booked transfers were quoted at about €35 for a sedan and €44 for a minivan in October 2026, per vehicle each way, and a metered taxi costs roughly €25 to €35. You can [compare transfers on GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA), and our [Faro Airport to Vilamoura guide](/guide/faro-airport-to-vilamoura-with-golf-clubs) has the details.

We've included a small hire car because the courses are spread across the resort: Laguna and Millennium are on the west side, about 10 minutes from the marina hotels. Kayak's average for a small car at Faro Airport is about €15 a day, so you can [compare car hire for your dates](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw).
Buggies and other golf extras

Vilamoura Golf doesn't publish a buggy hire price, so ask when you book. Buggies must stay on the paths, or in the rough where there are none, and only two players and two bags are allowed per buggy. See our [guide to golf buggy hire in the Algarve](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve) for other courses.

**An offer worth knowing:** on new bookings made by 31 December 2026, Laguna includes a free shared buggy, for play from 19 October 2026 to 31 December 2027. It isn't valid from 1 April to 31 May or from 16 September to 18 October 2027.
How to spend less on a Vilamoura golf trip
**Go in July and August.** The same four rounds cost €531 then, against €709 in March, April and May.

**Swap the Old Course for a second round elsewhere.** The Old Course is the dearest of the four by a long way, so replacing it with another round on Millennium or Laguna saves between €91 and €169, depending on the month. Compare them in [Vilamoura Old Course vs Millennium](/guide/vilamoura-old-course-vs-millennium-which-one-should-you-play).
**Stay somewhere with a kitchen.** Both the value and mid-range examples have rooms or apartments with kitchen facilities, which can cut your food costs.

content.text: Most Algarve golf courses are within about an hour of Faro Airport. Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo are the closest, at around 20 to 30 minutes, Vilamoura takes about 30 to 35, Portimão about 55, and the far west beyond Lagos up to about 1h 15. Here's the drive time to every course open to visitors, what a taxi or transfer costs, and which options work when you're carrying a golf bag.
Drive times from Faro Airport to every course

content.note: Road-routing estimates from the airport terminal without traffic, rounded to the nearest 5 minutes, checked November 2026. Resorts and transfer companies sometimes quote a little less, and summer traffic can add more. San Lorenzo is left out because it is closed for renovation until 2028.
content.caption: Courses listed from nearest to furthest

content.text: What a taxi or transfer costs

Taxis from the airport run on the meter, so there's no fixed fare. Portugal also brought in a new national taxi tariff on 23 October 2026, and drivers have until 21 January 2027 to update their meters, so you could be charged under either one this winter. That's why the ranges below are wide: the low end is a weekday daytime trip on the new tariff, and the high end is a night or weekend trip on the old one.

content.note: Taxi ranges are our own estimates from the published tariffs. Sedan prices are quotes published by a fare-comparison site in October 2026, for up to three passengers (Quinta do Lago from a local operator's website), and vary by date. Confirm the price before you travel.
rows: Quinta do Lago, Vale do Lobo
content.caption: Approximate one-way cost per vehicle

content.text: The A22 motorway, which most of these routes use, [has been toll-free since 1 January 2025](https://www.theportugalnews.com/news/2025-04-25/assurance-that-algarve-motorway-remains-toll-free/97183), so ignore any older guide that adds tolls to the fare.
Getting to the course with a golf bag
This is where golfers have different needs from other holidaymakers. A golf bag in a travel cover is usually well over a metre long, which rules out some options and makes others awkward.
Pre-booked transfer

This is the easiest choice for most golfers. You give the company your flight number, and the driver meets you in arrivals. The key is to **say how many golf bags you're bringing** when you book, so they send a vehicle that fits them. Four golfers with four bags will almost always need a minivan. You can compare prices and vehicles on [GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA).
Taxi

Taxis wait outside the terminal, and one or two golf bags will often fit in the boot of a larger car, sometimes with the rear seat folded. A standard taxi only carries four passengers, and four people with four golf bags won't fit. The new tariff is reported to drop the old €1.60 luggage supplement, leaving only €0.80 for booking by phone or app, but you may still see the supplement on a meter that hasn't been updated yet.
Uber and Bolt

Both operate at Faro Airport, and the app directs you to the pickup point. They can be good value for a solo golfer, but it's a gamble with a golf bag: [Uber's airport page](https://www.uber.com/global/en/airports/fao?id=308) says cargo space isn't guaranteed and bases its luggage guidance on bags of 158cm in combined dimensions. Choose UberXL or a similar larger car, and message your driver about the bag before they arrive.
Bus and train

Faro Airport has no train station, so you'd first need a bus or taxi into Faro. The Vamus Aerobus (line 56) runs seasonally from the terminal to Albufeira, Lagoa, Portimão and Lagos, at a reported €11 per person. It may work for a light traveller going to a town centre, but buses and trains don't drop you at the golf course, and you'd still need a taxi for the last stretch. With a full golf bag, we wouldn't plan a trip around them.
Hire car

If you're playing several courses across different areas, a car often works out best, and it gives you freedom over early tee times. Choose the size carefully: a small hatchback may not take even one travel bag without folding the seats, and four golfers will want a people carrier. You can compare airport hire on [EconomyBookings](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw).
Which option should you choose?

Staying at one resort and playing nearby? A pre-booked transfer is simple, and you can arrange taxis between courses as you need them. Playing three or more courses in different parts of the Algarve? Hire a car, as several daily taxis soon cost more. Travelling alone and light? A taxi or Bolt is often cheapest for short trips such as Quinta do Lago or Vilamoura.
If you'd rather not travel with clubs at all, you can [hire a set at Faro Airport](/guide/hiring-golf-clubs-at-faro-airport), which makes all of the above easier.
Guides by area

Each of these compares the options for your part of the Algarve: [Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo](/guide/faro-airport-to-quinta-do-lago-vale-do-lobo-with-golf-clubs), [Vilamoura](/guide/faro-airport-to-vilamoura-with-golf-clubs), [Albufeira](/guide/faro-airport-to-albufeira-with-golf-clubs), [Carvoeiro and Silves](/guide/faro-airport-to-carvoeiro-and-silves-for-golfers), [Portimão and Alvor](/guide/faro-airport-to-portimao-and-alvor-for-golfers), [Lagos](/guide/faro-airport-to-lagos-with-golf-clubs), and [Tavira and Monte Rei](/guide/faro-airport-to-tavira-and-monte-rei-with-golf-clubs).

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to the Algarve costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

**Travelling as a group?** Our guide to [Algarve golf trips for groups and golf societies](/guide/algarve-golf-trips-for-groups-and-golf-societies) covers golf villas and apartments, booking tee times together, buggies and minivans.

**These figures are for a trip you organise yourself, booking the hotel, green fees, car and food separately. They aren't package prices.** Several hotels on the estate sell their own golf packages, which may cost more or less. Your total will depend on your dates and where you stay. **Last checked: November 2026.**

content.text: What a Quinta do Lago golf trip includes

Each example uses the same trip as our [guide to the cost of an Algarve golf trip](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost): **5 nights, four rounds, and two people sharing a room and a small hire car**, with costs shown per person. We've counted two rounds on the [South Course](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south) and one each on [North](/courses/quinta-do-lago-north) and [Laranjal](/courses/quinta-do-lago-laranjal).

**Included:** green fees, hotel room, small hire car, and food and drink. **Not included:** flights, fuel, tolls, car insurance extras, buggies, club hire and range balls. Breakfast may be extra, depending on the rate you book.
Quinta do Lago green fees by month

Quinta do Lago doesn't publish a public price list. These are the standard online green fees for one round of 18 holes, from the club's own online booking, sampled in October 2026. Prices change with demand, so check the booking site for your dates.

content.text: The [South Course](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south) is the dearest of the three, and at up to €264 it's among the most expensive rounds in the Algarve. Of the 34 courses whose prices we track, only Monte Rei and the Vilamoura Old Course reach a higher standard fee. All three Quinta do Lago courses set a handicap limit of 28 for men and 36 for ladies.
Where to stay: three example hotels

These are only examples to show how the costs add up. There are plenty of other options, and our [guide to hotels near Quinta do Lago golf](/guide/hotels-near-quinta-do-lago-golf) covers more of them. Prices are the lowest "from" rates we found in October 2026, for the whole room, so we've split them between two people.

**Value:** [WOT Algarve Soul](https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html?ss=WOT%20Algarve%20Soul%20Almancil), simple apartments and studios on the Almancil side, from about €54 a night. It's about 11 minutes' drive from the courses, so you'll need the car.

**Mid-range:** [Vilar do Golf](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/vilar-do-golf.html), apartments beside the South Course, two minutes from the clubhouse, from about €103 a night. Each apartment has a kitchen, which can bring food costs down.

**Premium:** [Hotel Quinta do Lago](https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html?ss=Hotel%20Quinta%20do%20Lago%20Almancil), the estate's original five-star hotel on the Ria Formosa lagoon, from about €397 a night. Its own golf packages include a courtesy shuttle to the courses, but our example assumes you book separately.

content.text: Hotel prices are higher in summer

Our hotel figures are autumn "from" rates, so treat them as the starting point. According to Statistics Portugal (INE), the average rate for an occupied room in the Algarve was **€217.80 in August 2025**, the highest of any region in Portugal, while in January 2026 the Algarve's average was below the national figure of €92.10. These are averages across all accommodation, not our example hotels, but expect to pay noticeably more in summer.
Food and drink

Travel budget guides commonly suggest about €40 to €60 per person a day for eating out in the Algarve, although none of them is an official survey. We used €40 a day for the value trip, €50 for the mid-range trip and €60 for the premium trip. Restaurants on and around the estate can easily cost more.
Getting to Quinta do Lago and around

Quinta do Lago is only about 20 km from Faro Airport. Pre-booked transfers were listed from about €34 per vehicle each way in October 2026, and a metered taxi costs roughly €20 to €30. You can [compare transfers on GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA), and our [Faro Airport to Quinta do Lago guide](/guide/faro-airport-to-quinta-do-lago-vale-do-lobo-with-golf-clubs) has the details.

We've included a small hire car because the courses and hotels are spread around the estate, and you may want to play nearby Vale do Lobo too. Kayak's average for a small car at Faro Airport is about €15 a day, so you can [compare car hire for your dates](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw). If you stay beside a course and don't need a car, transfers could cost you less.
Buggies and other golf extras

A buggy isn't included in the standard online green fee at Quinta do Lago, and the club doesn't publish a hire price, so ask when you book. Players must be 16 or over to drive one. See our [guide to golf buggy hire in the Algarve](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve) for other courses.

**A winter offer worth knowing:** from 1 December to 31 January, North and Laranjal sell a rate of €170 per person for two players sharing a buggy. That's the same as the standard online green fee we sampled for those courses in December and January, so the buggy effectively comes free.
Is Quinta do Lago expensive for golf?

Yes, for both green fees and hotels. The South Course costs €188 to €264 for a round, against as little as €57 at the cheapest courses we track. To keep costs down, go in January and December, play North or Laranjal instead of a second round on South, and look at the winter buggy offer. If budget matters more than the venue, see [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).

**Comparing destinations?** See what the same trip costs in [Albufeira](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-albufeira-cost), [Vale do Lobo](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-vale-do-lobo-cost), [Vilamoura](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-vilamoura-cost), [Monte Rei](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-monte-rei-cost) and [Lagos and Portimão](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-lagos-and-portimao-cost), or read our [guide to the cost of an Algarve golf trip](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost).

**Only have a weekend?** Our [guide to a golf weekend in the Algarve](/guide/golf-weekend-in-the-algarve) costs a Friday-to-Monday trip with two rounds on the South Course and the Vale do Lobo Royal, plus three other bases near Faro Airport.

content.text: Taxi or transfer for such a short trip?

On a run this short, the meter rarely gets high enough to hurt, which makes the taxi rank outside arrivals hard to beat for one or two golfers. Under Portugal's new national tariff, which began on 23 October 2026, a weekday daytime trip works out at about €20. A taxi still on the old tariff until its meter is updated, or a late-night arrival, could reach the mid-€20s.

A transfer earns its keep when you're a group. [Algarserra](https://www.algarserra.com/faro-airport-transfers-to-quinta-do-lago) lists a four-seat car at €34 and an eight-seat van at €44 per vehicle, so a four-ball with bags in the van pays €11 each. You can also compare offers from several companies on [GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA). Either way, mention the golf bags when you book, because a car with four passengers won't carry four sets.
Uber, Bolt and the bus

App cabs make most sense on a route this short, as a higher demand price still won't come to much. The problem is the bag: a small hatchback may not take one, so pick a larger car in the app and let the driver know.

Vamus line 55 stops in Almancil on its way from the airport to Vilamoura, but both resorts are several kilometres south of the town. You'd still need a taxi for the last part of the journey, so with clubs it's simpler to take one from the start.
Do you need a hire car here?

Often not. Quinta do Lago's three courses and Pinheiros Altos sit side by side, and the two Vale do Lobo courses share one resort, so a golfer staying nearby can get around with short taxi rides. A car becomes useful if you also want to play Vilamoura, inland [Ombria](/courses/ombria) or further west. Compare prices on [EconomyBookings](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw).
Travelling without clubs

Renting saves you the oversize baggage queue and leaves more room in any car. ClubsToHire hands sets over in the arrivals hall, and our guide to [hiring clubs at Faro Airport](/guide/hiring-golf-clubs-at-faro-airport) compares the alternatives.
Where to next

For places to stay, see our guides to [hotels near Quinta do Lago](/guide/hotels-near-quinta-do-lago-golf), [hotels near Vale do Lobo](/guide/hotels-near-vale-do-lobo-golf) and [hotels near Ombria](/guide/hotels-near-ombria-golf). You can also browse [courses around Almancil](/almancil/golf-courses) or check our [drive times to every Algarve course](/guide/faro-airport-to-algarve-golf-courses).

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guides to how much a golf trip costs if you book it yourself, for [Quinta do Lago](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-quinta-do-lago-cost) and [Vale do Lobo](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-vale-do-lobo-cost), with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

content.text: Why a hire car suits this part of the Algarve

Six courses sit within a fairly short drive of each other here, some near the coast and others inland, and that's what makes this a good base for a week of golf. It also means you're unlikely to stay at one all week, and repeated taxis between them are what make a car worthwhile. The A22 has been toll-free since January 2025, and the route from the airport is straightforward.

Choose the size with care. A travel bag is long, and four golfers will need a people carrier rather than a family hatchback. You can compare airport rental companies on [EconomyBookings](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw).
Transfer or taxi if you're not driving

If you're staying at one resort, such as Amendoeira, or at a Carvoeiro villa close to a course, you may not need a car. A sedan to Carvoeiro was quoted at about **€63** in October 2026, though listings vary from around €41 to €65 by company, so it pays to compare on [GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA). For Amendoeira and Silves, ask for a quote to your exact address.

By taxi the range is wide because two tariffs are in use until 21 January 2027: about €52 on a weekday under the new one, and €68 to €81 under the old one. Golf bags are simply a question of fitting, so a larger car is the one to look for at the rank.
Can you get there by bus or train?

Only if you have plenty of time. The Vamus Aerobus stops in Lagoa, but Carvoeiro has no bus station of its own, so you'd change there, and one guide reports that taking local buses from the airport can take more than three hours. Trains don't help much either: the airport has no station, and from Silves station you'd still need a taxi to reach a course. We wouldn't try either with a golf bag.
Or skip the bag altogether

Hiring clubs for the week makes a smaller rental car possible. [ClubsToHire](/shops/clubstohire-faro-airport) in the airport's arrivals hall and the shops in our [Algarve rental directory](/shops) are good places to start.
Where to stay around Carvoeiro and Silves

Our hotel guides cover [Pestana Carvoeiro golf](/guide/hotels-near-pestana-carvoeiro-golf), [Vale de Milho](/guide/hotels-near-vale-de-milho-golf), [Amendoeira](/guide/hotels-near-amendoeira-golf) and [Silves Golf](/guide/hotels-near-silves-golf). See also the course pages for [Carvoeiro](/carvoeiro/golf-courses) and [Silves](/silves/golf-courses), or the [full table of drive times from Faro Airport](/guide/faro-airport-to-algarve-golf-courses).

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to the Algarve costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

content.text: What these Algarve golf trip costs include

Every example uses the same trip: **5 nights, four rounds of golf, and two people sharing a room and a small hire car**. Costs are shown per person, so a solo golfer would pay the full room and car price.

We chose 5 nights because there's no official, up-to-date average for golfers in the Algarve, but the president of Portugal's national golf industry council put the typical stay at about five nights in 2024. He said British golfers tend to stay three to four nights, Scandinavians and Germans six to seven, and North Americans 10 to 14. A 2020 study for the Portuguese Golf Federation used seven nights and five rounds for visiting golfers across Portugal, based on 2018 data. Four rounds in 5 nights is our own assumption.

**Included:** green fees, hotel room, small hire car, and food and drink. **Not included:** flights, fuel, tolls, car insurance extras, buggies, club hire and range balls. Hotel breakfast may also be extra, depending on the rate you book.
Three example Algarve golf trips

These are only examples to show how the costs add up. Plenty of other courses and hotels could suit the same budget, and we chose these because we had prices to check. Green fees come from each club's own price list or online booking, checked in October 2026, and they can change with demand.

Boavista's handicap limit is 26 for men and 34 for ladies, which is lower than many courses, so check yours first.

content.text: Why the hotel cost is the least certain figure

Our hotel prices are the lowest "from" rates we found in autumn 2026, and we couldn't confirm rates for specific dates in January or April. That's why the totals say "from". Expect to pay more in busy periods, and check your exact dates before you rely on these figures.

Summer makes the biggest difference. According to Statistics Portugal (INE), the average rate for an occupied room in the Algarve was **€217.80 in August 2025**, the highest of any region in Portugal. In January 2026, the Algarve's average was below the national figure of €92.10. These are averages across all types of accommodation, not the prices of our example hotels, but they show why a summer trip will usually cost more than the totals above.
Food and drink: an estimate, not a price list

Travel budget guides commonly suggest about €40 to €60 per person a day for eating out in the Algarve, although none of them is an official survey. We used €40 a day for the value trip, €50 for the mid-range trip and €60 for the premium trip. A good dinner at a resort could easily cost more.
Getting around: hire car or transfers

We used a small hire car because the example courses are spread out. Kayak's average for a small car at Faro Airport is about €15 a day, or €75 for 5 days before fuel and tolls. Its averages across all car types range from about €9 a day in January to €25 in July, so treat these as a guide and [compare car hire for your dates](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw).

If you're staying near your courses, you may not need a car. Pre-booked sedan transfers from Faro Airport were quoted at about €34 to Quinta do Lago, €35 to Vilamoura and €81 to Portimão in October 2026, per vehicle and each way. You can [compare transfers on GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA). See our guides to [Faro Airport to Vilamoura](/guide/faro-airport-to-vilamoura-with-golf-clubs) and other Algarve areas for details.
Flights and your golf bag

We've left flights out of the totals because fares vary so much by date, airline and departure airport. Remember to add the cost of your golf bag, which varies by airline. We have guides for [Ryanair](/guide/ryanair-golf-clubs-what-it-costs-to-fly-with-your-own-set-to-the-algarve), [easyJet](/guide/golf-clubs-on-easyjet-rules-sizes-and-what-it-actually-costs) and [Jet2](/guide/jet2-golf-clubs-fees-weight-limits-and-why-you-shouldn-t-leave-booking-late).
Golf extras to budget for

These aren't in the totals, so add them if you need them. Buggy hire is €55 for 18 holes at Alto, €50 at Salgados and €45 at Boavista. Some courses don't publish a price, so see our [guide to golf buggy hire in the Algarve](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve). Hiring a full set of clubs costs €45 at Pestana's courses, such as Alto, and €50 at Salgados.
How to spend less on your Algarve golf trip
**Compare months.** The same four rounds on our value trip cost €313 in January and €504 in April. Check the green fees page for each course, as the cheapest month varies.
**Look at twilight rates.** Alto, for example, lists a twilight rate of €50 from 15:00, against €75 to €140 for its standard round. Just make sure there's enough daylight to finish.

**Choose lower-priced courses.** Green fees vary widely, from €57 at [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio) to over €300 at the most expensive times on some premium courses. See [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).

**Look for rates with a shared buggy.** If you want a buggy anyway, a combined rate can be simpler than adding one later. Santo António's 2026 list, for example, has one round for two players with a buggy at €124 to €147 in total.
Is a package cheaper than booking it yourself?

This guide doesn't answer that, because it only covers trips you book yourself. Package prices depend on the company, dates and what's included, so compare a real quote with your own total, using the same hotel, courses and dates.

**Only have a weekend?** Our [guide to a golf weekend in the Algarve](/guide/golf-weekend-in-the-algarve) costs a Friday-to-Monday trip with two rounds, from four bases within about 45 minutes of Faro Airport.

**Travelling as a group?** Our guide to [Algarve golf trips for groups and golf societies](/guide/algarve-golf-trips-for-groups-and-golf-societies) covers golf villas and apartments, booking tee times together, buggies and minivans.

content.text: What a Lagos and Portimão golf trip includes

Each example uses the same trip as our [guide to the cost of an Algarve golf trip](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost): **5 nights, four rounds, and two people sharing a room and a small hire car**, with costs shown per person. We've counted one round each at [Alto Golf](/courses/alto-golf) and [Morgado](/courses/morgado) near Portimão, and at [Boavista](/courses/boavista) and [Espiche](/courses/espiche) near Lagos.

There are plenty of other courses in this part of the Algarve, including [Palmares](/courses/palmares), [Penina](/courses/penina-championship), [Alamos](/courses/alamos), [Pestana Ferragudo](/courses/pestana-ferragudo) and [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio). We left Palmares and Penina out of the totals only because we don't have their green fees for every month.

**Included:** green fees, hotel room, small hire car, and food and drink. **Not included:** flights, fuel, tolls, car insurance extras, buggies, club hire and range balls. Breakfast may be extra, depending on the rate you book.
Lagos and Portimão green fees by month

These are standard green fees for one round of 18 holes. Alto Golf's come from Pestana's official price list, and the others from each club's own online booking, sampled in October 2026. Prices change with demand, so check before you book.

content.note: Sources: Pestana Golf's official price list for Alto Golf; each club's online booking for the others, sampled October 2026.
content.caption: Standard green fees, 18 holes

content.text: Green fees in this part of the Algarve are generally lower than around Vilamoura and Quinta do Lago: none of these four courses costs more than €140 a round in our data. Handicap limits differ, though. Boavista allows a maximum of 26 for men and 34 for ladies, which is stricter than most, while Morgado allows 28 and 36, and Alto Golf 36 for both, according to its scorecard.
Where to stay: three example hotels

These are only examples to show how the costs add up. We picked hotels between Portimão and Lagos so all four courses are within reach, and there are plenty of other options, as our guides to hotels near [Penina](/guide/hotels-near-penina-golf-resort), [Boavista](/guide/hotels-near-boavista-golf) and [Morgado and Alamos](/guide/hotels-near-morgado-and-alamos-golf) show. Prices are the lowest "from" rates we found in autumn 2026, for the whole room, and some only apply in quieter months, so we've split them between two people.

**Value:** [Casa Penina Guesthouse](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/casa-penina.html), a tiny guesthouse beside the Penina course rated 9.7 on Booking.com, from about €53 a night in the quieter months. It has a two-night minimum, and breakfast costs €12 per person extra. It's about 15 minutes from Alto Golf and 33 from Espiche.

**Mid-range:** [Pestana Alvor Praia](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/pestanaalvorpraia.html), a five-star clifftop hotel above Praia dos Três Irmãos, which can cost under €90 a night in winter. It's about 5 minutes from Alto Golf and 30 from Boavista.

**Premium:** [Iberostar Selection Lagos Algarve](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/iberostar-lagos-algarve.html), rated 8.9, from €126 a night on the hotel's own website. It's about 13 minutes from Boavista and 28 from Alto Golf.
