content.text: Hotel prices are higher in summer

Our hotel figures are autumn "from" rates, so treat them as the starting point. According to Statistics Portugal (INE), the average rate for an occupied room in the Algarve was **€217.80 in August 2025**, the highest of any region in Portugal, while in January 2026 the Algarve's average was below the national figure of €92.10. These are averages across all accommodation, not our example hotels, but expect to pay noticeably more in summer.
Food and drink

Travel budget guides commonly suggest about €40 to €60 per person a day for eating out in the Algarve, although none of them is an official survey. We used €40 a day for the value trip, €50 for the mid-range trip and €60 for the premium trip.
Getting to Lagos and Portimão

Golf around Portimão and Alvor is about 55 to 65 minutes from Faro Airport, and Lagos is further still. A pre-booked sedan to Portimão was quoted at about €81 in October 2026, and a taxi runs from about €60 to €95. To Lagos, one-way transfers cost about €80 to €110. You can [compare transfers on GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA), and our guides from Faro Airport to [Portimão and Alvor](/guide/faro-airport-to-portimao-and-alvor-for-golfers) and to [Lagos](/guide/faro-airport-to-lagos-with-golf-clubs) have the details.

At this distance, and with courses spread between the two towns, a hire car makes the strongest case of any Algarve trip. Kayak's average for a small car at Faro Airport is about €15 a day, so you can [compare car hire for your dates](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw).
Buggies and other golf extras

Buggy hire costs €55 for 18 holes at Alto Golf and €45 at Boavista, while Morgado and Espiche don't publish a separate price. Espiche's online booking sells rates that include a buggy, so compare them before adding one. See our [guide to golf buggy hire in the Algarve](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve) for more.
How to spend less on a Lagos and Portimão golf trip
**Go in December.** The same four rounds cost €294 then, against €466 in March and April.
**Use twilight rates.** Pestana lists a twilight rate at Alto Golf of €50 from 15:00, against €75 to €140 for its standard round.

**Add a low-cost round.** [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio), west of Lagos, has special-offer green fees of €57 to €68 on its 2026 price list, against a public rate of €108. See [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).

**Comparing destinations?** See what the same trip costs in [Albufeira](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-albufeira-cost), [Quinta do Lago](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-quinta-do-lago-cost), [Vale do Lobo](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-vale-do-lobo-cost), [Vilamoura](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-vilamoura-cost) and [Monte Rei](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-monte-rei-cost), or read our [guide to the cost of an Algarve golf trip](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost).

excerpt: Every 18-hole Algarve golf course ranked by its official slope and course rating, from Monte Rei at the top to the gentlest courses for higher handicaps.

content.text: Which are the **hardest golf courses in the Algarve**? Rather than give you our opinion, this guide uses the official numbers: the course rating and slope rating that the Portuguese Golf Federation (FPG) gives every course for handicap purposes. They are the same figures used to work out your playing handicap, so they're the fairest way to compare one course with another.

All ratings come from the FPG's national course rating table, checked in November 2026. We cross-checked it against Pestana Ferragudo's 2026 scorecard and GolfPass's listing for Monte Rei, and the figures matched. Clubs re-rate their courses from time to time, so an older scorecard may show slightly different numbers.
How slope and course rating work

**Slope rating** measures how much harder a course is for an average club golfer than for a scratch golfer. It runs from 55 to 155, and 113 is a course of standard difficulty. The higher the slope, the more shots a higher-handicap player will need there compared with an easier course.
**Course rating** is the score a scratch golfer is expected to shoot from a given set of tees. A course rating above par means even a very good player should expect to score over par.

Both figures depend on the tees you play. Each course has several ratings, one for each set of tees, and the longest tees always give the highest numbers. To compare like with like, the table below uses each course's hardest men's tees, which is how hard the course can play. Tee colours aren't consistent between clubs, so we don't compare by colour.
Algarve golf courses ranked by slope rating

content.note: Each figure is the highest the FPG gives that course: the men's longest tees for the first two columns, and the women's hardest tees for the last. Courses with several loops (Vila Sol, Pinheiros Altos, Castro Marim and Palmares) show their hardest combination. The private Els Club in Vilamoura is not included because visitors can't book it. Source: FPG national course rating table, November 2026.
content.caption: 18-hole Algarve courses, hardest tees

content.text: Each course also has its own page with the ratings for every set of tees and a course handicap calculator, such as [Monte Rei's slope rating](/courses/monte-rei/slope-rating) or [Quinta do Lago South's](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south/slope-rating). You'll find the link on every course page.
The five hardest golf courses in the Algarve
1. Monte Rei: slope 147

[Monte Rei](/courses/monte-rei), Jack Nicklaus's course in the hills of the eastern Algarve, has the highest slope rating in the Algarve. From its longest tees it has a slope of **147** and a course rating of **75.6**, more than three and a half shots over par 72. That slope is also the joint highest of any course in Portugal on the FPG's table, level with West Cliffs at Óbidos. It's hard for women too: its hardest women's tees have a slope of 144.
2. Penina Championship: slope 143

[Penina Championship](/courses/penina-championship), Sir Henry Cotton's 1966 course near Portimão and the oldest in the Algarve, is rated **143** from its back tees, with a course rating of 73.7 on a par 73. Its hardest women's tees share the Algarve's top women's slope of 144 with Monte Rei.
3. Amendoeira Faldo: slope 142

[Amendoeira Faldo](/courses/amendoeira-faldo), designed by Nick Faldo near Silves, has a slope of **142** and a course rating of **74.5** from its longest tees. Its forward tees are much kinder, though: the gap between its hardest and easiest men's tees is one of the widest in the Algarve.
4. Pinheiros Altos: slope 141

[Pinheiros Altos](/courses/pinheiros-altos) in the Golden Triangle has 27 holes. Its Original Course combination is the toughest, with a slope of **141** and a course rating of 73.2. Its other loops are rated between 135 and 139 from the same tees.
5. Vilamoura Pinhal and Vale do Lobo Ocean: slope 140

Two courses share fifth place. [Vilamoura Pinhal](/courses/vilamoura-pinhal), laid out through pine forest, has a slope of **140** and a course rating of 74.0. [Vale do Lobo Ocean](/courses/vale-do-lobo-ocean) is also 140, with a course rating of 74.1 on a par 73. Just behind them, [Quinta do Lago South](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south) is rated 139 and [Boavista](/courses/boavista) 138.
Hard from the back, fairer from the front

A high slope doesn't mean a course is out of reach. Playing from shorter tees brings the numbers down a long way. At Monte Rei, the men's forward tees are rated 130, against 147 from the back. At Amendoeira Faldo, the men's slope drops from 142 to 123 from the red tees.

So if you're keen to play one of the courses at the top of this list, choose your tees carefully, and check the club's handicap rules first. Our guide to [handicap rules in the Algarve](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve) has the limits for each course.
What the slope means for your handicap

Your playing handicap changes from course to course, and slope is the reason. Under the World Handicap System, your course handicap is your Handicap Index multiplied by the slope and divided by 113, plus the difference between the course rating and par.

Take a golfer with a Handicap Index of 18. From Monte Rei's longest tees (slope 147, course rating 75.6, par 72), their course handicap is **27**. From the yellow tees at [Pestana Ferragudo](/courses/pestana-ferragudo) (slope 113, course rating 67.7, par 72), it's **14**. That's 13 more shots on one course than the other, which says a lot about how different the two are.
The gentlest 18-hole courses

At the other end of the table, [Pestana Ferragudo](/courses/pestana-ferragudo), which opened in 2026, has the lowest slope of any 18-hole course in the Algarve: **118** from its longest tees. [Silves](/courses/silves) is rated 120 and [Benamor](/courses/benamor) 121. A low slope doesn't always mean an easy walk, though, so if hills are a concern, see our guide to [hilly golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/hilly-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).

If you're new to the game, our guide to [the best Algarve golf courses for beginners](/guide/the-10-best-algarve-golf-courses-for-beginners) looks beyond the numbers at handicap rules, layout and practice facilities.
Short courses

Some 9-hole courses are rated as two loops of nine. [Penina Resort Course](/courses/penina-resort) is rated 122 from its yellow tees, [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs) between 102 and 107 for men, and [Balaia](/courses/balaia), a par-3 course, 84. [Vale de Milho](/courses/vale-de-milho) doesn't appear on the FPG's table. For more short options, see [the Algarve's best par-3 golf courses](/guide/the-algarve-s-best-par-3-golf-courses).
Frequently asked questions
What is the hardest golf course in the Algarve?
On the official ratings, Monte Rei, with a slope of 147 and a course rating of 75.6 from its longest tees. Penina Championship (143) and Amendoeira Faldo (142) come next.
What is the hardest golf course in Portugal?
On the FPG's table, Monte Rei and West Cliffs at Óbidos share the highest slope rating in Portugal, 147. Monte Rei has the higher course rating of the two, at 75.6 against 74.5.
What is a good slope rating for a beginner?

The lower, the better. A slope of 113 is standard difficulty, and most Algarve courses are rated well above that from their back tees. Choosing the forward tees is the easiest way to make any course more manageable.
Want to compare courses yourself? Open the [Algarve golf course map](/) to filter by difficulty, price and handicap.

excerpt: Where to stay to play Balaia, Albufeira's nine-hole par-3 course: the resort apartments on the course plus eight well-rated hotels within 13 minutes, from about €50 a night, with drive times, breakfast hours and golf perks.

content.text: [Balaia Golf Village](/courses/balaia) is home to one of the most relaxed rounds in the Algarve: a nine-hole course near Albufeira where **every hole is a par 3**, from 67 to 160 metres off the yellow tees. You can get round in under two hours, or play it twice for 18, which makes it ideal for beginners, families and anyone who wants to work on their short game.

This guide covers where to stay to play Balaia. All nine hotels below are rated at least 8 out of 10 by guests and are **within about 13 minutes of the course**, from the resort apartments on the doorstep to five-star clifftop hotels at Falésia.
Map of hotels near Balaia Golf Village
The black pin is the golf club (tap it to see course details). The blue pins are the hotels in this guide; tap one to check prices and availability.
How we chose these hotels

Every hotel here is rated at least 8 out of 10 by guests on Booking.com and is no more than about 13 minutes from the golf club by road. Drive times are calculated by road to the clubhouse. Breakfast hours and golf services come from each hotel's own website wherever possible, and we only mention a golf perk if the hotel actually states it.

Prices are the lowest average nightly rates we found in October 2026, usually for the quietest months of the year. Spring and autumn, peak golf season, cost more, so treat them as a guide rather than a quote.
Staying on the course: Balaia Golf Village

content.name: Balaia Golf Village Resort
content.text: The apartments that surround the course, and the obvious base if Balaia is your main round. Resort guests pay **€40 for a day's golf instead of the €50 visitor rate**, and the resort's "Algarve Golf Break" includes three nights in a Superior apartment, breakfast and dinner, two rounds at Balaia and a courtesy car. There are six outdoor pools, a free indoor pool, jacuzzi and gym, and three restaurants. Guest scores sit right on 8 out of 10, a little lower than the rest of this list, but nothing else puts you this close to the first tee.
perks: Green fee €40 for resort guests (€50 visitors)
Free indoor pool, jacuzzi and gym

content.text: Best value hotels near Balaia (under €100 a night)

content.name: Alfagar Village
content.text: Clifftop apartments above Santa Eulália beach, just three minutes from Balaia and rated 8.8 by guests. It has no golf services of its own, but it is one of the closest and best-value options, with a heated indoor pool and gym for the cooler months, massages on request and a paid airport transfer.

content.name: The Pátio Suite Hotel
content.text: Self-catering apartments with pools and a kids' club, 11 minutes from Balaia. The hotel says it is **just 200 metres from the Pine Cliffs golf course**, which makes it a smart base for playing both of the area's short courses on the same trip.
perks: 200 m from Pine Cliffs golf (per the hotel)

content.name: Grande Real Santa Eulália Resort & Hotel Spa
content.text: A large five-star resort on Santa Eulália beach, four minutes from Balaia, that can be surprisingly affordable out of season. The concierge sells green fees for local courses, breakfast starts at 7.30am and there is a 1,000 m² thalassotherapy spa.
perks: Green fees sold at the concierge

content.text: Mid-range hotels near Balaia (€100 to €150 a night)

content.name: Jupiter Albufeira Hotel – Family & Fun
content.text: A family hotel with a water park, kids' club, playground and spa, eight minutes from Balaia. Golfers will appreciate the **early risers' continental breakfast from 6.30am**, before the main breakfast opens at 7.30, which makes a first tee time easy. There is free transport to Praia dos Pescadores and Albufeira centre.
perks: Free transport to the beach and Albufeira centre

content.name: PortoBay Blue Ocean
content.text: The **highest-rated hotel on this list (9.2 on Booking.com)**, on the clifftop at Olhos de Água, eight minutes from Balaia. It is not adults-only, but has a lounge area reserved for adults and a calm, couple-friendly feel.

content.name: Hotel Vila Galé Cerro Alagoa
content.text: A practical four-star in Albufeira itself, for golfers who want restaurants and nightlife within walking distance in the evening. Breakfast is served **from 7am** and Balaia is about 10 minutes away by car.
Luxury hotels near Balaia

content.name: EPIC SANA Algarve Hotel
content.text: A five-star resort above Falésia beach that offers **special green fees at various Algarve golf courses**. Breakfast runs from 7am to 11am and there is a large 1,500 m² spa. Balaia is about 13 minutes away, and Pine Cliffs is even closer.
perks: Special green fees at Algarve courses

content.name: Pine Cliffs Hotel, a Luxury Collection Resort
content.text: The luxury choice for short-course golfers: the resort has **its own nine-hole course**, with the famous Devil's Parlour hole over the cliffs, and resort guests pay less to play it. Balaia is 10 minutes away, so you can play both in a day. See our guide to [hotels near Pine Cliffs](/guide/hotels-near-pine-cliffs-golf-course) for the other properties on the resort.
perks: Lower green fees for resort guests

content.text: Balaia green fees and what to know before you play

On Balaia's 2025–26 price list, a day's golf costs **€50 for visitors** and €40 for resort guests and under-14s. Green fee plus a half set of hire clubs is €80, a pull trolley is €5 and a bucket of 24 range balls costs €2. There are also weekly and monthly passes if you plan to play every day.

The course is open every day of the year from 8am to 6pm, and you can book a tee time online, by phone or at the golf reception in The Lake House, which also serves food and drinks. Every player must carry their own set of clubs. The resort's guest information says a handicap is required, without giving a limit, so check with the club when you book.

Next door, Club Med Da Balaia includes group golf lessons at Balaia Golf Club in its all-inclusive stays. It is booked directly with Club Med rather than through Booking.com, which is why it is not in our list.
Tips for golfers staying near Balaia

**Pair it with Pine Cliffs.** The area's two short courses are only 11 minutes apart, so you can easily play both. Not sure which suits you better? Read [Balaia vs Pine Cliffs](/guide/balaia-vs-pine-cliffs-which-quick-round-near-albufeira-should-you-play).

**Add a full 18 in Vilamoura.** The [Vilamoura Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course) is about 22 minutes away and [Salgados](/courses/salgados) about 24, so a base near Balaia also works for a longer round or two.
**Getting there.** Faro Airport is about 40 km away by road, and a hire car is the easiest way to reach the course and the rest of the Algarve.
Frequently asked questions
Which hotel is closest to Balaia Golf Village?

Balaia Golf Village Resort itself, whose apartments surround the course. The closest alternatives are Alfagar Village, about three minutes away, and Grande Real Santa Eulália, about four minutes away.
Can you play Balaia if you are not staying at the resort?
Yes. Balaia Golf Club is open to visitors every day, with a daily green fee of €50 on its 2025–26 price list. Resort guests pay €40.
What is the cheapest place to stay near Balaia?
Balaia Golf Village Resort has apartments from about €51 a night in November, and Alfagar Village and The Pátio Suite Hotel start at about €60.
Playing several courses? Find the best base for your trip

If Balaia is just one stop on your golf trip, try **Find Your Base** on the [Algarve Golf Map](/). Pick the courses you want to play and it shows you the area that sits closest to all of them, along with well-rated hotels nearby, so you spend less time driving and more time on the course.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Albufeira costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-albufeira-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: Hiring a car at Faro Airport for a golf trip: which car fits your golf bags, where the desks are, how deposits work and why the A22 is now toll-free.

content.text: Hiring a car at Faro Airport is the easiest way to play golf in different parts of the Algarve. Book an **estate car** if there are two or three of you with golf bags, or a **people carrier** for a four-ball. Expect to need a **credit card** for the deposit unless you buy the rental company's own full cover. The main Algarve motorway, the A22, has been **toll-free since January 2025**. You can compare prices from the companies at Faro Airport on [EconomyBookings](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw).
Which car fits your golf bags?

Rental sites quote boot space in litres, but a golf bag is long and rigid, so the shape of the boot matters as much as its size. Estates usually take golf bags better than an SUV that looks bigger from the outside. This is a rough guide from Leading Courses, a tee-time booking site, based on published boot sizes:

content.note: Source: Leading Courses, 'How many golf bags actually fit in a rental car?', 14 August 2026. Indicative figures based on boot specifications, not loading tests.
content.caption: How many golf bags fit, by car class

content.text: Rental companies guarantee a car class, not a model ("or similar"), so leave yourself some margin. Stand bags are easier to fit than large cart bags, and laying the driver and woods loose on top of the bags often makes the difference. If you'd rather not fly with clubs at all, see our [golf club rental guide](/club-rental).
Picking up your car at Faro Airport
According to Faro Airport, the car rental desks are just outside the terminal: as you leave the baggage reclaim area, they are on the right. Six companies have desks there:

content.note: Source: Faro Airport (ANA) car rental page, checked 17 November 2026. Check your pick-up time against these hours if your flight lands late.
content.caption: Car rental desks at Faro Airport

content.text: Other companies, often the cheaper ones on comparison sites, are based outside the airport and take you there by shuttle bus. Centauro, for example, says its shuttle leaves from near the P4 car park, to the left as you come out of arrivals, every 10–15 minutes, and its Faro office is open from 07:00 to 23:00. Allow extra time for the shuttle, both when you arrive and when you return the car.
Deposits, credit cards and "no deposit" car hire

Faro Airport's own advice is that you need a credit card, because rental companies use it to hold a security deposit, and that some companies do not accept debit cards for the deposit. The deposit usually matches the **excess**: the most you would pay if the car is damaged. It is blocked on your card when you collect the car and released when you return it undamaged.

**"No deposit" usually means buying the rental company's own full cover.** Goldcar, for example, says its Super Relax cover removes the need to leave an excess deposit, and Centauro says that with its full cover you will not need to leave a deposit. Even then, some companies take a separate deposit for fuel: Goldcar charges for the tank of fuel at pick-up and refunds it when you bring the car back full.

If you buy a separate excess insurance policy instead, it can be much cheaper, but the rental company will still block the full deposit on your card. Goldcar's terms say so explicitly: with third-party insurance, the excess deposit is blocked and any damage is charged to it, and you then claim the money back from your insurer. Check the deposit and the accepted cards in the terms before you book, not at the desk.
Tolls: the A22 is free

The A22, the motorway that runs the length of the Algarve from Lagos to the Spanish border, has had **no tolls since 1 January 2025**, as confirmed by Infraestruturas de Portugal, the company that runs Portugal's roads. Some older guides still say otherwise.

By law, every rental car in Portugal has an electronic toll device, and companies charge a small daily fee for it: Sixt charges €2.23 a day up to €22.30, and Hertz €2.21 a day up to €22.14. Both say they refund the fee if no tolls are recorded during your rental. So if you only drive around the Algarve on the A22 and local roads, you may get it back. You will pay tolls if you drive further, for example on the A2 motorway towards Lisbon.
Driving between the golf courses

Most trips between the Algarve's golf areas use the A22, which runs a few kilometres inland, parallel to the coast. The old coast road, the N125, goes through the towns and is slower. Our guide to [where to stay in the Algarve for golf](/guide/where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf) shows how many courses are within 15 and 30 minutes of each base, and every course page on our map shows the drive time from Faro Airport.
Tick the courses you want to play in **Find Your Base** and the map shows the area where they are all a short drive away, with the hotels inside it.
content.title: Plan your drives before you book
content.buttonLabel: Find your base on the map

content.text: Hire car or transfers?

Transfers make sense if you stay close to the courses you want to play. Once you play in different areas, a car can work out cheaper. As an example, here's a week based in Vilamoura with four rounds, using one transfer company's published one-way prices for up to four golfers:

content.note: Based on Algarserra's published prices from Vilamoura (one way, per vehicle, up to 4 golfers), checked 17 November 2026. Airport transfers not included.
content.caption: Example: four rounds from Vilamoura by transfer

content.text: Compare that with a quote for an estate car or a people carrier for your dates on [EconomyBookings](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw), and remember that a car also covers the trips to and from the airport, restaurants and the beach. If you'd still rather not drive, our guide to [golf transfers in the Algarve](/guide/algarve-golf-transfers-without-a-car) covers hotel shuttles, taxis and transfers, which you can also book on [GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA).
Before you drive away

**Photograph the car** all the way round, including the wheels and the windscreen, before you leave the car park, and make sure any damage is noted on the rental agreement. **Check the fuel policy:** with full-to-full, fill up near the airport before you return the car. **Don't pay twice for cover:** if you already have excess insurance, say no to the extra cover at the desk, but remember the deposit will be blocked. **Allow time for the return,** especially with an off-airport company and a shuttle to catch.

excerpt: Where to stay to play Gramacho and Vale da Pinta: Pestana's own golf apartments on the course, four top-rated resorts five minutes away and value and clifftop options in Carvoeiro, with drive times, golf perks and green fees.

content.text: Pestana Carvoeiro is a two-course golf resort in the countryside just north of Carvoeiro. [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho), designed by Ronald Fream with Nick Price, is a par-72 layout through valleys and rocky terrain, while [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta), Fream's par-71 from 1992, winds between ancient olive and carob trees and is often considered the stronger of the two. The two clubhouses are only about a kilometre apart.

This guide covers the best hotels near Pestana Carvoeiro golf: Pestana's own golf apartments on the Gramacho course, four excellent resorts within about five minutes, and good-value and clifftop options in and around Carvoeiro, all within 15 minutes.
Map of hotels near Gramacho and Vale da Pinta
The black pins are the two courses (tap one to see course details). The blue pins are the hotels in this guide; tap one to check prices and availability.
How we chose these hotels

We include a hotel if it is rated at least 8 out of 10 on Booking.com, or at least 7.8 if it offers specific golf services, and is within about 15 minutes of the courses by road. Drive times are to the Gramacho clubhouse and are calculated by road, not in a straight line. Golf services come from each hotel's own website wherever possible.

Prices are the lowest nightly rates we found in October 2026. Where the hotel publishes a 'from' price on its own website we use that; otherwise we use the lowest rate on a price-comparison site, checked against an earlier search. Check current rates with the link.
Staying on the Pestana golf resort

content.name: Pestana Gramacho Residences
content.text: Pestana's own golf apartments, set on the Gramacho course and the only place to stay inside the resort. You get the golf academy on your doorstep, a free internal shuttle and breakfast from 7am, and rooms start from about **€56 a night** on Pestana's own website, with studios and one and two-bedroom apartments for groups. Its **7.8 on Booking.com** is a little lower than the rest of this list, but nothing else is this close to the first tee.
perks: Rooms, studios and apartments with kitchens

content.text: Resorts next to the courses
These four are all within about five minutes of Gramacho and eight of Vale da Pinta, in the quiet countryside between the courses and Carvoeiro.

content.name: Vale d'Oliveiras Quinta Resort & Spa
content.text: A five-star spa resort on the same road as the Pestana golf resort, about 400 metres from Gramacho according to the resort and four minutes by car. Breakfast starts at 7.30am, there is an à la carte restaurant and 24-hour room service, and children up to 12 stay and eat free on half board, which makes it a good family choice. From about €69 a night in October.
perks: Children up to 12 stay and eat free on half board

content.name: Vale da Lapa Village Resort
content.text: Five-star villas set in gardens five minutes from Gramacho, with a spa, indoor pool and restaurant. At **9.3 on Booking.com** it is one of the best-rated resorts in Carvoeiro, and the villas suit a group of friends who want their own space. From about €91 a night in October.

content.name: Quinta do Algarvio Village
content.text: Self-catering apartments with full kitchens and a saltwater pool heated in winter, five minutes from Gramacho and rated a remarkable **9.4 on Booking.com**. One-bedroom apartments start from €85 a night on the operator's own website, and members of its Carvoeiro Clube Group club get golf discounts within the group. There is no breakfast service, so stock the fridge.

content.name: Monte Santo Resort
content.text: A five-star resort of spacious suites and townhouses with kitchens, six minutes from Gramacho and seven from Vale da Pinta. Breakfast is included, served as a buffet at its Aroma restaurant, and there is a wellness centre with sauna, Turkish bath and jacuzzi for after your round.
Best value near Pestana Carvoeiro golf

content.name: Pestana Palm Gardens
content.text: Pestana's clifftop studios and apartments in Carvoeiro, from about **€54 a night** on Pestana's own website. Pestana says guests get **benefits and discounts at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta**, which makes this the best-value way to stay with the group that runs the courses. Breakfast is charged separately, but every unit has a kitchen. About 13 minutes to Gramacho.
perks: Discounts at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta

content.name: Água Hotels Riverside
content.text: The cheapest well-rated hotel near the courses, on the Arade river near Ferragudo, about 11 minutes from Gramacho and 10 from Vale da Pinta. Breakfast starts at 7am, which suits early tee times, and the gym opens at 6am. Some guests find the décor a little dated, but for a golf trip on a budget it is hard to beat.
Hotels on the Carvoeiro coast
Stay on the coast if you want restaurants and the sea on your doorstep in the evening. Both are about 15 minutes from the courses.

content.name: Vale d'El Rei Hotel & Villas
content.text: A quiet, very well-rated hotel and villa complex east of Carvoeiro, rated **9.0 on Booking.com**. Breakfast starts at 7.30am, there are three outdoor pools and a wellness centre, and the free transfer into Carvoeiro means you can have dinner in the village without driving. About 14 minutes to Gramacho.

content.name: Tivoli Carvoeiro Algarve Resort
content.text: A five-star clifftop resort a short walk from Carvoeiro village, with sea views, a full spa and indoor and outdoor pools. It is one of the best-known golf-holiday hotels in the area: UK golf tour operators sell packages here with rounds at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta. From about €108 a night in October.
Pestana Carvoeiro green fees and what to know before you play

Gramacho and Vale da Pinta share the same green fees. Pestana's price list shows **€95 for 18 holes in low season** (December, January and June to August), €155 in high season (November, February, May and September) and €180 in premium season (March, April and October). Twilight rounds from 3.30pm cost €55, and a buggy is €55.

In summer, look out for Pestana's special: two players with a shared buggy for €184 from June to August (€92 each), also valid at Silves Golf. You need a handicap of 27 or lower for men and 35 for ladies; read more in [do you need a handicap to play golf in the Algarve](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve).
Tips for golfers staying near Pestana Carvoeiro

**Play both courses.** They are very different, and the green fees are the same. Not sure where to start? Read [Gramacho vs Vale da Pinta](/guide/gramacho-vs-vale-da-pinta-which-pestana-carvoeiro-course-should-you-play).

**More golf nearby.** [Pestana Ferragudo](/courses/pestana-ferragudo) is about 12 minutes away, the [Vale de Milho](/courses/vale-de-milho) par-3 course about 10, and the [Penina](/courses/penina-championship) courses about 20. See also our guides to [hotels near Ferragudo golf course](/guide/hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course) and [Vale de Milho](/guide/hotels-near-vale-de-milho-golf).
**Getting there.** Faro Airport is about an hour's drive east, and Portimão is 15 minutes west if you want a bigger town for an evening out.
Frequently asked questions
Which hotel is closest to Gramacho and Vale da Pinta?
Pestana Gramacho Residences is on the Gramacho course itself. Outside the resort, Vale d'Oliveiras is about four minutes away and Vale da Lapa and Quinta do Algarvio about five.
What is the cheapest place to stay near Pestana Carvoeiro golf?
Água Hotels Riverside, from about €49 a night, Pestana Palm Gardens from about €54, and Pestana Gramacho Residences on the course itself from about €56.
Do Pestana hotel guests get golf discounts?

Pestana says guests at Pestana Palm Gardens get benefits and discounts at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta. Members of the Pestana Guest Club also get from 10% off their stay. Ask about golf rates when you book.
Playing several courses? Find the best base for your trip

If Pestana Carvoeiro is just one stop on your golf trip, try **Find Your Base** on the [Algarve Golf Map](/). Pick the courses you want to play and it shows you the area that sits closest to all of them, along with well-rated hotels nearby, so you spend less time driving and more time on the course.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to the Algarve costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

excerpt: Algarve green fees with the buggy and extras added, Pestana's two-player buggy deal, and the cheapest course of each type, from official prices.

content.text: The cheapest green fee isn't always the cheapest round. At some Algarve courses the price includes a buggy; at others you pay €40 to €55 on top. Add club hire, range balls and a trolley, and a course that looked expensive can work out cheaper than one that looked like a bargain. This guide to **best value golf in the Algarve** compares what you actually pay, not just the headline green fee.

We don't rank courses by quality, because that comes down to taste. Instead we look at what your money gets you: whether a buggy is included, which deals bundle one in, and the cheapest course of each type, from sea views to tournament history. Prices come from each club's official price list or its own online booking for the 2026/27 season, checked in October and November 2026. It isn't a complete list: we've only included courses where the club publishes enough information, so a course missing here may still be good value. Always confirm the price when you book.
The real price of a round with a buggy

This table adds the buggy to the lowest green fee for one player, at the courses that publish a buggy price or include one. The cheapest months differ from course to course, so the totals don't all apply at the same time of year.

content.note: Most clubs don't say whether the buggy price is per buggy or per person. If it is per buggy and you share with a partner, your half costs less. Boavista's tariff doesn't say whether its €45 covers 18 or 9 holes. Sources: club price lists and online booking, October and November 2026.
content.caption: Lowest 18-hole green fee plus buggy, for one player

content.text: The surprise is how well the buggy-included courses come out. [Ombria](/courses/ombria) near Loulé dropped to €85 with a shared buggy in June, and still cost €99 to €101 in July, August, September and December. [Amendoeira](/courses/amendoeira-oconnor)'s online rate of €100 in December and January includes a buggy if one is available, which is less than one player pays for a green fee and buggy at Gramacho, Vale da Pinta or Silves in the same months.

If you're happy to walk, the order changes: Santo António, Benamor and Boavista are then the cheapest on this list. Our [guide to golf buggy hire in the Algarve](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve) has the rules and the courses that don't publish a buggy price.
Pestana's two players and a buggy deal

Pestana's official price list has a summer special for two players sharing one buggy at its Algarve courses. In every case it costs less than two green fees plus a buggy, and at most courses less than two green fees on their own, so the buggy effectively comes free.

content.note: Source: Pestana Golf price list, checked November 2026.
content.caption: Pestana summer special: two players and one buggy

content.text: To put that in context, two standard green fees at Gramacho cost €190 from June to August, before you add a €55 buggy. The special is €184 for both of you with the buggy. In the second half of May and in September, two green fees cost €310 against a special of €270. At Alto Golf in summer the special is €4 more than two green fees, but it includes the €55 buggy. If you're travelling as a pair and playing a Pestana course in summer, this is usually the rate to book.

Other clubs run similar bundles at different times of year, including Quinta do Vale, Quinta da Ria, Quinta de Cima and Quinta do Lago. The buggy guide lists the [current buggy offers](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve) with their dates.
The cheapest course of each type
Value depends on what you want from a round. Here's the lowest price we found for each kind of course, based on the same official prices.
Sea views: Boavista from €74

Of the 18-hole courses tagged **ocean view** on our map, [Boavista](/courses/boavista) above Lagos is the cheapest, from €74 in January, June, July, August and December. It's a hillside course, so think about a buggy. For the Algarve's most famous sea hole, the clifftop 16th on [Vale do Lobo Royal](/courses/vale-do-lobo-royal), green fees start at €116 in January, February, November and December. If nine holes are enough, [Vale de Milho](/courses/vale-de-milho) costs €22 and [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs) from €57. See [the best ocean view golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-best-ocean-view-golf-courses-in-the-algarve) for more.
A buggy in the price: Ombria from €85

[Ombria](/courses/ombria), [Amendoeira](/courses/amendoeira-faldo) and [Monte Rei](/courses/monte-rei) include a buggy in the green fee, and Ombria is the cheapest of the three. At [Vale do Lobo](/courses/vale-do-lobo-ocean), full-paying adults get a shared buggy with the Sunset rate, which costs €76 to €101 depending on the month.
A course you can walk: Salgados from €78

[Salgados](/courses/salgados) near Albufeira sits on flat land behind the beach, and Where2Golf says players generally walk it. It costs from €78 in January, July and August. [Penina Championship](/courses/penina-championship) is similarly flat and costs about €77 through booking agents, though the club itself hasn't published current rates. [Vilamoura Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium), another flat course, is €88 in December. Our guide to [Algarve golf courses you can walk](/guide/algarve-golf-courses-you-can-walk) has the full picture.
Tournament history: Penina from about €77

[Penina Championship](/courses/penina-championship), Sir Henry Cotton's 1966 course and the first in the Algarve, says it has hosted the Portuguese Open ten times. At about €77 it's the cheapest way we found to play a course with tour history. [Vila Sol](/courses/vila-sol), which hosted the Portuguese Open in 1992 and 1993, costs from €140, or €104 each with Pestana's summer special for two. The [Vilamoura Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course), which hosted the event in 1979, starts at €215 in December.

content.text: Club hire is the extra that adds up fastest over a week. Over four rounds at a Pestana course, it comes to €180, which can be more than your airline charges to fly your own clubs. Compare the two with our [airline golf bag guides](/guide) and the [club rental options](/club-rental) before you decide. Getting to the course costs money too, and our guide to [Faro Airport to Algarve golf courses](/guide/faro-airport-to-algarve-golf-courses) covers transfer and car hire costs.
Cheaper ways to play the same course

**Play late.** Twilight rates can cut a green fee by a third or more. Pestana's are €50 to €80, from 1:30pm at Ferragudo and 3pm or 3:30pm at its other courses, with a twilight buggy at €40. See our [twilight golf guide](/guide/twilight-golf-in-the-algarve), and Santo António's is €35 from 1:30pm. Our guide to [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve) lists more.

**Pick your months.** At most courses, December, January and June to August are cheapest, while March, April and October cost the most. The [Algarve golf season guide](/guide/algarve-golf-season-best-time-to-play-golf) explains the trade-offs.
**Book the bundle, not the parts.** If you want a buggy, look for a rate that includes one before adding it on arrival. The deals above are the clearest examples.
Frequently asked questions
Is golf expensive in the Algarve?

It depends on the course. The cheapest 18-hole rounds start at €57 to €67 in low season, while the best-known courses, such as Monte Rei, Quinta do Lago South and the Vilamoura Old Course, start at €188 to €215. Most courses fall between the two. Our guide to [how much a golf trip to the Algarve costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost) puts green fees together with flights, hotels and transport.
Which Algarve golf course is the best value?

There's no single answer, because it depends on what you want. If you need a buggy, Ombria and Amendoeira come out well because theirs is included. If you walk, Santo António, Benamor and Salgados are hard to beat. If you're a pair playing in summer, Pestana's two-player deal is one of the best rates we found.
Are buggies included in Algarve green fees?

Usually not. Of the courses we checked, Ombria, Monte Rei and Amendoeira include one, and Vale do Lobo includes a shared buggy with its Sunset rate. Elsewhere, buggy hire costs €40 to €55 where the club publishes a price.
